title: Commanders rule out G Sam Cosmi, S Nick Cross for Week 4
summary: The Commanders went to London on Tuesday night to prepare for Sunday's game against the Colts, but a couple of players did not make the trip.
full_text: The Commanders went to London on Tuesday night to prepare for Sunday's game against the Colts, but a couple of players did not make the trip. Right guard Sam Cosmi and safety Nick Cross both stayed in Washington and they have been ruled out for this week's game. Cosmi has a concussion and a throat injury while Cross is recovering from internal injuries that required him to have surgery after the team's Week 2 game in Dallas. Nick Allegretti replaced Cosmi in Week 3 with Lucas Patrick at center. Quarterback Jayden Daniels (left elbow), linebacker Frankie Luvu (groin), and tight end Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) all made the trip after missing the Week 3 win over the Seahawks. Their status for Sunday will be determined later in the week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Through three games, Brock Purdy still hasn't been sacked
summary: The 49ers are the fourth team since 1990 to allow zero sacks in their first three games.
full_text: 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy has started three games this season, thrown 83 passes, and still not been sacked. That's a rare achievement: The 49ers are just the fourth team since 1990 to allow zero sacks through three games of a season, joining Andy Dalton with the 2014 Bengals, and Peyton Manning with the Colts in 1999 and again in 2005. Purdy has done an excellent job this season of recognizing where the pass rush is coming from and getting rid of the ball quickly, and he has also taken off running when pressured. On 10 carries this season, Purdy has 93 rushing yards and eight first downs. Purdy is leading the league with nine touchdown passes and a 133.1 passer rating and has moved up to No. 2 in the MVP odds . Up next for the 49ers is a game against the Broncos, who led the NFL in sacks last year and are tied for seventh in the league in sacks this year. Continuing to avoid the pass rush will be a key to Purdy's attempt to lead the 49ers to a 4-0 start.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Giants don't plan to add Odell Beckham Jr. to the practice squad "at this time"
summary: The full scope of the moves the Giants made on Tuesday made their point clear.
full_text: The full scope of the moves the Giants made on Tuesday made their point clear. They could no longer justify giving a roster spot to veteran receiver Odell Beckham Jr. Beckham is gone, and receivers Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones have joined the 53-man roster. It's simple; Berrios and Jones play special teams. Beckham doesn't. And it's not a simple shuffling between the roster and the practice squad. Via Jordan Raanan of ESPN, the Giants aren’t expected to sign Beckham to the practice squad "at this time." The reunion with Beckham provided the Giants with a feel-good story, one the fans embraced. Reality has since settled in. With starting quarterback Jaxson Dart lost due to a knee injury, the Giants need to get the most out of every player on the team. Beckham wasn't doing enough. It was time for him to go. Whether he lands elsewhere remains to be seen. Other teams, like the Rams and 49ers, have needs. More injuries are inevitable. Last year, Beckham didn't play at all. It remains to be seen whether that will be the case for the balance of 2026.
author: Mike Florio

title: In the offseason, Giants weren't interested in Joe Flacco
summary: Quarterback Joe Flacco became a free agent in March.
full_text: Quarterback Joe Flacco became a free agent in March. Before re-signing with the Bengals, he explored his options. The Giants weren't one of them. Per a league source, Flacco had interest in the Giants. The Giants did not have interest in Flacco. At the time, the Giants had Jameis Winston under contract through 2026. He has since signed a two-year extension. Flacco, who played with the Ravens and current Giants coach John Harbaugh for more than a decade, eventually returned to the Bengals, on a one-year, $6 million deal. And the Bengals surely wouldn't have been willing to part with Flacco in the days since Giants quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a knee injury; they need to have Flacco around, in the event starter Joe Burrow suffers another injury. Still, the Giants could have had Flacco in March. While they'd never admit it, they could be privately kicking themselves that they didn't reciprocate his offseason interest. The Giants instead will proceed with Winston, backed up by J.J. McCarthy. They surely hope Winston plays well enough to hold the job. If he doesn't, McCarthy will surely get a chance at some point.
author: Mike Florio

title: Cowboys agree to terms with DBs Juanyeh Thomas, Alex Austin
summary: The Cowboys have been hit hard by injuries in their secondary, which is why they had four defensive backs in town to workout.
full_text: The Cowboys have been hit hard by injuries in their secondary, which is why they had four defensive backs in town to workout. They worked out defensive backs Juanyeh Thomas, Alex Austin, Shemar Bartholomew and Tyrek Funderburk as well as linebacker Germaine Pratt on Tuesday. They are signing Austin, a cornerback, to the practice squad, according to Matt Zenitz of CBS Sports. They are also signing Thomas, a safety, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. It is unclear whether Thomas is signing with the active roster or the practice squad. Austin, a seventh-round pick of the Bills in 2023, has played games for the Patriots and Texans. He has played 29 games with six starts and has 31 tackles, eight passes defensed and an interception. Thomas signed with the Cowboys as an undrafted free agent in 2022. He has appeared in 36 games, recording 62 tackles, five passes defensed and a forced fumble. Cowboys safeties Malik Hooker (fractured forearm) and P.J. Locke (foot) are on injured reserve, and Jalen Thompson (hamstring) will head there this week. Cornerbacks Shavon Revel (knee/ankle) and Cobie Durant (hamstring) also are injured.
author: Charean Williams

title: Joe Buck hopes Troy Aikman stays at ESPN
summary: Joe Buck recently re-upped with ESPN.
full_text: Joe Buck recently re-upped with ESPN. His long-time partner, Troy Aikman, is still waiting. Buck recently said he hopes Aikman will stick around. Appearing on 97.5 The Fanatic in Philadelphia, via Brandon Contes of Awful Announcing , Buck made it clear that he doesn't want to call games without Aikman in the booth. “I’m pretty well on record, having begged out of my last years at Fox to follow him to ESPN, where I stand on all that ,” Buck said. “I legitimately love the guy like a brother. We’re basically the same age; I’m 57, he’s 59. We’ve both been through divorce. We’re both girl dads. Twenty-five years, you’re sharing a lot of life together. Forget games and in the booth and all that stuff. "So, I hope so. I mean, both of us were up. It wasn’t like we were doing some national signing day where we walk in arm-in-arm and then sign contracts at the same time. We’ve always kind of kept that stuff separate. I’m obviously hopeful, to say the least, that something gets done. But that’s kind of his world, and ESPN’s world, and I’ve got to kind of mind my own yard in that stuff. I think that’s the best way to be.” At one point, it appeared that Buck and Aikman were a package deal . That changed, when Buck signed and Aikman didn't. ESPN is rolling the dice by waiting. Aikman could end up at CBS or Amazon. Of course, ESPN would also have the flexibility to put the Mannings or Pat McAfee in the booth with Buck. Then there's the white whale known as Travis Kelce. He was already sniffing around Amazon last year. He'll be able to pick his spot — and name his price — if he retires from playing after 2026. It's also impossible to overlook the reality that Aikman's desire to double dip by working for the Dolphins and ESPN could make him less attractive. Aikman can't enter team facilities, and he can't attend practice. Others who don't work for an NFL team (or who don't partially own the team) face no such restrictions. Aikman recently " called bullshit " on the notion that other broadcasters don't have conflicts of interest. Sorry, Troy, but you're missing the point. You work for the Dolphins, and you've said it was smart for them to take advantage of the things you learn while covering other teams. There's a very real difference between navigating friendships and owing a duty as a paid employee to a team that expects you to leverage your access to that team's benefit. If ESPN has other options, why keep a guy who has one hand tied behind his back because he sees no issue with covering all 32 teams while working for one of them? Aikman is good, but he's not John Madden (then again, no one is). ESPN could throw money at a bigger name than Aikman, and ESPN wouldn't have to worry about the new hire having a side hustle in the form of employment by a team.
author: Mike Florio

title: Josh Allen remains the MVP favorite, but Brock Purdy is lurking
summary: Even with no touchdown passes and a pair of interceptions on Sunday against the Chargers, Bills quarterback Josh Allen remains the clear MVP favorite.
full_text: Even with no touchdown passes and a pair of interceptions on Sunday against the Chargers, Bills quarterback Josh Allen remains the clear MVP favorite. His Week 3 performance actually improved his odds. Allen has gone from +500 to +260 to win his second NFL MVP award. Behind him currently is 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, at +425. Purdy deserves to be high on the list. The 49ers are 3-0, and Purdy has an off-the-charts passer rating of 133.1. He has nine touchdown passes on only 83 attempts, with one interception. He's averaging 9.5 yards per attempt. Purdy also has 93 rushing yards and a touchdown. Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson is currently +600, and Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes sits at +800. Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow is at +850, and Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence has odds of +1000. Bears quarterback Caleb Williams, who was initially off the board after his hamstring injury, is buried in the field at +5500. Patriots quarterback Drake Maye, who came in second a year ago for the MVP award, is at +8000. Last year's winner, Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford, currently has odds of +2800.
author: Mike Florio

title: Case Keenum's Monday night performance shows importance of having three quarterbacks
summary: Last night, Bears quarterback Case Keenum played in a regular-season game for the first time in 1,009 days.
full_text: Last night, Bears quarterback Case Keenum played in a regular-season game for the first time in 1,009 days. He played well, and the Bears won. The fact that the Bears had him on the roster proves the importance of having three quarterbacks who can be trusted to play, if necessary. When the starter is injured, the team is one injury away from needing a QB3. That's what happened to the Bears. With everyone trying to figure out the extent of Caleb Williams's absence due to a hamstring injury, no one knew that Tyson Bagent (who nearly beat the Vikings in Week 2 after replacing Williams) was in the concussion protocol. Enter Keenum. Bears coach Ben Johnson got to work on crafting a game plan based on Keenum's skills and abilities. Without Keenum, the Bears would have likely rushed to get Bagent ready, once he was cleared to play. Bagent wouldn't have been as ready as Keenum was. It's an important aspect of roster construction to have a third quarterback who'll be able to step in effectively, if the first two are injured. Not just on game day, but in the important days preceding the game. The teams that don't are taking a calculated risk that could lead to that one extra loss that could result in narrowly missing the playoffs once the dust settles on the regular season. For the Bears, the Week 3 win over the Eagles becomes the difference between 1-2 and 2-1 — and the head-to-head tiebreaker with Philadelphia could become critical to figuring out the playoff tree come Week 18.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Ramsey says he has a broken wrist
summary: In advance of Thursday night's game at Cleveland, Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey was listed as limited in practice on Monday and Tuesday, with a wrist injury.
full_text: In advance of Thursday night's game at Cleveland, Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey was listed as limited in practice on Monday and Tuesday, with a wrist injury. Via Brooke Pryor of ESPN, Ramsey told reporters on Tuesday that his wrist is broken . Will he be able to play with it? "It's just going to be about seeing if I'm able to protect it and also still be myself in a good enough capacity where I feel like if I go out there, I won't be letting any of my teammates down," Ramsey said. Via Pryor, Ramsey has a brace/cast on his wrist. Ramsey, an eight-time Pro Bowler, has played every snap through the Steelers' first three games of the 2026 season.
author: Mike Florio

title: Report: 49ers to sign Dante Pettis to the practice squad
summary: The 49ers are signing wide receiver Dante Pettis to their practice squad, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report.
full_text: The 49ers are signing wide receiver Dante Pettis to their practice squad, according to Jordan Schultz of The Schultz Report. Pettis was one of nine players to work out for the team on Tuesday. Injuries have decimated the 49ers wide receivers' room, with Ricky Pearsall out for the season, Christian Kirk still on injured reserve and De'Zhaun Stribling and Demarcus Robinson missing time. Mike Evans left Sunday's win over the Cardinals with a rib injury. The 49ers signed veteran Brandin Cooks to the practice squad last week. Pettis, 30, entered the NFL with the 49ers as a second-round pick in 2018, and he had 467 yards and five touchdowns as a rookie. The 49ers waived him during the 2020 season, and he has since played for the Giants, Bears and Saints. In eight games with the Saints last season, Pettis made nine catches for 127 yards.
author: Charean Williams

title: Ravens-Cowboys from Brazil attracts 24.9 million viewers
summary: International football does better on TV when it can be played in windows that traditionally get bigger numbers.
full_text: International football does better on TV when it can be played in windows that traditionally get bigger numbers. The Week 3 Ravens-Cowboys game in Brazil landed in the best window yet for any international game — 4:25 p.m. ET on a Sunday afternoon. And it delivered. CBS has announced that 24.9 million watched the 34-31 thriller. It's the biggest audience yet for any NFL game not played in the U.S. Frankly, we would have expected an even larger number. It's the Cowboys, for crying out loud. America's team goes to South America. Throw in a two-time MVP in Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson and make it a high-scoring game that went down to the wire, and it feels like it should have been closer to 30 million than 25 million. The NFL's annual early-morning European games begin this weekend, witha whopping six 9:30 a.m. ET kickoffs in seven weeks. (So much for the pregame shows.)
author: Mike Florio

title: With No. 9 taken in New York, J.J. McCarthy switches to No. 18
summary: Nine is no more.
full_text: Nine is no more. In more ways than one. Giants quarterback J.J. McCarthy, who created a game-day alter ego he dubbed NINE after his jersey number, won't be wearing it in New York. Tight end Isaiah Likely has No. 9. Instead, McCarthy will wear No. 18. Does it matter? For some players, it does. Still, it's the thing that dehumanizes them. That makes them not known by their name or their likeness but by an interchangeable designation. The unavailability of No. 9 in New York is a product of the recent liberalization of number assignments for skill-position players. Previously, single digits were the territory of quarterbacks and kickers. Now, they're all over the field.
author: Mike Florio

title: Bucs sign QB Brett Rypien to the practice squad
summary: The Buccaneers are signing quarterback Brett Rypien to their practice squad, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports.
full_text: The Buccaneers are signing quarterback Brett Rypien to their practice squad, Rick Stroud of the Tampa Bay Times reports. Rypien visited the Bucs on Tuesday. The team won't have Baker Mayfield for a minimum of three weeks as he recovers from a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand. Undrafted rookie Jalon Daniels will start Sunday against the Packers. The Bucs are expected to sign Easton Stick to the 53-player roster to serve as Daniels' backup. Rypien, the nephew of Super Bowl XXVI MVP Mark Rypien, was with the Rams in 2023 when Bucs offensive coordinator Zac Robinson was the quarterbacks coach. Rypien has been with nine other NFL teams and has appeared in games with the Broncos, Rams and Bengals. He has played 11 games, going 2-2 as a starter.
author: Charean Williams

title: Texans sign RB Dare Ogunbowale off Raiders' practice squad
summary: The Texans signed running back Dare Ogunbowale off the Raiders' practice squad on Tuesday, the team announced.
full_text: The Texans signed running back Dare Ogunbowale off the Raiders' practice squad on Tuesday, the team announced. Ogunbowale, 32, was with the Texans the previous four seasons. He has appeared in 63 games with Houston, playing 730 offensive snaps and 1,058 on special teams. In his time with the Texans, Ogunbowale has had 91 rushing attempts for 295 yards and three total touchdowns. He has not appeared in a game for the Raiders in 2026. In his career, Ogunbowale has appeared in 114 games with nine starts and has totaled 286 touches for 1,444 yards and seven touchdowns.
author: Charean Williams

title: Kevin Zeitler had a visit with the Packers
summary: The Packers have added a pair of veteran offensive linemen in the past couple of days and they may not be done addressing the area.
full_text: The Packers have added a pair of veteran offensive linemen in the past couple of days and they may not be done addressing the area. Tuesday's transaction report from the NFL shows that guard Kevin Zeitler visited with the team. The Wisconsin native and Wisconsin alum has been out of the league since wrapping up the 2025 season with the Titans. Zeitler started all 16 games he played in Tennessee and has 213 career starts since entering the league as a 2012 second round pick of the Bengals. The Packers signed Laken Tomlinson to their active roster and Mekhi Becton to their practice squad earlier this week.
author: Josh Alper

title: Giants put Brian Burns on IR, sign WR Charlie Jones off practice squad
summary: The Giants' roster moves on Tuesday included moving linebacker Brian Burns to injured reserve.
full_text: The Giants' roster moves on Tuesday included moving linebacker Brian Burns to injured reserve. Burns tore his ACL in Sunday's loss to the Titans and will join quarterback Jaxson Dart on the sideline for the rest of the 2026 season. Abdul Carter and Kayvon Thibodeaux will be the main contributors off the edge in Burns's absence. The Giants also released wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. on Tuesday and they filled the two open roster spots with wide receivers. Braxton Berrios is one of them — as previously reported — and Charlie Jones is the other one. Both wideouts were on the practice squad. Jones played in 33 games for the Bengals over the last three seasons and had three touchdowns as a returner — one punt return and two kickoff returns — while playing a limited role on offense.
author: Josh Alper

title: Brian Schottenheimer: I hurt the team in loss to the Ravens
summary: Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said there was "no explanation" for how the team closed out the game.
full_text: Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer tried to explain his decisions over the final 28 seconds of Sunday's loss to the Ravens in Rio, but the guy who runs the show in Dallas made it clear on Tuesday that those explanations fell on deaf ears. Team owner Jerry Jones said that there is " no explanation that you’re satisfied with" for how the Cowboys went from first down on the 1-yard-line to losing on a last-second field goal by Ravens kicker Tyler Loop. At a press conference later in the day, Schottenheimer said that he damaged the team's chances with his decisions over a sequence that included a timeout with 14 seconds left, coaching Dak Prescott to throw a ball away on third down rather than try to get the ball into the end zone and having Brandon Aubrey kick the ball deep after his game-tying field goal. "I didn’t do very good in the final 28 seconds ," Schottenheimer said. "When you talk about finishing the game — when you look at our two games that we’ve lost, we haven’t finished — that was a big part of this one. I felt like I overcoached Dak on third down, kinda affected his decision making a little bit. And I let that kinda bleed over to my decision about kicking the ball. . . . I’ll take accountability for it. It’s football and life, that's what happens. I hurt our chances to win that game. I’ll be better and I’m better than that." Schottenheimer said Jones "understands there was a mistake that was made" and vowed that "those things won't happen again" in the future. He also stressed that the whole team has to be stronger in the fourth quarter if they want to avoid more painful losses in the future.
author: Josh Alper

title: Vikings sign LB Kyle Van Noy to active roster, place TE Josh Oliver on IR
summary: The Vikings signed outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and quarterback Max Brosmer from their practice squad to their 53-player roster.
full_text: The Vikings signed outside linebacker Kyle Van Noy and quarterback Max Brosmer from their practice squad to their 53-player roster. Brosmer's promotion was previously reported. Van Noy joined Minnesota's practice squad before the season and was elevated for each of the first three games. He has totaled seven tackles, including four for loss, and 1.5 sacks. Minnesota also placed tight end Josh Oliver on injured reserve. He tore his biceps while blocking on a field-goal attempt Sunday. Receiver Jeshaun Jones completed a three-game suspension by the NFL and reverted to the 53-player roster. Minnesota also terminated the contract of punter Johnny Hekker, who signed to the Vikings' practice squad last week before signing to the active roster on Saturday. Hekker filled in for undrafted rookie Brett Thorson, who injured his hamstring in Week 2. Hekker punted eight times for 372 yards, averaging 46.5 yards and netting 41.5. He placed two inside the Buccaneers' 20-yard line and booted a long of 63 yards. Hekker also cleanly held for two extra points and three field goals by Reichard, who has made 26 consecutive field goals. Additionally, Minnesota signed outside linebacker Kenny Dyson, Jr. to its practice squad and released running backs Jerome Ford and Jaret Patterson and defensive lineman Jonathan Harris from its practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Panthers sign G Torricelli Simpkins to their 53-man roster
summary: The Panthers are set to be without guard Damien Lewis for a little bit, so they added some offensive line depth on Tuesday.
full_text: The Panthers are set to be without guard Damien Lewis for a little bit, so they added some offensive line depth on Tuesday. They announced that they have signed guard Torricelli Simpkins off of their practice squad. Simpkins signed with Carolina ahead of the regular season. Simpkins played in 15 games and started twice for the Saints last season. The Panthers waived linebacker Maema Njongmeta in a corresponding move. He had three tackles and a forced fumble in Sunday's loss to the Browns. Linebacker Cam Gill and offensive lineman Isaia Glass signed to the practice squad while guard Chandler Zavala was released from that roster to wrap up the day's moves.
author: Josh Alper

title: Nick Saban tiptoes around obvious issue with capping player pay but not coach pay
summary: One of the best arguments against the Protect College Sports Act comes from the obvious hypocrisy between placing artificial limits on player compensation and no limits on coach compensation.
full_text: One of the best arguments against the Protect College Sports Act comes from the obvious hypocrisy between placing artificial limits on player compensation and no limits on coach compensation. There is no argument to justify the disconnect. That hasn't stopped those trying to limit player freedoms from trying to come up with one. Former radio host Doug Gottlieb, who has coached the University of Wisconsin Green Bay basketball program to a buyout-worthy record of 22-43 over two seasons, argued last week that " coaches are worth more than players , they just do more." Right or wrong, that's not the issue. The issue is whether one group of workers should have their pay limited in the name of "saving" college sports and whether another group should be able to follow the rules of a free marketplace. Former college football coach Nick Saban, who now works for ESPN and as a political operative aimed at getting the PCSA passed (I'd love to know how much, if anything, he's getting paid to be a primary face of that effort), tried a similar approach while appearing Tuesday on First Take . "Well, but these things are totally different markets ," Saban said in response to the clear double standard, via Awful Announcing . "Like, that's like asking me, does a student's scholarship equal the professor's pay? I mean, how much value does a coach create for a university?" First, let's get past the "scholarship" bullshit. Student-athletes are no longer students. They're employees, the same as the coach, the professor, and everyone else who provides services to a university. The actual cost to the school of having another student attend (or not attend) class is no longer relevant to the analysis. For many of the capable players, they're majoring if anything in football — just don't ask for the real stats on the placement rate. And with the schools turning their Advanced Football Studies coursework into many millions of dollars, they're entitled to be paid now, especially since there's a small chance of being paid later. Second, Saban still avoids the issue. For players, capping their pay is supposedly necessary to "saving" the entire collegiate sports system. For coaches, it continues to be "grab what you can while you can." Saban then pivoted to the question of coaching buyouts, which also have gotten out of control. With, for some reason, no effort to get Congress to intervene. "You know, rather than worry about amount of money people make," Saban said, "I think the thing that has been difficult is when coaches get fired, and they have these huge buyouts. And everybody says, 'Well, how can the university afford to pay him that?' I think you can figure out, OK, you can't have any more than a five-year contract or whatever it is. And maybe the buyout can only be so much. But I think that's maybe a better way to approach it than try to make these two things — they're different markets, you know? Players' market's different than coaches' market." Whether Saban realizes it or not, he's admitting to the existence of a disconnect by conceding that a certain type of limit should be placed on coaching compensation. He's just suggesting something that doesn't limit the pay a coach receives. He wants to limit the amount the coach would be owed if/when the school decides to fire one coach and hire another. From player pay to professor pay to coaching pay to coaching buyouts, there are business decisions that every university must make in a way that balances the budget. In the past, the administrators were able to do that with a line item for "player compensation" that was $0.00. Now, it's harder to balance the budget. They still should be expected to do it. The issue isn't chaos created by players being allowed to participate in capitalism. It's chaos created by mismanagement. Schools make purchases they can't afford, when it comes to the revenue-generating sports programs — especially since those programs are required for some reason to subsidize the non-revenue-generating sports. This shouldn't be a political issue. It should be a "hire better businesspeople" issue. Businesspeople who know how best to generate maximum revenue and to carve it up responsibly. How to restrain themselves from pulling out all the stops to attract the next shiny object, player or coach, in the hopes of earning even more revenue. The entire effort to cap player pay cuts against the supposed American ideal that stands for two simple words: Get paid. Given that one side is very well organized and funded and that the other is disorganized and voiceless, the effort to turn freedom on its head has had success in the Senate. Here's hoping that the House of Representatives takes the basic concepts of U.S. financial liberty a little more seriously than 77 Senators have.
author: Mike Florio

title: Jalen Hurts: I felt fine during concussion check, wish they could have expedited things
summary: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts had to leave the game for a concussion evaluation after getting hit on the sideline during Monday night's loss to the Bears, and that proved costly for the Eagles: They were in the red zone at the time, but they came away with no points when backup quarterback Andy Dalton threw an interception.
full_text: Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts had to leave the game for a concussion evaluation after getting hit on the sideline during Monday night's loss to the Bears, and that proved costly for the Eagles: They were in the red zone at the time, but they came away with no points when backup quarterback Andy Dalton threw an interception. Hurts said after the game that by the time Dalton threw that interception, he thought he had done everything he needed to do to satisfy the requirements of the league's concussion rules, but the medical people hadn't yet given him clearance to return to the field. "I was still waiting. Just waiting for the thumbs up. I felt fine, we already checked it. I don't know the extent of the process. Obviously wish they could have expedited things. I felt fine," Hurts said. It was an unfortunate sequence for the Eagles, who would have tied the game 7-7 with a touchdown and extra point but instead stayed behind 7-0 and trailed for the rest of the game. But the NFL is always going to prioritize taking the time to conduct the evaluation over hurrying a player back onto the field. Hurts found that out the hard way.
author: Michael David Smith

title: Jets sign K Jason Sanders to the active roster, cut K Blake Grupe
summary: The Jets signed kicker Jason Sanders to the active roster, the team announced.
full_text: The Jets signed kicker Jason Sanders to the active roster, the team announced. They waived kicker Blake Grupe and cornerback Jordan Clark. The Jets also added two offensive linemen — Nick Dawkins and Jimmy Morrissey — to the practice squad. Sanders, who leads the Jets with 20 points and has connected on 5-of-6 field goal attempts, was a practice squad elevation for each of the team's first three games. He was successful on three field goal tries — 52, 51 and 33 yards — in Tennessee and had one make from 32 yards against Green Bay. On Sunday against the Lions, Sanders made a 42-yard field goal in the third quarter. A seventh-round pick of Miami in the 2018 draft, Sanders ranks third in Dolphins franchise history with 826 points. His 84.6 field-goal percentage is the highest (minimum 50 attempts) in team annals, and his 221 field goals are second only to Olindo Mare. Grupe spent the summer in Indianapolis before the Jets claimed him off waivers on Aug. 31. Clark joined the practice squad on Aug. 31 before signing to the active roster on Sep. 15. He appeared in two games this season, lining up in 17 special teams snaps.
author: Charean Williams

title: Raiders sign WR Cody White, place WR Jack Bech on IR
summary: Raiders receiver Cody White has three receptions this year.
full_text: Raiders receiver Cody White has three receptions this year. All three have gone for touchdowns in the last two weeks. Now he’ll get to see if he can keep that going, as White has been signed to Las Vegas’ 53-man roster. Having been on the practice squad, White was out of elevations. He has been on the field for 56 percent of special teams snaps and 16 percent of offensive snaps so far this season. White, 27, has appeared in 33 career games since entering the league as an undrafted free agent in 2020. As a corresponding move, the Raiders have placed receiver Jack Bech on injured reserve. He suffered a fractured forearm during Sunday’s victory over the Saints. Additionally, the team added receiver Phillip Dorsett to the practice squad and released receiver Justin Shorter from the practice squad.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Dolphins sign ILB Shaka Heyward off Bengals' practice squad
summary: The Dolphins signed inside linebacker Shaka Heyward off the Bengals' practice squad, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Dolphins signed inside linebacker Shaka Heyward off the Bengals' practice squad, the team announced Tuesday. Heyward has appeared in 18 career games in two seasons with Cincinnati (2024-25). He has totaled eight tackles, including one tackle for loss, on defense, adding 14 tackles and one forced fumble on special teams. He entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent with Cincinnati in 2025. The Dolphins also announced signing offensive guard James Ester to the practice squad. Ester initially joined the Dolphins on May 14 when they claimed him off waivers from the Packers. He entered the NFL in 2024 as an undrafted free agent with Green Bay, where he spent two seasons (2024-25) on the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Commanders announce Austin Ekeler signing, placement of Leo Chenal on IR
summary: The Commanders have made it official with Austin Ekeler.
full_text: The Commanders have made it official with Austin Ekeler. Washington announced the club has re-signed Ekeler after he had spent the last two seasons with the club. Ekeler suffered a torn Achilles in Week 2 of last season. He had appeared in 12 games with six starts for Washington in 2024, recording 733 yards from scrimmage with four total touchdowns. “We'll get him into the mix and see what the next three days looks like ," Quinn said, via Zach Selby of the team’s website. "It's cool to have Austin here. He's a great teammate and really one respected teammate here. It was definitely good to have him back into today.” The Commanders placed linebacker Leo Chenal on injured reserve to open up a spot for Ekeler. Chenal underwent season-ending neck surgery on Monday morning, which head coach Dan Quinn said went well. Additionally, the Commanders placed linebacker Marvin Jones Jr. on the practice squad injured list.
author: Myles Simmons

title: Patriots place OL Greg Van Roten on injured reserve
summary: The Patriots placed offensive lineman Greg Van Roten on injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday.
full_text: The Patriots placed offensive lineman Greg Van Roten on injured reserve, the team announced Tuesday. Van Roten started at right guard, with Mike Onwenu on injured reserve, but he left Sunday's game in the second quarter with a thigh injury. Walter Rouse replaced Van Roten. Van Roten, 36, appeared in all three games this season after signing with the team Aug. 18. He has played for the Packers (2012-13), Panthers (2017-19), Jets (2020-21), Bills (2022), Raiders (2023) and Giants (2024-25). He also had short offseason stints with the Seahawks (2014) and Jaguars (2017) and spent two seasons with the Toronto Argonauts (2015-16) of the Canadian Football League. The Patriots also announced they have released linebacker Riley Wilson from the practice squad. Wilson, 24, signed with the Patriots as a rookie free agent on July 22 and spent the first three weeks of the season on the practice squad.
author: Charean Williams

title: Rams hopeful S Kamren Kinchens can return this week
summary: Safety Kamren Kinchens was among the Rams players who missed Sunday night's loss to the Broncos and head coach Sean McVay gave an update on his status on Monday.
full_text: ''' Safety Kamren Kinchens was among the Rams players who missed Sunday night's loss to the Broncos and head coach Sean McVay gave an update on his status on Monday. Kinchens has missed the last two games with a hamstring injury, but McVay made it sound like there's a fairly good chance that he'll be able to play in Philadelphia in Week 4. "Looking good, we’re hopeful we’ll get him back ," McVay said in an interview with the team's website. Kinchens had nine tackles in the Rams' Week 1 loss to the 49ers. He played in every game for the team over the 2023 and 2024 seasons. The Rams are also hoping to get wide receiver Puka Nacua back this week and Wednesday's practice report should provide some more clues about both players' chances of getting back on the field.
author: Josh Alper

title: Jim Harbaugh gives Mike McDaniel a vote of confidence
summary: The Chargers offense ranks 20th, and quarterback Justin Herbert has three touchdowns and four interceptions and his passer rating of 73.4 ranks 26th.
full_text: The Chargers offense ranks 20th, and quarterback Justin Herbert has three touchdowns and four interceptions and his passer rating of 73.4 ranks 26th. Los Angeles has more turnovers (six) than touchdowns (five) as a team. Coach Jim Harbaugh said he has not considered taking control from offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel. "No, we trust Mike. We believe in Mike ," Harbaugh said, via Austin Knoblauch of the Los Angeles Times . It's not like Harbaugh has any other option but to publicly give McDaniel a vote of confidence and hope the former Dolphins head coach can fix it. Harbaugh hired McDaniel this offseason to add a dynamic element to the offense, which hasn't happened yet. While Harbaugh issued his first public criticism of Herbert, saying Monday that Herbert needs " to be better " in his decision-making, the head coach hasn't done the same with McDaniel. "We're searching for every possible way to give ourselves an advantage," Harbaugh said. "Every possible way to not beat ourselves." In his postgame comments, Herbert pushed back against the idea that McDaniel's scheme is too complex. "He's definitely a guy that we need to lean on; he's done such an incredible job," Herbert said, via Jonah Bronstein of the Associated Press. "It's on us as an offense to run the plays the way he sees them, listen to coaching, and do our job to make those plays. And we haven't done that for him. So obviously, we feel horrible ."
author: Charean Williams

title: Bengals put CB Jalen Davis on IR, sign TE Tanner Hudson to active roster
summary: The Bengals announced several roster moves on Tuesday afternoon.
full_text: The Bengals announced several roster moves on Tuesday afternoon. They confirmed the previously reported signing of wide receiver Mitchell Tinsley off of the Texans' practice squad and that they have waived wide receiver Ke'Shawn Williams. They also placed cornerback Jalen Davis on injured reserve and signed tight end Tanner Hudson off of their practice squad. Davis injured his hamstring in Sunday's loss to the Steelers. Davis started two of the team's three games this season and made 10 tackles. He'll have to miss at least four games before he will be able to return to the lineup. Hudson has played in two games this year and he has three catches for 17 yards. He played in 38 games for the team over the past three seasons.

title: Prisco's Week 4 NFL picks: Eagles upset Rams, Texans over Cowboys

full_text:
With this week's NFL games , the first of October, it's time to put the stink of my picks in September away. It wasn't great.
I went 8-8 straight up last week and 6-9-1 against the spread. That brings my straight-up record to 29-19 for the season. My ATS mark is a dismal 21-26-1.
Let's just say I am happy October is here.
The first two weeks of October are when we start getting a true gauge on the NFL teams . We find out who is a contender or pretender.
That makes it a little easier to pick games. I hope anyway.
The goal now is to get over .500 ATS. Then it's time to act like a contender.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
Can you believe this is a big game in the AFC North? Both teams are 2-1 and the Browns are one of the surprise teams so far. The Steelers looked good last week, beating the Bengals , but the Browns have played well against them in Cleveland. Upset special. Browns get to 3-1.
Pick: Browns 21, Steelers 20
Both teams won for the first time last week and now head to London to play this week. Then Colts defense showed improvement last week, while the Commanders defense made some big plays. Look for the Colts and Commanders to both score a lot, but it's the Colts who will win it late.
Pick: Colts 31, Commanders 30
The Patriots are on the road for the second straight week and they are coming off a bad showing at Jacksonville. Drake Maye is struggling. That will continue here. Josh Allen gets back on track after a so-so game last week. Bills win it,
Pick: Bills 30, Patriots 17
The Jets are playing on the road for the second straight week, while the Bears are playing on a short week. Chicago looked good in blowing out the Eagles Monday night. It looks like Tyson Bagent will be in at quarterback. Look for Chicago to keep rolling as they get to 3-1.
The Bengals are back home after two weeks on the road, losing to the Steelers last week. The Jaguars beat up the Patriots last week, but this is a tougher challenge with Joe Burrow and that passing game. The Jaguars lead the league in scoring defense, but that won't hold up here. Bengals take it.
Pick: Bengals 23, Jaguars 17
The Giants didn't do a lot on offense in the victory over the Titans last week, but the weather was brutal. The Cardinals are coming off a road loss to the 49ers , but they did some good things in that game. Against a lesser opponent than San Francisco, I think Arizona will find a way to win it.
Pick: Cardinals 24, Giants 21
The Eagles looked awful Monday night in the loss to the Bears, while the Rams blew a lead at Denver Sunday night. This is a long trip to try and make up for that. The Rams play well on the East Coast, but I think this will be an Eagles team that is refocused. They take a close one.
These two are hurting right now in a lot of spots, but the Bucs will be without quarterback Baker Mayfield . That means rookie Jalon Daniels will make his first NFL start. That's a challenge, even at home. Look for Jordan Love to play better here as the Packers get a much-needed victory.
This is the Derrick Henry Revenge game. The Titans let him walk three seasons ago, and Baltimore is glad they did. Look for Henry to be the focal point of the offense. The Titans are lifeless right now on offense and they are playing back-to-back road games. This won't be pretty.
Pick: Ravens 33, Titans 14
The schedule-maker didn't do the Cowboys any favors by putting them out on the road after the loss to the Ravens in Brazil. The 0-3 Texans are home for the third time in three weeks. The defense was better last week and I think that will be the difference here. The Texans' offense will be better than it has been in recent games, too.
Pick: Texans 24, Cowboys 18
This is a challenging road game as the Dolphins face that tough Minnesota defense, led by former Dolphins coach Brian Flores. You know he will be amped to play the team that fired him. The Miami offense will be without star runner De'Von Achane , which will make it even more challenging. Look for that Vikings defense to get some takeaways to lead to points. Vikings big.
Pick: Vikings 27, Dolphins 10
This is a battle of undefeated teams. Few saw that coming. Both teams are coming off road victories. These games are always fun to watch, with the rivalry being what it is. But the Chiefs will win this as Patrick Mahomes has a big day.
Pick: Chiefs 29, Raiders 24
This is one of the best games of the week. The Broncos are coming off an impressive comeback victory over the Rams Sunday night. The 49ers have rolled to a 3-0 record behind Brock Purdy . Look for that to continue here. Purdy has a big day as the 49ers stay undefeated.
Pick: 49ers 28, Broncos 21
The Chargers are 0-3 and coming off a long trip in losing to the Bills. The Seahawks were upset last week by the Commanders. That will get their attention, which won't be a good thing for the Chargers. Look for that Seattle defense to come up big against Justin Herbert .
Pick: Seahawks 30, Chargers 20
The Panthers are really banged up and Bryce Young is hurting to go with a bunch of other injuries. They played short-handed in the loss to the Browns last week.  The Lions won a high-scoring game with the Jets Sunday and this one will be just like it. Look for Jared Goff to play well here as the Lions win a road game.
Pick: Lions 31, Panthers 26
The Falcons impressed last Thursday in blowing out Green Bay on the road. Getting Michael Penix back at quarterback matters. They will continue to give it to Bijan Robinson in this one. The Saints will get theirs behind Tyler Shough . It's high scoring, and the Falcons will win it.
Pick: Falcons 33, Saints 30

title: Giants release Odell Beckham Jr.: Landing spots for veteran pass-catcher include Rams
summary: New York parts ways with the wide receiver for the second time
full_text:
The New York Giants are releasing wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. , per NFL Media . The news comes on the heels of the Giants' 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, where Beckham played just six offensive snaps and saw one target. He leaves New York for the second time in his career, having played a total of 20 offensive snaps in three games with zero catches this season.
OBJ, who was selected by New York with the No. 12 overall pick in the 2014 NFL Draft , ranks second in franchise history behind Amani Toomer in receiving yards with 5,476. He also ranks fourth in receiving touchdowns with 44. His return to the Giants was one of the more fun and nostalgic storylines of the offseason, but he found himself low on the depth chart behind Malik Nabers , Darnell Mooney and Malachi Fields .
"I have an opportunity to rewrite some of the last bit of the chapter," Beckham said in August after making the Giants' final 53-man roster. "Don't know, last year, whatever it is, I just know I'm going to give my all. But definitely had that moment where it was like you could let out some of the pain that I feel like I went through. It was just very healing, very emotional, something I was very happy about."
Fans wanted to see more of Beckham during his short second stint in New York. Just this past Sunday, those at MetLife Stadium chanted for Beckham.
#Giants fans chanting they want “OBJ.” They want to see @obj more involved: pic.twitter.com/XSIVevobrP
ESPN points out that the Giants had to decide on the placement of wide receiver and punt returner Braxton Berrios , who is now out of practice squad elevations. He has now been signed to the active roster. Jordan Schultz reports that Beckham will not be returning to the Giants' practice squad, as he's looking for an opportunity to play right now.
Beckham hit the ground running in his NFL career, putting up 1,305 yards receiving and 12 touchdowns in his first season in just 12 games played. His 108.8 receiving yards per game led the league. Beckham's best campaign came in 2015, when he caught 96 passes for 1,450 yards and 13 touchdowns.
After five seasons with the Giants, Beckham was traded to the Cleveland Browns . He recorded his fifth 1,000-yard season in 2019, then tore his ACL in 2020. As the situation in Cleveland cratered in 2021, Beckham was released and joined the Los Angeles Rams . He won a Super Bowl ring that year, but re-tore his ACL in the final game. Beckham sat out the 2022 season, spent one year with the Baltimore Ravens , and then 2024 with the Miami Dolphins before taking another one-year break in 2025.
So, OBJ still wants to play. It remains to be seen if there will be any interest in him given that he turns 34 in November, but there could be some opportunities. Let's take a look at four potential landing spots for Beckham.
Reuniting with the Rams does make some sense. Puka Nacua has missed two straight games with a nagging groin/hip issue, leaving Davante Adams and Konata Mumpfield as the leading receivers. The Rams are off to a surprising 1-2 start following the Sunday night loss to the Denver Broncos .
OBJ isn't a game-changing type of talent at this stage of his career, but he does have familiarity with Matthew Stafford and Sean McVay.
The Kansas City Chiefs could be in the market for a veteran wide receiver. That room needs some help, as Patrick Mahomes is still relying on 36-year-old Travis Kelce to be his leading receiver. Rashee Rice has 190 yards receiving through three games, with Tyquan Thornton behind him at 108 yards receiving. If there's one weakness with the Chiefs, it's probably the wide receiver position.
The New England Patriots are off to an embarrassing 1-2 start, and fans are starting to ask questions about quarterback Drake Maye following his three-turnover performance in the 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. A.J. Brown is sidelined with a high ankle sprain, which has put more pressure on Mack Hollins , Romeo Doubs and DeMario Douglas . Hollins is the only one who is averaging more than 50 yards per game.
The Patriots benefitted from veteran wideout Stefon Diggs last year, who was their leading receiver during the Super Bowl run. Beckham would not have the kind of impact Diggs did on this offense, but he could be an option for Mike Vrabel.
The Las Vegas Raiders are a surprising 3-0 this season despite having one of the weaker wide receiver rooms in the NFL. Tre Tucker leads the team in receiving with 189 yards, then the next leading wide receiver is Jalen Nailor , who has 52 yards receiving through three games. This unit just lost Jack Bech to a broken forearm, so if OBJ wants to play, Sin City could be an option.
author: Jordan Dajani

title: Jerry Jones sounds off on Cowboys' coaching gaffes at end of Week 3 loss in Brazil: 'We made mistakes'
summary: Brian Schottenheimer took blame for the final-minute clock management against the Ravens, but Dallas' owner made it clear he expects the coaching staff to learn from the breakdown without making any staff changes
full_text:
The Dallas Cowboys coaching staff made several questionable decisions during the final minute of the team's 34-31 loss in Brazil on Sunday, and it's safe to say that Jerry Jones was not happy with what he saw.
During an interview on Tuesday with 105.3 the Fan in Dallas, Jones was asked how he felt about the coaching gaffes at the end of the game and whether the coaching staff offered him an acceptable explanation for why they happened.
"There is no explanation you're satisfied with. None," Jones told 105.3 the Fan in Dallas. "Let's be sure that we all understand that. They [the coaches] don't have one that they're satisfied with."
Jones was specifically asked about Brian Schottenheimer's decision to use a timeout with just 14 seconds left to play in the game. On a second-and-goal from Baltimore's 7-yard line, Dak Prescott scrambled for a 2-yard gain and that's when Dallas used its third and final timeout. With the Cowboys heading into a third down, it was pretty clear they were only going to run one more play, and if that failed, they were going to kick a field goal. Since they were only going to run one more play, they could have called a timeout with about 10 seconds left -- instead of 14 -- and that would have left the Ravens with almost no time to use at the end of the game.
The third-down play is where another questionable coaching decision came in. On the play, which was coming out of the timeout, Schottenheimer said he told Prescott to throw it to George Pickens or throw it away.
"It had to go to [Pickens] or throw it away," Schottenehimer said of the play. "He was throwing it away. That's on me. I overcoached him."
Prescott ended up throwing it away so quickly that the clock only ran from 14 seconds down to 10, and he threw it away even though Pickens appeared to be open.
Dak throws it away when George Pickens had the separation for a TD. pic.twitter.com/JyP9dMytvN
During a press conference on Tuesday, the Cowboys' head coach admitted that he could have done a better job at the end of the game.
"I'm man enough to take mistakes. I make a lot of mistakes. I'm certainly not perfect," Schottenheimer said, via ESPN ."I hurt our chance to win that game and I'll be better. And I'm better than that. I'm better than I performed in the last 28 seconds."
After the third-down failure, Brandon Aubrey tied the game at 31 with a short field goal. Following the kick, the clock still had seven seconds left, which was enough time for Baltimore to get in position for a game-winning 56-yard field goal from Tyler Loop . If the Cowboys had burnt some more time before using their timeout or not called for a touchback on the ensuing kickoff following Aubrey's field goal, the game almost certainly would have gone to overtime.
"We made mistakes during that time," Jones admitted. "There's no question about it, so there is no explanation, but there's an evaluation of how not to make the same mistakes again, which is what you should be doing. You can't get that back."
The good news for Schottenheimer, who's in his second season as the Cowboys' head coach, is that it doesn't sound like Jones is ready to fire anyone over the loss. As a matter of fact, Jones sounds even more optimistic about the season following the painful setback.
"We will be better from this experience that we had with Baltimore and what happened to us at the end of the game," Jones said, via ESPN . "A win would have given you another way of couching it as far as having growth and enthusiasm for having won a game like that because we did come back and we came back in an impressive way. All of that makes us realize we really are just at the beginning of what I hope is an exciting year for us."
Yes, it was a tough loss for the Cowboys, but it's still early in the season and they're still very much alive to win the NFC East. With Philadelphia also losing in Week 3, the 1-2 Cowboys are just one game out of first place behind both the Giants (2-1) and Eagles (2-1) heading into Week 4.
author: John Breech

title: Predicting NFL's first coaching change of 2026: Why Todd Bowles, Jim Harbaugh are in greatest danger
summary: Sluggish starts put these coaches in danger of becoming the first to lose their job
full_text:
The first head coach firing of the 2025 NFL season came on Oct. 13. The year before that, Oct. 8 was the first fateful day. With the calendar about to flip from September to October, history suggests at least one unfortunate coach will be out the door in the coming weeks, and there are a few candidates that may be in line for an in-season pink slip.
Some worked their way off scalding seats over the first three weeks of the 2026 season. Aaron Glenn (New York Jets) and Shane Steichen (Arizona), for instance, both have a win under their belts and were competitive in their losses. They could be out the door by the end of the year, but the chances that these highly scrutinized leaders become the first casualties of the coaching carousel are slimmer than they appeared at the beginning of the month.
At the same time, surprisingly rough starts for a few teams placed new pressure on coaches to right the ship. The Chargers and Packers , for instance, have a combined one win despite opening the year as perceived postseason contenders.
Five of our NFL writers at CBS Sports convened for a roundtable discussion to determine which coaches are at the highest risk of becoming the first to lose their jobs in 2026. Here are the responses.
"The Buccaneers coach had arguably the hottest seat in the NFL coming into the season, and not much has changed. In fact, his seat is probably hotter. After going 8-9 and missing the playoffs last year, Bowles fired most of his staff, which is typically a last-ditch effort before the entire operation gets overhauled. The rearranging of the deck chairs hasn't done much to turn the tide in Tampa, with the Bucs stumbling to a 0-3 start to the season. Each of those losses has come in one-score games, and the organization just feels stale. With Baker Mayfield (thumb) dinged up, it may only get worse from here.
"I'd keep an eye on Week 5 when the Bucs travel to Dallas to face the Cowboys on 'Thursday Night Football' as a possible spot where a change could be made. If they fall to 0-5, that mini-bye after a Thursday night game — especially if the primetime loss is one-sided — has been a pocket where changes have been made in the past."
"Todd Bowles is a firing waiting to happen. Baker Mayfield is hurt, and he was playing poorly before that. The offensive line and the offensive ecosystem as a whole have regressed under new offensive coordinator Zac Robinson . Coaches can usually survive striking out on one coordinator who runs the other side of the ball — Bowles did after he hired and fired Josh Grizzard within the span of a year last season — but rarely can they do so two straight years without any postseason success.
"The defense has been largely good, which is a point in Bowles' favor, but let's see if it can hold up against improved competition in the coming weeks without Mayfield."
"The Chargers were supposed to have a team capable of winning the franchise's first playoff game since the Philip Rivers era. Instead, the Chargers are 0-3 and are employing an offense that looks like it came straight from 'The Longest Yard.' Justin Herbert has regressed, and it's quickly become apparent that Mike McDaniel and Jim Harbaugh are indeed an odd couple.
"The odds of Harbaugh being the first canned coach only increase when you consider the Chargers' upcoming four games are against the Seahawks , Broncos , Chiefs and Rams . It's possible the Chargers fire Harbaugh during their Week 7 bye if things don't improve by then. Would that lead to McDaniel becoming interim coach?"
"The Chargers are continuously the 'what if' team, with the league's top 'what if' quarterback in Justin Herbert. But 'what if' doesn't win football games. Los Angeles dropped to 0-3 after a 24-16 loss to the Buffalo Bills . Despite forcing five turnovers and sacking Josh Allen four times, L.A. couldn't win, and alarm bells are ringing. The Chargers have the sixth-worst completion percentage (59.1), are tied for the third-fewest passing touchdowns (3), and are tied for second in interceptions (4).
"The team is very concerning, and year after year, it seems they cannot reach, or even get close to, their ceiling. Jim Harbaugh took over as the head coach in 2024, and in the two seasons he's been there, the Chargers haven't made it past the wild card round, even when they had the talent to. If things keep going the way they are, Harbaugh will be looking for a new coaching job for 2027. Their schedule going forward isn't doing them any favors, and they could easily go 1-6, or worse, to start the season."
"The Packers committed to Matt LaFleur in the offseason with a multi-year contract extension, so moving on from him less than a year later would require team president Ed Policy to eat crow and likely leave the franchise on the hook for millions of dollars in guaranteed salary. But what about the start to this season suggests LaFleur belongs on the sideline? His only win came in overtime against the Jets , and he just sustained a Week 3 drubbing at the hands of the previously winless Falcons . The offense is a mess, the defense seems to have regressed and the path back to the playoffs is treacherous. There are three other legitimate contenders vying for the NFC North crown.
"LaFleur is the longest-tenured active coach without a Super Bowl appearance, and he only has one postseason win without Aaron Rodgers . Packers fans are losing confidence in his ability to turn the campaign around, and even if he did, the track record suggests there is nothing to be excited for in January. The last time the Packers made a coaching change, they fired Mike McCarthy in-season. LaFleur could be in for the same fate if this year continues its downward spiral."
author: Carter Bahns
