title: Six lessons learned in Week 3: Texans, Eagles offenses in major trouble, officials need help
summary: Plus, it's Brock Bowers' world and we're just living in it
full_text:
September NFL football is officially over, and through three weeks, we have undefeated teams both surprising ( Raiders ! Vikings !) and unsurprising ( Bills , Chiefs ) as well as 0-3 teams both surprising ( Texans ?! Chargers ?!) and unsurprising (sorry, Dolphins ).
And there's a big glut in the middle, too. How about the superteam Rams sitting at 1-2 on the young season, with Puka Nacua and Myles Garrett not having played since the season opener? How about the Browns , thought to be in play for the No. 1 pick, having won two straight?
The early NFL season always holds plenty of unexpected developments, and while it's all that's happened so far and all that we can judge off of, there is still so far to go. With October looming, we can still consider it the early part of the season and acknowledge that this might just be what some teams are ... and what they will be going forward.
These are the six lessons we learned in Week 3.
Good coaches overcome adversity. Look at what Ben Johnson did last night with 38-year-old third-string quarterback Case Keenum starting in the Bears ' 27-7 win over the Eagles .
Now look at what the Eagles did. Jalen Hurts looked lost all night, never more so than on this fourth-quarter interception that all but ended the game.
T.J. Edwards on his INT game 🏈 @PHIvsCHI on ESPN Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/N1jrfstPRo
If Hurts is lost, it's in part been because Sean Mannion doesn't have a map. Saquon Barkley ran the ball 11 times for 73 yards in the first half, a 6.6-yard average. He ran the ball four times for 9 yards in the second half.
This was a two-possession game for the Eagles' first two drives of the second half. All three were three and outs. Barkley ran for 7 yards on the first play of the second half, but a pass behind the line of scrimmage lost 2 yards, and Hurts threw incomplete on third-and-5. On the next drive, a 3-yard loss on another throw behind the line of scrimmage derailed things.
Mannion's offense, so far, doesn't fit Hurts, and vice versa. Mannion wants to attack the middle of the field and play under center. Hurts simply doesn't do that -- or really hasn't much. There were times when opportunities over the middle were there; Hurts hit some and missed others.
And then there's an offensive line that's more liability than powerhouse. Moving Cam Jurgens to left guard in Landon Dickerson's absence looks like a bad decision. Hurts has always been prone to getting antsy when pressured, and a more leaky offensive line in a new system exposes that. He has no dominant run game to lean on; in fact, the run game is mediocre overall. There's no A.J. Brown easy button.
Philadelphia is 27th in offensive success rate with exactly zero easy answers. It is still early, and the Eagles are 2-1. Sometimes the answers aren't going to be easy, but they can still be found. The Eagles have to dig deep to overcome issues at every position on offense.
Another game, another miserable showing from the Texans' offensive line. It started early, when on a fourth-and-1, Houston brought a sixth offensive lineman -- Blake Fisher -- onto the field. With six offensive linemen and two tight ends packed in tight against a struggling defense, 1 yard should be available, right?
Wrong. Fisher ended up flat on his face, and tight end Cade Stover lost at the point of attack, too. The Texans have now failed to gain a first down on third/fourth down and 2 yards or fewer five times this season, tied for most in the league.
Here's David Montgomery barely avoiding a safety by making a free defender miss in the backfield, bouncing off one of his own blockers and fighting for dear life just to get to the line of scrimmage.
Texans run blocking: not great! pic.twitter.com/lFlpniOpLQ
There were ugly individual losses in pass protection, too. All three of Indianapolis' sacks came from interior defensive lineman -- DeForest Buckner and Adetomiwa Adebawore both had an individual sack, and they teamed up for the third. All three came without blitzing, and the two solo sacks came on wins right away. Buckner beat left guard Keylan Rutledge ; Adebawore beat right guard Wyatt Teller .
Even more concerning, though, is the impact the short-yardage failures are having on DeMeco Ryans . Both this week and last week, Houston failed on a fourth-and-1 run in the first half. Last week, Ryans opted for a 58-yard(!) field goal instead of going for it on a fourth-and-1. Ka'imi Fairbairn missed. This week, Ryans opted to punt on a fourth-and-4 down nine points with under eight minutes left.
Of course, one could say he's stuck between a rock and a hard place, because the running game is bad, and without Nico Collins and Jayden Higgins the passing game is really limited. Still, he is leaving potential points on the table, and this offense needs all the points -- real and potential -- it can get. He also badly mismanaged the clock late in the game, but that's another subject entirely.
The Texans started 0-3 last year. They went on to win 12 of their final 14 games. But it is extremely hard to envision this team doing the same. The defense is still very, very good, but even discounting Week 1 against Josh Allen , it hasn't been as good as it was last year. Combine that with an offense that has no margin for error and some poor coaching, and you get three one-score losses.
Most people watch games to root for their teams, whether it's their NFL team , their Fantasy team or whatever squad they're interested in.
But sometimes it's fun to watch for the players, and my goodness, Bijan Robinson and Jahmyr Gibbs are bringing it.
Green Bay just could not tackle Bijan Robinson last night. 29 CAR, 194 RUYDS, 2 TD, 2 REC, 19 REC YDS, 213 Total YDS https://t.co/vq8kcw1Qlv pic.twitter.com/pah6ke8NCR
JAHMYR GIBBS PUT THE LIONS ON HIS BACK AGAINST THE JETS TODAY. 20 CAR, 99 RUSH YDS, 7 REC, 65 REC YDS, 3 TD vs Jets Gibbs scored Detroit’s final three touchdowns, including the game winner with 2:30 left. https://t.co/1bp32xPyRn pic.twitter.com/I18QPquFyF
It's a great time to watch elite running back play. If you miss the old, ground-and-pound days, well, you're getting them, just in a more modern way. Through three weeks, the NFL's league-wide rushing rate is at its second-highest through 2008. The top three teams in rushing expected points added -- the Jaguars , Bills and Chiefs -- are a combined 8-1.
But if you like the new-age game, running backs are getting involved in so many ways as pass catchers, too. After deep passing dominated the 2010s and early 2020s, defenses changed. They got smaller, they got faster, and they stopped allowing throws over the top. Offenses are quietly hitting back by getting bigger and meaner running the football and finding creative ways to use running backs and tight ends in the passing game. It's a fun back-and-forth.
After missing the first two games due to minor knee surgery, Brock Bowers was back like he never left: 10 catches on 13 targets, 116 yards and a score. His route chart is a thing of beauty.
anyone want to say this Brock Bowers graphic isn't a chart from a #1 receiver? pic.twitter.com/PeqzISYUtV
Note not only where the lines end, but where they start. Bowers is all over the place, but many times out wide. Check out these numbers:
CBS Sports NFL Draft analyst Mike Renner had some great film on this , but here's my favorite play:
Kirk Cousins ➡️ Brock Bowers for the TD! @LVvsNO on CBS/Paramount+ Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/RdmXB55pgE
(For those wondering about the list above, he's a left slot receiver here.)
Bowers is a tight end only in name. On that play, he gets a safety, Jonas Sanker , in coverage. Sanker never has a chance. Bowers is too fast.
Klint Kubiak unlocked Jaxon Smith-Njigba last year. He's going to do the same with Bowers.
I have been pretty uninspired by the Steelers ' plan for years. Bring in a mediocre-at-best quarterback, surround him with a mediocre-at-best offense, field a solid defense, hope you get a few bounces your…
author: Zachary Pereles

title: NFL Week 4 picks and score predictions: Browns shock Steelers on Thursday night, Texans get first win
summary: Here's your weekly dose of John Breech's NFL picks
full_text:
I'm not saying the NFL should cancel Week 4, but Roger Goodell might at least want to think about postponing it a few days so we all have time to recover from the craziness of Week 3. There were 12 games decided by one score, which was tied for the most of any week ever in NFL history.
There were some highs in Week 3, there were some lows, and then there was whatever the Packers did in that Thursday night game against the Falcons. I would say it was the worst performance of the week, but then the Eagles showed up on Monday night and got torched by a third-string quarterback in Case Keenum. In related news, Case Keenum now has more TD passes (2) on the year than Drake Maye.
If you didn't know that Keenum was still in the NFL, don't worry, I think that describes almost everyone. Speaking of everyone, I would now like to share my picks with everyone, so let's get to them.
Actually, before we get to the picks, here's a quick reminder that you can check out the weekly picks from every CBSSports.com NFL expert by clicking here , but you were probably already well aware of that since I mention it every week.
One thing that I don't mention every week is that I also write an NFL newsletter for CBS Sports and if you want so subscribe to it, you just need to go here and enter your email . If you sign up, you'll be getting an email to your inbox twice a week that will be full of football news and maybe some cat photos.
Alright, I'm going to stop begging you to sign up for things so that we can get to the picks.
All lines via DraftKings ; All times ET
I never thought I would say this about the Cleveland Browns, but they might be the most underrated team in the NFL. Two months ago, we were all laughing at their QB battle, but now, Todd Monken is laughing at us. And if he's not, he should be, because the QB he gave the job to has the Browns TIED FOR FIRST IN THE AFC NORTH heading into Week 4.
I can't remember the last time I used the words "Browns" and "First place" in the same sentence, but I have to think it was before COVID. I can't be sure, because I don't really remember anything before COVID. Any time the Browns are in first place, even if it's early in the season, it's still worth mentioning, because this team hasn't won a division title since 1989.
Do you know who was born in 1989? Taylor Swift. Do you know who once sang the national anthem at a Steelers game? Taylor Swift. And the Steelers lost that day ... you know what, I have no idea where I was going with that point, so let's move on.
On paper, the Steelers feel like the better team in this game, but I haven't used paper in three years, so I'm not sure that fact actually means anything to me.
When I'm trying to make a pick in a Steeles-Browns game, the only thing I care about are trends, and there are two trends telling me to pick the Browns to win.
First, the Steelers are possibly the worst Thursday night road team the NFL has ever seen. If the Steelers had to play 17 Thursday road games, they would go 0-17. Since the AFL-NFL merger in 1970, the Steelers are 3-16 in Thursday road games, and it actually gets worse: They're 0-9 in divisional road games that are played on a Thursday.
They had a chance to end the streak in 2024 with a game in Cleveland against the 2-8 Browns, but they lost. They had a chance to end the streak in 2025 with a game against JOE FLACCO, but they lost to the Bengals. Flacco had only been on the Bengals' roster for nine days when he faced the Steelers and he still managed to throw for 342 yards and three touchdowns in a Bengals win.
The Thursday road losing streak against divisional opponents started in 1980 with a loss to the Houston Oilers, and it's now been going on for 46 years. This streak has been going on for so long that the Steelers have played two divisional games against opponents who aren't even in their division anymore (Jaguars and Oilers/Titans).
The other trend here is that the city of Cleveland has basically been a black hole for the Steelers. It's like they forget how to play football whenever they have to make the trip to Northern Ohio. The Browns have somehow won four straight home games against Pittsburgh.
And now, the Steelers have to send out their 42-year-old quarterback to start a game on just three days rest. If there's one thing no 42-year-old ever wants to do, it's play two NFL games in five days. I'm taking the BROWNS in an upset.
PICK: Browns (+2.5) 19-16 over Steelers
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (Fox, Stream: Fubo -- try for free))
Jerry Jones might have a lot of friends in the NFL, but apparently, he's not friends with anyone in the NFL scheduling department, because that's the only way to explain what the Cowboys are dealing with this week.
The Cowboys spent Week 3 in Rio de Janeiro, which meant they had to fly 10 hours to South America and then 10 hours back. The one-way trip to Rio covered more than 5,200 miles. Every team that has ever had to fly that far for a game got a bye or extra rest the following week, but not the Cowboys. That's right: The Cowboys are the FIRST team in NFL history to fly at least 5,000 miles for a game and not get any extra rest for their next game. Not only do the Cowboys have to play in Week 4 without any extra rest, but they have to play ON THE ROAD.
Before this year, the NFL had held two games in Brazil and both of those games were played on a Friday. That gave the teams involved two extra days of rest before playing their next game, but the Cowboys won't be getting that.
Here's what Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer had to say about the schedule last week, "The schedule is the schedule, and we will play anybody anytime, anywhere, but it's a unique schedule for sure."
When an NFL coach uses the word "unique" in a situation like this, you can easily read between the lines. I think what Schottenheimer was trying to say is "It's a dumb schedule and I can't believe the NFL did this to us," but instead, he chose his words carefully.
And just in case you're wondering, the Ravens are in a similar situation, but not really. They're getting the Titans at HOME for their post-Brazil matchup. That seems slightly easier than a road game against the Texans.
The Texans are going to be desperate and they're going to be facing a tired Cowboys team that's going to be emotionally exhausted after losing a heartbreaker to the Ravens. Before this week, only two teams had to travel at least 4,400 miles for a game without getting any extra rest the following week: 2021 Dolphins and 2025 Broncos, who both went to London.
How did things go for those two teams after their long trips? With 11 minutes left in the fourth quarter, the Dolphins trailed their game 27-14 while the Broncos trailed 26-8. This means the two teams got outscored a combined 53-22 for the first 49 minutes of each game. That doesn't sound like good news for the Cowboys.
In the post-Brazil special, I fully expect the Cowboys to struggle in the first half before bouncing back in the second half only to lose. That seems like the most Cowboys thing possible that could happen this week.
PICK: Texans (-2.5) 23-20 over Cowboys
Sunday, 1 p.m. ET (CBS, Stream on Paramount+ )
You may not have noticed because it's the Jaguars and nobody ever seems to notice what they're doing, but Liam Coen is quietly building an unstoppable juggernaut in Jacksonville. The Jaguars have won 10 of their past 11 regular-season games, and those 10 wins have come by an average of 20.6 points per game.
The Jaguars are beating people so badly that Trevor Lawrence is regularly being benched well before the game is over.
Trevor Lawrence has been pulled early in seven of the #Jaguars last 11 games. Here’s how much time was remaining in each. - 4th Quarter (8:07) vs #Chargers - 4th Quarter (6:05) vs #Titans - 4th Quarter (7:08) vs #Colts - 4th Quarter (13:51) vs #Jets - 4th Quarter (13:17) vs…
If you have Trevor Lawrence in fantasy, you should probably just get rid of him since he doesn't even play the entire game…
author: John Breech

title: Raiders' surprising 3-0 start: Will Las Vegas see Fernando Mendoza at all this season?
summary: Kirk Cousins has fended off the No. 1 overall pick through three weeks
full_text:
The Las Vegas Raiders have been one of the early-season surprises through the first three weeks, jumping out to a perfect 3-0 record. That includes a 35-27 win over the Saints in New Orleans, where they scored 19 unanswered points in the second half to pull off the comeback. Already, they've matched their win total from last season's 3-14 campaign and have made some history in the process.
They are just the second team in NFL history to start 3-0 after consecutive 13-plus loss seasons, joining the 1980 San Francisco 49ers . They are also just the third team in the past 20 years to start 3-0 after winning three or fewer games the prior year (2006 Saints and 2013 Chiefs ).
For our conversation here, we'll point out that Las Vegas is the fourth team in the Common Draft Era to start 3-0 after drafting first overall the previous spring. Lost in the shuffle of this stellar start to 2026 is the biggest question that loomed over the organization — and still does — when they first embarked on it:
When will we see Fernando Mendoza take over as QB1?
The Raiders selected Mendoza with the No. 1 overall pick at the 2026 NFL Draft after the Heisman Trophy winner put together one of the greatest seasons in college football history, leading the Indiana Hoosiers to a perfect season and a national championship. He is the unquestioned future in Las Vegas, but this 3-0 start does appear to kick the eventual ascension down the road, at least momentarily.
The biggest reason why there hasn't been a clamoring for Mendoza to step into the big seat is that Kirk Cousins has been on fire. Coming out of Sunday's Week 3 action, Cousins is tied for the most passing touchdowns (9) among qualified quarterbacks (min. 50 pass attempts). He's also eighth in the NFL in passer rating (107.2) and EPA per dropback (0.18).
Cousins joined Tom Brady (2015 and 2021) as the only players in NFL history age 38 or older to have at least nine passing touchdowns through the first three games of the season. He also tied a Raiders franchise record for the most consecutive games with three or more passing touchdowns (three). And he did most of that without his go-to pass-catching option in tight end Brock Bowers , who made his season debut in Week 3 and caught 10 of his 13 targets.
Even if the Raiders found a way to still be 3-0, had Cousins struggled through these first three weeks, there would be a groundswell to elevate Mendoza. Because he's essentially been a top-10 quarterback in the NFL, Cousins has quieted that talk and removed any pressure on first-year head coach Klint Kubiak to make a move under center.
The Raiders couldn't have asked for a better start to the season, but things can change in an instant in the NFL.
While they should get credit for starting the year 3-0 (especially that win over the Saints on Sunday), their opening slate hasn't exactly been a murderer's row of top-tier NFL talent. The Dolphins , who they soundly defeated in Week 1, might end up being the worst team in the NFL when the dust settles on the 2026 season. Then, in Week 2, they took down a Chargers team that is 0-3 and one of the biggest disappointments of the year . Even New Orleans is young, with a quarterback in his first season as the full-time starter, and he turned the ball over on his final three possessions in Week 3.
Again, credit to the Raiders for taking advantage of those opportunities put in front of them, but the road ahead is a bit more difficult. That starts with a home matchup against the 3-0 Kansas City Chiefs, who are currently road favorites over Las Vegas.
Here's a look at the Raiders' next eight games:
Las Vegas' matchups against the Patriots (Week 5) and Jets (Week 8) are its most winnable games over this stretch, but both are on the road. Even if you give the Raiders wins in those spots, they likely won't be favored in any of those remaining matchups, potentially setting up a 2-6 skid. That'd bring them to 5-6 before traveling to Cleveland to face the Browns in Week 12, before a bye.
If they are entering that bye week at .500 on the year (or worse), there will be chatter to bring in Mendoza if they haven't already.
Ruling out a possible injury to Cousins that would thrust Mendoza into the starting role, I do think this hot start could buy the veteran some leeway to hold onto the job for the foreseeable future.
That said, the earliest a change could make sense would be that Week 8 matchup at the New York Jets . If the bottom falls out from under the Raiders and they drop their next four games and fall under .500, the tone of the season changes and Kubiak could look to the top pick against the Jets to turn the tide.
After that, the Week 14 home matchup against the Los Angeles Chargers coming out of the bye week would be another window for Mendoza to rise to QB1. If the Raiders fall out of contention by that point and/or Cousins has fallen off, it'd be wise to pivot to the young quarterback to get him reps.
If Las Vegas is still vying for playoff positioning, however, and wants to keep riding with Cousins, rubber could meet the road in Week 15 when they host the Denver Broncos. That game could very well determine playoff positioning if things remain as they stand. If the Raiders fall on the wrong side of that matchup, giving Mendoza the final three starts beginning with a home matchup against the Tennessee Titans in Week 16 would be the prudent move. At that point, the focus shifts from contending to building for 2027, with Mendoza as the centerpiece.
The short answer is yes. It's totally fine if Mendoza barely sees the field over his rookie season. While teams have largely played their first-round quarterbacks from the get-go, there are many ways to skin a cat. Kubiak has spoken at length about taking a slow approach when developing a young quarterback, and we've seen that work in the past. Most notably, Patrick Mahomes played just one game as a rookie, starting the regular-season finale against the Broncos during the 2017 campaign. Before that, he sat behind Alex Smith . I think Mahomes turned out just fine. Of course, that doesn't mean that Mendoza is earmarked for the same career trajectory, but it's just an example of a player becoming a star despite not seeing the field much as a rookie.
author: Tyler Sullivan

title: NFL MVP race entering Week 4: Josh Allen stays No. 1, but the field is closing fast
summary: A wide receiver, two running backs and even a defensive player join the quarterbacks in our ranking of the NFL's leading MVP candidates
full_text:
Who will win the league MVP in 2026? To find out, we're doing a week-by-week ranking of the candidates most likely to win the honor. This week alone, we saw four players enter the conversation who weren't considered this time a week ago. Several other players either moved up or down in our weekly ranking of MVP candidates. But the quarterback of the Buffalo Bills still has the lead, and that's where we start.
If the MVP vote happened today, Allen wins. That was the case last week, and it's still the case now, even if the gap between him and the field has closed a bit.
The 2024 league MVP, Allen, already made history by becoming the first player with five or more touchdown passes and three or more touchdown runs through the first two games. On Sunday, Allen threw his first two interceptions of the season, but he also ran for a pair of scores and joined Jim Brown (1958), Stephen Davis (1999) and Priest Holmes (2003) as the only players to rush for two touchdowns in their first three games of a season.
The league's reigning Offensive Player of the Year, Smith-Njigba is once again making a case to become the first receiver to win league MVP. He closed the gap on Allen after catching a season-high 10 passes for 128 yards and two touchdowns in Seattle's 33-31 loss to Washington.
The 24-year-old Smith-Njigba is on pace to make history. He leads the NFL in receptions (27, tied with New Orleans' Chris Olave ), receiving yards (406) and touchdown catches (six). He is on pace to shatter both Randy Moss' single-season record for touchdown receptions (23 in 2007) and Calvin Johnson's single-season receiving yardage record (1,964 yards in 2012). He's also on pace to break Michael Thomas' single-season receptions mark (149 in 2019).
It's impossible to ignore the Raiders ' history of older quarterbacks who have enjoyed career rebirths after joining the silver and black. Joe Plunkett overcame obscurity to lead the Raiders to an unexpected title in 1980, Rich Gannon won MVP and led the Raiders to a Super Bowl in 2022, and Cousins is currently writing his own story for the 3-0 Raiders.
The more the Raiders win, the more Cousins' MVP case becomes a real possibility.
Purdy continued to help his MVP case in Week 3 by helping the battered 49ers improve to 3-0. Purdy threw for a season-high 297 yards and four touchdowns (with no picks) in San Francisco's 36-30 win over the Cardinals .
Through three weeks, Purdy is tied for the NFL lead in touchdown passes (nine) and is eighth in passing yards (789). He's also completed an impressive 72.3% of his passes and has thrown just one interception.
Walker ran for 70 yards on 18 carries and a touchdown in Kansas City's 24-10 win over Miami.
The reigning Super Bowl MVP, Walker, is first in the league with 360 rushing yards. He is on pace to become only the 10th player in NFL history to rush for over 2,000 yards in a season. Walker has also been an asset for Patrick Mahomes as a receiver. He caught his second touchdown pass of the season during Sunday's win.
Already a two-time league MVP, Mahomes has again put himself in the conversation this year. In helping lead the Chiefs to a 3-0 start, Mahomes has thrown seven touchdowns against just two picks while completing an impressive 68.4% of his passes.
Mahomes, who missed the final three games of the 2025 season after he tore his left ACL and LCL, could also be considered the front-runner for Comeback Player of the Year through three weeks. For him to have a chance at winning MVP, Mahomes and the Chiefs will likely need to dethrone Denver as AFC West champions.
Robinson earned a spot on this list after his monster performance in Week 3 that contributed to the Falcons ' blowout win over the Packers on prime time. Robinson had 215 all-purpose yards against the Packers that included 194 yards and two touchdowns on 29 carries.
The performance moved Robinson into second in the NFL (behind Walker) in rushing through three weeks. His 467 all-purpose yards are the most in the NFL among offensive players.
While it's expected at this point, Goff's prolific numbers shouldn't be overlooked. Goff is tied for third in the league in touchdown passes, fifth in completion percentage and sixth in passing yards. He has yet to throw an interception.
Like Mahomes, an unexpected division title for the Lions would certainly boost Goff's MVP hopes. The odds of that happening have increased with Caleb Williams ' recent injury, the Packers' ongoing struggles without Micah Parsons and the Vikings ' quarterback instability.
Burrow lost some ground, but he still deserves a spot on this list after throwing for 282 yards and three touchdowns (and completing 75.7% of his passes) in Cincinnati's 30-27 loss in Pittsburgh. Statistically, the game was Burrow's best of the season so far.
The Bengals ' loss was sealed when Burrow took a strip sack with less than a minute to play, but the defeat was largely the byproduct of two mistakes by Cincinnati's punt return unit that set up 10 of the Steelers ' 30 points.
Given the fact that only two defensive players in history have won league MVP, the odds of Rousseau winning MVP are about as good as you or me winning the lottery. That said, Rousseau should be considered a long-shot contender.
Rousseau's 6.0 sacks are two more than the league's next-closest players ( Will Anderson Jr . and Mason Graham ). He's joined Mark Gastineau (in 1984) and Hall of Famer Kevin Greene (in 1998) as the only players to have three straight games with two or more sacks to open a season.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: When will J.J. McCarthy start for Giants? Why John Harbaugh could make QB change sooner than expected
summary: McCarthy must learn a new offense and prove he can protect the football, but Jameis Winston's uneven play could speed things up
full_text:
John Harbaugh didn't come to New York to lose. The 64-year-old Super Bowl-winning coach plans to win early and often with the Giants , who are 2-1 and an early-season NFL surprise.
Harbaugh's expectations do not change despite Jaxson Dart's season-ending injury (the Giants also lost Brian Burns to a season-ending injury on Sunday). He admitted Monday that as soon as Dart went down, he and the Giants' brass sought to improve their quarterback room. That led to Monday's trade for JJ McCarthy , a former first-round pick whose time with the Vikings was as odd as it was bizarre.
Injuries, inconsistent play and the arrival of Kyler Murray (and McCarthy's response to it) prevented McCarthy from realizing his potential with the Vikings, who are off to a 3-0 start this season. When McCarthy was on, he showed flashes of the player that compelled Minnesota to take him with the 10th overall pick in the 2024 draft.
"I think he's a strong, young quarterback, has some experience in the National Football League," Harbaugh said of McCarthy , who just three years ago led Michigan to a national title under for Jim Harbaugh. "Obviously, was a very high draft pick, very talented player and is going to make us a stronger football team."
John Harbaugh has had success changing quarterbacks during a season. In 2018, he replaced Joe Flacco with then-rookie Lamar Jackson after Baltimore started 4-5. Jackson went 6-1 as Baltimore's starter that season while foreshadowing what was to come for the eventual two-time league MVP.
No one is comparing McCarthy to Jackson, but it's certainly possible that McCarthy -- if nothing else -- can provide temporary stability for the Giants at the NFL's most important position.
Week 9 would be the logical answer given the Giants' Week 8 bye. There's a very good chance, however, that McCarthy will make his debut as the Giants' starter much sooner than that.
Let's start with the fact that the Giants' Week 9 game will be in Philadelphia, which isn't exactly a great place for a young quarterback who is making his first start with a new team. If the Giants do decide to wait until after the bye to start McCarthy, their Week 10 home game against the Commanders would make more sense.
In Harbaugh's perfect world, Jameis Winston would play well enough to keep the job. Changing quarterbacks in-season is a tall order, especially for a first-year coaching staff.
Winston's recent performances, however, would suggest that Harbaugh will likely need to make a quarterback switch soon. Winston struggled mightily against the Rams . He was much more accurate on Sunday against the Titans but he only managed to throw for 118 yards while averaging just 8.4 yards per completion.
If today's Giants were built like the 1990 Giants (who won a Super Bowl with a backup quarterback), there's a chance that they could stay in the hunt with Winston. The Giants don't have an offense that can carry a quarterback; while their defense is good, Burns' injury reinforces that New York can't rely on it to carry them on a weekly basis.
If Winston doesn't improve over the next two weeks, it's certainly possible to make a change when New York hosts the Saints in Week 6. That would give him time to watch Winston against the Cardinals and the Commanders (in Washington) before taking the reins. It would also give him two games of work heading into the bye week.
Along with learning the offense, McCarthy will have to prove to Harbaugh that he can take care of the ball. That was a huge issue in Minnesota and was likely one of the reasons why things didn't work out with the Vikings. That will have to change if McCarthy is going to make the most of his second chance, whenever that happens.
author: Bryan DeArdo

title: Prisco's NFL Week 4 Power Rankings: Bills claim No. 1 status while Vikings continue to climb
summary: Pete Prisco shares his latest Power Rankings of the 2026 NFL season, including some big drops for some of last week's top teams
full_text:
Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores is a madman when it comes to calling defense.
The philosophy is simple, really: Blitz, blitz, and blitz some more. He has taken defense and made it truly fun to watch.
The Vikings are blitzing at a rate of 73-78% of passing plays, depending on the site giving out the data. That is by far the highest percentage in the league — and it's not close.
They are a zone-blitz unit that shows a ton of looks that confuse offensive lines and quarterbacks to the point that the passers are often left seeing ghosts even when the pressure isn't there. It's why the Vikings lead the league in sacks with 14 and are quickly becoming a team opposing quarterbacks fear.
They registered six sacks of Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Baker Mayfield in their 23-16 victory Sunday, a game in which they made the Tampa Bay offensive line look bad. They also ran through backs and tight ends in pass protection, and Mayfield was jumpy all day.
It looked like Minnesota was playing with 13 players on defense all day long.
The Vikings are 3-0 because of that defense. Their quarterbacks haven't thrown for over 168 yards in a game because they haven't needed it, thanks to that dominant defense.
Minnesota is up to No. 4 in my Power Rankings as Flores continues to show off his impressive defensive mind. If the offense, with Kyler Murray back under center, can get some flow in the passing game, this is going to be a tough team to beat week in and week out. It's also going to make for tough weeks for opponents to recover after playing them, since they beat you up on defense.
The Buffalo Bills move to the top spot of my rankings after the Seattle Seahawks lost to the Washington Commanders . Buffalo beat the Los Angeles Chargers despite turning the ball over five times. That's the sign of a good team.
There are five undefeated teams left. They are Buffalo, San Francisco, Kansas City, Minnesota and the Las Vegas Raiders . The Raiders are the real surprise of the group as Kirk Cousins has led them to a fast start.
The Raiders aren't in my top 10 yet, but if they beat the Chiefs this week in Vegas, it will be time to truly pay attention. That's not to take away from their great start. Who saw them at 3-0? I didn't.
As for the bottom team, Miami stays there, although the Tennessee Titans are pushing them hard for that spot as the Titans' offense continues to struggle with Cam Ward .

title: Where is the @#?$%&0! Cardinals pass rush?
summary: Everyone who follows the Arizona Cardinals knows that this new offense, installed by head coach Mike LaFleur, will take time for the roster to get acclimated. Patience is assuredly needed. But the defense seems to be struggling in games so far this season. RELATED: SWEAT NAMED TO THE 2026 NFL TOP-100 One aspect that is […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Dante Stills #55 of the Arizona Cardinals enters the field before an NFL game against the San Francisco 49ers on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Everyone who follows the Arizona Cardinals knows that this new offense, installed by head coach Mike LaFleur, will take time for the roster to get acclimated. Patience is assuredly needed. But the defense seems to be struggling in games so far this season. RELATED: SWEAT NAMED TO THE 2026 NFL TOP-100 One aspect that is pretty glaring is the lack of a pass rush. Why? Part of the reason is the 3-4 formation. Oftentimes, their opponent is blocking five on three. This forces the defense to send an outside linebacker instead of using another defensive end, as is the norm in the 4-3. Yes, linebackers are speedier, but offensive linemen are employed along the front for a reason: they are huge. A guy like LB Baron Browning has good speed within his 255-pound frame, but how does he match up with a 325-pound offensive tackle when engaged? The use of the 3-4 also allows the other team to not have to keep their running back in to block. For a team like the San Francisco 49ers, being able to utilize RB Christian McCaffrey as an outlet receiver all game is gold. Five blockers can handle a rush, even when they send another defender, or even two. Their offensive line is never outmatched. Sweat had a critical penalty that could have swayed the game. We are not playing disciplined or inspired ball. — JamMasterJ (@Kosher_dude) September 28, 2026 First off the list is EDGE rusher Josh Sweat. Last year, this cat had 12 sacks, 17 QB hits, 13 tackles for loss, 9 hurries, 7 knockdowns, 2 batted passes, 540 snaps, and 28 pressures to go along with his 30 total tackles. This year so far? Three tackles, 0 sacks, 1 tackle for loss, 0 batted passes, 0 QB hits, 3 hurries, and 3 pressures. His Pro Football Focus (PFF) grade in a three-game sample is a lousy 42.3. In going back through film of the first three games, he just isn’t getting any type of penetration into the offensive backfield. He doesn’t have a good first step and absolutely no burst. What’s wrong with him? And he has played just 49% of all defensive plays, so it’s not like he is out there all game. Get this: Sweat is ranked 111th out of 112 EDGE rushers this year. Nose tackle Roy Lopez is the inside man. One thing he is doing is plugging his gap and being a good run stopper. So far, he has just eight tackles, four each against the Los Angeles Chargers and the Seattle Seahawks, but zero tackles in the San Fran contest. He is not a pass rusher, and never has been. He will stay home and patrol the “A” gap and is difficult to move. Offensive coordinators have to design runs to other gaps because Lopez ain’t moving. His stats this year: 8 total tackles, 0 tackles for loss, 0 batted passes, 0 sacks, 0 QB hits, 1 hurry, 1 pressure, and has played 62% of defensive snaps. Because other teams cannot run into his lane, his PFF grade is a respectable 71.4, which is 24 th among 125 qualified interior defensive linemen. His run-defense grade of 73.5 has him ranked 9th. DT Walter Nolen usually lines up on the left side. He is on a rotational basis, but he is getting his share of snaps with 110, which is 62%. The issue is that he isn’t getting much as far as penetration into the pocket. As far as run stopping, he is doing above average, but as a pass rusher? 2026 stats: Three starts, 4 total tackles, 0 sacks, 2 QB hits, 0 tackles for loss, 0 batted passes, 1 hurry, and 3 pressures. His PFF grade is just average at 52.4. His pass-rush grade of 63.1 is better than his run-stoppage rating, which ranks Nolen 52nd among 125 qualified interior defensive linemen. Wasn’t Nolen supposed to be this dominant pass-rushing defensive tackle? When does that begin? The other DT is Dante Stills . So far, minimal pass rush in his three starts. One sack, 9 total tackles, 1 QB hit, 1 batted pass, 1 tackle for loss, 3 hurries, and 5 pressures. Has played 58% of defensive snaps. PFF grade of 55.0. The backup to Stills is DE Darius Robinson . He has played on just 37% of defensive reps, so he is strictly a rotational guy. 8 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 0 sacks, 0 QB hits, 0 batted passes, 2 hurries, and 2 pressures. PFF grade of 60.7. DT L.J. Collier is the backup to Nolen and has played 39% of snaps. His issue is that he cannot disengage from offensive linemen, who then move him at will. His PFF grade of 49.5 is self-explanatory. Only three tackles in three games tell his story. 0 sacks, 0 tackles for loss, 0 batted passes, 0 QB hits, 2 hurries, and 2 pressures. Price fumbles, Zaven Collins recovers. Big turnover for #AZCardinals . — Darren Urban (@Cardschatter) September 20, 2026 LB Zaven Collins has not always been used to rush the passer. He drops back into coverage quite a bit and is utilized as a stand-up linebacker on most snaps, and his main job is run defense. And he is good at that. But he does take off into the backfield. 44% of snaps means he is playing less than half of each game, so there’s that. His stats: One start, 11 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 0 QB hits, 2 batted passes, 1 fumble recovery, 0 sacks, 1 hurry, and 1 pressure. PFF grade of 90.1. His run-defense grade of 90.5 is ranked 2 nd, while he grades out at 60.1 in pass rushing. LB Baron Browning will line up at times as an EDGE rusher and then attempt to get into the offensive backfield, but his main job is run defense at the second level. He has two starts, along with 4 total tackles, 1 tackle for loss, 0 sacks, 1 QB hit, 0 batted passes, 0 hurries, and 1 pressure. PFF grade of 66.3 with a pass-rush grade of 59.4, which is ranked 66th among 109 qualified edge defenders. As anyone can see, the Cardinals just aren’t getting any type of pass rush. In looking back at the first three games, the opposing quarterback was rarely flushed and had to escape the pocket. Versus the 49ers, QB Brock Purdy had plenty of time to survey the field on just about every passing down. What this does is vastly affect the defensive backfield, which now must shadow their man for much longer than the play was designed. The Cardinals’ defensive backs aren’t getting help by forcing the QB to throw early or go through just two progressions instead of four. This killed the defensive effort against San Francisco as Purdy picked and chose who to throw to all game without much hassle from the pass rush. What is wrong with Sweat? In looking at the game film, he rarely gets by his offensive tackle. Where is the pass rush from Nolen and Stills? In the offseason, positions such as offensive guard and tackle were addressed, as were running back and backup quarterback. But nothing changed with the defensive line other than the team lost its second-most productive sack master, DT Calais Campbell. Currently, Arizona is ranked 27 th in the league in sacks with four. One of those stud pass rushers with the third overall pick would have been nice, but that was then; this is now. Sign a good free agent? Gone are Za’Darius Smith, Jadeveon Clowney, A.J. Epenesa, and Von Miller. What can be done? The list of available free-agent EDGE rushers has been picked over pretty well. title: What is the status of the Cardinals’ offensive line?
summary: The Arizona Cardinals have only played three games this year and currently sit at 1-2-0 in the league’s toughest division. However, both losses are to division foes. With a new head coach, Mike LaFleur, brought over the offense from the Los Angeles Rams. He also learned these principles from the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CA - SEPTEMBER 13: Paris Johnson Jr. #70 of the Arizona Cardinals drops back to block during an NFL football game against the Los Angeles Chargers during an NFL football game at SoFi Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Arizona Cardinals have only played three games this year and currently sit at 1-2-0 in the league’s toughest division. However, both losses are to division foes. With a new head coach, Mike LaFleur, brought over the offense from the Los Angeles Rams. He also learned these principles from the San Francisco 49ers. Both teams are highly successful with potent offensive outputs. RELATED: CARDINALS KEEP IT CLOSE What is the status of the Cardinals’ offensive line so far? Having difficulties already after just a few games, or providing this offense with a solid foundation? In the offseason, GM Monti Ossenfort had a mission to improve this group. He did not re-sign OGs Evan Brown and Will Hernandez and allowed OTs Kelvin Beachum and Jonah Williams to find gainful employment elsewhere. Currently, Brown is the starting center for the Houston Texans, while the others remain out of football. 🚨RED ZONE TD🚨 @JBrissett12 ➡️ @mcbtrey #SEAvsAZ | 📺 FOX pic.twitter.com/BP9I9YuZvc — Arizona Cardinals (@AZCardinals) September 20, 2026 After Week 2, the Cardinals offensive line was ranked collectively as a group at #20 by Pro Football Focus (PFF), up one spot from Week 1. In the loss to the Seattle Seahawks, four of the five starters earned PFF grades above 60.0. First off, OG Isaac Seumalo was the splash signing in free agency. How is he doing so far? Seumalo has played every snap at left guard (209) with a PFF grade of 63.1. He is regarded as an excellent pass protector, but his run-blocking grades sit at 46.1. He has no issues in pulls, but the problem is that he will whiff on blocking any defender, which defeats the purpose of pulling. He has allowed just one sack, two QB hits, seven pressures, and has zero penalties called on him. RT Elijah Wilkinson was brought over from the Atlanta Falcons in free agency. In 2025, he started every game for the Falcons at right tackle and has played in 99 NFL games with 65 starts. So far, he has a PFF grade of 57.7 and is ranked 54th among 69 qualified offensive tackles. His issue is with run blocking. He grades out at 52.4 in this aspect and is ranked 56th at the OT position. He is an above-average pass blocker, though. Wilkinson has allowed just one sack, three QB hits, and six pressures. He has only two penalties accepted. He has played every snap at RT this year, with 212 snaps. C Hjalte Froholdt is this group’s rock. Like the others, he has also played every offensive snap, which is par for him since he has never missed a single rep since he landed in the desert in 2023. His PFF numbers are 57.5 for the year so far, ranking him 19 th out of 32 qualified centers. He has allowed only three pressures with zero sacks and zero QB hits and has had only one accepted penalty. RG Isaiah Adams played in Week 1 and this past weekend’s contest against the San Francisco 49ers, and missed the second game against the Seahawks. In those two contests, he played every snap at right guard. He has an overall PFF grade of 68.5 and is an exceptional run blocker (71.4). His pass-protection rating is 55.3. That breaks down to allowing only one sack, one QB hit, four pressures, and zero penalties called. RG Jon Gaines spelled Adams in Week 2. His PFF grade for the one game was 69.6. Excellent pass blocker and ranked 9th out of 68 guards. His situation included zero sacks, one QB hit, one pressure, and zero penalties. Finally, the top dog. LT Paris Johnson is showing why the Cardinals spent the sixth overall pick in the first round back in 2023. The only knock on him is his durability. In only a three-game capsule, Johnson grades out at 80.8. The breakdown is a pass protection grade of 82.1 and an 81.1 run-blocking rating. This man is the meat and potatoes for the Cardinals. He has played every snap this far (fingers crossed), allowed a single sack, two QB hits, four pressures, and had three penalties accepted. As anyone can see, run blocking is the greatest issue with the offensive line. This new offense is predicated on the short passing game and being able to run the ball. Not being able to gain yardage via the run impairs the offense in numerous ways. This new offense has the best running back from April’s NFL Draft, who was finally the featured back against the 49ers. He was a step away from taking it to the house on several carries. This offense also features a capable backup in Tyler Allgeier and, when ready, James Conner. The horses are in the stable. By having a capable run game, the offence can win the possession game and dictate the game clock. This Cardinal’s offense has to be capable of grinding it out late in the second and fourth quarters if needed, yet the team ranks 24th in run-block win rate and sits among the bottom tier of NFL teams averaging fewer than 95 rushing yards per game. That is a huge problem. 2026 PFF run blocking grades (after 3 games): RT Elijah Wilkinson: 52.4 RG Isaiah Adams: 71.4 RG Jon Gaines: 64.2 C Hjalte Froholdt: 57.3 LG Isaac Seumalo: 46.1 LT Paris Johnson: 81.1 Against San Fran, this offense completely dominated the 49ers in the first half of the game. Time of possession was 21:01 for Arizona to San Fran’s 8:59, yet the Cardinals were losing 17-6. Their offense converted touchdowns, whereas the Cardinals punted after long drives or converted field goals. Arizona possessions in the first half: punt, punt, punt, FG, FG. Somehow, this offense has to find a way to finish. Michael Wilson full extension 😳 @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tCtNiEEWex — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 In the above clip, look at how much of a wall the offensive line provided QB Jacoby Brissett. As a group, they are doing a lot of things right. Everyone is in unison that this new offense will need to blossom, but being patient isn’t an easy task. This offensive line has been together now for three games. Perhaps it can improve and give Brissett clean pockets. But at times, it has struggled. ESPN metrics show that no Cardinals offensive lineman ranks inside the Top-20 at their respective position for pass-block win rate, nor in the Top-10 for run-block win rate. This new offense will only go as far as the offensive line allows.

title: Falcons vs. Saints: Let’s #TailgateTogether, because some things are bigger than football
summary: Some things are bigger than football. Even during Hate Week. As we look toward to the Falcons’ next game, Monday Night Football against the Saints in Week 4, I want to raise awareness of a wonderful organization supporting the unhoused community in New Orleans: #TailgateTogether. Allen Keller, one of the Saints fans at the center […]
full_text: Photo by Rich von Biberstein/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Some things are bigger than football. Even during Hate Week. As we look toward to the Falcons’ next game, Monday Night Football against the Saints in Week 4, I want to raise awareness of a wonderful organization supporting the unhoused community in New Orleans: #TailgateTogether. Allen Keller, one of the Saints fans at the center of this organization, explained to Canal Street Chronicles back in 2022 how this initiative began . “It started from Saints tailgates,” Keller said. “We’d have a ton of food left over, so we’d bring that out to the homeless. But the thought of giving the homeless our leftovers didn’t feel right to me. So we started cooking the homeless their own separate, fresh meal.” #TailgateTogether is a Mutual Aid Group with a primary focus of feeding and clothing the houseless community in New Orleans on a bi-weekly basis. We also assist with Hurricane relief and feeding underprivileged schoolchildren. All of our work has been vetted, verified, and documented. — Allenk_81 (@allenk81.bsky.social) 2024-11-15T14:51:12.556Z Keller, along with fellow Saints fan Katherine Seals and others, have put their time, energy, money, and care into #TailgateTogether, and have turned this into a year-round enterprise providing fundamentally important support and resources to vulnerable people in New Orleans. And they couldn’t do it without the support of volunteers and donors. “There have been hundreds of volunteers over the years. Many volunteer as their schedule allows, and I genuinely consider everyone who has ever volunteered as a part of #TailgateTogether. Because it truly takes all of us,” Keller told SB Nation. The Office of Homeless Services and Strategy budget in New Orleans was cut from $3.6 million dollars to just $700,000 annually in 2025, and the 2025 Super Bowl in Caesars Superdome brought with it legislation persecuting people for sleeping in public and sweeps of encampments that displaced people who already didn’t have anywhere else to go. Unity of Greater New Orleans reports that there are over 1,500 unhoused people in New Orleans who urgently need help and resources. About 72% of these people do have temporary shelter, but there aren’t enough beds or resources for everyone. It’s complicated by the fact that people from all over Louisiana who don’t have stable housing come to New Orleans, assuming that a larger metro area will have more resources. “We see a lot of individuals who are dropped off here from hospitals and rehab centers from all across the state every single day, because there is a lack of resources in other smaller communities,” Sarah Parks, the executive director of Grace at the Greenlight , said to New Orleans’ WDSU back in June 2026. “So we literally are taking care of our state’s homeless population here in New Orleans.” And while Hurricane Katrina ravaged the city 20 years ago , housing shortages, gentrification, and unaffordable housing stemming from the recovery efforts have exacerbated the issue, making it even harder for people who need housing. #TailgateTogether can’t solve all of these societal problems. But they can, and do, give the unhoused community good meals, resources for their comfort, safety and hygiene, and a few hours of fellowship each week all year long with a group of folks who treat them like people worthy of kindness, respect and friendship — because they are. I’m heading to New Orleans on Saturday, and will be volunteering with #TailgateTogether on Sunday morning before I cover Monday Night Football (the Superdome has restrictions around weekday tailgates, and the group likes to make sure the community has a consistent day and time to rely on). If you’re coming to New Orleans for the game and want to join us, let me know and I’ll share the details when I have them! And if you’d like to support the work of #TailgateTogether, you can donate money directly to Allen . I have donated as much as I’m able over the years, and can personally vouch for the fact that your money will go directly toward serving people who need our help. You can also purchase items off #TailgateTogether’s Amazon wish list to help support people in need every day, not just Sundays. I root for the Saints’ downfall on the field every single week, and Monday will be no different. But #TailgateTogether is bigger than football, and it’s an honor to get to serve alongside these good folks on Saturday. I hope you’ll join me, whether that’s donating your time, money, or simply spreading the word about #TailgateTogether to help raise awareness of the important work they’re doing to care for their community.

title: It’s all up to Michael Penix Jr. now
summary: Opportunities in the NFL rarely are clean and easy. Jalen Hurts needed Carson Wentz to get hurt to get his shot at being the Eagles’ franchise quarterback, and had to be terrific to seize ahold of that job. Tom Brady needed Drew Bledsoe to get hurt to find his way on to the field and […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - SEPTEMBER 24: Michael Penix Jr. #9 of the Atlanta Falcons stands on the sideline during the national anthem prior to the game against the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field on September 24, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images Opportunities in the NFL rarely are clean and easy. Jalen Hurts needed Carson Wentz to get hurt to get his shot at being the Eagles’ franchise quarterback, and had to be terrific to seize ahold of that job. Tom Brady needed Drew Bledsoe to get hurt to find his way on to the field and kick off his legendary career. Tyler Allgeier seized a job and watched it fade when the Falcons drafted Bijan Robinson, only to land in Arizona with a clear shot at a starting job and see Arizona draft Jeremiyah Love. Players like Geno Smith, Sam Darnold, and Baker Mayfield had to wander in the wilderness before they landed in the right spot and got a little bit of luck en route to a starting job. Sometimes the path clears itself and it’s all up to you, sometimes it’s open a crack and you need help forcing it open, and other times the door closes as quickly as it opens. For Michael Penix Jr., the opportunity is crystal clear. It wasn’t when the Falcons drafted him, because he had no idea how long Kirk Cousins would be parked in the starting job in front of him. It certainly wasn’t when he tore his ACL last November and watched the front office and coaching staff that drafted him get canned this spring, or when the new regime added Tua Tagovailoa to compete with him. Yet right now, heading into Week 4 of a 2026 season that has been a real roller coaster, Penix is the unquestioned starter and has 14 weeks of runway to prove he’s the franchise quarterback for Kevin Stefanski, Ian Cunningham, and Matt Ryan. It’s an opportunity that’s as clear-cut as possible, and now it’s all up to Penix. I started writing this piece before the Green Bay game, but that game made it clear the door is open. Unless Penix simply can’t convince this staff he’s the guy because of his injury history, he has a real chance of getting this team to pick up his fifth-year option and beginning to think of locking him up long term. If he’s hurt or ineffective in the weeks ahead after that impressive deubt, that chance is gone and the Falcons will invest in a new 2027 starter, with Penix relegated to backup duty or trade bait. I truly believe he has a long leash before the team turns to Tua Tagovailoa, who was the starter to begin the year simply because Penix wasn’t ready—and then of course Tua also got hurt, opening this door early—and I truly believe that the increasingly uncertain crop of 2027 quarterbacks can only help him. I’m also not suggesting this is the perfect opportunity. The Falcons got the ball out of Penix’s hand faster than any other quarterback this week in part to help him out in his debut, but also because this line has been a bit suspect in pass protection early. Tommy Rees still hasn’t found an effective way to use Kyle Pitts, and Atlanta’s still trying to figure out what they have beyond Drake London in the receiving corps. There are challenges here. But this is a line Penix has played with an knows well outside of Jawaan Taylor and a talented group of weapons headlined by Bijan Robinson, Drake London, and Kyle Pitts. The cupboard is hardly bare here and we aren’t getting Zac Robinson keying in on Penix infrequently utilizing play action and hardly ever putting Penix under center; this is going to be an attack that gives Penix every chance to hit layups and tries to pry open deep targets for him to work with. If there’s a franchise quarterback here, Penix will have his chance to show it, even if this Falcons team isn’t ultimately a contender. The road here was rocky and the team will have to do its part to ensure Penix is successful. But in a league where opportunity knocks with conditions, Penix is getting a fairly rare chance to simply step into this job and earn it over the long haul. It’s all up to him now, and my fervent hope is that he proves to be the guy.

title: Ravens host 3 OL for workouts, including former Lions C Graham Glasgow
summary: The Baltimore Ravens hosted a trio of offensive linemen for workouts on Tuesday following injuries to centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic. Headlining the group was Graham Glasgow, a 10-year veteran with 136 starts for the Lions and Broncos under his belt, including a few dozen at center. He was joined by Kingsley Eguakun, his […]
full_text: DETROIT, MI - DECEMBER 04: Graham Glasgow #60 of the Detroit Lions runs out of the tunnel prior to an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at Ford Field on December 4, 2025 in Detroit, Michigan. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens hosted a trio of offensive linemen for workouts on Tuesday following injuries to centers Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic. Headlining the group was Graham Glasgow, a 10-year veteran with 136 starts for the Lions and Broncos under his belt, including a few dozen at center. He was joined by Kingsley Eguakun, his backup in Detroit last year, and Kyle Hergel, who finished the 2025 season in Chicago working with then-Bears, now-Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle. Glasgow will immediately be an appealing name to Ravens fans for his experience at center and contributions to the Lions’ strong offenses over the past few years. His release in March due to a failed physical designation will require a thorough medical evaluation of his knee, but he could be Baltimore’s best, most obvious solution to their current crisis. With over 3,500 career snaps at both center and right guard, he could move Ioane back to his natural position and use his decade of experience – including two years under Ben Johnson, Doyle’s mentor – to help Lamar Jackson at the line of scrimmage. Eguakun and Hergel profile more as depth options. The former started two games in place of Glasgow in Detroit last year and only plays center; the latter has not played in the regular season since 2024 and can line up at all three interior spots.

title: Ravens open as massive favorites in Week 4 vs. winless Titans
summary: The Baltimore Ravens’ Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints seemed like a potential trap game with an early 8.5-point line. A perfect storm of injuries, penalties, coaching miscues, and some poor officiating brought about a Ravens loss by seven points, representing a 15.5-point swing from the original line. Week 4 seems significantly less […]
full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Robert Saleh of the Tennessee Titans looks on during the first quarter against the New York Giants at MetLife Stadium on September 27, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Elsa/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens’ Week 2 matchup against the New Orleans Saints seemed like a potential trap game with an early 8.5-point line. A perfect storm of injuries, penalties, coaching miscues, and some poor officiating brought about a Ravens loss by seven points, representing a 15.5-point swing from the original line. Week 4 seems significantly less likely to bring such surprises. The Ravens are 11.5-point favorites for their upcoming face-off with the winless Tennessee Titans ( via FanDuel Sportsbook ). Robert Saleh’s defense ranks 10th in points and yards allowed, but the Titans offense has mustered just 37 points and 748 yards through three games, both bottom-three marks in the NFL. Saleh has been in this position before. The last time he faced the Ravens, his 2022 Jets defense held Lamar Jackson to just 230 total yards and the rest of Baltimore’s backfield to just 46 rushing yards. New York’s offense, though, produced only two field goals, went two-for-14 on third down, and turned the ball over three times, leading to a 24-6 Ravens victory. This week’s contest could go in a similar direction. The Ravens are scrambling for answers along their offensive line after “long-term” injuries to Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic , the only centers on the 53-man roster or practice squad. First-round rookie Vega Ioane is likely the team’s immediate answer, but that will bring Andrew Vorhees into the starting lineup at right guard. Not only will Ioane have to pick up the center position after just a handful of snaps there during his 2024 junior season at Penn State, Vorhees will also have to bounce back after a rough 2025 campaign as the Ravens’ starting left guard. Head coach Jesse Minter was optimistic about left tackle Ronnie Stanley’s status during his Monday press conference, but his ability to return from a toe injury also remains to be seen. 2025 fifth-round pick Carson Vinson held up in his first regular-season start and the Titans’ edge rushers have not been especially productive so far, so that may be less of a concern than the interior shuffle. With Zay Flowers trending in a positive direction, the Ravens offense should still be able to put up points, but it may not be able to mount long drives and dominate every second of possession time. Baltimore’s defense, though, will have a chance for a confidence-builder against their easiest opponent of the season. Tennessee is dealing with similar injury issues at right guard after placing starter Fernando Carmona and backup Jackson Slater on IR. Their running game has been solid, but quarterback Cam Ward is averaging just 168 passing yards per game and 5.7 yards per attempt. If the Ravens can built any sort of a lead and force Ward to start dropping back, their defensive line and secondary could feast.

summary: The Baltimore Ravens have lost both of the centers on their roster to “long-term” injuries, head coach Jesse Minter said on Wednesday. The team already lost Danny Pinter to a season-ending knee injury in training camp and Corey Bullock to a Panthers waiver claim during roster cuts – not to mention Tyler Linderbaum’s departure in […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MN - AUGUST 22: Baltimore Ravens guard Olaivavega Ioane (71) looks on after the NFL preseason game between the Baltimore Ravens and the Minnesota Vikings on August 22nd, 2026, at U.S. Bank in Minneapolis, MN. (Photo by Bailey Hillesheim/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Baltimore Ravens have lost both of the centers on their roster to “long-term” injuries, head coach Jesse Minter said on Wednesday. The team already lost Danny Pinter to a season-ending knee injury in training camp and Corey Bullock to a Panthers waiver claim during roster cuts – not to mention Tyler Linderbaum’s departure in free agency months earlier. Now, what? Zach’s take: The Ravens have massive center problems right now. Danny Pinter was already done for the season, and both Jovaughn Gwyn and Ethan Pocic had to be carted off the field during the Cowboys game in Brazil. Now, we know both will be out “long-term.” In the immediate future, the Ravens’ only response is to play rookie first-rounder Vega Ioane at center. He snapped the ball in Brazil when it was needed and didn’t make any mistakes in an extremely high-pressure situation. Baltimore does not have any other options on the roster or practice squad after choosing to keep Andrew Vorhees on the 53-man roster over Corey Bullock, who was claimed off waivers by the Panters. Minter indicated that both Gwyn and Pocic could go on IR, so the Ravens will need to make a signing this week in any event. In the long-term, if Gwyn and Pocic are out for the year, the Ravens will have to make a major trade for either a guard or center. That will depend on what’s available on the market and if Ioane is a viable option at center, which the Ravens will find out during Week 4. Now, it’s your turn!
