title: Chicago Bears Stock Watch: Keenum, Raymond shine in win over Eagles
summary: Monday night’s game looked like an uphill battle earlier in the week. The Eagles came into Chicago 2-0 and the Chicago Bears were without their dynamic quarterback and their young backup. Starting a third-string quarterback, even at home, against a perennial playoff team is rarely a recipe for success. But as fans are beginning to […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears looks to make a pass during the first quarter of the NFL game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Monday night’s game looked like an uphill battle earlier in the week. The Eagles came into Chicago 2-0 and the Chicago Bears were without their dynamic quarterback and their young backup. Starting a third-string quarterback, even at home, against a perennial playoff team is rarely a recipe for success. But as fans are beginning to become accustomed to, Ben Johnson had other plans. It was a familiar recipe at times, with the defense forcing three turnovers. However, it was the passing game that carried the load early for Chicago. Case Keenum looked like his Houston days in college, when he set all-time NCAA passing records that still stand. Once the Bears took a 20-7 lead, the run game got going. All in all, it was a very fun, team win for Chicago to move to 2-1 on the season and stay above .500 without Caleb Williams. Let’s run through it! Stock up Case Keenum, QB – Who says 38-years-old is old?! Not your 38-year-old author. 247 yards passing, two touchdown passes and a game-sealing rushing TD. He was making plays at all levels of the field, not just dinking and dunking. It was as perfect as you would want from a third-string QB. Kalif Raymond, WR – Three games into the season and weapons like Luther Burden III, Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland, who would have thought 32-year-old Raymond would be their leading receiver? Six catches, 90 yards and he capped it with a 41-yard touchdown that really blew the game open to Chicago’s side. Dillon Thieneman, S – The rookie led the Bears in tackles for the third straight game. He also notched his first career interception. He put himself in the absolute best spot, while former Bears QB Andy Dalton somehow didn’t see him. Stock down Rome Odunze, WR – Odunze continues to be confounding. He disappears for stretches in games, then he drops an open touchdown pass with no defenders around him and gets flagged for a false start on third-and-one near the goal line. But then he comes up with two or three big catches on a crucial drive. Here in year three, it’s time to see more consistency from the former ninth-overall pick. Jaylon Johnson, CB – Johnson has been up and down. He finished last night’s game strong, with five tackles and a TFL. But he was getting beat and looked like he was playing from behind for much of the game. It’s fair to wonder if he’s ever going to be able to recapture his glory from a few years ago. Sam Roush, TE – It’s often hard to pick a third player for “down” after a big win like that, especially when both sides of the ball played so well. So maybe it’s a choose-your-own-adventure here. But Roush diving on an already downed punt and causing a touchback was another rookie mistake just a week after a very rough outing against Minnesota. It’s a tough learning curve, and hopefully the rookie and fans will look back on this as a small blip on a successful career. Who is on your up and down lists this week? Let us know in the comments.
author: Sam Householder

title: Don’t cancel the Chicago Bears’ season just yet
summary: As someone who’s written a lot of articles and shared a lot of sports takes in my career, let me give you an invaluable piece of advice: Sometimes, it helps to wait a bit. Because the reality is, you don’t know what will happen. I know that concept gets lost in our “attention” economy, where […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Case Keenum #11 of the Chicago Bears celebrates after Kalif Raymond #14 scored a 41 yard touchdown against the Philadelphia Eagles during the fourth quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images As someone who’s written a lot of articles and shared a lot of sports takes in my career, let me give you an invaluable piece of advice: Sometimes, it helps to wait a bit. Because the reality is, you don’t know what will happen. I know that concept gets lost in our “attention” economy, where everyone feels like they have to share every thought in their mind because, well, that’s just what people do today. But I find it quite useful as a journalist, especially as one who wants to tell you the truth as opposed to one who just wants your clicks. Now, if I were to share some of the texts I sent to family and friends (which I won’t), you’d know I wasn’t entirely surprised by the Bears beating the Philadelphia Eagles on Monday Night Football, even with Case Keenum, their third-string quarterback, in the fold. Funnily enough, I had a whole post ready for Friday about how I had a decent amount of confidence in Keenum playing better than expected ready to go before my actual full-time job drove it from my mind. But I don’t mind that I didn’t send it. Because actually watching Monday’s game gives me a perspective I wouldn’t have had otherwise. Because, let me tell you, I was fully prepared to warn all Bears fans to make their peace with this season already and just prepare to flush it down the toilet. What’s another lost year, after all? But Keenum played far better than I anticipated he would, and the Bears as a whole far better than I predicted. (Maybe that Ben Johnson guy isn’t too bad after all.) Some of this might be a result of the Bears just knowing how to slow down an Eagles offense too reliant on its running game and too susceptible to droughts from a passing standpoint because their quarterback struggles to play from the pocket consistently. However, I think the most basic thing in all this is simply that the Bears and Johnson, no matter the odds stacked against them, are tougher than you think. Obviously, it was hard to see the Bears (on paper) winning a Monday Night Football game without star quarterback Caleb Williams, who—I don’t know if you heard—went down with a hamstring injury last week that could cost him the next month or so. Keenum, after all, is the third-string quarterback behind Tyson Bagent, who was in concussion protocol most of this week. Despite his experience as a starter who has won some big games, what could you realistically expect from him, right? But here’s the thing about the Chicago Bears: the grit from last season wasn’t a fluke. You don’t win all those one-score games without some mental toughness. That doesn’t just go away when your starting quarterback goes out. (At least, not if you have good leadership.) For all that talk about Johnson never having to start a backup QB in his career as an offensive coordinator or head coach, he sure looked like he had a good plan for Keenum to me. The veteran journeyman played like a man who knew what to expect and who didn’t intend to make any big mistakes on Monday, and his teammate benefited tremendously from that as Chicago’s surprising defensive performance continues. This isn’t just about one football game, though. After all, in a season with only 17 games in it, one game can have far more importance than you expect. Chicago being 2-1 on the season rather than 1-2 has already substantially boosted their odds of making the playoffs. If Chicago can simply break even through the next month or so without Williams, their odds feel even greater. You sign backups like Keenum the same way you invest in insurance: you pay them in case you need them. Don’t get carried away and think Chicago should keep a healthy Williams on the bench if Keenum’s playing well, of course. (That should be self-explanatory, but I know some of you can’t help yourselves.) If the Bears want any shot of winning the Super Bowl this year and beyond, Williams has to be under center. But right now, the Bears just need to survive until Williams can take the field again. Step 1 of that mission is now accomplished.
author: Khari Thompson

title: NFL Week 4 Power Rankings: Biggest September Surprises
summary: With Week 3 wrapping up, the NFL will turn the calendar to October as it heads into Week 4. Although the opening month of the season is over, there’s still plenty to learn about all 32 teams around the NFL. Week 2 brought key quarterback injuries, leading to multiple backups making starts and further clouding […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers reacts after throwing a touchdown pass to George Kittle #85 against the Arizona Cardinals in the fourth quarter at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images With Week 3 wrapping up, the NFL will turn the calendar to October as it heads into Week 4. Although the opening month of the season is over, there’s still plenty to learn about all 32 teams around the NFL. Week 2 brought key quarterback injuries, leading to multiple backups making starts and further clouding things for certain teams. With October on the horizon, here’s how our WCG Week 4 Power Rankings shake out. 1. Buffalo Bills (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: Continuity exists, despite a change at head coach. Is this the boost the Bills needed to get over the hump? Maybe this isn’t a huge surprise to some, but so far, Joe Brady has his team playing at as high a level as, if not higher than, former head coach Sean McDermott did. Quarterback Josh Allen is the frontrunner for MVP, and for the most part, they’ve looked like the best team in football. 2. San Francisco 49ers (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite more injuries (no surprise), they are a perfect 3-0, and the defense looks worthy enough to be considered Super Bowl caliber. Nick Bosa is hurt again. Their defensive line is in shambles. Mike Evans left with a rib injury on Sunday. Despite that, the 49ers are 3-0, and they look more complete than they did a year ago. There’s no reason to think that won’t continue. 3. Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: How quickly a 31-year-old Patrick Mahomes has returned to form is a credit to hard work, and of course, modern medicine. Not only are the Chiefs undefeated through September, but their star quarterback looks like he’s back to his normal self. Things got a little dicey against Miami, but Mahomes has a 7-2 touchdown-to-interception ratio, a 68% completion rate, and he’s averaging 270 yards per game. Life is good in Kansas City again. 4. Minnesota Vikings (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite more chaos at quarterback, the Vikings are a perfect 3-0. Will it last? Coming back against the Packers at home was one thing. Smoothing a high-scoring Bears offense was another. Now their defense has smothered a third team, and things look great for the Vikings so far in 2026. All of this, despite starting two quarterbacks through three games. All that bad luck from last year appears to be reversed this season. 5. Seattle Seahawks (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Their lone loss came with Sam Darnold playing all 60 minutes. Make no mistake, the Seahawks are one of the best teams in football. They’re also at their best when Darnold is under center. That said, it’s mildly surprising that their only loss of September came with Darnold at quarterback, and with the Jayden Daniels-less Commanders being the ones to do it. 6. Cincinnati Bengals (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: For the most part, the defense looks Super Bowl caliber. If that holds, the Bengals will be dangerous. Even with a disappointing loss to the Steelers on Sunday, fans have to feel good about the direction the Bengals are headed. Dexter Lawrence has helped transform this defense, and if everyone on the offense stays healthy, this will be a team no one wants to face all year. 7. Baltimore Ravens (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: The defense isn’t quite fixed under first-year head coach Jesse Minter, despite a highly paid and highly talented unit. To nobody’s surprise, the offense is back to looking like it normally does with Lamar Jackson under center. First-year offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has done a great job of keeping things explosive. Defensively, they still leave a lot to be desired. While they might be improved, it’s fair to wonder if they’ve improved enough to get back into the Super Bowl contender conversation. 8. Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: The Jaguars and Trevor Lawrence are quickly proving last year’s impressive run wasn’t a fluke. Jacksonville was one bad second half against the Broncos from being a perfect 3-0. Head coach Liam Coen became the quickest head coach to 15 wins in franchise history, and for the most part, everything is trending in the right direction. Quarterback Trevor Lawrence can also be included in that conversation. He’s playing at the highest level of his career. 9. Las Vegas Raiders (3-0) Biggest Surprise Through September: How real is their hot start? Eventually they’ll turn to Fernando Mendoza, but so far, Kirk Cousins has been more than up to the task. The most surprising team in the league through three games? The Las Vegas Raiders at a perfect 3-0 under first-year head coach Klint Kubiak. I’m not sure whether the offense under Cousins or their defense (which has given up just 54 points) has been more impressive. I’m not sure it’ll last, but Raiders fans have to be over the moon heading into October. 10. Chicago Bears (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: No Caleb Williams… No problem? Despite a disastrous Week 2 that cost the team three to four games with Williams out, Case Keenum helped deliver a winning month. It would have been easy to write the Bears off after last weekend against Minnesota simply. The offense looked anemic; they lost their starting quarterback, and overall, spirits seemed down heading into a pivotal early-season matchup against the undefeated Eagles. Instead, they have ridden two great defensive performances and a lifetime-from-Keenum performance to come out of September at 2-1 and in good shape moving forward. 11. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Saquon Barkley is still not himself, and because of that, the Eagles’ offense continues to teeter in the middle. Despite a 2-0 start, it was easy to look at the quality of their opponents, how they won those games, and wonder what was going on. The defense is no longer elite, but still plenty good enough. Although the offense isn’t “bad” by any stretch of the imagination, it still lacks the same pop we saw from a few years ago. They’re still in good shape moving forward in the NFC East, but it’s worth wondering if Sean Mannion is the answer at offensive coordinator. 12. Detroit Lions (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite their third new offensive play caller in as many seasons, the Lions’ offense is still pretty damn productive. It hasn’t looked the same as it did during Ben Johnson’s heyday, but they have scored exactly 31 points in each of their first three games. The bigger concern is the defense, which continues to give up far too many points, leading to a -2 point differential despite averaging 31 points per game offensively. 13. Denver Broncos (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite being 2-1, offensive regression has hit, and the Broncos have been left searching for consistency. Some will blame it on first-year play caller Davis Webb, while others will point to a bad start from quarterback Bo Nix. Regardless of how you cut it, it stands to reason that head coach Sean Payton could take back play-calling if things don’t improve drastically soon for more than one half at a time. We’ll see if they can string together a full game of good offense soon. 14. Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) Biggest Surprise Through September: Despite a new head coach and a 42-year-old quarterback, the Steelers look like a playoff contender. Count me as shocked as anybody. AFC North games are always close and usually ugly, but being able to pull out a win against the Bengals was an impressive feat. Hell, I’d even argue that it was Aaron Rodgers’ best game of the young season. Now, we’ll see if the offense can do enough to keep them well-rounded. 15. Los Angeles Rams (1-2) Biggest Surprise Through September: That vaunted…

title: Tee Higgins has been elite at catching passes and blocking
summary: It feels like Tee Higgins has been a little overshadowed by everything else going on around the Bengals’ offense. That probably won’t last. Higgins has come out of the gate absolutely cooking in 2026, and the numbers through three games are a pretty good reminder of just how valuable the Bengals’ WR2 really is. Through […]
full_text: It feels like Tee Higgins has been a little overshadowed by everything else going on around the Bengals’ offense. That probably won’t last. Higgins has come out of the gate absolutely cooking in 2026, and the numbers through three games are a pretty good reminder of just how valuable the Bengals’ WR2 really is. Through three games, Higgins has 14 catches for 244 yards, averaging an eye-popping 17.4 yards per reception, with a touchdown. He’s also coming off back-to-back 90-plus-yard performances after posting 95 yards against Houston and 90 against Pittsburgh. And there’s another number from Bradley Locker’s post that really puts his start into perspective: Higgins is averaging 81.3 receiving yards per game, which would put him on pace for more than 1,380 yards over a 17-game season. NFL receiver blocking efficacy/receiving ability through Week 3 The #Packers have a stud in Matthew Golden Also, look at all those #Jaguars WRs! pic.twitter.com/FjMVMEBTm4 — Bradley Locker (@Bradley_Locker) September 29, 2026 That’s some serious production. Locker’s tweet also shows how Higgins is highly effective as a run blocker. Scoring over 80 in both receiving and run-blocking grades shows just how great a start No. 5 is off to, as well as how complete of a wide receiver he is. Higgins has also been doing it without needing a ridiculous number of targets. He’s averaging fewer than five receptions per game, meaning Cincinnati is getting big chunks of yardage whenever Joe Burrow looks his way. The 6-foot-4 receiver has always been capable of making plays down the field, but there’s something particularly encouraging about seeing him establish this kind of consistency early. And that’s before we even get to what his presence does for Ja’Marr Chase. Defenses simply can’t afford to sell out to stop Chase when Higgins is playing like this. The Bengals can move Higgins around, attack different matchups, and let Burrow take whichever favorable matchup the defense gives him. Higgins isn’t just having a good start. He’s making it increasingly difficult for defenses to pick their poison against Cincinnati’s passing game. After three weeks, that’s a pretty encouraging development for a Bengals offense that will need all of its weapons if this team is going to make a run in 2026.

title: Bengals vs. Jaguars: 5 questions with Gus Logue of SB Nation’s Big Cat Country
summary: The Cincinnati Bengals return to Paycor Stadium this Sunday to take on the tough Jaguars. Jacksonville has had a couple of impressive victories this season, but they will be facing a motivated Bengals team that suffered a tough loss last week in Pittsburgh. To help us preview the game, we tapped the knowledge of Gus […]
full_text: Football: Cincinnati Bengals Ja'Marr Chase (1) in action, runs out of bounds after making a catch vs Jacksonville Jaguars at Paycor Stadium Cincinnati, OH 9/14/2025 CREDIT: Erick W. Rasco (Photo by Erick W. Rasco/Sports Illustrated via Getty Images/Getty Images) (Set Number: X164775) The Cincinnati Bengals return to Paycor Stadium this Sunday to take on the tough Jaguars. Jacksonville has had a couple of impressive victories this season, but they will be facing a motivated Bengals team that suffered a tough loss last week in Pittsburgh. To help us preview the game, we tapped the knowledge of Gus Logue over at Big Cat Country. We talked about a myriad of topics before Sunday’s big game. AC: The Jaguars are off to a nice start at 2-1. What’s the pulse on the viability of this team, as they have two dominating wins against teams of questionable caliber, but with Jacksonville also showing clear signs of improvement in year two under Liam Coen? GL: Jacksonville has an 11-2 regular-season record since last year’s bye week. Though it hasn’t exactly been a gauntlet of a schedule — and they’ve yet to pass the ultimate test of winning playoff games — the Jaguars are legitimate. They’re a balanced team that can win in a variety of ways. Trevor Lawrence looks unstoppable. The run defense is historically dominant. Ventrell Miller and Bhayshul Tuten have been superb replacing Travis Etienne and Devin Lloyd. And we even saw Travis Hunter catch his first NFL interception last week! Beyond postseason experience, Jacksonville’s biggest concerns are generating a pass rush and going against top pass rushes, but they’ve generally been able to mask those flaws. AC: After an explosive rookie season, Brian Thomas Jr. seemed to regress steeply in year two, and only has seven catches for 88 yards through three games this year. What’s going on there? Is there hope he will begin to turn things around? GL: It’s looking pretty grim right now. Thomas Jr. had two brutal drops in Week 2 that were reminiscent of his drops against Cincy in Week 2 last year. The Jaguars stopped sending him over the middle of the field a long time ago, but the issue now is that they’re not even throwing deep to him. Instead, Thomas Jr. has become a part-time player, mostly just running wind sprints from the X receiver spot. Sixth-round rookie Josh Cameron has taken reps from him, including most high-leverage situations. Cameron already has 2 touchdowns this year thanks to designated targets in the red zone. I waved off trade rumors about Thomas Jr. last year, but at this point, a change of scenery probably makes sense. BT is too talented to be a WR3/4 in Jacksonville when he could be a WR2/3 elsewhere. His game-breaking speed is being wasted because the Jaguars don’t trust him enough to design shot plays for him. Might as well recoup some draft capital, especially with Cameron looking good and Travis Hunter being available as depth. AC: Trevor Lawrence has looked much more capable under Coen and is off to a hot start this year, making plays through the air and with his legs. Are these further signs of him progressing as he hits the peak of his career, an indication of excelling against some opposing teams that are struggling this season, or a little bit of both? GL: By the grace of the football gods, Jacksonville didn’t have to face Myles Garrett in the season opener, but they’ve still played some stout units. The Browns, Broncos, and Patriots were all top-nine defenses by EPA/pass allowed last year, and they all rank top-15 so far this year. Lawrence has faced quality opponents in every game this season, and he’s responded with great performances, matching the aggressiveness of pass rushes by needling tight-window throws before pressure arrives. He’s admittedly had more head-scratching plays than we’d like to see — his 5.3% turnover-worthy play rate ranks seventh-highest among 37 QBs, per PFF — but we’re finally seeing the best of Lawrence for full 60-minute stretches. He’s lettin’ it rip. AC: Which player(s) have surprised you the most this year, in terms of their improvement? GL: Bhayshul Tuten, without a doubt. I actually went into the season thinking that Chris Rodriguez Jr. could end up earning the Jaguars’ starting RB job, but boy, does that seem silly now. Jacksonville’s rushing game is the Tuten show. He looks massively improved as a between-the-tackles rusher compared to last season. Even with Lawrence and the passing game humming, fans are clamoring for Coen to give Tuten the ball more. I also need to shout out DaVon Hamilton, who has always been a great run-stuffing nose tackle for the Jaguars — but currently, “Ham” is playing like a first-team All-Pro. He is single-handedly blowing up plays as we’ve never seen from him before. AC: As of the beginning of the week, FanDuel has Cincinnati as 2.5-point favorites at home this week. What’s your feeling about that line, and how do you see this game going? GL: Cincinnati’s defense is sure to bounce back after allowing Pittsburgh’s Aaron Rodgers to look like Green Bay’s Aaron Rodgers. At the same time, the Steelers hanging 30 points on the Bengals last week gives me confidence that the Jaguars’ offense will continue to fire on all cylinders. On the other side of the ball, I’m definitely terrified of Ja’Marr Chase, who has 31 catches for 391 yards and 2 scores in JUST THREE GAMES against the Jaguars in his career. We’ll see if Travis Hunter is up for that tall of a task. So long as Chase is relatively contained, I expect the Jaguars to cover the spread and win outright in a game that far exceeds the projected total of 51.5 points. Our thanks to Gus Logie over at Big Cat Country for the insight and Week 4 preview! Go check out the other side of the conversation there, too!

summary: The Bengals were brought down to earth on Sunday in Pittsburgh, and now they have the task of proving to everyone (possibly even to themselves) who they really are is the team that beat the Buccaneers and Texans in Weeks 1 and 2. full_text: The Bengals were brought down to earth on Sunday in Pittsburgh, and now they have the task of proving to everyone (possibly even to themselves) who they really are is the team that beat the Buccaneers and Texans in Weeks 1 and 2. They made a flurry of moves on Tuesday, including bringing Mitch Tinsley back from Houston’s practice squad. They weren’t the only team making roster moves. While Cincy brought Tinsley back to Cincinnati, the Miami Dolphins signed linebacker Shaka Heyward off the Bengals’ practice squad on Tuesday. In Week 4 the Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars, but they travel to Miami to play the Dolphins the following week where they could see Heyward on the field. Heyward a 2023 undrafted rookie out of Duke, logged 10 combined tackles in eight appearances. He is very much aware of the Bengals’ defensive inner workings and schemes, and Miami may be looking to take advantage. Here’s what else is going on: With Jalen Davis headed to IR with a hamstring issue, the most likely fix in the secondary is moving Dax Hill into the slot and calling on rookie third-round pick Tacario Davis to take over outside opposite DJ Turner . That’s what happened during the game in Pittsburgh. Hill is familiar with the nickel corner position, both with the Bengals and in college. Mark Duffner’s Nickname For Joe Burrow And Other Bengals-Jags Tidbits “I’m very excited about the Bengals continuing to improve the roster, and I’ll also say this,” Duffner says. “I hope like heck that this team can reach the heights that I hope they can and bring a championship to Mr. Brown. I’m very much pulling for that possibility to occur.” Solomon Wilcots lists several reasons the Bengals’ defense isn’t that much improved from where it was over the last couple seasons, the chief of which has been the team’s inability to tackle. He also points to the fact the Bengals’ defense has allowed 27 or more points in two of the team’s three games. The Bengals aren’t the only team making roster moves. While the Bengals brought Mitchell Tinsley back to Cincinnati from Houston’s practice squad, the Miami Dolphins signed linebacker Shaka Heyward off the Bengals’ practice squad. In Week 4 the Bengals host the Jacksonville Jaguars, but they travel to Miami to play the Dolphins the following week where they could see Heyward on the field. Bengals’ Tanner Hudson: Signed to Cincinnati’s active roster The Bengals signed Hudson off the practice squad to the active roster Tuesday. Hudson was elevated from the practice squad for two of the Bengals’ first three games of the regular season, accumulating three catches on as many targets for 17 yards. He’ll now be a part of the team’s 53-man roster moving forward and will contribute mostly on special teams and in a depth role on offense behind fellow tight ends Mike Gesicki, Drew Sample and Erick All.

title: The Good, The Bad and The Ugly from the Bengals’ 30-27 Loss to the Steelers
summary: Well, that one had pretty much everything you could want from a Bengals – Steelers game — except the result Cincinnati wanted. The Bengals walked into Acrisure Stadium at 2-0, traded punches with Pittsburgh for four quarters, and had the ball with a chance to win late. Instead, they walked out with their first loss […]
full_text: Well, that one had pretty much everything you could want from a Bengals – Steelers game — except the result Cincinnati wanted. The Bengals walked into Acrisure Stadium at 2-0, traded punches with Pittsburgh for four quarters, and had the ball with a chance to win late. Instead, they walked out with their first loss of the 2026 season, falling 30-27 after Chris Boswell’s 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining. There were plenty of positives to take from this one. There were also some very familiar problems. Here’s the good, the bad, and the ugly from Cincinnati’s Week 3 loss. The Good: Joe Burrow and the passing game Joe Burrow was really good Sunday. He completed 28 of 37 passes for 282 yards and three touchdowns, finishing with a 123.9 passer rating. He also opened the game by completing his first 14 throws and was 18-of-21 for 152 yards and two scores at halftime. More importantly, Burrow consistently made plays when the Bengals needed them. Ja’Marr Chase hauled in nine passes for 98 yards and a touchdown, while Tee Higgins added six catches for 90 yards and a touchdown. Mike Gesicki also came through with a 25-yard touchdown grab on fourth-and-2 in the fourth quarter to put Cincinnati ahead 27-24. Chase also crossed the 7,000-yard mark for his career, becoming just the fourth player in NFL history to reach that milestone in 81 games or fewer. That’s quite the receiving duo. And despite all the talk about Pittsburgh’s defense coming into this one, the Bengals moved the football. Cincinnati finished with 365 total yards, including 282 through the air. The offense did enough to win this game. The Good: Dexter Lawrence re-announces himself If anyone was wondering what the Bengals were getting when they acquired Dexter Lawrence, Sunday provided another pretty good answer. Lawrence recorded four tackles and two sacks of Aaron Rodgers, with both sacks coming on third down in the red zone. He also hit Rodgers three times and was a major reason Pittsburgh had to settle for field goals on its final two scoring drives. This was Lawrence’s first Bengals-Steelers game, and he certainly made an introduction. The defense ultimately gave up 30 points, but Lawrence and the defensive front were giving Cincinnati opportunities to survive some of the mistakes happening elsewhere. The Bad: The explosive plays allowed The Bengals’ defense had some really good moments. It also gave up some plays that simply can’t happen late in a close game. The biggest examples came on Pittsburgh’s go-ahead drive. Darnell Washington caught a pass and turned it into a 47-yard gain, and Jaylen Warren followed it with a 26-yard run. Those two plays moved Pittsburgh from its own 8-yard line all the way down to the Cincinnati 6 and set up Boswell’s go-ahead field goal. Warren finished with 127 rushing yards on 17 carries, while the Steelers produced 430 total yards. A trademark physical day from the Steelers. The Bengals’ defense was able to stiffen in the red zone, but continually allowing explosive plays is eventually going to catch up with you. It did Sunday. The Ugly: Special teams This is where things really started to unravel. The Bengals had a 20-17 lead in the third quarter when defensive end Cedric Johnson was flagged for roughing the punter, extending a Pittsburgh drive that eventually ended in a Steelers touchdown. Then, with Cincinnati leading 27-24 in the fourth quarter, Ke’Shawn Williams muffed a punt, giving Pittsburgh the ball at the Bengals’ 14-yard line. Ten Pittsburgh points came directly from those two special teams mistakes. That’s a massive swing in a three-point game. Joe Burrow and the offense shouldn’t have to be perfect, but when you’re playing an AFC North rival on the road, you can’t keep handing the other team short fields and extra possessions. The Ugly: The final drive Unfortunately, this is what seemingly everyone will remember. After Pittsburgh took a 30-27 lead, Cincinnati got the ball back with 2:08 remaining and still had a legitimate chance to win. The Bengals eventually moved into Steelers territory, but a pass to Chase Brown for minus-4 yards started to derail things. With 44 seconds remaining and facing a 3rd-and-8, Burrow dropped back from the Pittsburgh 38-yard line looking for a shot at the end zone. Derrick Harmon got to him, punched the ball out and Sebastian Joseph-Day recovered. Ballgame. Burrow said afterward that the Bengals were trying to take a shot into the end zone while avoiding a sack because they were already in field-goal range. It’s tough to put the entire loss on that play. There were plenty of mistakes before it. But that’s the play that ultimately ended Cincinnati’s final chance. The Bottom Line The Bengals lost a game they absolutely had a chance to win. That’s frustrating, especially because there was a lot to like. Burrow played well. Chase and Higgins were excellent. The offensive line did a strong job against T.J. Watt. Lawrence looked every bit like the defensive centerpiece Cincinnati hoped he would be. But the Bengals also committed six penalties for 40 yards , made two costly special teams mistakes, and allowed Pittsburgh to hit them with too many explosive plays. As Burrow put it after the game: “We just can’t shoot ourselves in the foot like that. You can’t win in this league when you do that.” That’s probably the simplest way to describe it. At 2-1, the Bengals aren’t suddenly a bad football team. But they just got a pretty good reminder of how little room for error there is against a divisional opponent — particularly when you’re playing on the road. And now comes the important part: seeing how they respond.
author: Anthony Cosenza

title: Bengals Tuesday Trenches: A bump in the road or is the sky falling?
summary: I’m an optimist. Obviously, things aren’t always black and white. Optimists aren’t always optimistic, pessimists aren’t always pessimistic. But generally speaking, I think you can lump most people into one of those two categories. The Cincinnati Bengals did just about everything they could on Sunday in Pittsburgh to lose. On paper, it was set up […]
full_text: Cincinnati Bengals quarterback Joe Burrow (9) covers his ears as he listens for a play call in the fourth quarter of the NFL Week 3 game between the Pittsburgh Steelers and the Cincinnati Bengals at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh on Sunday, Sept. 27, 2026. The Bengals fell to 2-1 on the season with a 30-27 loss on the road. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Co I’m an optimist. Obviously, things aren’t always black and white. Optimists aren’t always optimistic, pessimists aren’t always pessimistic. But generally speaking, I think you can lump most people into one of those two categories. The Cincinnati Bengals did just about everything they could on Sunday in Pittsburgh to lose. On paper, it was set up perfectly for the Bengals. The Steelers’ offense was borderline anemic heading into Week 3, while the Bengals’ defense was coming off a show of force in Houston, where they held the Texans to just six points. We knew Joe Burrow and the Bengals’ offense were going to score their points, and it felt like Cincinnati was on its way to a 3-0 start for the first time since 2015. Nope. The defense generated virtually no pass rush and allowed 42-year-old Aaron Rodgers to run around in the backfield like he was 15 years younger. Rodgers is a first-ballot Hall of Fame quarterback, so the fact that he led the Steelers to a victory isn’t shocking. The way he avoided pressure like he was Burrow’s age, though, certainly was. Special teams, which we almost never talk about outside of Evan McPherson—and that’s usually a good thing—was a disaster . The punt return unit essentially cost the Bengals 10 points. Pittsburgh scored a touchdown after Cedric Johnson’s roughing-the-kicker penalty extended a drive, then added three more after a muffed punt from Ke’Shawn Williams set the Steelers up at Cincinnati’s 14-yard line. Then, just when Burrow got the ball back with plenty of time to lead a game-winning drive, he was sacked for the first time all afternoon. And he fumbled. Game over. The loss isn’t going to kill them. We’re only through Week 3, and this was their first division game. If they finish the regular season 5-1 in the division and 16-1 overall, they’ll obviously have the No. 1 seed and would be among the favorites to win the Lombardi Trophy. That’s how you can look at this if you’re an optimist. That’s how I look at it, and it’s how I’ve always been. It’s probably one of the reasons I haven’t gone insane as a Bengals fan, although I’ll admit I can occasionally drift into borderline delusion. To me, this is just a bump in the road. The idea that the Bengals were going to go undefeated—even within the division—was always unrealistic. The AFC North is brutal. These four teams know each other intimately, and because of that, almost every divisional game turns into a slugfest. Every team, no matter how good, typically has an ugly loss or two during the regular season. If the Bengals were going to have one, maybe it’s better to get it out of the way early. Of course, that’s the optimist talking. How about you? Do you see this as a bump in the road during what could still be a championship season, or has the sky already fallen? Sound off. Random thoughts about the game: Amarius Mims was outstanding against future Hall of Fame edge rusher T.J. Watt. Watt’s star may be fading while Mims’ is rising, but regardless, the Bengals’ right tackle didn’t allow Watt to even sniff the quarterback. For the vast majority of the game, the offensive line looked pretty good. The sack at the end just happened to come at the absolute worst possible time. The run game, especially when Burrow was under center, looked explosive again. It’s a shame the Bengals got themselves into a position where they had to play catch-up and move away from it. The Bengals’ defense came into the game tied for the league lead in sacks, while the Steelers were starting a new right guard and right tackle. You certainly wouldn’t have known it from watching Sunday. I am still very much anxiously awaiting my first look at Landon Robinson on the field. He was a healthy scratch again. I’m concerned about the secondary. DK Metcalf and Michael Pittman Jr. are obviously NFL-caliber receivers. They aren’t in the same league as Ja’Marr Chase and Tee Higgins, though, and the Bengals’ secondary—which practiced against the best wide receiver duo in football all summer—looked lost at times. Covering tight ends continues to be an issue, and so does tackling. I know Darnell Washington is a massive human being, but Bengals defenders were bouncing off him like he was made of rubber. Defenses are not going to let Burrow beat them deep with Chase and Higgins, but that has opened up the underneath passing game—which can essentially serve as an extension of the run game—as well as the middle of the field. I’d like to see Dohnte Meyers get more involved. Getting the ball in his hands in space could force defenses to think twice about devoting so much attention to Chase and Higgins. The Bengals’ run defense was incredible against the Texans, but Jaylen Warren and the Steelers gashed Cincinnati all afternoon. Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and finished with 127 yards. Rodgers completed passes of more than 20 yards to five different receivers. That’s… not ideal. I think it’s becoming clear that the Bengals are thin at linebacker and in the secondary. We knew that heading into the season, but I’m surprised it may be coming back to bite them this early. Now the Bengals come home to face a Jacksonville Jaguars team that just dropped 35 points on New England’s vaunted defense. If Cincinnati’s defense doesn’t look more like the unit we saw in Week 2, the Bengals could be in trouble. We may be looking at a shootout. Hopefully, for my blood pressure, we aren’t. Relative Song Lyrics: The sun’s gonna rise tomorrow Somewhere on the east side of sorrow You better pack your bags west Stick out your chest, and then hit the road The sun’s gonna rise tomorrow Somewhere on the East side of sorrow Don’t give it a reason to follow Let it be, then let it go

title: Week 4 Browns NFL Power Rankings: Cleveland enters the Top 20
summary: It is Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns rose another 5 spots this week, making that a total of 10+ spots they’ve improved after back-to-back wins. All teams in the AFC North are 2-1, but the Bengals’ stock took the biggest hit this week. Overall, the Browns went up by […]
full_text: It is Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season, and the Cleveland Browns rose another 5 spots this week, making that a total of 10+ spots they’ve improved after back-to-back wins. All teams in the AFC North are 2-1, but the Bengals’ stock took the biggest hit this week. Overall, the Browns went up by 5.1 spots from week-to-week to have an overall ranking of 20.7 . Here is a summary of how the Cleveland Browns are viewed across mainstream media outlets in NFL Power Rankings heading into Week 4 of the 2026 NFL season. CBS Sports – No. 25 (up 3 spots) Who had them going 2-1 to start, especially after the blowout loss to the Jaguars in Week 1? They are tied for first place in the AFC North. ESPN – No. 24 (up 5 spots) Fantasy surprise: QB Deshaun Watson Expectations were low for Watson, who had performed like one of the worst NFL quarterbacks since joining Cleveland in 2022 and was returning from two Achilles tears. His ADP had him ranked as the QB29, but he’s the QB10 so far this season. Watson’s passing numbers (587 yards, five touchdowns) are modest, but he has turned the ball over only once, and he’s using his legs well. His 105 rushing yards ranks fourth among quarterbacks. NFL.com – No. 17 (up 6 spots) The Browns’ defense is back and playing a cohesive brand that rivals the best units in the NFL over the last two weeks. Mason Graham is off to a fantastic start, Jared Verse has started to make an impact and Carson Schwesinger picked up right where he left off in last season’s Defensive Rookie of the Year campaign. Deshaun Watson also seems to have rediscovered a fourth-quarter clutch mode we haven’t seen from him since he was in Houston. Cleveland’s offense needs to be better, but the Browns have definitely looked competent and earned the last two wins. Sporting News – No. 21 (up 7 spots) Deshaun Watson is putting the Browns in good positions to win in close games. Getting the Buccaneers and Panthers back-to-back brings some needed good offensive vibes under Todd Monken. Don’t forget about Mason Graham living up to be a defensive game-changer. Yahoo Sports – No. 20 (up 4 spots) The Browns have two close wins against the Buccaneers and Panthers, who are a combined 1-5 this season with the only win between them coming against a Cooper Rush-led Falcons team. Cleveland was outgained 360-259 by the Panthers at home on Sunday and caught a nice break that Deshaun Watson’s late interception was nullified due to a questionable roughing the passer penalty. If you want to buy the Browns’ 2-1 start that’s fine, but there are not a lot of signs that this is sustainable going forward. If there is an argument to be made that the Browns can keep this going, it’s their defense. After a horrific Week 1 against the Jaguars, the defense has been sixth in the NFL in EPA allowed per play over the last two weeks. Mike Rutenberg took over defensive coordinator job from Jim Schwartz this past offseason and the opening game was concerning, but the group has settled in since then. Bleacher Report – No. 20 (up 8 spots) The Cleveland Browns are racking up wins against the NFC South, beating the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Carolina Panthers by close margins. Deshaun Watson only completed about half of his pass attempts in the previous outing, but he’s doing enough to lead the Browns to victories, throwing two touchdown passes without an interception in back-to-back games. We’ll see how Cleveland handles a little success in a division matchup against the Pittsburgh Steelers coming up on a short week. USA Today – No. 18 (up 4 spots) An unanticipated Deshaun Watson breakout vaulted them back to a 2-1 record and a four-way tie atop (at the bottom?) of the AFC North. full_text: (Photo by Frank Jansky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Cleveland Browns and Pittsburgh Steelers will resume the AFC’s longest-running rivalry on Thursday night in downtown Cleveland. It is also one of the league’s strangest rivalries, as both teams have rarely been good at the same time. The Browns dominated for the first 20 years, winning 31 of the first 40 meetings with the Steelers. The 1970s were dominated by Pittsburgh, the 1980s by the Browns, and things have gone decidedly in Pittsburgh’s favor since 1999. Although the Browns have won four in a row at home against the Steelers, and six of the last seven overall in Cleveland. full_text: On a short week, the injury reports are huge for all NFL teams. For the Cleveland Browns, likely missing starting center Elgton Jenkins could be a big deal, with HC Todd Monken confirming that Luke Wypler would start in his place, with Parker Brailsford as the backup. The Browns are hopeful that CB Tyson Campbell can return after missing a week and got positive news with OL Teven Jenkins returning to practice for the first time since hurting his back. The big news on Wednesday was that Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey is dealing with a broken wrist, but is still hopeful that he can find a way to play in Week 4’s Thursday Night Football in a game that will decide who walks into Week 5 with the top spot in the AFC North. Ramsey, listed as limited on the Pittsburgh practice report, was seen with some kind of cast on his wrist at practice today: Jalen Ramsey said today that his wrist is broken. title: Browns need to keep the WRs on track
summary: The Cleveland Browns’ comeback win on Sunday against Carolina overshadowed a relatively poor day for the wide receivers.  Cleveland’s “big 3” of Jerry Jeudy (zero targets), Denzel Boston (four targets), and KC Concepcion (nine targets) were targeted a total of 13 times, but only pulled in four receptions for 50 yards and no touchdowns.  While […]
full_text: (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Cleveland Browns’ comeback win on Sunday against Carolina overshadowed a relatively poor day for the wide receivers. Cleveland’s “big 3” of Jerry Jeudy (zero targets), Denzel Boston (four targets), and KC Concepcion (nine targets) were targeted a total of 13 times, but only pulled in four receptions for 50 yards and no touchdowns. While some of that can be attributed to quarterback Deshaun Watson misfiring on some passes, most notably to Concepcion, it will be difficult to win without more production from the position. Head coach Todd Monken was asked about the situation on Tuesday, primarily the adjustment that rookies have to make at the NFL level, and said the bumps are to be expected and have nothing to do with the talent or work habits of either rookie receiver : “First of all, you talk about two young men that are diligent, highly intelligent; it’s important to them to get it right. And at times we forget that they’ve played three games in the NFL, because we want to move them around; we want to find different spots we can play them, right? And at times it’s counterproductive, because we just haven’t gotten through all of the nuances that go with each spot, whether you’re inside or you’re outside, or whether you’re in the boundary or to the field, what looks you get on a given week. “And that’s some of the struggles we’re having offensively with so many young players, whether it’s a tight end or running back or O-line, you’ve got so many things that come up where you’re like, ‘OK, there’s not as much to really refer back to from an experience standpoint.’ And those aren’t excuses; we’ve got to be cleaner, we’ve got to play a lot better, got to coach it better. But those guys are constantly on top of their stuff, and you can see it, and that’s a real credit to them at a young age. And they’ve got a lot of reps doing it, but they’re only going to continue to get better and better and better once they play extended plays and extended games.” It is not all on the receivers, of course, as the offensive line needs to give the quarterback time to throw and the quarterback has to deliver a catchable pass, something that Watson struggled with for much of the game against the Panthers. Wide receivers with 20+ targets and <81 receiving yards through the first three weeks of the season, since 2000. KC Concepcion joining a distinguished line of Browns pass catchers. pic.twitter.com/1tSCq2D3WR — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 29, 2026 For his part, Watson highlighted the importance of time on task for the rookies : “There are different looks (from the defense). At the same time, these guys are rookies, KC and (Denzel) Boston. Especially playing any receiver, or any person who knows that playing in the slot in the NFL is a lot. It’s a lot of different moving parts, a lot of different coverages. They can match; they can zone off; you’ve got linebackers, defenders. So, it takes some time to be able to recognize all the different coverages and things that defenses can do. “And it’s week to week. Every team is different. You’re not going to get the same that you did in Tampa versus Carolina, same thing moving forward on Thursday night. So, that’s just kind of, the more reps, the more experience that we get playing with each other and seeing the same thing, it’ll get better for sure.” But what about the lack of targets for Jeudy, the team’s presumptive No. 1 receiver, who has two receptions on the season (both in Week 1) and has been targeted only once in the past two games? To his credit, Watson said his focus is on keeping the offense moving, rather than forcing the ball to any one particular player : “At the end of the day, you got to take what the defense gives you. I think teams know we want to be explosive, but at the same time, you got to let it come to it. It’s got to happen naturally. Once you try to force those explosives and throw it downfield, and now you’re sitting at third-and-long, those are wasted plays. So, you’ve got to take them when those opportunities come and hit them. But at the same time, if it takes 20 plays to get a touchdown, then hey, that’s what we’re going to do.” I got into it with Panthers fans on our revamped WR room, so I thought I would annoy them and update the Denzel Boston V Tet Mcmillan numbers. Did the #Browns snag a Wr1 in Rd2. #NFL #Dawgpound pic.twitter.com/mkNubbmf6s — Bearded Browns (@Bearded_Browns) September 29, 2026 It has only been three games, and outside of a rough outing against the Panthers, both Boston (top among rookies with 195 receiving yards) and Concepcion (second among rookies with 12 receptions) have been off to a good start. As for Jeudy, the talent is there, so it is fair, for now, to expect him to get going sooner rather than later. Even so, the Browns are not going to be able to survive offensively if the wide receivers are not an active part of the passing game, so Thursday night against the Pittsburgh Steelers seems like a good time to get everyone back on track. title: Browns Week 4: Scouting the Pittsburgh Steelers- Something new or the same as always?
summary: The Cleveland Browns prepare for their AFC North opener against their hated rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers. Like the Browns, the Steelers underwent a coaching change this past offseason, but when it comes to their quarterback situation, this will be the last season we see quarterback Aaron Rodgers play in the NFL. On paper, Pittsburgh returns […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns prepare for their AFC North opener against their hated rival, the Pittsburgh Steelers . Like the Browns, the Steelers underwent a coaching change this past offseason, but when it comes to their quarterback situation, this will be the last season we see quarterback Aaron Rodgers play in the NFL. On paper, Pittsburgh returns the same team that made the postseason last year but made minor tweaks. New coach, same QB Mike Tomlin is now working for NBC Sports. After spending a year away from coaching, Mike McCarthy is now coaching the Pittsburgh Steelers. If Mike McCarthy has an NBA head coach counterpart, he would be Doc Rivers (who also works for NBC Sports). Outside of one championship that he won, McCarthy’s resume is average at best. His departure from the Packers was somewhat messy, but he was later hired by the Dallas Cowboys. Despite having numerous winning seasons with the Cowboys, McCarthy could never get them out of the divisional round, despite some years of the team having the talent to make a deep playoff run. It’s too early to tell if going from Tomlin to McCarthy is an upgrade, but McCarthy’s coaching staff is slightly better than Tomlin’s staff from last year. In regard to the quarterback, Aaron Rodgers will retire after this season. Rodgers hasn’t been as good during his prime, but he is still showing that he’s capable of being a competent quarterback despite his clear limitations. Are the Steelers actually good? It’s too early to tell, but no one knows how good the Steelers are. On paper, the roster seems the exact same as last year despite a couple of new additions. Despite the team being 2-1, the two wins that the Steelers have aren’t exactly impressive . The Atlanta Falcons could’ve beaten them if quarterback Cooper Rush didn’t start, and special teams is the reason why the Cincinnati Bengals couldn’t leave Pittsburgh with a win. The ceiling/floor still remains the same, but it’s hard to imagine this team actually making a deep playoff run due to their limitations eventually catching up to them. This team isn’t bad, but it’s hard to say if they are actually good. The defense might be better, scheme-wise The one unit that has slowly dropped off over the years is Steelers defense. Maybe not anymore. Defensive coordinator Teryl Austin was a liability, and going from Austin to Patrick Graham was an upgrade. The unit remains the same on paper, but on the field, the defense looks different. Linebacker T.J. Watt is being moved around and not relegated to one spot, defensive tackle Cam Heyward is still defying Father Time, and defensive tackle Derrick Harmon seems to be making the leap. The secondary has some reliable veterans in Jalen Ramsey and Jamel Dean, but the situation surrounding Joey Porter Jr. is one that can’t be ignored. Porter Jr. hasn’t played this season, but he could play on Thursday night. After not reaching a new deal on a contract, Porter Jr could be traded to another team and the Steelers would be open to it. Overall, this unit could be better than what we have seen in recent years. Are you concerned about the Steelers in Week 4 or think they are just an older, struggling team? Join the conversation! title: Browns make 5 roster moves on Tuesday, ahead of Thursday Night Football vs. Steelers
summary: Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry has rarely met a roster move that he did not consider seriously and/or make. Berry is known for “churning” the bottom of the 53-man roster and the practice squad. Monday afternoon, we covered a report that the Browns flip-flopped two roster moves they had made last week at the cornerback […]
full_text: Cleveland Browns GM Andrew Berry has rarely met a roster move that he did not consider seriously and/or make. Berry is known for “churning” the bottom of the 53-man roster and the practice squad. Monday afternoon, we covered a report that the Browns flip-flopped two roster moves they had made last week at the cornerback position on the practice squad . On Tuesday, those two moves were among five that became official ahead of the team’s Thursday Night Football matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers : Browns added 2 to their practice squad CB Myles Bryant, as reported Monday night TE John FitzPatrick Browns released 2 from their practice squad CB D’Angelo Ross, as reported Monday night TE Messiah Swinson Cleveland also released veteran OL Kendrick Green from the injured reserve list, freeing him to sign with a team when he’s healthy enough to pass a physical. As shared by the team: Bryant (5-9, 192) is in his seventh NFL season out of Washington. Originally signed by New England as an undrafted free agent in 2020, he has appeared in 77 career games with the Patriots (2020-23) and the Texans (2024-25). He has recorded 173 career tackles, two sacks, four interceptions and 17 passes defensed. He spent time on the Browns’ practice squad earlier this season. Bryant will wear No. 27. FitzPatrick (6-7, 262) is in his fifth NFL season out of Georgia. Originally drafted by Atlanta in the sixth round in 2022, FitzPatrick has appeared in 33 career games with the Falcons (2022-23) and Packers (2024-25). Ross was elevated from the practice squad in Week 1 this season. Swinson has not played in an NFL regular-season game after going undrafted in the 2024 NFL Draft. Green, a third-round pick of the Steelers in 2021, played one game for the Browns in 2025 and has 37 career appearances in four seasons in the NFL.

title: Browns need to ‘spread the help’ versus the Steelers in Week 4
summary: The Cleveland Browns are 2-1 heading into a big Thursday Night Football matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers, where the home team is the underdog. Despite the Browns strong start and playoff contention early in the season, Cleveland’s offensive line has not performed well. Whether it is PFF grades, earning Frownies, or just the overall film, […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns are 2-1 heading into a big Thursday Night Football matchup with the Pittsburgh Steelers, where the home team is the underdog . Despite the Browns strong start and playoff contention early in the season , Cleveland’s offensive line has not performed well. Whether it is PFF grades , earning Frownies , or just the overall film, very few are lauding the unit upfront. The line was also not one of the reasons mentioned by fans for why the team is 2-1: The line’s concerns only grow if center Elgton Jenkins cannot play on Thursday . This offseason, OL Spencer Fano was considered the capstone of the new and improved Browns offensive line. The first offensive lineman selected in the 2026 NFL draft, Fano has not played poorly but, as noted in takeaways from Week 3 , Cleveland’s offense has done him no favors: Rookie Spencer Fano put on an island; looked like a rookie much of the game. Cleveland’s offense didn’t give him a lot of help and expected him to hold up. Unfortunately, it looks like film from the first two games showed that Fano could be beaten inside because Carolina attacked him there a lot. This analysis was backed up by former Browns and Ohio State Buckeyes star LeCharles Bentley a day later : I wish the Browns spread the help in pass protection a bit better. It’s a tall ask for a rookie left tackle to be on an island. In his Substack article, Bentley showed a video where Cleveland slid protection to the right, with five blockers for just three Panthers defenders. That not only left Fano blocking one-on-one, but also gave his defender a much larger area for his defender to attack. Instead of having a left guard and another defender directly to Fano’s right, Zion Johnson is blocking no one between the center and right guard: This is not a mistake by Johnson; instead, it was the protection call by the offense. Against an aggressive, veteran, and versatile Steelers defense, the Browns need to heed Bentley’s desire to “spread the help in pass protection” in Week 4. Otherwise, Deshaun Watson may not have a chance to get the offense going. How do you feel like Fano has played so far as a rookie? title: Browns big concern going into Week 4 vs. Steelers on Thursday Night Football
summary: The Cleveland Browns began Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season with five new starting offensive linemen. In the history of the league, that has never happened before. The Browns did not offer new deals to four of the five departing offensive linemen and waited to see if LG Joel Bitonio was coming back. This […]
full_text: The Cleveland Browns began Week 1 of the 2026 NFL season with five new starting offensive linemen. In the history of the league, that has never happened before. The Browns did not offer new deals to four of the five departing offensive linemen and waited to see if LG Joel Bitonio was coming back. This meant starting over and building something new. RELATED: WEEK 4 INJURY REPORT One of the new offensive linemen signed during free agency was C/OG Elgton Jenkins from the Green Bay Packers . In college, he was named First Team All-American and a two-time SEC Academic Honor Roll recipient. So, he’s smart, which is a condition for playing center because this position must read the defensive front, identify who the middle linebacker is on each play, and indicate to his linemates potential blitzers. #Browns starting center Elgton Jenkins in the concussion protocol and might have to miss the #Steelers game Thurs night; Tytus Howard's 3 false starts 'not okay': Takeaways –> https://t.co/GLBIEZAjp7 — Mary Kay Cabot (@MaryKayCabot) September 28, 2026 Jenkins came out of training camp as the starting center and has played every snap in this position this year. Yet, he is now listed on the Browns injury report with a concussion. Which is odd, because he played every down in the victory over the Carolina Panthers. It’s unclear when the concussion first occurred, when it was diagnosed, and why he was allowed to continue to play until the final gun. What could have happened is that while in the locker room, somebody noticed something wasn’t right with him or he woke up Monday morning feeling off. Next is a focused neurological exam, balance test, and memory evaluation. If diagnosed with a concussion, the player enters the official Return-to-Participation Protocol. This becomes a five-step process without any set time limit and is then cleared by the team doctor. Next, he is evaluated by an independent neurological consultant before the athlete can be cleared for play. What is known, however, is that he is on the injury report and there is a good possibility that Jenkins will not play against the Pittsburgh Steelers on Thursday Night Football. Monday injury report for #Browns and #Steelers , although neither practiced so projected. Concussion for center Elgton Jenkins and knee for Tylan Wallace. Austin Barber and Spencer Fano aren’t listed. pic.twitter.com/BXiM3CnHq8 — Chris Easterling (@ceasterlingABJ) September 28, 2026 Which is a huge problem. The center is the quarterback of the offensive line. It is Jenkins’ job to yell out protection calls and read the defensive front pre-snap so the rest of the linemen know who to block. He has the experience and has gelled nicely with his new linemates. It is a special position with special duties besides blocking on his own. And now, that line leader will be missing. In his stead will be either Luke Wypler or rookie Parker Brailsford, who was taken in the fifth round in this year’s NFL Draft. Both had plenty of success at the college level at the center position. Wypler played well last year during the few games he started in. He’s was also really good in pass blocking last year especially during Bills and Steelers game last year. — Liam Scoops Mcilwee (@LiamScoops) September 28, 2026 Wypler is the best bet since he is now in his fourth NFL season and has played in 25 games with six starts, including subbing for C Ethan Pocic in the final five games last season. He played every snap against the Chicago Bears, Buffalo Bills, and Steelers in Weeks 14 through 16 and then 67.3% of the time in the finale versus the Cincinnati Bengals. He appeared in every game last season, plus all three contests this year. However, he has had zero offensive snaps this season. Brailsford was a high school standout and was named First Team Arizona 5A All-State and a state champion in football. He has a history of being prepared in the game and also in life. It’s what most centers are made of. His feet never stop moving, and he is able to handle twist moves and delayed blitzes. Although he had a terrific camp and was mentioned by several media outlets as perhaps the best center, he doesn’t have any actual NFL game experience. Brailsford has been listed as inactive in each of the three contests so far. Which means he hasn’t been able to line up on special teams coverage teams or block on punts and field goals. He hasn’t tasted anything related to a real game. If Wypler is the new center, certainly the coaching staff will activate Brailsford as his backup for the Pittsburgh game. Regardless, losing Jenkins will become a huge hole. This offensive line has come a very long way and is just getting to form some consistency and build a cohesive unit. Now, this. Plus, Jenkins has really melded with QB Deshaun Watson in this new offense. Because of the short turnaround from Sunday’s game to the Thursday night event, the Browns practiced a walkthrough on Monday, and Jenkins was listed as DNP (did not participate). The protocol parameters are pretty stiff in the NFL. It will be almost impossible for Jenkins to clear the mandatory concussion protocol in time. title: Browns TE Harold Fannin Jr. continues on a strong trajectory
summary: Harold Fannin Jr. has been an important player to watch on the Cleveland Browns’ offense to start the season, and his impressive performance streak continued against the Carolina Panthers. In the Browns’ 21-18 win over the Panthers, Fannin Jr. recorded seven receptions for 51 yards and two touchdowns. It was another great showing that continued to show his role on […]
full_text: Harold Fannin Jr. has been an important player to watch on the Cleveland Browns’ offense to start the season, and his impressive performance streak continued against the Carolina Panthers. In the Browns’ 21-18 win over the Panthers, Fannin Jr. recorded seven receptions for 51 yards and two touchdowns. It was another great showing that continued to show his role on this Cleveland offense. One of Fannin Jr.’s touchdowns came during a crucial fourth-quarter drive, further showing that the moment is never too big for him. He contributed when it mattered most. It is highly likely that the Browns will find themselves in similar situations throughout the rest of the season. There will be close games and moments where the offense has to find a way to make a play. Fannin Jr. establishing himself as a reliable tight end and pass catcher could be the difference in some of these one-score games. After a rookie season where he had 72 receptions, 731 yards, and six touchdowns, all team highs, Fannin saw additions to the Browns passing game in KC Concepcion and Denzel Boston . The second-year tight end may not get over 100 targets this year, but his value to the team will continue to rise, as we saw in Week 3. It is still very early in the season, and there is a lot of football left to be played, so Fannin’s contributions could definitely change. These early weeks have been very promising, though, for the connection between him and quarterback Deshaun Watson . title: Cowboys news: Brian Schottenheimer takes the blame for Week 3 loss
summary: After Sunday’s loss to the Baltimore Ravens, head coach Brian Schottenheimer faced criticism for controversial calls in the last 28 seconds of the game. From a strange third-down throwaway pass in scoring position to a kickoff out of the endzone that left the defense exposed and set up the Ravens’ win, Schottenheimer addressed it all […]
full_text: Photo by MAURO PIMENTEL / AFP via Getty Images | AFP via Getty Images After Sunday’s loss to the Baltimore Ravens, head coach Brian Schottenheimer faced criticism for controversial calls in the last 28 seconds of the game. From a strange third-down throwaway pass in scoring position to a kickoff out of the endzone that left the defense exposed and set up the Ravens’ win, Schottenheimer addressed it all during his Tuesday press conference. Brian Schottenheimer takes responsibility for loss to Ravens: ‘I deserve the criticism’ – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Credit to the Dallas Cowboys head coach for not shying away from the criticism. “I didn’t do very good in the last 28 seconds,” Schottenheimer said. “I think when you talk about finishing the game, which I really think you look at our two games that we’ve lost, we haven’t finished. And that was a big part of this one…” “My dad had a rule: One play at a time. Because it happened to him. He made a decision on a play, it didn’t go good, he was pissed off about it, and it affected another decision. And I think that’s kind of what happened to me. So, I’ll take accountability for it. It’s football and life. It’s what happens. But I hurt our chance to win that game. I’ll be better, I’m better than that. I’m better than I performed in the last 28 seconds.” Cowboys Injury Roundup: Key Dallas defenders to miss multiple weeks – Patrik Walker, DallasCowboys.com The Cowboys will take the field against the Houston Texans without a few more defensive starters due to injury. Their narrow loss to the Baltimore Ravens in Rio also came with additional injuries to the group, highlighted by Jonathan Bullard, Jalen Thompson and Shavon Revel. This all comes only one week after losing Cobie Durant and being forced to place P.J. Locke on injured reserve, and even that came just seven days after seeing Malik Hooker and DeMarvion Overshown go down in the season opener with a fractured forearm and hamstring injury, respectively. Dallas Cowboys expected to add two DBs as injury concerns mount in the secondary – Joseph Hoyt, Dallas Morning News With injuries mounting in the secondary, Dallas added a few free agents. Through three weeks, the Cowboys only have two of the five starters they had on opening day left in their secondary: cornerback DaRon Bland and first-round defensive back Caleb Downs. The Cowboys are expected to add two defensive backs in the wake of those injuries, people familiar with the situation told The Dallas Morning News : cornerback Alex Austin and former Cowboys safety Juanyeh Thomas. Jerry Jones says ‘there’s conversations going on’ for potential additions to Cowboys roster – Tommy Yarrish, DallasCowboys.com Despite the 1-2 start, Jerry Jones still feels confident the Cowboys could make a move to improve their team in the here and now. “I’d just say we’re right on top of it,” Jones said. “We’re very aware of the moving parts out here, we should be. And communication is a big part of that. It’s a big part of that. Communication at all levels, at my level, at Stephen’s level, and the scout’s level. We all have contacts, and this is a time when you really can have discussions that could be productive. The answer to your question is yes, there’s conversations going on.” Column: The Dallas Cowboys’ season faces a crucial October stretch – Nick Harris, Fort Worth Star-Telegram There’s no question October will be an important month for the Cowboys given their start to the season. Coming into the season, you could have easily pinned each of the next four opponents as playoff contenders in their respective conferences. Houston, Green Bay and Philadelphia were all playoff teams a year ago, and Tampa Bay lost the NFC South playoff spot in Week 18. title: Cowboys signing safety Juanyeh Thomas
summary: The Dallas Cowboys are depleted at the safety position with Malik Hooker nursing a fracture in his forearm that may need another week. Also, P.J. Locke is on injured reserve with a foot injury and Jalen Thompson will head there shortly due to a hamstring injury that’s expected to keep him out for 4-6 weeks. […]
full_text: Photo by Logan Bowles/Getty Images The Dallas Cowboys are depleted at the safety position with Malik Hooker nursing a fracture in his forearm that may need another week. Also, P.J. Locke is on injured reserve with a foot injury and Jalen Thompson will head there shortly due to a hamstring injury that’s expected to keep him out for 4-6 weeks. In light of this, the Cowboys have signed Juanyeh Thomas after a workout on Tuesday. This is his second stint with the team. Sources: The #Cowboys are signing S Juanyeh Thomas, bringing him back to where his NFL career began. Thomas joined Dallas as an undrafted free agent and played in 36 games from 2022-2025, recording 62 tackles, 5 PBUs and 1 forced fumble. https://t.co/A5JQSvHGfS pic.twitter.com/qtkHCLQ9xp — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 29, 2026 Thomas went undrafted in 2022 out of Georgia Tech before he was signed by the Cowboys. He was unable to make the final roster, but Thomas did make the practice squad for the season. In January, of 2023, he signed a reserve/future contract. He then made the final roster that year after performing well in the preseason. Thomas logged 190 snaps on defense with one start and registered 22 tackles and four pass breakups in 16 games. In 2024, Thomas saw action in 13 games and tallied 14 tackles, one pass breakup, and one forced fumble in 94 snaps. He saw his most action last season as he played 266 snaps in seven games with three starts as he amassed 26 total tackles. Unfortunately, he was placed on the reserve/non-football illnes list last November due to chronic migraine headaches that affected his vision. Thomas was also a huge contributor on special teams with 706 snaps logged from 2023 to 2025. Dallas decided not to tender Thomas as a restricted free agent during the offseason. As a result, be signed a one-year deal worth $1.3 million with the Indianapolis Colts back in March. He would be released in August because of migraine issues in training camp. The Cowboys needed some bodies at safety as they were down to Markquese Bell and Alijah Clark. Thomas provides a veteran presence with experience playing significant snaps. It remains to be seen what he’ll contribute in 2026, but he’s certainly a valuable piece to have with the injuries at safety in Dallas.

title: 3 trades Cowboys should consider after injury bug hits their secondary
summary: Injuries were starting to become a concern prior to the Dallas Cowboys trip to Brazil. They are even more so now heading into Week 4 to take on their interstate rival, the Houston Texans. It was recently announced safety Jalen Thompson, defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, and cornerback Shavon Revel are expected to miss multiple weeks […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - DECEMBER 29: Jessie Bates III #3 of the Atlanta Falcons looks on against the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium on December 29, 2024 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Timothy Nwachukwu/Getty Images) | Getty Images Injuries were starting to become a concern prior to the Dallas Cowboys trip to Brazil. They are even more so now heading into Week 4 to take on their interstate rival, the Houston Texans. It was recently announced safety Jalen Thompson, defensive tackle Jonathan Bullard, and cornerback Shavon Revel are expected to miss multiple weeks with injuries, which will severely deplete Dallas’ defensive depth even more. Here’s a list of the Cowboys current injured players on defense: LB DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring, multiple weeks) CB Cobie Durant (hamstring, multiple weeks) S P.J. Locke (foot, IR) S Malika Hooker (forearm, multiple weeks) S Jalen Thompson (hamstring, IR?) DT Jonathan Bullard (calf, multiple weeks) CB Shavon Revel Jr. (knee, multiple weeks?) LB Marist Luifau (hand, IR) That’s eight defensive players who were expected to play a role the Cowboys will have to find a way to replace for multiple weeks. And to make matters worse, more than half of them are in the secondary. As a result, Dallas is running out of bodies to deploy at both safety and cornerback. It’s no wonder they were one of the teams joining an interest in training for Pittsburgh Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. last week prior to their trip to Brazil. He’d be an immediate upgrade at CB, but Jerry Jones is going to pay a hefty price, both in draft capital and in a long-term extension, to bring this trade to fruition. Instead of trying to pull of a blockbuster trade to land Joey Porter Jr., the could target some more cost effective players to acquire via trade to help their injury decimated secondary. Below are three options they should kick the tires on. CB Kris Abrams-Draine, Denver Broncos Abrams-Draine is currently buried on the depth chart in Denver and only has three starts under his belt in two years in the league. Despite that, the former 2024 fifth-round pick has shown starting ability when given the opportunity and could immediately help the Cowboys depth issues at CB if acquired via trade. He still has the remaining of this year and next season playing on his rookie contract and shouldn’t cost more than a future Day 3 draft pick. CB Nahshon Wright, New York Jets Reuniting with Wright could be a win-win for everyone. He was a former third-round pick by the Cowboys in 2021 and before being traded to the Minnesota Vikings for Andrew Booth in 2024. After his brief stint in Minnesota, he signed a one-year deal with the Chicago Bears where he had a Pro Bowl season with five INT’s. He’s now with the New York Jets on a one-year, $5.5 million deal, but has been a healthy scratch so far this year. A future Day 3 draft pick could land him as well. S Jessie Bates III, Atlanta Falcons Bates has been one of the better ball-hawk safeties in the league for years now. It’s rumored he could be available for trade and Bleacher Report has his current value as a future fourth-round pick. He would be the most costly option on this list, but also is the only one with years of starting experience in the league. It probably wouldn’t take them as long to get up to speed on Christian Parker’s scheme, making him the most plug-and-play trade target.
