title: Detroit Lions facing crossroads with Cade Mays, Juice Scruggs
summary: Through three weeks of the season, Detroit Lions backup center Juice Scruggs has been one of the better NFL players at the pivot. Scruggs’ PFF grade of 71.5 current ranks fourth among all NFL centers, and Scruggs ability to be a force in the run game (78.7 run defense grade, second-best) has helped Detroit regain […]
full_text: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-SEPTEMBER 27: Quarterback Jared Goff #16 and center Juice Scruggs #70 of the Detroit Lions during the second half of an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Jorge Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images Through three weeks of the season, Detroit Lions backup center Juice Scruggs has been one of the better NFL players at the pivot. Scruggs’ PFF grade of 71.5 current ranks fourth among all NFL centers, and Scruggs ability to be a force in the run game (78.7 run defense grade, second-best) has helped Detroit regain some of the rushing efficiency that was lost last season. The Lions currently rank sixth in rushing success rate (48.2%) per NFL Pro and fourth in average yards before contact per carry (2.06). During his weekly radio appearance on 97.1 The Ticket, Detroit Lions coach Dan Campbell had high praise for how Scruggs has played so far. “He really fits us,” Campbell said. “He’s a pro. Man, he’s high energy. He’s the same guy every day. He busts his tail, and he’s getting better. He’s getting better for us at the center position. So, man, he’s a good fit for us.” This offseason, the Lions acquired Scruggs in a trade that sent David Montgomery to the Houston Texans. At that point, Scruggs was in line to be a top reserve at both the center and guard positions. But after Cade Mays suffered a broken wrist early in training camp, Scruggs was pulled out of the competition for starting left guard and plugged in as the starting center. However, the Lions are nearing an interesting crossroads with Scruggs. Lions coach Dan Campbell gave an update on Mays’ recovery from the wrist injury, and it sounds like he could return to the team somewhere around their Week 6 bye. “Right now, we’re kinda hoping around the bye, somewhere in there,” Campbell told 97.1 The Ticket on Tuesday morning. “Before or after the bye with him, but he’s doing a great job. He really is.” That begs the question: what do you do with Scruggs when Mays is healthy and ready to go? The Lions gave Mays a three-year, $25 million contract to be their center for the next few years, so it seems unlikely Detroit would keep him sidelined. But if Scruggs is still playing well, it would be hard to bench him, too. Campbell was asked by radio host Jon Jansen if Scruggs would re-enter the competition at left guard to potentially start there, and the Lions’ coach offered a brief and powerful answer. “Absolutely.” Campbell was not asked if he would consider keeping Scruggs as the starting center. Right now, the starting left guard position is being held by Christian Mahogany, but he was in tight competition with Ben Bartch before a foot injury sidelined Bartch recently. Campbell praised how Mahogany played against the Jets. “I thought he had a winning performance,” Campbell said. “I thought he played good enough for us to win. I thought he ran off the football. I thought he was violent, played a physical game. There’s a couple of these little things he had got his feet out of whack that he’s got to clean up, just staying honed in on the technique of it. But, that’s it, man. Just the consistency.” The majority of Scruggs’ experience in his three previous seasons in the NFL has been at the guard position, but in 2024, he started eight games at center and produced 64.5 PFF grade, good for 19th out of 38 qualifying centers over that span. He also started 13 games at center in his final year at Penn State in 2022. Mays is not eligible to come off of injured reserve until after this week’s game against the Carolina Panthers. After that, we’ll have to see how Detroit opts to shake out the rest of their offensive line.

title: Joey Porter Jr. trade: Weighing the pros, cons of Detroit Lions making the move
summary: Rumors have been swirling for weeks, but the Joey Porter Jr. trade speculation peaked on Sunday when several national reporters said the Detroit Lions were among a “handful of teams” who have reached out to the Pittsburgh Steelers inquiring about the availability of the 26-year-old cornerback. Per the same reports, the Steelers are open to […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - OCTOBER 12: Joey Porter Jr. #24 of the Pittsburgh Steelers breaks up a pass during the fourth quarter in the NFL 2025 game against the Cleveland Browns at Acrisure Stadium on October 12, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Lauren Leigh Bacho/Getty Images) | Getty Images Rumors have been swirling for weeks, but the Joey Porter Jr. trade speculation peaked on Sunday when several national reporters said the Detroit Lions were among a “handful of teams” who have reached out to the Pittsburgh Steelers inquiring about the availability of the 26-year-old cornerback . Per the same reports, the Steelers are open to listening to offers but “would want a strong compensation package”—which is vague and obvious. At the tail end of this week’s Lions vs. Jets recap PODcast, our crew discussed the pros and cons of the Lions making such a move. Sunday’s game reminded us again that Detroit’s outside cornerbacks are currently a liability. Even their CB1, D.J. Reed, has struggled through the first few weeks of the season. Beyond that, the Lions are still tinkering with their best option at second outside cornerback. Is it Rock Ya-Sin, who was strong last year but was effectively benched in Week 3? Is it Roger McCreary, who has flashed at both outside and nickel, but also struggled against the Jets? Or is it Ennis Rakestraw, who looked very solid in a small situational role on Sunday and doesn’t have a ton of experience? If there are that many questions at cornerback, doesn’t Porter provide some answers? But adding talent isn’t just a matter of whether the player will help the team or not. Porter would undeniably improve Detroit’s defense. The cost, however, is something that the Lions will have to deeply grapple with. It’s unclear right now how much Porter would cost, but on the PODcast, we go through some recent cornerback trades to gauge the market. And that’s only half of the conversation about trading for Porter. The Steelers cornerback is also seeking a contract extension as he currently rides out the final year of his rookie deal. Would Porter be willing to play out the final year without an extension in Detroit? That’s unclear, but the Lions will have to seriously consider inking him to a long-term deal if they acquire him, and the team has been doing a delicate salary cap balancing act for the last couple of years now that they have some top-end market deals on the books. If Detroit trades and signs for Porter, how much will that disrupt their current plans for 2026 and beyond? Will it cost them their ability to re-sign some of their players, or can they cook the books enough to make this happen without jeopardizing their future? There are two more facets of this potential trade to consider: First, how good is Porter? Fans tend to get stuck on one or two players and romanticize them without considering their weaknesses. Will Porter be able to come in and immediately play like a CB1? Another thing to consider is whether Lions general manager Brad Holmes would even do it. While he’s made in-season trades before, he has never added a young, long-term piece and extended them before they’ve even played a down in Detroit. This would mark a pretty big break from Holmes’ reputation, but is it finally time for him to adjust his strategy? We discuss the entire topic below on this week’s PODcast. title: Discussion: Rank the NFC North after 3 weeks of the 2026 season
summary: We’re three weeks in the 2026 NFL season, and we’re starting to figure out a lot about teams. Though sample sizes are still pretty small, and it’s hard to fully judge a team when we don’t really know too much about the opponents they’ve played. So any sort of sweeping judgments should be avoided. But… […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 20: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings and head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears meet on the field following the game at Soldier Field on September 20, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Geoff Stellfox/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’re three weeks in the 2026 NFL season, and we’re starting to figure out a lot about teams. Though sample sizes are still pretty small, and it’s hard to fully judge a team when we don’t really know too much about the opponents they’ve played. So any sort of sweeping judgments should be avoided. But… the NFL news cycle is 24/7, and there’s nothing wrong with a little analysis after one-sixth of the season is through. Yes, teams will continue to get better or worse. Yes, injuries will continue to alter the trajectory of each team. But why not have a little fun before we get too deep into the season? The NFC North standings are probably a little surprising to most, although it certainly isn’t a shock to see that three of the four teams are sporting a winning record. As a reminder, here’s how things look after Week 3: Minnesota Vikings: 3-0 Detroit Lions: 2-1 Chicago Bears: 2-1 Green Bay Packers: 1-2 So today’s Question of the Day is: How would you rank the NFC North after three weeks of the season? My answer: Let’s start with something I think almost everyone can agree on right now: the Packers look definitively like the worst team in the division. They are a somewhat miraculous comeback away from starting the season 0-3, and their drubbing at the hands of the Atlanta Falcons on Thursday was embarrassing on all levels. Their offense (23rd in points scored) is broken, with an offensive line that is being held together by scotch tape. Their defense (29th) may somehow be worse. They aren’t only the worst team in the division right now, they have a solid argument for a bottom five team in football. That could change if they get some things figured out on offense, but it looks bad right now. Note: they are 30th in DVOA. The other three teams are difficult to rank. The Vikings have the best record because of their insane defense (first in DVOA, second in points allowed). However, their offense remains pretty stagnant (30th in DVOA, 17th in points scored). The Bears are coming off a very impressive win over the Eagles on Monday night, but we can’t forget how much the Vikings humbled them at home in Week 2—holding them to just three points. The Lions have one of the most efficient offenses in football (third in scoring, eighth in DVOA), but their defense is a massive liability right now (32nd in scoring, 28th in DVOA). The only thing that is clear to me is that you have to put the Vikings ahead of the Bears because of the head-to-head win. That leaves the Bears and the Lions, and I think both teams are in similar boats. Their offenses are going to be awesome and reliable this year, but they’ve got serious questions about their defense. Honestly, though, I trust the Bears’ defense a little more, because of their consistent ability to force turnovers. So my ranking right now would be: Vikings Bears Lions Packers How would you rank the four NFC North teams after three weeks? Share your thoughts in the comment section below by joining our community. summary: Now that there have been three weeks of NFL action in the books, let’s take a look at what national media outlets think of this year’s Green Bay Packers team. Obviously, we all expected more from the Packers this year, as the team has gone 1-2 during their “easy” stretch of the schedule, and Green […]
full_text: Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images | Getty Images Now that there have been three weeks of NFL action in the books, let’s take a look at what national media outlets think of this year’s Green Bay Packers team. Obviously, we all expected more from the Packers this year, as the team has gone 1-2 during their “easy” stretch of the schedule, and Green Bay hasn’t won a game in regulation since December 7th. But how bad has the Packers’ stock fallen? Here’s how 11 analysts ranked Green Bay in the broader scope of the NFL. Green Bay Packers power rankings ESPN: #20 Bleacher Report: #22 CBS Sports: #22 Sports Illustrated : #22 The Score: #23 NBC Sports: #25 Yahoo! Sports: #25 FOX Sports: #26 USA Today : #26 The Athletic: #27 NFL.com: #28 The average analyst has the Packers ranked around 24th, right on the borderline of the team being a bottom-quarter club in the NFL going into Week 4. Not great! I am getting asked about the Packers cap situation for 2027 a lot right now. Here is a quick update. ✅Yes – Includes: Rollover, Cap Increase, Adjustments, ERFA Tenders, PS Futures, PPE Raises, Draft, In-Season Reserves 🚫No – Does Not Include: Restructures, Extensions,… pic.twitter.com/ngbat1lShV — Ken – Packers Cap (@KenIngalls) September 29, 2026 Considering the Packers’ cap situation moving forward (in short, the money is spent), they really need to figure it out with this roster. Will they do it? We’ll see! For what it’s worth, here’s what ESPN, which had the Packers ranked the highest in the league at 20th, had to say about Green Bay: Coming off last season’s torn ACL, Kraft was ninth among tight ends in our draft rankings. Through three games, he’s 27th in fantasy points at the position. Kraft has just nine catches for 108 yards and no touchdowns despite not being on a snap limit. As bad as the Packers’ offensive line has been, the Packers still rank tied for fourth in the NFL in passing yards per game. But Kraft has not been a big part of that. — Rob Demovsky I’m not sure that Tucker Kraft looks fully healthy right now. Before he went down last season, Kraft’s yards-after-catch ability was what the Packers hung their hat on against split-safety coverages, as they also struggled to run then (though not to the extent that they are right now). If they could get Kraft going, that would be great. Anything will help right now. The Packers’ lowest ranking this week came from the league’s website, which only had them ahead of the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (their Week 4 opponent), Miami Dolphins, New England Patriots and Tennessee Titans. Yes, they were ranked behind two winless teams, the Los Angeles Chargers and Houston Texans. Matt LaFleur accurately summarized Thursday’s 21-point loss to Atlanta in the postgame interview, calling it a “humbling night.” Green Bay’s offense lacks a running game and is putting too much on the shoulders of Jordan Love, and the defense’s inability to tackle effectively doomed the Packers in their second defeat. It’s fair to say they could easily be 0-3 right now, and I’m not sure where they go from here. If these issues persist against the Buccaneers in Week 4, we’ll be entering crisis territory. If they lose to the Buccaneers, it’s going to be a riot for the Packers-Bears game in Week 5, which has already been flexed to noon local . Green Bay is set to debut their new alternative uniforms in honor of the team’s shareholders for that game. Spoiler: The shareholders won’t be too happy if they start the season 1-3.

title: The Packers’ running game is historically bad
summary: We’ve talked about the offensive line ad nauseum (Latin for “until it makes you barf on your pants”) here at Acme Packing Company, and every statistic we dig up is more ad nauseating than the last. I’ve mostly been focused on the passing game because I will be sad if Jordan Love dies or becomes […]
full_text: SAN FRANCISCO, CA - NOVEMBER 19: Running back Herman Fontenot #27 of the Green Bay Packers runs behind a block from teammate Blair Bush #51 during a game against the San Francisco 49ers at Candlestick Park on November 19, 1989 in San Francisco, California. The Packers won 21-17 (Photo by George Rose/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve talked about the offensive line ad nauseum (Latin for “until it makes you barf on your pants”) here at Acme Packing Company, and every statistic we dig up is more ad nauseating than the last. I’ve mostly been focused on the passing game because I will be sad if Jordan Love dies or becomes David Carr, but we should pay some attention to the running game as well. The Packers have as of this moment gained 146 rushing yards in their three games this season , which is the third-lowest total over any three game streak for the Packers since the merger . In fact, since the merger, the Packers have had only five spans of three games where they gained less than 150 rushing yards. It’s really four because two of those streaks from the 1990 season overlap, but still, it’s very bad. The most recent streak prior to this one was in 2006 when the Packer rushing attacked gained 47 yards on the ground against the Vikings, 44 yards against the Tom Brady Patriots in a 35-0 shellacking where Brett Favre was knocked out and replaced by a young Aaron Rodgers, and 51 yards against the Seahawks for a total of 142 yards. The worst such streak occurred in 1990 among a time of desperation when Don Majkowski was not playing, and all of the terrible Packer running backs from the original Nintendo Tecmo Super Bowl were on the team. The streak, in which the Packers rushed for 127 yards over a three-game span, began on December 2nd in a 23-7 loss to the Vikings in an epic Anthony Dilweg versus Rich Gannon/Herschel Walker matchup . For the Packers, first-round pick (19th overall) Darrell Thompson gained 17 yards on three carries (not bad!), Herman Fontenot gained 15 yards also on three carries (also not bad!), Plan B Free Agent acquisition Michael Haddix gained 10 yards on 6 carries (bad, and confusing!), and Keith Woodside gained six yards on 1 carry. Dilweg chipped in 11 yards on scrambles for a total of 59 yards. Why did Michael Haddix out-carry everyone else? Why did Anthony Dilweg attempt 29 passes in a game that was 6-0 at half time? Who knows, the Lindy Infante Packers were wild. The Packers next dropped a 20-14 game against the Seattle Seahawks , who got 157 yards rushing from Derrick Fenner and John Williams on 33 carries. Countering the Seahawks’ attack, Haddix carried 4 times for 10 yards, Darrell Thompson chipped in 1 carry for 1 yard, and Mr. Woodside, took three carries for -3 yards. Quarterbacks (never a good sign when plural) Anthony Dilweg and Blair Kiel combined for 5 yards on the ground for a grand total of 13 yards on 10 carries. And finally, the following week, the Packers lost 31-0 to Randall Cunningham and the Eagles . Did Randall outrush the entire Packer team? You bet! Did the Packers play two quarterbacks again? Also yes, as Kiel and Dilweg combined for 4 rushing yards. Also contributing were Michael Haddix who broke out with a robust 31 yards on 7 carries, while Darrell Thompson gained 9 yards on 6 carries. Herman Fontenot lost 7 yards on his one carry, and speedy white receiver Jeff Query took some kind of end around nonsense for a huge 18-yard gain. All told, the Packers gained 55 yards on the ground. So basically, the current level of Packer futility running the ball is on par with an era where the Packers were splitting time with two backup quarterbacks and also between four running backs. It is really bad, and while I gave the 1990 Packers guff for relying so much on Michael Haddix, I would genuinely prefer Michael Haddix to Marshawn Lloyd, even though he’s 64 years old and holds the NFL record for fewest yards per carry for a player with at least 500 carries (really!) . Hopefully the new offensive line acquisitions this week matter, but the running backs were almost as bad and could stand some turnover as well.

title: Packers-Bears game in Week 5 flexed to Noon Central kickoff
summary: When the NFL released its 2026 regular season schedule, one of the premier games on the docket was in Week 5 when the Green Bay Packers host the Chicago Bears. With the two teams splitting the 2025 regular season series and playing a thriller in the Wild Card round, FOX chose to make the first […]
full_text: GREEN BAY, WI - DECEMBER 07: Teams wait for the ball to be snapped during a game between the Green Bay Packers and the Chicago Bears on December 7, 2025 at Lambeau Field, in Green Bay, WI. (Photo by Larry Radloff/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images When the NFL released its 2026 regular season schedule, one of the premier games on the docket was in Week 5 when the Green Bay Packers host the Chicago Bears. With the two teams splitting the 2025 regular season series and playing a thriller in the Wild Card round, FOX chose to make the first of the two matchups between the NFL’s oldest rivals one of the network’s priorities, claiming it for the late afternoon “Game of the Week” timeslot at 3:25 PM Central time. Through three weeks, however, that decision appears to have backfired. The Packers have stumbled to a 1-2 record, barely eking out their sole win in overtime against the New York Jets, while the Bears will not have the services of starting quarterback Caleb Williams for a few more weeks as he works through a hamstring strain. That backfire is now fully complete, as the NFL has flexed that Packers-Bears game out of the late afternoon time slot and into the early afternoon. Kickoff for the game at Lambeau Field will now be at 12:00 Noon Central Time, leaving FOX with a more desirable 49ers-Seahawks matchup to send out to a national audience as the late game. This also means that the Packers’ new “Rivalries” uniforms will get a much smaller viewership. This is the game when the team is scheduled wear those uniforms for the first time , while the Bears will debut theirs in the rematch at Soldier Field on Christmas Day. Moving this game also makes this only the second time in over 20 years that both Packers-Bears games will kick off at Noon Central, though the holiday rematch will still get a national broadcast. That oddity also happened in 2024 — though the teams’ week 18 time slot was not set until the very end of the season — but had not been the case prior to that since 2004, a year that also featured a season-ending matchup.

title: Green Bay Packers News: Brian Gutekunst makes an attempt to fix offensive line
summary: Offensive line? Yeah, consider that fixed. The Packers have signed not one (Cordell Volson), not two (Laken Tomlinson), but three (Mekhi Becton) linemen that nobody else wanted to put on their 53-man roster. Checkmate, everybody else. Contender status has been restored in Green Bay. Color me underwhelmed by the Packers’ sudden urgent desire to fix […]
full_text: FOXBOROUGH, MASSACHUSETTS - JANUARY 11: Mekhi Becton #73 of the Los Angeles Chargers looks on during the national anthem prior to an NFL wild card playoff game against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium on January 11, 2026 in Foxborough, Massachusetts. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Offensive line? Yeah, consider that fixed. The Packers have signed not one (Cordell Volson), not two (Laken Tomlinson), but three (Mekhi Becton) linemen that nobody else wanted to put on their 53-man roster. Checkmate, everybody else. Contender status has been restored in Green Bay. Color me underwhelmed by the Packers’ sudden urgent desire to fix their offensive line. Though Brian Gutekunst has seemingly answered fans’ pleas to add to the offensive line, we should have healthy skepticism about any lineman available in late September. The last few seasons of NFL football have shown the world the value of a good offensive line (and the Packers have shown what can happen with a bad one, for that matter), and I don’t think anybody’s just letting good prospects sit at home on their couch when they play a position as important as we understand the line to be. Still, at least they’re doing something, right? The Packers’ trio of offensive line acquisitions are all former starters. Not all of their previous work is good, mind you, and Tomlinson in particular is well into the “journeyman” phase of his career, though he was once a Pro Bowl caliber player. They may be limited now, but each of them has a more impressive resume than anyone the Packers have put on the field at guard to this point. Even if Tomlinson’s Pro Bowl came when Donovan Jennings still had two seasons of college ball to go, he’s a far sight more accomplished than his younger counterpart. It boils down to this: at least they’re doing something. Is it too little too late? Quite possibly, even probably. But at least it’s something, and if it makes the Packers more watchable for the rest of the season, they’ll have accomplished something. Packers working on offensive line from different angles | Packers.com I like this approach much better than the “don’t work on the offensive line at all” idea they went with for the first three weeks. Can Mekhi Becton and other veterans signings save Packers offensive line? | Packers Wire Even if the answer here is “probably not,” trying something is better than not trying anything. Matt LaFleur believes Packers offense needs to deliver more ‘body blows’ | Packers News ($) If the Packers can figure out a way to grind out a few yards on the ground, it could open things up for the rest of the offense. Packers-Buccaneers Matchups: Both Teams Have Huge Advantages | Sports Illustrated I don’t want to hear about any advantages the Buccaneers have. How active NFL players continue to redefine all-time sack list | ESPN This article makes a big deal about how Myles Garrett has averaged 14 sacks a year for the last five seasons, but it doesn’t really focus much on how he’d have to keep up that pace for more than five more seasons to break the all-time sack record, and he’d be 37 by the time he does it. California duo set Lego World Map record in under 5 hours | UPI I like a good Lego as much as the next guy, but this is pretty intense. title: Houston Texans Opening Odds vs Dallas Cowboys
summary: The Texas-sized showdown of the Houston Texans (0-3) against the Dallas Cowboys (1-2) is more exciting on paper than in reality. These two teams have struggled out of the gate and are desperate to turn their seasons around in Week 4. FanDuel has you covered whether you’re from Texas or just looking for some additional […]
full_text: The Texas-sized showdown of the Houston Texans (0-3) against the Dallas Cowboys (1-2) is more exciting on paper than in reality. These two teams have struggled out of the gate and are desperate to turn their seasons around in Week 4. FanDuel has you covered whether you’re from Texas or just looking for some additional action this weekend. Below are the Spread, Moneyline, and Over/Under heading into the game against Dallas. The Spread: Texans -2.5 Considering the Texans are 0-3 and haven’t looked competent on offense since the first half of the first game of the season, this is an astonishing line. I cannot imagine Reliant Stadium will be rocking. If anything, this could be a stadium quick to turn on the team if they fall behind. The Cowboys, though 1-2 entering the contest, have scored 20, 37, and 31 points. Houston hasn’t proved it can move the ball against even the weakest of defenses, as seen against the Colts, which doesn’t bode well against a high-powered offense. Until the Texans win a game, take the opponent and the extra points for insurance. Moneyline: Texans -136 The Texans are 3-4 all time against the Cowboys. Given their recent struggles and lack of anything expected to change, It’s hard to believe the Texans can steal a win against the Cowboys. DeMeco Ryans on his coaching impact & if they have any plans to make changes on the offensive side of the ball including Nick Caley calling plays: “Nope my impact is just fine.” “Nope, we’re all in this thing together.” pic.twitter.com/a2AIzDvfbA — Houston Stressans (@TexansCommenter) September 28, 2026 What will be interesting to watch is if the defense can keep a lid on the Cowboys passing attack. Derek Stingley Jr. and Kamari Lassiter have not impressed and are concerning when paired up against CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. At this juncture in the seasons, it’s difficult to believe the Texans will outright beat an opponent. Wait till they are, hopefully, on a role before taking them straight up. Over/Under: 47.5 The Texans went well under last week’s line of 44.5 against the Colts as well as the 45.5 mark against the Bengals, but managed to blow out the Over/Under against the Bills in a high-scoring matchup. This Over/Under is a tad elevated compared to the two previous lines, most likely due to the high-octane offense in Dallas. That said, Houston’s current offensive form doesn’t bode well to betting the over. If Nico Collins is back in the lineup, then the over is something to consider. Collins’ presence unlocks the passing game and lessens the pressure on the run. The Cowboys defense have allowed a bevy of points thus far. They’ve given up 28, 20, and 34 points in their three matchups. Given how porous their defense has been AND if Nico Collins is set to go Sunday, then take the Over in a competitive and integral matchup between two teams vying to keep their seasons alive early in the 2026 campaign.

title: The Day After the Day After: Houston Texans fall 19-17 to the Indianapolis Colts
summary: The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 3: Is Ed Ingram that critical to the O-line? Nico Collins’ absence the past two games […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Keenan Allen #10 of the Indianapolis Colts reacts after catching the ball for a first down during the first half of the game against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Day After the Day After…when the raw, immediate emotions from the aftermath of a game diminish into the realm of clarity and the proverbial (or literal) hangover no longer haunts the mind. With that, a review of Week 3: Is Ed Ingram that critical to the O-line? Nico Collins’ absence the past two games is undeniable, as Stroud is sans his biggest weapon/security blanket, especially in the red zone. Yet, maybe a bigger loss is Ed Ingram. Also out these past two games, the right side of the line has been mediocre at best and beyond horrid at worst. The big 4th down stuffs in the past two games came from defensive penetration along the right interior of the line on short-yardage run plays. Ingram is not the best pass blocking guard out there (reference how badly he got beat against Buffalo on that final drive of the game), but the Texans did have success running the ball that game. Maybe it was Buffalo’s defense, but Houston rushed for 124 total yards in that game on 32 rushes. Houston has totaled only 130 yards on 30 rushes in the two games since he went out. He might return next week, but groin injuries can be a bit difficult to project. The Final Minutes (again): The difference between victory and defeat is incredibly small in the NFL. The Texans could feel justified in thinking they should be 2-1 vs. 0-3. However, it was actions or inactions in the final minutes that doomed the Texans (again). After going up 17-16 on Marks’ short TD run, the Colts had more than enough time to get into range for the go-ahead FG. Being indoors, they probably wouldn’t need much in total yardage. They got one bonus when Fairbairn could not land his kick short of the end zone. It was close, but the Colts’ returner caught the ball with enough of his body still in the end zone. Thus, the Colts started at the 35. Then, the defense, which had played its best game of the season to date, gave up a 20-yard gain that put the Colts right in FG range. With around a minute left in the game, Houston having all 3 timeouts and the Colts going a bit conservative, Ryans curiously decided to hold on to those, eschewing taking a timeout until 29 seconds left. Ryans seemed to hope for a big defensive stop (not as likely at this point) or a FG miss (not as likely either). Perhaps he takes the timeouts and the Colts still move the ball, but he did his mercurial offense no favors by reducing their possession time. Then the Colts forced Houston to return a kickoff, killing more time. Houston did have the timeout and moved the ball to midfield, but subsequent play-calling and the Colts’ defense limited Houston to a Hail Mary attempt. Much like the Buffalo, Houston had its chances to win at the end, but it didn’t happen on this day….again. Kickoffs…still a work in progress for Houston: Fairbairn is still more prone to kick the ball to the end-zone, generating touchbacks that gives offenses the ball at the 35. If he could get the ball to fall within the landing zone, that increases the chances that Houston could pin opponents further back. Then again, Houston’s kick coverages haven’t been as stellar as in years past. Concurrently, a Houston’s returner had an awkward situation in the first half when he allowed a kick to bounce in the landing zone, but then corralled the ball to take a knee in the end zone. Houston only got the ball at the 20 for that, which did not help the offense. These are small things, but it is small things adding up to the 0-3 start. The Critical Play: 1st Quarter, 9:47, HOU Ball, 4th and 1 at the IND 31 (Montgomery rush to the right for no gain) Another 4th and short inside the opponent’s territory. This coming after Will Anderson Jr. gave Houston its first forced turnover inside Colts’ territory. Three plays got Houston 9 yards, bringing them to 4th and 1. Given where the ball was on the field, the Texans could have gone for the FG (a projected 48-yarder indoors). However, you could understand going for the jugular and making a statement. Instead, the Colts’ defensive interior blew up the play for no gain. Indy used the subsequent possession to take a 3-0 lead and strategic control of the game. Yes, this was early in the game, and Houston did come back to take a brief lead late, but that play represented so much wrong about the team right now. The Texans are 0-for-5 in their last five 4th Down attempts. Weren’t Smith, Teller, Montgomery, et al supposed to fix this? FUN WITH NUMBERS: 53%: Combined conversion percentage by the Colts on 3rd/4th down attempts. The Colts went 7 of 15 on 3rd downs and 2 for 2 on 4th downs. This kept drives alive, helped in time of possession, field position…basically all of the big numbers. Those extra conversions helped the Colts run 20 more plays than Houston, making a significant impact on the game. 1: Number of NFL teams all-time that made the playoffs starting 0-4 . Think this upcoming game against Cowboys wasn’t big enough? If the Texans lose this game, they fall to 0-4. In the Super Bowl era, only 1 team ever started 0-4 and made the playoffs: The 1992 San Diego Chargers, who started 0-4, then went on to win 11 of their last 12 to make the postseason. Houston is the only squad this century to start 0-3 (twice) and make the postseason. Matching that Chargers team wasn’t part of the plan coming into the year…oh, and that Chargers team? Lost in the Divisional Round. GAME BALLS: DE Will Anderson, Jr. 7 total tackles (5 solo)/2.5 sacks/3 TFLs/2 FFs/1 FR. After a relatively slow start against Buffalo, Anderson is back to full-on nightmare mode. Houston doesn’t take the lead in the 4th without his forced fumble. Had Houston held on to win, that play would have been the critical moment. Colts PK Spencer Shrader: 4 for 4 on FG, including two 50+ yarders, 1/1 on XPs. On a day when the Colts desperately needed to snap their 9-game losing streak (and 4-game home losing streak to Houston), he gave them 13 points….and all with an injured groin, and coming back from a missed season due to an ACL/MCL injury. SHOULD BE FORCED TO LISTEN TO THE B-SIDE TRACKS OF ALL OF THE LATE JIM IRSAY BAND’S GREATEST HITS ON REPEAT WHILE ONLY EATING FROM MRBEAST BURGER. C Evan Brown: The Houston O-line interior, notably the right interior, did not represent itself well in this game, especially in the 1st half. The Colts’ defensive interior had their way with that side of Houston’s O-line, from the key 4th down stuff in the 1st Quarter to surrendering three sacks. The play somewhat improved in the second half, with even some of the best Texans’ runs coming along the right side of the line. However, Brown had more bad than good to his ledger. HC DeMeco Ryans: This season seems to showcasing the worst of Ryans’ coaching style. Questions about his decision-making related to 4th downs and timeouts are getting magnified for a team with championship aspirations. Then, he had some curious post-game comments about a unified locker room. Perhaps the standard coach-speak, but for a team that is once again 0-3, you wonder if there are some other issues bubbling underneath (especially with recent comments from Stroud about the offense). If there are divisions or locker-room grumblings at 0-3, they generate news. At 0-4, they become the headlines. Now 0-3 and 0-1 in the division, Houston returns to Reliant to resume their interstate (or interregional battle) with the Dallas/Deep Southern Oklahoma/Deep Southwestern Arkansas Cowboys in a must-win game for both teams for so, so many reasons. Kickoff is slated for this coming Sunday at noon CDT on Fox.

title: How good do you feel about the Colts’ first win?
summary: In football, we judge our teams by wins and losses. It makes sense, otherwise we’d have something like figure skating or the X Games where you get scored by judges, or like the old college football polls deciding a national champion. Careers can be defined by the amount of wins your team can amass, so […]
full_text: In football, we judge our teams by wins and losses. It makes sense, otherwise we’d have something like figure skating or the X Games where you get scored by judges, or like the old college football polls deciding a national champion. Careers can be defined by the amount of wins your team can amass, so anytime you get one, you should feel good about it. We got one of those valuable wins on Sunday and added it to the divisional and conference win total by knocking off a rival, during Rivalry Week. With Rivalry Week, comes a new uniform concept. In theory and maybe even on the runway, I liked the look. I hope that those blue helmets make more appearances. However, when coupled with the roof being open on game day, I spent most of the time wondering just who did what? I relied on the announcers much more than I prefer and found it hard to determine who was getting playing time. I might like them with the roof closed, or if they were on the road, but I have to go thumbs down after one game. Check back if we somehow find ourselves 5 – 0 in them, or we win a big playoff game. If that were the case, I might just get one for myself. I don’t have a prevailing sentiment on the game, other than a win is a win. The much maligned defense showed much better, but I have to wonder if the same folks who said our offenses feasted on weak teams last year, will say that the D had a good day against a bad offense. I did think we tackled better, but I am concerned that we got zero pass rush when it was needed most. Shouldn’t you accidentally force a turnover each game? We have one in three games. I think we would win a lot of games if we held opponents to 17 points each week, but I’m going to need a bigger sample size before I ease up on Lou. As far as the offense goes, I think ball security from DJ is worrisome. We need to figure out a way keep the edge rushers from collapsing the pocket. I think Jones is better when he can get outside, so try to force the rush to the inside, or be able to ride them far enough outside that there is a lane in that vacated spot. He just doesn’t feel that pressure from his blind side consistently enough. Other offensive suggestions: We have to take our deep shots. Trust your WR to make a play. We need to loosen up those shorter routes and the way that teams swarm to JT, there has to be some one-on-one matchups. Could we mix in some No Huddle possessions? Figure out what their D likes, personnel wise, on 1st down and script some plays that work against it, while keeping our same players on the field. It doesn’t have to be the first series, but something that you can go to. Also, why does Jones need a wrist band? This is a guy that was accepted into Princeton. We lose a little time on the play clock and take away time for our QB to make adjustments, by adding that extra step. I thought we found a way to get Warren more involved, but we shouldn’t forget that Cox and Ogletree are capable receivers as well, who do not get the same attention as 84. My last thought is that I still don’t think Steichen understands the difference between FG “range” and a chip shot. While still outside of “range” we huddled, with less than two minutes left. It eventually made the Texans use a TO, but if you playcall that series well, they never see the ball again. If you are that concerned that your QB will not make a good call at the line, you either are not confident in your guy, or you are too confident and controlling with your own abilities. Are you afraid DJ will turn the ball over? If so, you have a different kind of problem. This didn’t come out as I expected as an optimist after a divisional win, but we definitely have some things to clean up.

(Photo by Jeffrey Brown/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images According to head coach Shane Steichen, while he was seen in the press box during Sunday’s win on a scooter and with a heavy cast on his reinjured left heel, there has been no change regarding Indianapolis Colts wideout Alec Pierce’s current planned means of recovery (via FOX59/CBS4’s Mike Chappell): Alec Pierce was seen in press box Sunday on a scooter and with a heavy cast on left foot. Through the first two starts, and working his way back into form, Pierce had just 5 receptions for 72 total receiving yards, but as the Colts undisputed best deep threat, they’ve already felt his loss in other ways: It's a small sample size (3 games), but Shane Steichen's creativity on explosive pass plays is being tested w/o Alec Pierce (heel) and even Ashton Dulin (ankle): *Daniel Jones averaging 6.2 yds/att. – T-24th *Colts receivers averaging 9.2 yds/rec. – 28th — Mike Chappell (@mchappell51) September 29, 2026 The Colts' run game with Alec Pierce on/off the field since 2025: ON: 4.75 YPC (2nd) 2.49 yards before contact/attempt (4th) +0.083 EPA/rush (1st) OFF: 3.46 YPC (30th) 1.38 yards before contact/attempt (30th) +0.053 EPA/rush (5th) @FantasyPtsData — Ryan Heath (@RyanJ_Heath) September 29, 2026 Can you spot the outlier? pic.twitter.com/PlHP9WSZ8j — Ian Hartitz (@Ihartitz) September 29, 2026 Having wideout Ashton Dulin (ankle) return, who’s “making progress” from his own injury, could help make up for at least some of Pierce’s absence, although no individual player on this current Colts roster is fully capable of replacing him outright—as he’s one of the best in the business regarding his elite deep threat skill-set.

title: Colts have quietly been one of the NFL’s most disciplined teams
summary: There have been plenty of things to criticize about the Colts through the first three weeks of the season. Penalties have not been one of them. Indianapolis has committed just 15 accepted penalties for 100 yards through three games, according to the league-wide numbers posted by Ari Meirov. Only the Raiders have given up fewer […]
full_text: INDIANAPOLIS, INDIANA - SEPTEMBER 27: Head coach Shane Steichen of thew Indianapolis Colts walks up the sidelines during the first half against the Houston Texans at Lucas Oil Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Indianapolis, Indiana. (Photo by Michael Hickey/Getty Images) | Getty Images There have been plenty of things to criticize about the Colts through the first three weeks of the season. Penalties have not been one of them. How many penalty yards every NFL team has this season: pic.twitter.com/RbqvgKUnKL — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) September 29, 2026 Indianapolis has committed just 15 accepted penalties for 100 yards through three games, according to the league-wide numbers posted by Ari Meirov. Only the Raiders have given up fewer penalty yards at 90, while the Colts are tied for the third-fewest accepted penalties in the NFL. Five penalties per game is a good number on its own, but the 100 total yards is probably the more important part. Indianapolis has avoided the massive holding calls, unnecessary roughness penalties and other mistakes that can completely flip a possession. They have averaged just over 33 penalty yards per game, which is a manageable number for an offense and defense already dealing with enough other problems. It has been especially important because of how close the last two games have been. The Colts went to Kansas City and took the Chiefs all the way into overtime before eventually losing. One week later, they needed Spencer Shrader’s late field goal to beat Houston 19-17 and finally snap their losing streak. When games are being decided by one possession, giving away 10 or 15 yards at the wrong time can be the difference between getting into scoring range and punting, or forcing an opponent into third-and-long rather than handing them an automatic first down. Indianapolis has mostly avoided those self-inflicted mistakes. There is also something to be said for the type of penalties the Colts have managed to stay away from. False starts, illegal formations and pre-snap mistakes are usually the easiest ones to control. Holding calls are going to happen over the course of a season, especially along the offensive line and in the secondary, but the best teams generally avoid stacking one mistake on top of another. That is where the Colts have been pretty clean so far. They have not been constantly putting themselves in first-and-20 or extending opponents’ drives because somebody lost focus after the whistle. Considering how inconsistent other parts of the team have looked, it has at least given them a chance to stay in games rather than making things even harder on themselves. Some credit has to go to Shane Steichen and the coaching staff for that. I have been critical of Steichen plenty of times, but discipline is part of coaching too. If a team is repeatedly committing procedural penalties, lining up incorrectly or losing control after plays, that ultimately reflects on the staff. The opposite should also be acknowledged. Through three weeks, the Colts have generally played clean football from a penalty standpoint. It does not mean they have been a particularly clean team overall. The defense was historically bad through the first two weeks, the receiver group has already been hit hard by injuries and the Colts still sit at 1-2. Avoiding penalties does not erase any of that. It does make life easier. The NFL is too competitive to constantly give away free yards. The difference between a manageable third down and a drive-killing third-and-long can be one holding penalty. The difference between forcing a punt and keeping a drive alive can be one late hit. Indianapolis has not completely eliminated those mistakes, because no team does, but it has done a better job than almost everyone else through three weeks. Whether that continues over a 17-game season is another question. Penalty totals can change quickly, and one ugly afternoon can distort the numbers. For now, though, the Colts are second in the league in fewest penalty yards and near the top in fewest accepted penalties. For a team that has made plenty of things difficult on itself already this season, at least penalties have not been one of them.

title: Jaguars leap up NFL power rankings entering Week 4
summary: The Jacksonville Jaguars made history more than once in their Week 3 thumping of the New England Patriots. Via Jaguars PR: The Jaguars are good — but how do they stack up with the best teams in the league? As Week 4 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense […]
full_text: JACKSONVILLE, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Trevor Lawrence #16 of the Jacksonville Jaguars reacts after throwing a touchdown pass during the game between the Jacksonville Jaguars and the New England Patriots on September 27, 2026 at EverBank Stadium in Jacksonville, Fl. (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Jacksonville Jaguars made history more than once in their Week 3 thumping of the New England Patriots. Via Jaguars PR: Liam Coen became the fastest coach in franchise history to reach 15 wins, and the first NFL coach to win 15 of his first 20 games since Matt LeFleur in 2019. Jacksonville’s six-game home winning streak is the third-best in franchise history. The team scored 34+ points in each of those games; only the 2012 Broncos and 1960 Chargers have longer streaks of scoring 34+ points at home. The Jaguars haven’t allowed an individual rusher to reach 75 yards in 20 straight games, tied for the NFL’s fourth-longest such streak in the last 50 seasons. The defense has also recorded an interception in nine straight games and a takeaway in eight straight. The Jaguars are good — but how do they stack up with the best teams in the league? As Week 4 approaches, we rounded up the latest NFL power rankings to get a sense of how the Jaguars are viewed nationally. Pro Football Talk: 5 (last week: 7) From Mike Florio : Get used to the possibility of seeing a lot of teal in L.A. during Super Bowl week. Sports Illustrated: 5 (11) From Conor Orr : Fourth in EPA per play on offense. Fourth in EPA per play allowed on defense. The only negative on the Jaguars’ resume right now is a difficult early-season cross country road trip to Denver. In short, the Jaguars are a legitimate contender that will only look better a month from now. Yahoo Sports: 7 (8) From Frank Schwab : You can’t simply dismiss a bad half, because those count too. But if we take out the second half of Jacksonville’s Week 2 game against the Broncos — many teams wear down in the second half at Denver’s altitude, particularly early in the season — the Jaguars have outscored their three opponents 79-19. Had Jacksonville played a little better against the Broncos in the second half, perhaps their dominant start would be getting more attention. Maybe the Patriots will prove to be a bad team, but they were 14-3 last season and won the AFC, and Jacksonville beat them 35-6 on Sunday. Trevor Lawrence has a 107.8 passer rating this season, and his career high over a full season is 95.2. There are many things to like about the Jaguars’ start. The Jaguars have some tough games coming up (at Bengals, vs. Eagles in London, vs. Texans in London, vs. Colts, at Ravens) but keep your mind open to the Jaguars being one of the NFL’s best teams this season. NFL.com: 7 (9) From Nick Shook : What a nice get-right week for the Jaguars, who handled the Patriots with ease and even tousled their hair for good measure. Congratulations are in order for Travis Hunter, who recorded his first career interception amid a runaway win for Jacksonville. CBS Sports: 7 (10) From Pete Prisco : They bounced back from their first loss with a dominant victory over the Patriots. The defense, which is No. 1 in the league in points allowed, came up big in that one. Bleacher Report: 8 (10) From Gary Davenport : There is zero question that the Jaguars are the best team in the AFC South. With a trip to Cincinnati and a visit from the Eagles next up, the Jaguars have an opportunity to stake their claim as a legit Super Bowl contender as well. USA Today: 8 (11) From Nate Davis : Their two wins at EverBank Stadium have come by an aggregate score of 69-16. Too bad they only have four more games their this season. Fox Sports: 10 (12) From Ralph Vacchiano : It feels like Trevor Lawrence and the Jaguars haven’t come close to their best game yet. Liam Coen’s offense hasn’t been anything special. Lawrence had his second straight game with less than 200 yards passing. RB Bhayshul Tuten still hasn’t topped 75 rushing yards in a game. And yet Jacksonville still won two of its three games by two-plus touchdowns. Go figure. Maybe it’s because those wins were against Cleveland and New England. I want to believe. I really do. But we will probably learn a lot more about this offense in Cincinnati next week. ESPN: 10 (13) From Michael DiRocco : Fantasy surprise: WR Brian Thomas Jr. With Parker Washington’s emergence and the reliability of Jakobi Meyers, the targets were expected to be spread out somewhat evenly among Jacksonville’s receivers. But Thomas had a great offseason and the Jaguars wanted to push the ball downfield more, so expectations were high for the WR40 in our preseason projections. Now, Thomas has just seven catches for 88 yards and no TDs. Rookie Josh Cameron (two TD catches) has earned almost equal playing time, too. At this point, it’s almost impossible to expect consistent fantasy production out of Thomas. The Athletic: 10 (14) From Josh Kendall and Chad Graff : The Jaguars have won 10 of Trevor Lawrence’s last 12 starts, and the No. 1 pick in the 2021 draft is finally playing like a franchise quarterback. Since mid-November, Lawrence has more touchdowns than any quarterback in the league (26) and the second-highest passer rating (106.5). He had three touchdowns and one interception Sunday as the Jaguars manhandled the New England Patriots. title: Chiefs Film Review: Patrick Mahomes was dealing in Miami
summary: Before we turn the page to the Kansas City Chiefs’ big-time Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders, the spotlight deserves to stay on quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ performance against the Miami Dolphins a little longer. He completed 20 of 24 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns; with the interception factored in, he registered […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images Before we turn the page to the Kansas City Chiefs ’ big-time Week 4 matchup against the Las Vegas Raiders , the spotlight deserves to stay on quarterback Patrick Mahomes’ performance against the Miami Dolphins a little longer. He completed 20 of 24 passes for 246 yards and two touchdowns; with the interception factored in, he registered a 119.8 passer rating without being sacked. The box score doesn’t match the eye test; Mahomes played with the ultimate confidence, using misdirection and play action to exploit soft spots in Miami’s coverage. We looked at what went into tight end Travis Kelce coming open for a 48-yard gain to start the game , but there were more examples that showcased how well the Chiefs’ leader is playing right now. Here are some of my favorite examples from the game (using good ol’ .gifs!) Staying cool On the big throw to Kelce, it stood out how nonchalantly Mahomes sidestepped pressure and unloaded the pass across the field. After that, he kept the calm swagger. On this misdirection play, Mahomes rolls out and identifies running back Kenneth Walker as covered in the flat. That makes wide receiver Tyquan Thornton the target coming across the field at the sticks. With edge rusher Chop Robinson in his face, Mahomes keeps his cool by buying time for Thornton to clear Robinson, allowing a simple sidearm pass to be completed for a first down. Coming out of a fake handoff from under center, Mahomes reads the Dolphins’ coverage against Kansas City’s two-man route concept to that side. With the pass rusher coming on, Mahomes nonchalantly fakes out the cornerback middling the routes, making him bite on Kelce in the flat and opening up a window for Thornton to come down with the sideline catch. Influencing defenders’ movements Play action is a great first step to widening throwing windows, but Mahomes takes the next step when he’s in a rhythm by using his body language and shoulder fakes to move defenders. He did it in the play above with nonchalant ease, and he kept toying with Miami’s zone defense. Watch the Dolphins’ defenders in the middle of the field bail when he turns his shoulder to Kelce and climbs the pocket. He was setting up tight end Noah Gray with ample space to work on the checkdown. He’ll do something similar here, approaching the line of scrimmage and grabbing the attention of defenders, but this time it brings them forward, giving wide receiver Rashee Rice room to roam down the sideline for a crucial play late in the fourth quarter. Then there’s the touchdown throw to Kelce that iced the win. Just like he did to get Thornton open on the sideline as previously mentioned, Mahomes stunned the cornerback with a shoulder fake, prying open enough of a window to give Kelce a jump ball. He processes it all at a rapid pace, delivering the pass just before edge rusher Josh Uche lays him out after easily beating left tackle Kahlil Benson. A fadeaway, downfield dime — just for fun This was my favorite throw of Mahomes’ performance against the Dolphins, and it’s not just because it was a 40-yard dime as he faded away from an oncoming defender, but because he also passed up a wide-open Xavier Worthy streaking across the field. There’s a chance Worthy scores if the ball gets to him. Whether it was Gray or Worthy receiving a confidence boost from the big play, it was a positive for the pass-catching group moving forward.

title: The Chiefs are the fourth-most explosive offense in the NFL
summary: It’s been refreshing to see big plays in the Kansas City Chiefs’ offense again. Each win of the team’s 3-0 start to the 2026 season has featured them, whether on the ground or through the air. According to Football Data Scientist Sam Hoppen on Twitter, the Chiefs have been generating explosive plays at the fourth-highest […]
full_text: (Photo by David Eulitt/Getty Images) | Getty Images It’s been refreshing to see big plays in the Kansas City Chiefs ’ offense again. Each win of the team’s 3-0 start to the 2026 season has featured them, whether on the ground or through the air. According to Football Data Scientist Sam Hoppen on Twitter , the Chiefs have been generating explosive plays at the fourth-highest rate in the NFL. Offensive and defensive explosive play rates: pic.twitter.com/UXkcXoLRNy — Sam Hoppen (@SamHoppen) September 29, 2026 An explosive run is an attempt that gains 10 or more yards, while an explosive pass is a 20-yard gain through the air. The Chiefs rank fifth in explosive run and pass rates, combining to sit behind only the Buffalo Bills , Baltimore Ravens and San Francisco 49ers in terms of the league’s best at executing big plays this season. The Chiefs have hit on the explosive plays in many different ways, whether it was a fourth-and-one handoff to running back Kenneth Walker that scored from 60 yards out in Week 1 against the Denver Broncos or a play-action pass to tight end Travis Kelce that gained 48 in Week 3. Walker has the third-most runs of 10 or more yards in the NFL, according to NFL Next Gen Stats ; he sits behind only the Bills’ running back James Cook and the Detroit Lions ’ back Jahmyr Gibbs. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has also had a couple of runs over 10 yards. Kelce has two monster gains on his 2026 highlight reel so far, but he is one of six Chiefs players to record a reception for 20 or more yards this year. Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has been spreading the rock this year, and the threat of a handoff has allowed more space for his pass catchers to work. Hoppen also shares that the Chiefs’ defense ranks in the middle of the pack in allowing explosive plays. Kansas City’s run defense has allowed explosive runs on 12% of handoffs, ranking 20th among NFL teams, but the pass defense has been more sound: Only 4% of the pass attempts the Chiefs have faced this year have gained 20 or more yards, good for the 10th-best rate in the league.

title: Numbers Never Lie: 4 notable Chiefs stats to know through three weeks
summary: Numbers never lie, right? There are so many statistics to parse through during the NFL season that some can be misleading. After each game, it’s a good exercise to review NFL “Next Gen Stats” and “Premium Stats” from Pro Football Focus and find the numbers that paint a picture not only of the game, but […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Numbers never lie, right? There are so many statistics to parse through during the NFL season that some can be misleading. After each game, it’s a good exercise to review NFL “Next Gen Stats” and “Premium Stats” from Pro Football Focus and find the numbers that paint a picture not only of the game, but of what to expect from the Kansas City Chiefs moving forward. Here are four season-long statistics after three games and what they could mean for the rest of the season: 1. Under pressure, Patrick Mahomes is averaging 10.9 yards per pass attempt Quarterback Patrick Mahomes has generated 9.7 Expected Points Added (EPA) over the 28 dropbacks he has been under pressure so far this season, according to Next Gen Stats. He leads all NFL players in yards per pass attempt and EPA when under pressure; here’s the remainder of the top 5: 2. Josh Allen: 9.6 yards per attempt, -0.8 EPA 3. Tyler Shough: 9.1 yards per attempt, -16 EPA 4. Geno Smith: 9 yards per attempt, -2.8 EPA 5. Jared Goff: 8.2 yards per attempt, -5.5 EPA Whether it’s the eye test or the advanced metrics, it’s clear that Mahomes is dealing so far this year. Both of his interceptions look more like mistiming or miscommunication with a wideout than putting the ball in harm’s way. Mahomes threw the Week 3 interception behind wide receiver Rashee Rice, but the Miami Dolphins made a spectacular play to force the turnover. Regardless, Mahomes has been locked in, whether it’s within the scheme or outside of it due to pressure. Kansas City’s coaching staff needs to limit the times he is pressured moving forward, but he’s playing well enough to make it work regardless. 2. Two Chiefs are in the Top 10 for yards after catch Head coach Andy Reid gets a lot of credit for an offense that produces as many yards after catch as any NFL offense in modern history, but this year’s improved run game has a lot to do with tight end Travis Kelce (156 yards) and wide receiver Rashee Rice (120 yards) ranking first and eighth among all NFL players in yards after catch through three weeks. Kelce and Rice excel at finding soft spots in zone coverage, the primary defensive strategy on early downs when anticipating the run. You’ve seen the Chiefs’ offense use play action and misdirection to maximize the open throwing windows downfield to these two, but the individual players deserve credit for making the most of it with their different abilities to get upfield after the ball’s in their hands. 3. L’Jarius Sneed is allowing an 80% completion rate in coverage According to PFF , Sneed has been targeted 25 times in coverage this year while playing in the slot most of the time (98 of 148 snaps). He has been faulted on 20 catches totaling 195 yards, with 116 yards coming after the catch. Quarterbacks are generating a passer rating of 112.5 when throwing at Sneed. He has also drawn three penalties. He is one of the only soft spots in what has been a sound Chiefs coverage unit… 4. The Chiefs’ defense is the third-best in the NFL by EPA per pass play Only the Jacksonville Jaguars (-0.27) and the Chicago Bears (-0.23) have outperformed the Chiefs’ defense (-0.21) so far in allowing the fewest EPA per pass play. The Chiefs are allowing just 5.4 yards per pass play, the sixth-lowest rate in the NFL. The team’s pressure definitely needs to step it up — Kansas City has the seventh-lowest sack rate (3.7%) in the league — but the Chiefs’ outside cornerbacks have looked sound in coverage when healthy. Rookie Mansoor Delane and second-year corner Nohl Williams will only get better as the season continues.

title: NFL Power Rankings Week 4 Roundup: Chiefs’ hot start has them near top
summary: The 2026 NFL regular season’s Week 3 featured the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Miami Dolphins, moving to 3-0, one of five NFL teams with that record. Let’s see how the national media responds in this week’s sampling of power rankings: NFL.com: 2 (Up from 4) The Chiefs are very aware of who they are […]
full_text: (Photo by Carmen Mandato/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 2026 NFL regular season’s Week 3 featured the Kansas City Chiefs beating the Miami Dolphins , moving to 3-0, one of five NFL teams with that record. Let’s see how the national media responds in this week’s sampling of power rankings: NFL.com : 2 (Up from 4) The Chiefs are very aware of who they are just three weeks into the season. They didn’t need to fully exert themselves on Sunday, earning a professional win against a scrappy but undermanned Dolphins team. They decreased Kenneth Walker III’s touches, too, which was a requirement for me in such a matchup, especially with most of the season still ahead. ESPN : 3 (Up from 4) Fantasy surprise: RB Kenneth Walker III Most fantasy owners knew Walker was a good choice, especially after his impressive postseason run to help the Seahawks win the Super Bowl. But not even the Chiefs could have expected this level of production from Walker, who has the second-most total fantasy points at RB this season. He has already produced 442 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns. Walker is the first player in franchise history to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within the first three weeks, per ESPN Research. — Nate Taylor The Athletic : 3 (Up from 4) QB confidence: All the way back Patrick Mahomes is tied for second in the NFL in passing touchdowns (seven) and looks as scary as ever now that he’s sharing a backfield with Kenneth Walker III. Walker leads the league in rushing (360 yards), and Mahomes is using play action at a higher rate (32.1 percent) than he ever has. Mahomes was 20-of-24 for 246 yards Sunday to hold off the surprisingly plucky Miami Dolphins. — Chad Graff and Josh Kendall Pro Football Talk : 2 (Up from 4) The Chiefs are back . . . to playing with their food before winning easily. — Mike Florio CBSSports.com : 3 (Up from 5) At 3-0, the people who buried them need to admit they were wrong. They play a big one this week at Las Vegas against the unbeaten Raiders. — Pete Prisco Yahoo! Sports : 4 (Up from 6) The Chiefs are 3-0 but if there’s a concern, it’s still the passing offense around Patrick Mahomes. In particular, Xavier Worthy has been surprisingly quiet. In three games, he has 18, 25 and 20 yards. Miami has a poor secondary and Worthy managed only two catches for 20 yards. The hope that the 2024 first-round draft pick could break out in his third season is dwindling. Other than that, the Chiefs are doing well. The worry is what happens if Kenneth Walker, who is carrying the offense, wears down under the biggest workload of his career or misses time. There’s not much else around him for Mahomes to work with. — Frank Schwab USA Today : 2 (Up from 5) RB Kenneth Walker III is averaging a league-best 120 rushing yards per game while continuing to give every indication he’s unlocked the AFC’s top-ranked offense anew. Next, a battle for first place in the AFC West at Las Vegas, where QB Patrick Mahomes is 6-0. — Nate Davis Sports Illustrated : 2 (Up from 3) Here is a bit of a mea culpa and explainer on why the Kansas City Chiefs are very real. I’d check it out if I were you . — Conor Orr FOX Sports : 4 (Up from 8) Everyone was finally convinced they were back to their old, dynastic selves, and then they go and let a terrible Dolphins team hang around for an awfully long time. But they are 3-0 and not every game can be perfect, I guess. They’re on the rise, though. They have a whole new dimension with RB Kenneth Walker III, and they still have the ever-dangerous Patrick Mahomes and an array of weapons. Kansas City also has a pretty soft schedule. With the Raiders up next, they’re looking at 4-0 heading into their bye. So I have a feeling this isn’t the last stop on their climb up the charts. Stat To Know : With the Chiefs win on Sunday, Patrick Mahomes passed Tom Brady for the third-most wins by a player in his first 10 seasons since 1950. — Ralph Vacchiano
author: Ron Kopp Jr.

title: AP NFL Power Rankings Week 4: Jaguars crash Top 5
summary: New challenge unlocked for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs: drive down the field for a game-winning field goal in seven seconds or less, as the Baltimore Ravens accomplished on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, against the Dallas Cowboys. The Brazil tilt was the first game in NFL history in which both teams […]
full_text: (Photo by David Rosenblum/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images New challenge unlocked for quarterback Patrick Mahomes and the Kansas City Chiefs : drive down the field for a game-winning field goal in seven seconds or less, as the Baltimore Ravens accomplished on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, against the Dallas Cowboys . The Brazil tilt was the first game in NFL history in which both teams scored in the final 10 seconds of a regular-season game. It headlined another wild week of NFL action, which whittled the remaining unbeaten down to only five. And they were all who we expected, right ? Among the 3-0 unbeatens are the Chiefs, Buffalo Bills and San Francisco 49ers —solid franchises of the past decade. Joining the unbeaten club are two of the more surprising teams (represented in our power rankings as such, as they have shot up the rankings)— the Las Vegas Raiders and Minnesota Vikings . I think I speak for all of Chiefs Kingdom when I say it’s fun to look forward to a Chiefs-Raiders matchup again, as they’ll clash in Week 4. The rivalry is more fun when there are stakes and both teams are competitive. But let’s not get too far ahead of ourselves. Let’s see how the AP power rankings shook out this week. Biggest risers: Pittsburgh Steelers, Jacksonville Jaguars , and Cleveland Browns +7 Biggest fallers: New England Patriots and Green Bay Packers -8 This week, along with myself, staff voters were: Caleb James, Ron Kopp Jr., Rocky Magana, and Jared Sapp . 1. San Francisco 49ers (3rd) I’m going to take the low-hanging fruit here. Brock Purdy has looked purdy nice to start this season. He currently holds the second-highest MVP odds. 2. Buffalo Bills (2nd) Five turnovers and still coming away with the win is tough to do. 3. Kansas City Chiefs (4th) I give myself headaches trying to do the mental gymnastics of the haters who believe the conspiracy theories of the refs favoring the Chiefs. 4. Jacksonville Jaguars (11th) In true Jaguars fashion, they aren’t getting the respect they probably deserve. The top two storylines I saw coming out of this one? Josh Hines-Allen fighting a ball boy for Travis Hunter’s first career interception ball. And Trevor Lawrence oddly kneeling down at the 1-yard line instead of scoring a touchdown with eight minutes left. 5. Seattle Seahawks (1st) The return of quarterback Sam Darnold did not spell victory for the ‘Hawks. They suffered their first loss since November 2025. 6. Baltimore Ravens (7th) The flight from Rio back to Baltimore was about 10 hours. The Ravens took possession with seven seconds left in the fourth quarter to win. This means Ravens’ players could have watched their game-winning drive 5,142 times on the flight home. 7. Cincinnati Bengals (5th) The quarterback who supposedly has ice running through his veins falls up short in the 4th quarter—once again. Burrow sure gains a lot of national respect from that Super Bowl loss, checks notes, five years ago. 8. Philadelphia Eagles (6th) This team reminds me of the 2025 Kansas City Chiefs. A team that looks tired, bored, and like the league has figured them out. They need some sort of shakeup. 9. Minnesota Vikings (9th) A 3-0 start, and they shipped quarterback JJ McCarthy to New York for draft capital. The McCarthy selection will go down as one of the biggest blunders in their franchise history. 10. Los Angeles Rams (8th) I’d be livid as a Rams fan over that pass interference call that negated a game-sealing interception in the fourth quarter. But also, maybe don’t give a 16-point halftime lead or throw a pick-six to put you in that do-or-die spot? 11. Chicago Bears (10th) Although Caleb Williams was on the sideline in a hoodie, the Bears still looked like one of the top teams in the NFC with journeyman Case Keenum. 12. Las Vegas Raiders (18th) Alright, respect where it’s due. The Raiders have looked solid to start the year and have already matched their 2025 win total. But enough of that…. IT’S RAIIIIIDERS WEEK. 13. Detroit Lions (14th) Jahmyr Gibbs is an absolute cheat code on the football field. 14. Denver Broncos (13th) How long can this team survive by winning bizarre games with absurd fourth-quarter comebacks? 15. Dallas Cowboys (16th) Such an insane and hilarious way for the Cowboys to lose a football game. 16. Pittsburgh Steelers (23rd) Credit where credit is due. Pittsburgh delivered a solid divisional win. Now they must repeat on a short week against Cleveland. 17. Indianapolis Colts (22nd) The Colts achieved their first win on American soil in almost a full calendar year! 18. New Orleans Saints (17th) Tyler Shough impresses even in the loss. The Saints could really go on a run and surprise some folks. Their next six opponents are the Falcons, Vikings, Giants, Steelers, Browns, and Panthers. A fairly favorable schedule. 19. New York Giants (21st) If your starting quarterback goes down, it’s favorable to have the Tennessee Titans on your schedule the following week. 20. New England Patriots (12th) What is wrong with Drake Maye? Talk about regression. 21. Arizona Cardinals (24th) What would you give up for the Chiefs to acquire Marvin Harrison Jr.? 22. Cleveland Browns (29th) Browns fans really are an unlucky bunch. They’re upset if they lose, yet upset if they win because they hate their current quarterback. 23. Green Bay Packers (15th) Dreadful performance in front of the home crowd at Lambeau. Does head coach Matt LaFleur make it through the season? 24. Houston Texans (19th) This has to be one of the least-talked-about teams in the NFL. On paper, one of the league’s top defenses. But for the second season in a row, they’re 0-3. 25. Atlanta Falcons (31st) An offensive explosion at Lambeau has reignited faint hope in Atlanta. When Bijan Robinson and Drake London are both hot, and they get competent quarterback play, this offense will be tough to slow down. 26. Carolina Panthers (20th) Honestly, I was shocked to find out the Panthers will be gracing our television screens in primetime next week. 27. Washington Commanders (28th) The team is the lowest in our power rankings and is coming off the most solid win in Week 3. But there isn’t much to be excited about with this team. 28. Los Angeles Chargers (25th) Chiefs fans honestly couldn’t lose with the matchup on Sunday. Either the Bills were embarrassed at home by the 0-2 Chargers or the AFC West offseason champs fell to 0-3. I’ll take this result. 29. New York Jets (27th) The Jets honestly look to be improved this season. But from the outset, it is obvious they are already looking forward to 2027. 30. Tampa Bay Buccaneers (26th) Baker joins the list of starting quarterbacks to miss time this season. What a brutal season for the Bucs, and one has to wonder how long head coach Todd Bowles has a job. 31. Miami Dolphins (32nd) With Devon Achane going down for the season, 0-17 may legitimately be in the cards. 32. Tennessee Titans (30th) This season will produce the most depressing country songs ever written in Nashville.
