title: Chiefs Mailbag: When will Cyrus Allen see the field?
summary: Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs! The box score and advanced metrics paint a prettier picture than the Chiefs’ Week 3 24-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins felt as the actual game unfolded. Let’s see […]
full_text: (Photo by Scott Winters/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Welcome back to the Arrowhead Pride Mailbag ! Throughout the season, keep watching The Feed for an opportunity to submit your questions about the Kansas City Chiefs ! The box score and advanced metrics paint a prettier picture than the Chiefs’ Week 3 24-10 victory over the Miami Dolphins felt as the actual game unfolded. Let’s see what’s on our readers’ minds ahead of an unexpected showdown of 3-0 teams Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders . John 1963 asks: Has quarterback Patrick Mahomes lost faith in wideout Xavier Worthy? Or is he not getting open? Only two targets Sunday. The Chiefs ran only 49 offensive plays on Sunday, making it a difficult sample to determine who the staff may be fading on or who simply didn’t factor into a truncated game plan. I think there is evidence that Tyquan Thornton has more trust on deep routes than Worthy does. Worthy still seems preferred to his fellow speedster on short and intermediate routes, although second-year man Jalen Royals is trending up in that category. Worthy’s 17-yard catch on Sunday was one of the better routes we have seen him run in 2026, and he came down with a high pass from Mahomes. But right now, if the deep throws are going to Thornton and Rashee Rice, and Travis Kelce is getting so much intermediate work and racking up yards after the catch, where is Worthy’s ceiling to improve on a dismal showing so far this season? Worthy and Mahomes both spent the offseason recovering from major surgery, so it’s still a bit early to write off his season. But if he isn’t a more effective piece of the offense coming out of the Week 5 bye, I think you could see his snaps start trending down dramatically. FoxBot2021 asks: If Rashee Rice stays on this kind of pace for 1k and maybe 5-6 TDs, and IF he can walk the straight and narrow, do the Chiefs give Rashee a short 2-3 year deal like they did with Tyreek Hill? The ship has sailed on Rice signing an extension as Hill did in 2019. Hill signed a three-year extension after his final season on his original rookie contract. So the Chiefs really had four seasons to pay off what was then a very controversial three-year deal. Ultimately, the Chiefs traded “The Cheetah” ahead of the extension’s final season in 2022. Rice is now three games into the final season of his rookie deal and set to be one of the most interesting free agent cases next offseason. He is currently on pace for 1076 receiving yards and six touchdowns, with his targets increasing each week. With Rice coming off of his own offseason surgery, I expect his production to rise further from what we are seeing. With running back Kenneth Walker getting significant check-down work in the passing game, Rice’s current 6.4-yard average depth of target would easily set a career high if it holds. That said, the Chiefs will need to have some serious conversations about his future. The wide receiver franchise tag for 2027 is currently estimated ( per Over the Cap ) at $30.9 million. Even if Rice becomes Kansas City’s first 1000 yard wide receiver since 2021, will that really be due to his transcendent talent — or a product of the Chiefs’ offense? Ultimately, I predict that Rice will be a Chief somehow in 2027. I don’t think the Chiefs will eat the salary cap room to use the tag — but I also don’t think teams will line up to pay him as a No. 1 wideout. If he has to prove himself — on and off the field — for one more season, I think Rice will ultimately decide the Chiefs give him the best chance to put up numbers that eventually get him paid. AzDiamond asks: Is defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo going to going to give cornerback L’Jarius Sneed the Daniel Sorenson and Ben Nieman treatment or will he play Chris Roland-Wallace and/or rookie Jadon Canady in the slot? The last two weeks, offenses have thrown quick passes to Sneed to mitigate anything the Chiefs might do to pressure the quarterback. His lowest passer rating allowed through three games is 89.6 in Week 1. I am not sure it will become the frustrating situation Chiefs fans saw with Sorensen and Nieman in the past. Spagnuolo clearly has an affinity for Sneed, but that is true for multiple players in the current secondary. With safety Chamarri Conner likely to return in Week 4, I am wondering whether he will take on some of the rotational third-safety role and let Roland-Wallace absorb some of Sneed’s slot work. Roland-Wallace played only 12 defensive snaps on Sunday but led the team’s defenders with a 93.2 coverage grade per Pro Football Focus . One solution I am wondering we’ll see after the bye is Nohl Williams taking on some of the slot work, with veteran Kristian Fulton rotating in outside. After playing the first two weeks in relief of rookie Mansoor Delane heavily, Fulton did not see the field against Miami. Canady has played in more than two-thirds of the special teams snaps the last two weeks, and I am not sure the team can currently spare him unless absolutely necessary. I expect the fourth-round pick to have a learning year in 2026 and compete next summer for a significant defensive role. ChiefTigerfan24 asks: When will we see rookie wide receiver Cyrus Allen get some more offensive snaps? I would like to start working him in to see if the pre-season hype is real or not. I expected Allen to defy expectations and carve out a bigger role early in his rookie season. One complicating factor has been the usage of Royals, who I wasn’t totally sure would even make the team six weeks ago. Royals only has three catches for 17 yards, but all have come in three moments. One went for a touchdown, and his other two catches have yielded first downs. Whenever Allen’s first real action comes, I think it will be unexpected and the result of the Chiefs seeing something they feel he can exploit. With the chance to enter the bye at 4-0 and alone in first place in the AFC standings, I won’t be surprised if they find a situation to use him against the Raiders in Week 4. KaneMarko asks: Pass rush….where has it been the last 2 weeks? As the following two slates have unfolded, I truly believe that the Denver Broncos entered Week 1 with a terrible offensive game plan that made the Chiefs’ pass rush look more ready than it truly was. This is a young defense, and you should expect ups and downs. Pass rush and coverage tend to work hand in hand. The Chiefs are giving up too many frustrating third-down completions. A more dependable linebacker would also help mitigate the success teams are having against Kansas City on play-action. It was concerning to see Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis enter the game as the league’s most sacked quarterback and for the Chiefs not to get to him. It is also still early, and the Chiefs have less mobile quarterbacks on tap for their next two games in Kirk Cousins of the Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers ’ Justin Herbert. Chief Among Them asks The Vikings, Bills, Raiders, and 49ers all went 3-0 this Sunday, playing 0-3 and 1-2 teams in one-score games. Why is everyone acting like the sky is falling for the Chiefs, who was one of only three teams this week to win by more than one score? There’s really no way to explain to someone who didn’t watch the game why fans are mad. The Chiefs covered a 10-point spread, allowed only three points after halftime. Per Next Gen Stats , Kansas City never had less than a 76% win probability (and never less than 86% in the fourth quarter). Watching the game (and reading real-time reactions), I was reminded of another Week 3 contest against a seemingly terrible opponent. The eventual Super Bowl LVII champion Chiefs traveled to face the Indianapolis Colts for their third game — only to lose 20-17 to a team that ultimately finished the 2022 season 4-12-1. You can acknowledge that the past two weeks have raised some early concerns for the Chiefs while also appreciating that defeating any team by 14 points is a difficult…

full_text: (Photo by Jeff Bottari/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Kansas City Chiefs will take on the Las Vegas Raiders this week in a pivotal AFC West matchup, one of the biggest games in the rivalry’s modern history. Head coach Andy Reid set the tone on Monday when he spoke about the matchup during a video conference with local media. “I think it’ll be a great atmosphere for a football game,” Reid said. “I think they’ve done a nice job of improving their football team. This is what it’s all about, and I think it will be great for the fans. It’s a heck of a rivalry over the years, and the better the two teams are, the better the rivalry, so this is what it’s all about.” Chiefs Kingdom, bring the noise to the SB Nation app! Chat live throughout the game Browse with fewer ads Easily jump between communities Enjoy faster commenting and posting Download the SB Nation app on iOS or Android . Download the SB Nation app on your mobile device! For Apple devices, click here . For Android devices, click here . The latest Kansas City Chiefs news Chiefs and Raiders meet in Week 4 with AFC lead on the line | FOX4 KC For the Raiders, a 3-0 start seemed like a long shot considering the team’s form in prior seasons. For the first time since 2021, the Raiders come into Week 4 unbeaten at 3-0 and having already matched its win total from last season. In comparison, the Chiefs are halfway to matching their six victories from a disappointing 2025 season. A crucial point to Sunday’s matchup is both teams have already picked up a divisional win: The Chiefs over the Denver Broncos and the Raiders over the Los Angeles Chargers. Sloppy Wins Are Becoming A Kansas City Calling Card | Yahoo! Sports But there’s another side to this. The Chiefs play the Las Vegas Raiders on the road, then the Los Angeles Chargers on the road, which will be two more chances to see if the slop creeps in again. After that, though, the Chiefs get the Seattle Seahawks and a road tilt against the Denver Broncos, and if Kansas City isn’t executing the way they did during that first win over the Broncos, those little things will suddenly matter a lot more. Kansas City Chiefs HC Andy Reid gives latest injury updates on Josh Simmons, Chamarri Conner after Week 3 win vs. Miami Dolphins | A to Z Sports “I’ll tell you what,” Reid began. “I will let you guys know when Josh (Simmons) is coming back. I’ll be the first to tell you. So we’ll just see how that all works out.” Chiefs fans want to know whether Simmons will make his debut in Week 4, mainly because if he doesn’t, the team will have missed a chance to place him on injured reserve. NFL rules require players placed on injured reserve to miss at least four weeks before they can return to practice, be designated to return, and play in a game. 10 Quick Facts Following the Chiefs Week 3 Win Over Miami | Upon Further Review | The Mothership Quarterback Patrick Mahomes moved past Joe Montana in terms of career touchdown passes. Mahomes tallied his 274th career touchdown pass on Sunday, moving him past Joe Montana for 20th on the all-time list. It all helped Mahomes earn his 115th career start (including the playoffs), matching Tom Brady for the most victories through 150 starts in NFL history. Mahomes also now has 83 career games with multiple touchdown passes, which leads the NFL by eight games since 2018. Ex-Chiefs star expected to make ‘full recovery’ after scary injury | Chiefs Wire The former Wisconsin Badgers standout was a member of Kansas City’s Super Bowl LVII and LVIII rosters and played a key role in Steve Spagnuolo’s defense between 2022 and 2025. NFL insider Jordan Schultz shared the latest update on Chenal’s status in a post to his official Twitter account on September 28: According to Schultz, Chenal has feeling in all of his extremities, which bodes well for his recovery timeline. Around the NFL Case Keenum surprises in Bears’ win. What’s wrong with Eagles’ offense? | The Athletic Keenum, 38, filling in for the injured Caleb Williams, was impressive in his first NFL start since 2023, completing 24 of 34 passes for 247 yards and TDs to Luther Burden III and Kalif Raymond. His 1-yard run in the fourth quarter put the game on ice. The Eagles held the Bears’ running game in check after getting run over in a Black Friday loss last season, but Keenum beat them through the air. The last time he had more passing yards was Sept. 23, 2019, when he finished with 332 for Washington in a loss to the Bears. Giants trade for Vikings QB McCarthy but say Winston is QB1 | ESPN Giants coach John Harbaugh said after Sunday’s victory over the Tennessee Titans that Jameis Winston would remain the Giants’ starter even if the team added another quarterback. He reiterated that Monday after the trade for McCarthy. The Giants host the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday. “Jameis is starting. You guys asked me that [Sunday] night. He’s our starting quarterback, and that’s how we’re rolling,” Harbaugh said. “We’ll be ready to play this next game and going forward. Excited about Jameis. … I’m looking forward to seeing where we go, and as we go we’ll get a chance to build around Jameis’ strengths.” What happened to Drake Maye? Why his Year 3 collapse is getting harder to explain away | CBS Sports The difference is that Maye’s 2025 season was considerably more convincing. He wasn’t simply amassing stats. His EPA improved substantially, his turnover-worthy plays went down, and the deep ball became a real weapon: Maye completed 61.8% of his throws 20-plus yards downfield, one of the highest rates in the league. That looked like legit franchise-QB development, not a false positive. The biggest difference so far isn’t that Maye suddenly can’t make NFL throws. He can. It’s the mistakes that largely went missing last season that have come back, almost as if they’re making up for lost time. In case you missed it on Arrowhead Pride 5 things we learned from the Chiefs’ Week 3 victory in Miami Mansoor Delane will have his rookie moments, but… Dang, he is just a good football player. I feel like it took Delane a couple of drives to really get his feet wet and get into the rhythm, but once he did, he was a difference-maker on this defense. When you combine him and Nohl Williams on the outside, it’s going to be hard for opposing perimeter wide receivers to have much success against the Chiefs. title: RAMalytics: One reason why Rams’ passing game feels anemic
summary: One can attempt to mistakenly place blame for the Los Angeles Rams’ 1-2 start on either injuries or officiating. The real reason for LA’s shortcomings are the fact that their key players are not performing at star levels. Matthew Stafford has objectively been one of the worst quarterbacks in football so far. He’s certainly better […]
full_text: DENVER, CO - SEPTEMBER 27: Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford (9) listens for the play call as rain falls during a game between the Los Angeles Rams and the Denver Broncos at Empower Field at Mile High on September 27, 2026 in Denver, Colorado. (Photo by Dustin Bradford/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images One can attempt to mistakenly place blame for the Los Angeles Rams’ 1-2 start on either injuries or officiating. The real reason for LA’s shortcomings are the fact that their key players are not performing at star levels. Matthew Stafford has objectively been one of the worst quarterbacks in football so far. He’s certainly better than that and will likely rebound at some point. Colby Parkinson is on a milk carton instead of the box score. The offensive line has overall taken a step back in pass protection. Kobie Turner, Braden Fiske, Byron Young, and even Aaron Donald have disappointed on the defensive line. Nate Landman still hasn’t regained his early season magic from a year ago. For right now let’s focus on the Rams’ anemic passing attack. The theme of the 2026 NFL season is that defenses aim to take limit explosives and force opposing offenses to remain patient and live off short passes. This excerpt from Ted Nguyen at The Athletic helps set the scene. Offenses have loaded up on bigger bodies this offseason and seem to be gearing up to focus more on the running game, but can they force defenses to cycle back into putting a safety in the box? After speaking with defensive coaches, the collective answer was, surprisingly, no. Two-high defenses are here to stay. Quarterbacks and receivers are simply too good. Finding ways to slow the run, while making it hard to create explosive pass plays, is the key to modern defenses. Even if one or two teams become so explosive on the ground they force defenses to put the extra safety in the box, those offenses won’t be enough to change the defensive meta… According to defensive coaches, the evolution will continue with defenses finding ways to slow down the run game with light boxes, confusing the quarterback and scheming ways to attack protection plans. Putting an extra safety in the box simply creates too much risk for defenses for the league to cycle back in that direction. Pete Prisco from CBS Sports takes this analysis a step further. Offenses are stringing together longer drives. That takes more time off the clock. Ultimately each team has fewer possessions, fewer opportunities to score, and the margin between win and loss has never been tighter: What in the hell has happened to the NFL passing game? This was a league that once saw 5,000-yard passers, big downfield numbers, quarterbacks who let it fly, and coaches who weren’t afraid to let them do it. But last year, the average passing yards per game for NFL teams was the lowest since 2008… Think about this: NFL teams averaged just 209.7 passing yards per game last season, and just 10 years prior to that, teams averaged 243.8 yards per game. That’s a significant drop. In 2015, the league averaged 10.8 yards per catch. Last season, it was 10.2… That is spreading throughout the league. Make offenses be patient and make them drive the field. Fans love the big plays. Offensive coaches and players do, too, but getting them now almost means yards after catch rather than the ball in the air. What happened to the Rams specifically? As Prisco pointed out, yards after catch are at a premium. LA’s best YAC receiver, Puka Nacua, has missed two of three games. Terrance Ferguson is probably their next best pass catcher in this facet, and he was a nonfactor in Week 1 before exiting early in the third game. Nacua could return in Week 4 but Ferguson is unlikely to recover in time. Davante Adams is somehow 11th in the NFL in YAC with 105 yards after the catch point. It’s not necessarily something you would expect him to do well, but then again the ageless wonder Travis Kelce leads all players with 155 yards. Part of Adams’ success is volume. He’s 10th in receptions, fifth in targets, and ranks 26th in YAC/reception among all players with at least 17 targets. And then there are the quarterback and play caller. One thing is certain about Sean McVay and Matthew Stafford: both love long, vertical throws and make their living on explosive plays. Neither have historically demonstrated much of a knack for the short passing game. It’s not how they want to play, generally speaking. But 43.2% of Stafford’s attempts have come within 0-9 yards this season. That ranks 22nd among the 36 quarterbacks that meet the qualifying 20% target threshold. On such plays, Stafford ranks 32nd in Pro Football Focus (PFF) passing grade. Stafford has completed 37 of 48 passes (77.1%) for 320 yards, 2 TDs, 1 INT, 0 big-time throws, and 2 turnover-worthy plays in this category. LA’s signal caller is ninth in attempts between zero and nine yards. He’s 11th in first downs. His average depth of target of 3.9 yards on such plays puts him 30th in this group, so when Stafford is throwing short it’s usually very short. More telling is the company in the same range as him plus those at the top of the list. Towards the bottom: Bo Nix (26th; 60.3) – regressed notably from last season Malik Willis (27th; 58.0) – not yet an established starter Jordan Love (28th; 57.0) – one of the most disappointing players in 2026 Jalen Hurts (30th; 54.1) – in a new offense and struggling Matthew Stafford (32nd; 53.5) Joe Burrow (33rd; 52.7) – winning but not lighting up the scoreboard Sam Darnold (34th; 49.3) – struggled in first game back from injury At the top: Patrick Mahomes (1st; 89.2) – looks rejuvinated Josh Allen (2nd; 85.4) – seems unstoppable Jacoby Brissett (3rd; 84.1) – better than expected Drake Maye (4th; 82.1) – bucks my trend Kirk Cousins (5th; 81.4) – leading the 3-0 Raiders Drew Lock (6th; 81.2) – earned big offseason money Trevor Lawrence (7th; 77.7) – deserves MVP consideration so far At risk of oversimplification, those who excel in the short passing game are best-suited to succeed in today’s NFL. Defenses want quarterbacks to live and die by the deep ball. Those who can repeatedly take what the opposition is giving them over and over again without growing impatient will prevail. The short passing game has never been a strength or the Rams’ bread and butter under Sean McVay. It is something that needs to improve in order for LA’s passing game to right the ship. We will continue to gauge progress and check on this trend as we collect more information.
author: JB Scott

title: How is Aaron Donald’s return going so far?
summary: The Los Angeles Rams might have the worst defensive tackle group in the NFL through three weeks, and Aaron Donald is as much a part of those struggles as anyone else on the team. Regardless of how much anyone expected out of Donald following a two-year absence from football and skipping all of training camp […]
full_text: The Los Angeles Rams might have the worst defensive tackle group in the NFL through three weeks, and Aaron Donald is as much a part of those struggles as anyone else on the team. Regardless of how much anyone expected out of Donald following a two-year absence from football and skipping all of training camp as he mulled a return from retirement, the only thing that matters to the Rams is the product on the field as L.A. looks to rebound from a 1-2 start. It’s not going so good. And that’s hardly all on Donald, but he’s no less guilty than the rest of the unit. Aaron Donald’s pressure rate Out of 91 defensive linemen who qualify with enough snaps, Donald ranks 79th in terms of pressure rate at 4.8%. Per the NFL Pro website by Next Gen Stats, Donald has registered two pressures out of 42 pass rush snaps and only 12 defensive tackles are behind him in terms of pressure rate. Donald has 22 run defense snaps and three stops. A “stop” is any tackle that results in a “failed play” for the offense depending on down and distance. Donald’s former Rams teammate A’Shawn Robinson also has a low pressure rate at 4.5% with the Bucs, and only plays in 51.4% of the naps, but actually has 10 stops and one sack. For context, Aaron Donald’s pressure rate in 2023 was 12.9%. That was a tick higher than it had been the previous two seasons, but not as high as the 16.4% he posted in 2020, the 16.3% he posted in 2019, and well below the 19.2% he posted in 2018. Donald won Defensive Player of the Year in 2018 and 2020. So no, Donald is not the player he was when he retired, and even then he was not the player he was when he was the best defensive weapon in football. This is usually when fans chime in to say something like “So what? He took two years off, what did you expect?” and that’s completely besides the point: We’re here to talk about results, not excuses for results. This would be like if you gave your car keys to a 12-year-old kid to drive to the store and then he crashes the car. “Well what did you expect, you gave your keys to a 12-year-old kid who had never driven before” is a reasonable explanation for the accident, but it doesn’t fix your car . Through his first two games, Donald isn’t just an average defensive tackle who merely lacks the elite disruptive tendencies he used to have. By some measures, Donald is a bad defensive tackle relative to most starters. Unfortunately, the Rams don’t necessarily have any in-house upgrades to offset Donald’s snaps if he doesn’t improve. This is a unit lacking a presence by basically anyone else in the room with Donald. Other Rams defensive tackles Kobie Turner The second-worst pressure rate on the defense among defensive tackles belongs to Turner, at 6.1%. Turner has generated four pressures on 66 pass rush snaps. On the bright side, Turner does have an impressive 13 stops on 45 run defense snaps, but as a pass rusher he hasn’t offered anything yet. Turner entered 2026 averaging seven sacks per season and looking for a contract extension that will pay him like one of the best interior pass rushers in the NFL. However, L.A.’s hesitancy to extend him seems more obvious now because even his playing time is down to 62%. Most highly-paid defensive tackles don’t come off of the field more than one-third of the time. And yet Turner is by far the Rams’ best defensive tackle because him and Donald are the only two playing in more than 50% of the team’s defensive snaps. Braden Fiske Fiske has only played in 88 snaps, which is 49.2% of the team’s total. Following a rookie season with 8.5 sacks, Fiske has three sacks in his last 20 regular season games. He has a pressure rate of 7.8% (5 pressures, 64 pass rush snaps) but the devil is in the details: Fiske is not on the field for many obvious run situations: 75% of his snaps are in passing situations. The Rams traded a second-round pick to move up for Fiske in the second round and now he’s looking like a replacement level player without Florida State buddy Jared Verse. Winning games helps mask problems and it seems hard for many to admit that the Rams are one of the worst front offices in the NFL when it comes to managing their draft picks. Just imagine how many Super Bowls the Rams would win if they were good at drafting! Poona Ford Fan favorite Ford plays in only 38% of the snaps, which is because Ford is a detriment to any team’s pass rush. Out of 69 snaps, 45 are against the run. Ford has generated ZERO pressures on 24 pass defense snaps. As a run defender, he does have seven stops. But if I’m an offensive coordinator on third-and-three and I saw Poona Ford out there, I might just call a pass. Tyler Davis Nobody talks about Tyler Davis at all, even though he’s third on the team in total snaps among defensive tackles: Davis plays more than Ford. They probably don’t talk about him because he has not done much. Davis had a random seven tackle in Week 1, but only one tackle in the last two games. He has three pressures on 34 pass rush snaps. Davis is a type to come and go without any memories. Last season, he had a pressure rate of 7.3%. Ty Hamilton Hamilton has played 27 snaps, including 10 pass rush snaps. He has zero pressures. Rams total defensive line: 0 sacks Through three games, the Rams have three sacks: 1 by Wesley Bailey 1 by Byron Young 1 by Omar Speights Two of those sacks came against Jameis Winston and the New York Giants, not necessarily the most difficult assignment for a pass rusher. If you can even call Speights a pass rusher. (Which you can’t.) At first, the trade for Myles Garrett felt like it could be overkill. Now his absence is killing the Rams. Without Verse OR Garrett, the Rams have one of the worst pass rushing fronts in the NFL, hurt worse by the fact that the entire defensive tackle room is probably a bit too slow, not that overpowering, and isn’t getting the best coaching from Chris Shula to put them in a position to overachieve. As a unit, it’s a bad sign when Aaron Donald coming off of a two-year break is your best or second-best defensive tackle, and he’s not playing anything like the old Aaron Donald. QUINN MEINERZ BODY SLAMS AARON DONALD. WE HAVE NEVER SEEN A LINEMAN OWN DONALD LIKE THIS. 😳😳😳 pic.twitter.com/5aHcI7SFhM — MLFootball (@MLFootball) September 28, 2026 I don’t see how this group could get much better even after Garrett returns. Garrett may open up the defensive a little bit by commanding double-teams, but that only matters if you have players who can capitalize. Is that what you think of Fiske, Davis, and Hamilton? It’s not going to come from Ford. Will these results get better in a week? In a month? Who knows. L.A.’s next opponent, the Eagles, is not playing good ball so far this season and their offensive line is more vulnerable to interior pressure than they’ve been in years. The guards and centers don’t seem to be as good as the past. But aren’t Eagles fans saying the same thing on the opposite end? “Yeah, the Eagles offensive line sucks…but at least this week it’s the Rams!” Of course. You want to speculate about Aaron Donald and the Rams defensive line as a whole? Go for it. “They’ll be fine. They’ll bounce back. They’ll be great after he shakes the rust off.” There are plenty of “what ifs” and “just waits…” for those fans, and you know what…Maybe you’re right! But you want the truth? The only truth we have is what we’ve seen so far. And the truth is that the Rams do need to get better. The speculators must be proven right if the Rams defense is going to have any chance to stop the bleeding up front. Otherwise, the truth is that this is one of the worst defensive lines in the NFL.
author: Kenneth Arthur

title: Rams Power Rankings roundup: Week 4
summary: The LA Rams have dropped in most power rankings after losing to the Broncos on Sunday, but still linger around the edge of the top-10. After a dominant first half against Denver, three significant injuries before the second half flipped the script. Both the offense and defense struggled and the Rams surrendered a 16-point lead […]
full_text: The LA Rams have dropped in most power rankings after losing to the Broncos on Sunday, but still linger around the edge of the top-10. After a dominant first half against Denver, three significant injuries before the second half flipped the script. Both the offense and defense struggled and the Rams surrendered a 16-point lead to lose by four. Naturally, they dropped in all but one of the eight rankings listed. This sample of eight sites reflects the consensus, and the average ranking of these eight prognosticators is 8.5, up from last week’s 5.75. Pete Prisco : Dropped from 8 to 10 “The Dream Team is 1-2 after three weeks. So much for cruising to a Super Bowl. They need Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua back in the worst way.” Fox Sports Ralph Vacchiano : Dropped from 5 to 9 “They looked worn down against the Broncos, especially late in the game. They still are a top-10 team and might be even better once star defensive end Myles Garrett and WR Puka Nacua return.” NFL.com Nick Shook : Dropped from 8 to 13 “We’ve seen the Rams look flat (20-point loss to the 49ers in Australia), play like an elite team (22-point win over the Giants in Los Angeles) and collapse in a road game they led 16-0 at halftime (Sunday night’s defeat to the Broncos). It’s better to get these mistakes out of the way now, but we can all agree this isn’t how we expected L.A. to start its season.“ Mike Florio PFT: Up from 9 to 8 “With the Eagles and Bills coming up, the Rams need to flush Sunday night’s outcome quickly.” USA Today Nate Davis : Dropped from 4 to 6 “They probably got jobbed Sunday night, their 13 penalties − including five in the final two minutes − the most against them in Sean McVay’s 10-year tenure. They still nearly won … without WR Puka Nacua … without OLB Myles Garrett … with DL Aaron Donald producing four tackles and two pressures in two games … with a 1-for-4 red-zone night. It’s hardly time to panic here.“ SI Conor Orr : Dropped from 5 to 7 “If Myles Garrett is in that game are we talking about Denver erasing a 16-point deficit? The issue with the Rams is going to be patience as we wait for the team we were promised to finally materialize together. When Aaron Donald signed, I predicted it would look a little like trying to see the Dodgers at their playoff roster strength. That feels accurate a month into the season.“ Yahoo Sports Frank Schwab : Dropped from 4 to 6 “Dropping the Rams even this far doesn’t seem like it will age well. The Rams played on Sunday night at Denver, a team that is 16-4 in its last 20 games, and lost in the final minute after a bad defensive pass interference call. They were without two players who are arguably top 10 non-quarterbacks in the NFL, Myles Garrett and Puka Nacua. It was a reasonable loss. Check the Super Bowl betting odds: The Rams are still favorites at some books, or just behind the Bills. They’re 1-2 but don’t be fooled into thinking this isn’t a very good team. The Rams will be just fine.” NY Post Ryan Dunleavy : Dropped from 6 to 9 “The Rams suffered their largest blown halftime lead (16) points since 2001 in the loss to the Broncos. Matthew Stafford’s 33rd career interception returned for a touchdown — an NFL record — was a fourth-quarter killer. He threw for 390 yards — 137 of which went to Davante Adams. Josh Wallace had an interception — and could’ve had two if not for a controversial pass interference penalty.” Next Week: Philadelphia Eagles The Eagles are 2-1, having lost on Monday Night Football to the Chicago Bears, 27-7. But despite a winning record, both the offense and defense are having their struggles, as they are 23rd in scoring and 32nd in takeaways. Despite Philadelphia’s reputation, they are ripe for a Rams rebound.
author: John Newman

title: Could tight end injuries lead to debut of Rams rookie?
summary: Cornerback Jaylen Watson is not expected to play when the Los Angeles Rams face the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. The defensive back was carted off of the field on Sunday against the Denver Broncos when he dislocated his shoulder. Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed Watson and other injuries during his Monday press conference. […]
full_text: Cornerback Jaylen Watson is not expected to play when the Los Angeles Rams face the Philadelphia Eagles in Week 4. The defensive back was carted off of the field on Sunday against the Denver Broncos when he dislocated his shoulder. Rams head coach Sean McVay addressed Watson and other injuries during his Monday press conference . “He’ll probably be out for this week, and (it’s) something that we’ll see if we can kind of get him strengthened and harness it,” McVay said. “It’s something that he’s dealt with before, but not something that we’ve discussed, IR.” Watson signed a three-year, $51 million contract this offseason after playing his first four years in the league with the Chiefs. With Watson playing in the first half of the game, the Rams held the Broncos to 67 total yards and zero points. In the second half, with Watson on the sideline and his arm in a sling, the Broncos gained 197 yards and scored 30 points. Tight ends Colby Parkinson and Terrance Ferguson were also injured during Sunday’s loss to the Broncos. McVay said that Parkinson is day-to-day with a AC joint sprain in his shoulder. “We’ll see what that looks like for him,” McVay said. Ferguson has a medial ankle sprain and likely will miss Sunday’s game against the Eagles, per reports. This was an aggravation of an existing injury. Parkinson has played 61 percent of the team’s offensive snaps this season, and Ferguson 43 percent. The Rams’ run game suffered in the second half with Parkinson and Ferguson banged up. One interesting wrinkle to the tight end injuries is whether or not it could mean the debut of second-round rookie Max Klare this week. Klare has been a healthy scratch in all three games, but if Ferguson and Parkinson are both ruled out then he could be the next-best option for McVay’s 13 personnel. Coach McVay provides injury updates following Week 3. pic.twitter.com/KA9MTT015r — Los Angeles Rams (@RamsNFL) September 29, 2026 Puka Nacua, Kamren Kinchens updates: Two-time All-Pro WR Puka Nacua has missed the past two games with a lingering hip/groin issue, but McVay has hope that he will return to the team against the Eagles. “We’ll continue to see,” McVay said. “But if he is able to progress the way that we hope, there’s optimism that he’ll be able to play this week.” Here’s Puka Nacua working out on the side with a trainer during practice. pic.twitter.com/bNsaFPwe3p — Sarah Barshop (@sarahbarshop) September 25, 2026 The Rams sorely miss Puka’s presence on offense . Finally, Kamren Kinchens continues to rehabilitate his hamstring injury suffered during the 49ers game in Week 1 and his status is the one we don’t have any new information on from the coach.
author: John Newman

title: Jaylen Watson may be back for the Rams after Week 4
summary: Jaylen Watson appeared to be seriously hurt in Week 3 when he was helped to the sideline, and road a cart to the locker room, but apparently the Los Angeles Rams are not considering putting him on IR. Now, Watson’s injury may still be serious, but the good news for the Rams is that he […]
full_text: INGLEWOOD, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 21: Trent McDuffie #22, Jaylen Watson #35 and Quentin Lake #37 of the Los Angeles Rams celebrates a defensive stop against the New York Giants during the second quarter of the game at SoFi Stadium on September 21, 2026 in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jaylen Watson appeared to be seriously hurt in Week 3 when he was helped to the sideline, and road a cart to the locker room, but apparently the Los Angeles Rams are not considering putting him on IR. Now, Watson’s injury may still be serious, but the good news for the Rams is that he may be expected back sooner than later. It would be ideal for the Rams to see their team healthy with Myles Garrett, Puka Nacua and now Watson, but that hasn’t been the case. Instead, this team has been injured and their 1-2 record has been disappointing. The season isn’t over and the Rams haven’t looked helpless, but they’ve looked lesser in two out of three weeks. Hopefully the Rams get Watson and others back in time to make a push. Injury Updates: McVay says Terrance Ferguson (ankle) and Jaylen Watson (shoulder) likely out for Week 4 at Eagles; latest on Colby Parkinson (shoulder) and Puka Nacua (hip) (therams.com) “WOODLAND HILLS, Calif. – Rams head coach Sean McVay on Monday said cornerback Jaylen Watson sustained a dislocated shoulder in Sunday night’s loss to the Broncos. While Watson “probably” will miss this Sunday’s Week 4 road game against the Eagles, according to McVay, he will not be placed on Injured Reserve and that isn’t something they have talked about. “He’ll probably be out for this week, and (it’s) something that we’ll see if we can kind of get him strengthened and harness it,” McVay said. “It’s something that he’s dealt with before, but not something that we’ve discussed, IR.” Watson’s injury occurred around the 3:04 mark of the second quarter. He was carted back to the locker room after being evaluated in the medical tent. Prior to exiting with that injury, he had recorded two total tackles (one for loss) and two passes defensed.“ Rams get mixed bag update on Jaylen Watson after scary shoulder injury (sports.yahoo) “Rams head coach Sean McVay revealed Monday that Watson suffered a dislocated right shoulder late in the first half of Sunday night’s 30-26 loss to the Denver Broncos and will miss multiple games. There was at least one encouraging wrinkle: Los Angeles does not plan to place Watson on injured reserve, which would require him to miss a minimum of four games. McVay also indicated Watson has suffered a similar injury before.“ Rams Week 3 snap counts: How LA overcame several injuries vs. Broncos (ramswire) “The Los Angeles Rams suffered their second loss of the season on Sunday night, and this one was much different than the first. They blew a 16-point lead to the Denver Broncos , losing by a score of 30-26 on the road. Injuries have piled up for the Rams, forcing Sean McVay and Chris Shula to dip into their depth on each side of the ball. As a result, the snap counts look quite different than they did in Week 1 when Puka Nacua, Myles Garrett, Kamren Kinchens and Jaylen Watson were all fully healthy. Below is a breakdown of the playing time from Sunday night’s loss, including some separation at running back and a deeper rotation in the secondary.“ Broncos hang on to beat the Rams, who blow multiple leads and are a disappointing 1-2 to start this season (sports.yahoo) “Stafford has played a lot of football and he wasn’t fazed. He hit Konata Mumpfield for three straight completions, gains of 21, 9 and then a 48-yard touchdown to take back the lead. Mumpfield beat cornerback Riley Moss and was wide open downfield for Stafford’s pass. The Rams led 26-23. That just meant it was the Broncos’ turn to answer. Nix hit Bryant for 39 yards and Troy Franklin for 21, putting Denver in position to at least tie the game with a field goal. Two penalties, including a questionable one on Wallace, kept the drive alive. That led to the Nix touchdown, and the Rams couldn’t answer despite getting inside the red zone at the end. The Broncos are happy to be 2-1 after a rough Week 1 loss at Kansas City . The Rams aren’t quite as pleased with their start to the season.“ McVay, Rams won’t make excuses after pass interference call (espn.com) “[It] doesn’t really matter,” McVay said Monday. “It is what it is. That was the call that was made and there was a lot of opportunities that we had to be able to close the door on that game. … But I wouldn’t have any additional coaching points for how Josh [Wallace] plays through the cycle of the snap. But I’m not going to make excuses either and we’re not going to play the victim card.” The Rams were called for five penalties in the final two minutes of the fourth quarter, tied for the most by any team in a game since 2000, according to ESPN Research. Referee Bill Vinovich’s crew had thrown the second-fewest flags in the final two minutes of a game in the 2024 and ’25 seasons. The group threw only one flag in the last two minutes across the entire 2024 season.“ Terrance Ferguson Injury Could Force Rams to Change Their Offensive Identity (si.com) “The Los Angeles Rams received some injury updates on Monday following their loss on Sunday night to the Denver Broncos. During the game, tight end Terrance Ferguson left with an ankle injury while Colby Parkinson was clearly hampered. “Colby didn’t have any setbacks with his knee injury, but he did have an AC sprain to his shoulder. We’ll see what that looks like,” said head coach Sean McVay. “Terrance Ferguson had a medial sprain to his ankle. We’ll see what that looks like moving forward for him.” McVay: Medial ankle sprain for Terrance Ferguson (nbcsports) “Ferguson briefly departed after injuring his ankle in the team’s Sunday Night Football loss to the Broncos, returning for two snaps prior to departing again after his lone reception of the evening. The ankle injury now appears likely to cost the talented young tight end at least one game, with the potential for the absence to linger if the sprain is “more high than low.” McVay also relayed that fellow tight end Colby Parkinson suffered an AC sprain and is considered day-to-day. Veteran Tyler Higbee would be in line to operate as the primary receiving tight end after amassing 62 yards and a touchdown on eight receptions in Week 3, should both miss. Higbee should be added in all formats as a potential TE1 in the immediate future.“ NFL Week 3 Sunday aftermath: Tyler Loop’s heroics, Drake Maye concerns, Brock Purdy’s MVP form (nfl.com) “Football’s ability to inspire never ceases. Ravens kicker Tyler Loop rode a rocky path during his rookie campaign, culminating in a season-ending miss in the team’s Week 18 loss to the rival Steelers with the AFC North title (and the accompanying playoff berth) on the line. That pushed 44-yard kick attempt set in motion an offseason of change in Baltimore. Loop fended off questions about his future, keeping his job despite the immense fallout. A blocked attempt in Week 2’s disappointing loss to the Saints revived questions about the 2025 draft pick. Then, on Sunday in Rio de Janeiro, Loop got his shot to brush away the haze of the past. After the Ravens’ defense bowed up and kept Dallas out of the end zone late in the fourth quarter, seven seconds remained in 31-31 game. Lamar Jackson rocketed a missile that Zay Flowers leaped to snag for a 27-yard gain , with the receiver immediately getting down as Jackson called a timeout with 1 second remaining and the ball now at Dallas’ 38-yard line. Loop lined up the 56-yard attempt and calmly banged it through, with CBS Sports’ Jim Nantz eloquently calling the game-winning boot “a trio in Rio.” Ravens players celebrated with their sometimes-maligned kicker as they pulled off a last-second victory despite stumbles along the way.“ NFL news roundup: Jaycee Horn out indefinitely; Justin Jefferson, Breece Hall avoid serious injuries…

title: Malcolm Koonce comes alive in 4th quarter of Las Vegas Raiders’ Week 3 win over New Orleans Saints
summary: The outlook was looking grim for the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints. The Raiders began the fourth quarter down by five, and the Saints had the ball in scoring territory with about 13 minutes left on the clock. Then, defensive end Malcolm Koonce came up with a […]
full_text: (Photo by Jordon Kelly/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The outlook was looking grim for the Las Vegas Raiders in their Week 3 matchup against the New Orleans Saints . The Raiders began the fourth quarter down by five , and the Saints had the ball in scoring territory with about 13 minutes left on the clock. Then, defensive end Malcolm Koonce came up with a big strip-sack that led to a Las Vegas touchdown and a one-point lead after a failed two-point conversion. On the next possession, Koonce had a quarterback hit that resulted in New Orleans’ quarterback Tyler Shough’s pass floating up in the air and falling into the arms of cornerback Hezekiah Masses for another turnover. That set up an additional Silver and Black touchdown and what would be the final score in the 35-27 victory. In total, the edge rusher left the Big Easy with six pressures on 21 pass-rush snaps to earn the second-highest Week 3 pass-rush grade (pre -Monday Night Football , 91.6) at his position, per Pro Football Focus . He also had a pair of ‘ defensive stops ’ against the run, including stuffing an Alvin Kamara rush right at the line of scrimmage in the final frame, to be more than worthy of this week’s breakdown. While Malcolm Koonce had his biggest impact on the #Raiders win as a pass-rusher, he also had a handful of impressive reps against the run Great job using his hands to get extension on the block and cross the LT's face to make the tackle pic.twitter.com/rIdQe81rUd — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 28, 2026 While Koonce made his biggest impact as a pass-rusher last Sunday, he had a handful of quality reps against the run, too. This first clip doesn’t come from the fourth quarter, but it does serve as an example of how he affected New Orleans’ running game. The Saints come out in an I-formation with the tight end on the short side of the field. With Kwity Paye not being 100 percent while battling an illness in the days before the game, the Raiders were pretty consistent about putting Maxx Crosby on the strong side. New Orleans likely picked up on that and wanted to run at Koonce since he’s known as more of a pass-rusher, hence the formation. On top of that, the offense motions a wide receiver across the formation to get the linebackers to flow away from the play call, as they run inside zone to the weak side. That gets Nakobe Dean out of the B-gap, and the receiver in a reduced split is able to get inside positioning or cut off Taron Johnson (the nickelback), creating a rushing lane for the running back. However, Koonce does a great job of keeping his hands tight at the point of attack to get them on the left tackle’s chest. Then, he manages to get extension on the block with a long arm to cross the tackle’s face and make the play in the B-gap. While the Saints gain four yards on this play, it could have been much worse with no immediate defenders in the rushing lane. I don't think I've seen Malcolm Koonce have a better rep shedding a block than this… #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/Qj9kWqO0ZB — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 28, 2026 Here’s a look at the run stop against Kamara referenced above, and it’s a similar rep to the one we just dove into. The Saints are in the shotgun this time, and while he’s in a wide receiver stance, they put tight end Noah Fant on the short side of the field to dictate where Crosby lines up and run away from Crosby. Also, they’re running inside zone again, where Koonce is on the front side of the play and takes on a base block from the left tackle. While his hands aren’t as tight at the point of attack this time, I’ve been watching the 2021 third-round pick for his entire career and can’t remember a more violent or just overall better block shed from him. He uses his inside hand to execute a hump move and beat the tackle across the tackle’s face again, winning cleanly and meeting Kamara in the hole for no gain on third and one. Also, this was with about three minutes to go and the Raiders protecting an eight-point lead, and the very next play was Jermey Chinn’s strip sack that led to a turnover. Speed-to-power from Malcolm Koonce, and a good rep from Nakobe Dean, gets pressure on Tyler Shough and prevents Shough from finishing the throw on the deep shot to Vele #Raiders pic.twitter.com/dHFdOYxAiX — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 28, 2026 Moving onto Koonce’s pass-rush reps, we’re going to step outside of the fourth quarter again, diving into another impactful play that came late in the third quarter. It’s third and 10, and Shough has been the best deep-ball thrower in the NFL to begin the season. So, Kellen Moore dials up a shot play, and wide receiver Devaugh Vele has a step on Johnson. Meanwhile, Rob Leonard tries to scheme up a one-on-one opportunity for Crosby by running a simulated pressure out of a five-man front, where three down linemen are on Crosby’s side of the line. However, the Saints weren’t allowing him to have those opportunities, motioning the tight end inside to chip block Crosby before releasing on a flat route. The problem with that is it leaves their backup left tackle isolated against Koonce, with Dean blitzing and Kwity Pay dropping into coverage on the other side of the line. This is a situation where Koonce has to win his one-on-one matchup, especially against a shot play from the offense, and he does by turning speed into power to get pressure. Also, Dean does a great job of beating the running back to collapse the pocket. With two pass rushers at his feet, Shough can’t quite finish his throw and leaves it a little bit behind Vele, inviting Johnson back into the play to break up the pass for the third-down stop. Malcolm Koonce's strip sack -Leonard isolates the backup LT w/ a 6-man front, forcing OL to slide right -LBs blitz while DTs drop and Ni is a free rusher in B-gap -Koonce wins the 1on1 with a cross-chop around the edge for the sack #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/mpDY5QVOAK — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 28, 2026 This time, Leonard schemes up a one-on-one opportunity for Koonce, and the pass-rusher justifies the coach’s decision/play call. The Raiders come out in a six-man front with linebackers Quay Walker and Dean walked up on the line of scrimmage. They have four pass rush threats on the right side of the line, forcing four out of five offensive linemen to slide right while the running back inserts into the B-gap to pick up Dean. That isolates the left tackle, who is filling in after starter Kelvin Banks suffered an injury the week before, against Koonce. Post-snap, Walker and Dean blitz, while the two defensive tackles (Tonka Hemingway and Adam Butler) drop into coverage and Johnson is the free rusher in the B-gap. Additionally, Koonce gets a quick win with a cross-chop and shows off his bend to take an efficient path to the quarterback, nailing Shough from behind as Shough rears back to throw for the sack fumble. We also found out that Crosby likely didn’t play much baseball growing up (or at least wasn’t a good infielder) as he struggles to pick up the fumble! But hey, no harm, no foul, as he still recovers for the turnover off an excellent rep from his running mate. The Malcolm Koonce pressure to Hezekiah Masses INT -Koonce wins w/ a long-arm to hit Shough on the release -Good rep in Cover 2 from Masses to sink, protect the hole shot & track the ball in the air #RaiderNation pic.twitter.com/PE0zJn0sOk — Matt Holder (@MHolder95) September 28, 2026 We’ll wrap up with the pressure to interception that led to Vegas’ eight-point lead, and I included the sideline angle to highlight a good rep from Masses, too. Leonard does a good job of disguising the coverage by having Johnson follow Chris Olave across the formation when Olave motions, giving the indication they defense is playing man. Additionally, the Raiders are in a single-high or Cover 1 look pre-snap. However, they rotate into Cover 2 post-snap, where Johnson bluffs being the Tampa droper to get the…

title: Touchdown machine Cody White promoted to 53-man roster
summary: Cody White has become somewhat of a folk hero in these parts. And now he is a full-fledged member of the Las Vegas Raiders. In an expected move, the Raiders announced Tuesday that they have promoted White from the practice squad to a spot on the 53-man roster. To make room for White, second-year wide […]
full_text: . (Photo by Harry How/Getty Images) | Getty Images Cody White has become somewhat of a folk hero in these parts. And now he is a full-fledged member of the Las Vegas Raiders. In an expected move, the Raiders announced Tuesday that they have promoted White from the practice squad to a spot on the 53-man roster. To make room for White, second-year wide receiver Jack Bech was placed on the injured reserve. Bech broke his forearm. He must miss, at least, four games, but such injuries could extend beyond that timeframe. White was signed to the practice after he was cut by the Seattle Seahawks just before the season started. He was with with Raiders head coach Klint Kubiak last season. White was elevated for the first three games, which is the limited for practice squad players. So, this move was coming. White has three catches this season —- all for touchdowns. He has also be a playmaker on special teams. Bech, a second-round pick last season, has five catches for 48 yards this season. This season is big for his development, so this injury is a setback for the young receiver. Also Tuesday, the Raiders signed veteran receiver Philip Dorsett to the practice squad and released receiver Justin Shorter. Monday, they added receiver Tyler Scott to the practice squad. Dorsett was with the Raiders in training camp.

title: Las Vegas Raiders surging in Week 4 NFL Power Rankings with hot 3-0 start
summary: There were plenty of reasons to doubt the Las Vegas Raiders heading into the 2026 NFL season. However, sitting as one of five undefeated teams through September, the Raiders are impossible to ignore at this stage! As a result, the Silver and Black have shot up the Week 4 NFL Power Rankings. The Athletic 12. […]
full_text: (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) | Getty Images There were plenty of reasons to doubt the Las Vegas Raiders heading into the 2026 NFL season. However, sitting as one of five undefeated teams through September, the Raiders are impossible to ignore at this stage ! As a result, the Silver and Black have shot up the Week 4 NFL Power Rankings. The Athletic 12. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 22 QB confidence: Good — for now Kirk Cousins is tied for the league lead in touchdown passes with nine, and Las Vegas is unbeaten. What’s not to love? The schedule, for starters. After playing three teams with a combined one win, the Raiders have the Chiefs, Patriots, Bills and Rams up next. Cousins is 38, in Year 15 of his career and knows he was signed as a placeholder for No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza. If Cousins or his team falls off this pace, fans will start clamoring for the new guy. — Josh Kendall, Chad Graff It’s kind of funny that the Raiders’ win against the 1-2 Saints isn’t viewed as impressive, but the 1-2 Patriots and 1-2 Rams are viewed as a gantlet in the schedule. Don’t get me wrong, I agree that New England and Los Angeles are better than their early record indicates and are going to be tough matchups. But those two teams also have blowout losses on their resumes, while the only other blemish for New Orleans is a one-point loss in overtime to Detroit. As for Cousins, the analysis isn’t wrong; he is a placeholder for Mendoza. But give Captain Kirk credit. He’s playing well and silencing any calls for the rookie right now. ESPN 14. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 Fantasy surprise: RB Ashton Jeanty Jeanty got off to a strong start, recording 32.7 fantasy points in a Week 1 win over the Dolphins. But he has been inconsistent since then, averaging fewer than 3 yards per carry and 11.3 fantasy points in the past two games. Jeanty was expected to make a significant jump in Year 2 under new coach Klint Kubiak. His production should pick up if he gets more opportunities in the passing game, though Brock Bowers just returned for the Raiders from a meniscus trim. — Ryan McFadden For some context, Jeanty had 54 yards after contact to record just 48 rushing yards (meaning he was getting hit at or behind the line of scrimmage frequently) against the Chargers, per Pro Football Focus . So, I can blame that game on the offensive line. However, he had just 35 yards after contact to record 56 rushing yards last week, shifting the blame to the running back. The 2025 first-round pick didn’t have the same explosiveness and lateral movement skills that he normally shows, and the broadcast mentioned Jeanty had to get his ankle re-taped in New Orleans. That combination leads me to believe he reaggravated the sprained ankle he suffered at the end of training camp. Regardless, I think we should expect to see more touches for Mike Washington Jr., as Klint Kubiak said during a presser this week. NFL.com 10. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 22 Sure, I might be overreacting to the Raiders’ hot start, but how can I pass on the rare opportunity to push the Silver and Black into the top 10? Klint Kubiak has inspired this previously downtrodden franchise, and Las Vegas is playing a wildly entertaining brand of football built on contributions from both established (Kirk Cousins, Brock Bowers) and unknown players (fifth-round rookie Hezekiah Masses has three interceptions this season!). — Nick Shook Whatever credit Kubiak has received for the hot start/quick turnaround isn’t enough. How many coaches have come in and said they were going to change the Raiders’ culture, only to fall flat on their faces and get the same terrible results? Kubiak may not say much, but that’s because he does his talking on the field! Bleacher Report 11. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 20 At 3-0, the Las Vegas Raiders have already matched their entire win total from last season. It’s amazing how different a team can look thanks to organizational competency. It’s only the second time since 2002 this franchise opened a season with three straight wins. Are the Raiders legit, though? Obviously, the Miami Dolphins and Los Angeles Chargers aren’t good. The New Orleans Saints are highly competitive, but Kellen Moore’s squad has found ways to lose during his time as head coach. Next week’s matchup against the Kansas City Chiefs will provide a true test. Las Vegas should be ready for its upcoming matchup now that Brock Bowers is back. Much like Travis Kelce, Bowers isn’t an ordinary tight end. He’s the Raiders’ No. 1 target, as evidenced by 10 catches for 116 yards upon his return to the lineup. — Brent Sobleski The “true test” narrative has been discussed with Las Vegas every week since the season opener and is getting exhausting. To be fair, it is true. The Raiders have been facing a tougher opponent every week, and the Chiefs are one of the four other undefeated teams in the league right now. At this point, all the Raiders can do is continue to pass the exams and rack up wins. Sports Illustrated 9. Las Vegas Raiders Last week: 21 The Raiders are getting their Mariah Carey moment in this week’s power rankings. Every year, Carey peaks on the Billboard charts and we celebrate her arrival and understand her departure without judgement. Las Vegas has earned its moment here after a third shape-shifting victory, this time over the Saints. Brock Bowers is the most imposing receiver we’ve seen since peak A.J. Brown. — Conor Orr I can live with the schedule and test talk, but this is certainly a backhanded compliment. I get that the Chiefs are favored and have the track record to earn the benefit of the doubt, but can the Raiders lose a game before we start trying to predict their downfall? I appreciate Orr putting them in the top 10. However, the Mariah Carey comparison is certainly an attempt to “try to bring [the Raiders] down”.

title: Rookies Mike Washington, Zeke Masses come up big in Week 3 win
summary: Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints and what to look for Sunday at home against the Kansas City Chiefs: Fernando Mendoza:The No. 1 overall pick served […]
full_text: (Photo by Morgan Simmons/Getty Images) | Getty Images Here is a look at how the Las Vegas Raiders’ 2026 draft class (eight of the 10 picks are on the 53-man roster) fared in a 35-27 Week 3 win at the New Orleans Saints and what to look for Sunday at home against the Kansas City Chiefs: Fernando Mendoza: The No. 1 overall pick served as Kirk Cousins backup. He did not play. But he’s on a streak. Mendoza hasn’t been part of a team that has lost since 2024. Treydan Stukes: The Raiders’ second-round pick was out because of a concussion he suffered in Week 2. He is expected to be back this week and the Raiders need him against Travis Kelce. Trey Zuhn: The third-round pick played five offensive plays after playing two plays in Week 2. He was even lined up in an H-back role Sunday. Coach Klint Kubiak is finding ways to get his players involved. Jermod McCoy: The fourth-round pick played 12 special teams snaps, but none on defense. He played 18 defensive snaps in Week 2. Mike Washington: The fourth-round pick played 16 percent of the snaps after playing 19 percent of the snaps in the first two games. Washington made his snaps count as he had a 36-yard touchdown run in the third quarter to get the Raiders back in the game as they finished the game with 19 unanswered points. He has 102 rushing yards on 15 carries. Dalton Johnson: The fifth-round pick safety was a healthy scratch for the third straight game. Him being inactive with Stukes out isn’t a great sign. Zeke Masses: The fifth-round pick is now a clear starting cornerback. He started for an injured Darien Porter in Week 2. Porter was healthy in Week 3 and Masses still started. Masses made a big interception in the fourth quarter at the Saints and he has three interceptions in the past two games. He’s an exciting playmaker. Malik Benson: The sixth-round pick played four offensive snaps and two on special teams. He was targeted once with no catches and had one punt return for 13 yards.

Barry Jackson from the Miami Herald took a look at the change among the safeties and Hafley’s explanation: Safety Julius Wood playing nine snaps in a nickel/corner role for the first time. And Michael Taaffe and Dante Trader Jr. played all the snaps at safety after sharing time with Zayne Anderson during the first two games. Anderson, who started the opener at safety, played only on special teams. “We felt good the way Trader was playing, the way Taaffe was playing to keep them rolling,” Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley said. “The way those guys practiced last week and the communication between those two and having the same two out there constantly communicating and talking and practicing with one another, we just felt like that was the best way to kind of try to get the communication where we needed to be and I thought they did a really good job. Miami signed linebacker Shaka Heyward off of the Cincinnati Bengals’ practice squad. The move immediately adds Heyward to the Dolphins’ 53-man roster where he must remain for a minimum of three weeks according to NFL rules. Heyward — 26 years old — is the cousin of Cameron Heyward (Pittsburgh Steelers) and Connor Heyward (Las Vegas Raiders). He played in 18 games with the Bengals over the past two seasons — recording eight tackles on defense (three solo), including one tackle for loss, adding 14 special teams tackles (six solo) and one special teams forced fumble. The Dolphins also signed guard James Ester to their practice squad. Ester was previously with the Dolphins this summer after he was awarded to the team off of waivers following his release from the Green Bay Packers. A former defensive tackle in college at Northern Illinois, Ester spent his first two seasons in the NFL on Green Bay’s practice squad. title: Chiefs vs. Dolphins reactions: Tuesday Thoughts With The Earl
summary: The Dolphins lose again and fall to 0-3.  Here are my thoughts after a quick watch of the game. POSITIVES APLENTY IN THE GAME This game went as expected and yet… not as expected.  The steady descent to 0-17 appeared to be slowing down as the Dolphins looked like merely a bad team and not […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Miami Dolphins wide receiver Chris Bell (18) celebrates a reception as Kansas City Chiefs cornerback Mansoor Delane (5) looks on during a NFL game between the Kansas City Chiefs and the Miami Dolphins, on Sunday September 27, 2026, at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, FL.(Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Dolphins lose again and fall to 0-3. Here are my thoughts after a quick watch of the game. POSITIVES APLENTY IN THE GAME This game went as expected and yet… not as expected. The steady descent to 0-17 appeared to be slowing down as the Dolphins looked like merely a bad team and not the worst team ever assembled in the history of ever. The final score was both indicative and not indicative of how the game actually played out. Losing 24-10 looks bad in the box score, and it never really felt like they had a REAL chance to win. But the Dolphins were only down 17-10 with over 11 minutes left in the 4th quarter and had the ball at that point. Things didn’t turn out well, but the situation was not out of control like it had been in the previous 2 games. By the time the 3rd quarter ended in the first 2 games, the Dolphins had given up 27 points and 35 points respectively and the game was effectively over before the final period of the game. This game was still competitive. At least in the box score. Perhaps part of that was being at home. Perhaps they are starting to play a little better. Whatever it is, the Dolphins looked like maybe things could be starting to turn around. There were still some hiccups, such as the fumble deep in the opponent’s territory that could have yielded points. But the Dolphins still moved the ball, with 329 yards of offense, going 8-16 on 3rd down – 50% would be 8th in the league and the Dolphins are currently 12th at 41.5% – and gaining 19 first downs. Chris Bell stepped up in the absence of Caleb Douglas, with 4 catches for 67 yards. Malik Willis moved the ball on the ground well, picking up key yards for the Dolphins to extend drives. The Dolphins did not allow a sack for the first time all season. All of this is still a work in progress, but maybe, just maybe, it’s starting to turn around and things are starting to click. COACHING DECISIONS ARE STILL QUESTIONABLE After just one quick watch, I can’t tell you with certainty about all the play calls. There were a lot of screens and deep passes, and still not very many easy completions to be had. However, I CAN tell you with certainty that the worst coaching decision came before the game was ever played. You entered this game with 2 healthy running backs and the practice squad elevations were for a defensive end that played 8 defensive snaps and a backup linebacker that played 11 special teams snaps. Meanwhile, you lost your starting RB early on, forcing you to play with 1 healthy RB, who also missed snaps due to cramping, and forcing you to either use a WR at RB (more on that later) or throw the ball more. That is terrible decision making. The Dolphins traded for Jarquez Hunter and he remained on the PS, despite the fact they needed depth at the position before a snap was taken. This is terrible decision making and terrible planning. He or Carlos Washington Jr. will likely be added to the roster now that Achane is going to IR. This wasn’t the only issue I have with coaching. Yeah, the Dolphins held Mahomes and the Chiefs to 17 points until late in the 4th quarter. That has to count for something, right? Well, I have another issue and that is with the number 6. As is 6 is the total amount of incompletions the Dolphins have allowed in the last 2 games. The Dolphins tightened up on the run game, allowing 3.5 YPC and only 88 total rushing yards, despite Walker having a 22-yard run in that equation. But the defense simply cannot keep allowing QBs to complete passes at will against a softer than Charmin defense. The Dolphins were able to generate some pressure in this game despite not getting a sack. Mahomes is renowned for being able to make stuff happen off-script, but it is pitch-and-catch for everyone. Even past-his-prime Kirk Cousins only had 9 incompletions in 30 attempts. Both the Chiefs and 49ers had guys wide open all the time. It was sickening. Thankfully, the Dolphins get a QB this week that is not in the upper echelon of throwers. But if they allow Murray or Wentz to get completion after completion, then something needs to change. Maybe it’s the playcalling. Maybe it’s the playcaller. But allowing only 6 incompletions in 2 games is simply unacceptable. Incompletions can turn into much needed stops the defense has produced too few of this season. THIS AND THAT Speaking of pitch-and catch, Willis made some good plays, but he is also throwing into tight windows WAY too much. All the opponents have wide open guys. The Dolphins players are easily covered at all times. Washington and Coleman are small, slower players that are struggling to get separation. Bell has some skills but is still developing and getting back into shape. Perhaps Douglas would have made a difference in this game, but regardless, the Dolphins need pass catchers that can get open without needing scheme to do it. Malik Washington has his limitations, but his ability to generate yards after contact and force missed tackles makes him perfect for getting touches out of the backfield. I’m not suggesting running him 15 times a game. But 5-6 carries as a running back? Why not? Until it becomes ineffective, why not mix things up a bit? It would also allow for some unique plays that could for conflict on the defense. I hate the penalty on Chop Robinson. I’m not just saying that because it happened to a Dolphins player. The Dolphins were the beneficiary of the same call last week. The problem is that plays like that are so “bang-bang” that it’s nearly impossible for players to completely cease their momentum that quickly. It’s nearly impossible for players to change their trajectory that quickly. Remember when William Hayes injured himself against the Raiders in 2018 as he was trying to avoid landing on the QB? That flag should never have been thrown because the rule is stupid. I get the NFL wants to protect the QB. But it has gotten out of hand. Chop would have needed to decipher that the ball was out of Mahomes hand and eased off within less than a second; likely half a second or less. What if he does and Mahomes tucks the ball back and runs for a first down? Like how he has acted like he would run out of bounds, the defender would ease up, and then he’d get a couple more yards? Do the officials and the league care that the defender was “trying to ease up”? The easy solution: two-hand touch for a defender on the QB in the pocket. This keeps the QBs healthy as they will not be thrown to the ground. It eliminates the need for a defender to ease up because all he’ll have to do is put both hands on the QB. It eliminates the stupid “in the grasp” rule that allows QBs to escape a sack where a defender has him wrapped up. If the QB leaves the pocket, then he’s fair game. But in the pocket, it’s two-hand touch. It’s weak sauce IMO, but if that’s what the league wants, then my solution is the best. The 2017 Dolphins offense was the worst I have seen in many years. It’s the only the 3rd time since the horrid 2007 1-15 season where the Dolphins have scored fewer than 300 points (273 in 2010, 288 in 2012, and 281 in 2017). Those bad offenses averaged at least 17 points per game. The current Dolphins have scored 36 points and are averaging 12 points per game. That’s on pace for 204 total points, which would be the lowest in team history save for the strike shortened season of 1982 (198 points – 22 PPG). 12 PPG is 2.2 PPG less than last season’s worst offense, the Las Vegas Raiders. You have to go back to the 2009 season to find such ineptitude with the Rams averaging 10.9 PPG that season. The Dolphins are moving the ball…

title: Miami Dolphins’ Most Valuable Player | Week Three | Protection is key
summary: The Miami Dolphins didn’t defeat the Kansas City Chiefs in week three — they lost 24-10 — but they held their own against one of the best teams in the National Football League for much of the contest. It’s a moral victory for a team that has struggled through three weeks of the 2026 NFL […]
full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - AUGUST 20: Miami Dolphins center Aaron Brewer (55) speaks to the media during a New York Giants and Miami Dolphins joint practice at the Miami Dolphins Training Camp on August 20 2026, at the Baptist Health Training Complex in Miami Gardens, FL. (Photo by Doug Murray/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The Miami Dolphins didn’t defeat the Kansas City Chiefs in week three — they lost 24-10 — but they held their own against one of the best teams in the National Football League for much of the contest. It’s a moral victory for a team that has struggled through three weeks of the 2026 NFL season. If Miami continue to show incremental improvement as the year rolls on, the foundation that new general manager Jon-Eric Sullivan and new head coach Jeff Hafley have talked about wanting to establish will prove beneficial to future versions of Dolphins teams. One area the Dolphins needed to show improvement in was protecting the quarterback. Malik Willis had been sacked nine times through Miami’s first two games — 5 times against the Raiders in week one and 4 times against the 49ers in week two. Against the Chiefs, improvement was made — as Willis wasn’t sacked a single time on the afternoon. Miami Dolphins Week Three MVP – OC Aaron Brewer A major reason why Willis was able to avoid Kansas City’s pass rush was the play of Miami’s starting center Aaron Brewer. Brewer was the Dolphins’ highest graded offensive lineman by Pro Football Focus in week three — earning a 72.6 overall grade. Obviously Brewer did not give up a sack against the Chiefs — no one did — but through three games in 2026, Brewer has not allowed an opposing defender to bring his quarterback down a single time. With running back De’Von Achane being lost for the season due to an ACL tear, the Dolphins will need every single remaining healthy player to take a step forward if they want to continue make positive developments in 2026. Brewer is now Miami’s most impactful offensive player. His play this season will go a long way towards determining how many notches the Dolphins can put in the win column in 2026 and beyond. MVP TRACKER Week One – WR Caleb Douglas Week Two – LB Jacob Rodriguez Week Three – OC Aaron Brewer
