title: On the McCarthy Trade and Week 3 Observations
summary: NOTE: This article was 90% complete when the news broke that J.J. McCarthy had been traded to the New York Giants for a 2027 5th-round pick. My thoughts on the trade? Glad you didn’t ask. Not a fan. Nah, I hate it. Why? Let me count the ways: First, it’s official: we’ve now blown through […]
full_text: NOTE: This article was 90% complete when the news broke that J.J. McCarthy had been traded to the New York Giants for a 2027 5th-round pick. My thoughts on the trade? Glad you didn’t ask. Not a fan. Nah, I hate it. Why? Let me count the ways: First, it’s official: we’ve now blown through three 1st-round QBs in 15 years. It makes me sick. Now we have zero QBs signed for next season. Wonderful. What’s the strategy? If Kyler Murray turns it around and looks like 2018 Patrick Mahomes, what’s the guarantee he’ll come back? The Vikings are highly leveraged, with top contracts across other premier positions. If he continues to struggle, at 3-0 already, we likely won’t be in a position to select any of the top QBs available. Flores’ defense is playing at a remarkable, lights-out level, and we’d win at least two to three more games with me at QB. We are the Vikings, so anything is possible, but it’s extremely unlikely. Obviously, Carson Wentz is not the long-term solution. In other news, Kirk Cousins is over there leading the NFL in touchdown passes for the freakin’ 3-0 Raiders with a 107.2 QB rating. Yay! Second, it appears to confirm that Kevin O’Connell didn’t want McCarthy in the first place and that it was solely a Kwesi Adofo-Mensah decision. Despite feel-good PR quotes to the contrary, KOC apparently believes young QBs can, in fact, fail organizations. The “QB competition” in training camp now looks like a ploy to keep McCarthy’s trade value high in case a starting QB went down before the season, and a team grew desperate. When that didn’t happen, there was no choice but to drop him behind Wentz because the games would begin to count. What other conclusion can one draw? If he had any confidence that McCarthy could be the answer, why would he give up on a 23-year-old on a rookie contract for potentially two more seasons? To show how naïve I was, I actually believed the plan was to ride with Murray in 2026 as McCarthy developed, and then, short of a magical run to at least the NFC Championship Game, hand it back to a (finally) prepared McCarthy in 2027. McCarthy would be on the trading block only if Murray proved himself and signed an extension. Not one of my better takes. Third, am I imagining that, despite the developmental hiccups, McCarthy was 6-4 as a starter and that the road games against the Lions and Cowboys last year happened? The home game against the Commanders? The 4th-quarter comeback against the Bears? Were there no things to build on? Jayden Daniels can’t stay on the field. Drake Maye’s play so far in Year 3 looks like last year could have been a mirage, aided by a historically cupcake schedule. Are the Commanders and Patriots giving up on them? Let me conclude this rant by quoting… myself. Giving up after 10 starts would be incredibly misguided. If he goes on to become a great quarterback for another team and we’re back to square one in five years with no Super Bowl appearances, it could fracture a large part of the long-time fan base. That could be the final straw for those whose scars go back several decades. How much suffering can the human spirit endure? The Vikings seem to exist to answer that question. Best of luck in New York, J.J. McCarthy. We now return to our regularly scheduled programming. Week 3 Observations: Mixed Emotions Is this another 2016 or 2017? The Minnesota Vikings went 3-0 on Sunday, thanks to Brian Flores’ dominant defense and strong special teams. The offense was apparently there, too. As noted, a win is a win. There are no gimmes in the NFL, especially on the road, and the Buccaneers are a talented and dangerous team. It felt great to start 3-0, but that high quickly gave way to the creeping dread only Minnesota Vikings fans know. Winning like this isn’t sustainable, even though Flores and company will clearly try. About 10 minutes after the post-win high wore off, my tortured Vikings memory bank instantly transported me back to 2016, for good reason. Strong defense, quarterback chaos, and a 5-0 start. The record was smoke and mirrors, as we became just the seventh team in NFL history to start 5-0 and miss the playoffs. Of course, one of them was the 2003 Vikings, who went 6-0 and accomplished the unthinkable. I’d take those Shaun Hill-Sam Bradford offenses at this point, though. I quickly took that memory, crammed it into the smallest container I could find, and placed the heaviest object I could carry on top of it to ensure it never, ever escaped again. Then I do what I always do: convince myself otherwise. Sometimes reality comes along for the ride. In this case, it wasn’t difficult. I fast-forwarded a year to 2017. There was a strong defense and early quarterback chaos, but everything was just fine – well, for the rest of the season, anyway. A 13-3 record and a first-round playoff bye. After Sunday’s game, I’m torn about which direction this team is headed – and I hate it. Let’s recap it all. THE UTTERLY AMAZING The Flores defense. Listen, I’m not going to heap more praise on Flores and the defensive unit because that would be impossible. The numbers are the numbers: 1st in sacks, 1st in QB hits, 1st in fewest points per drive, 1st in DVOA, and 1st in EPA. Only 13.7 points allowed per game against three Pro Bowl-caliber QBs. The scariest part? The two long scoring plays Flores’ unit has allowed – the Christian Watson play in Week 1, and the Ted Hurst play on Sunday – stemmed from miscommunications that should be easy to fix moving forward. One reason for optimism, given the historical comparisons above, is that while those Mike Zimmer defenses were great, this is on another level. I’ve never seen a Vikings defense this dominant. I was entering my teenage years in the late ’80s, so maybe I am shortchanging those excellent units, but I think we are in uncharted territory post-Purple People Eaters. Oh, and there’s this… By the way, the Vikings' defense costs $94.1 million in 2026 — the sixth-lowest figure in the NFL. https://t.co/5BTD9uFlBH — Alec Lewis (@alec_lewis) September 28, 2026 Will Reichard, hero. “Kudos, my hero/Leaving all the best/You know my hero/The one that’s on/There goes my hero/Watch him as he goes” – Foo Fighters. THE GOOD Myles Price and the Special Teams. Special teams coach Matt Daniels has the unit cooking, ranking 2 nd in the NFL in EPA while flying all over the field. Myles Price was the difference yesterday and is playing like an All-Pro after three weeks. We all know how amazing the baby-faced assassin with the stellar hair has been. Let’s hope the all-around great play continues. The insurance policy offseason strategy. That’s what I called the front office’s actions last spring. This is a loaded roster that went 9-8 last season, despite arguably having the worst quarterback play in the NFL. This team needed insurance, and not the kind Flo the Progressive lady peddles on television. First, they needed to bring Flores back at all costs. Second, they needed a deep enough quarterback room to weather any storm, so Carson Wentz was brought back. We’re 3-0 thanks to those two prescient moves. Third, they brought in Jauan Jennings to cover for an injury to Justin Jefferson or Jordan Addison. Well, we are there. Although we avoided the worst-case scenario with Jefferson’s ankle injury, the safe bet may be to sit him against the 0-3 Dolphins. I remember Adam Thielen rushed back from a high ankle sprain in 2021, and it didn’t go well. Making sure he’s 100% for the post-bye gauntlet of @Det, Bills, @Packers, and @49ers should be the priority. While Jennings hasn’t factored in the offense yet, he shouldered the #1 workload in 2024 after injuries in San Francisco. Jordan Addison proved he can be a #1 in 2023 when Jefferson hurt his hamstring. You could do a lot worse than Addison-Jennings or Jefferson-Jennings if the injury bug bites again this season. THE BAD Kyler Murray so far. After one full game and 11 snaps in another, Murray is completing only 53% of his passes for 186 yards, 5.5 YPA,…

McCarthy as the inactive third quarterback on game days. Also announced were releases of running backs Jaret Patterson and Jerome Ford from the practice […]

(Photo by Julio Aguilar/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings announced a handful of roster moves on Tuesday afternoon: One move announced in this batch was Max Brosmer signing to the active roster, essentially replacing the traded J.J. McCarthy as the inactive third quarterback on game days. Also announced were releases of running backs Jaret Patterson and Jerome Ford from the practice squad, along with defensive lineman Jonathan Harris. Johnny Hekker’s contract was terminated, suggesting Brett Thorson is on track to play Sunday against Miami after missing Week 2 in Tampa Bay with a hamstring issue. It’s worth keeping an eye out to see if Hekker re-signs to the practice squad as an insurance policy — especially since the Vikings released three practice squad guys (and bumped up Brosmer) but only signed one (linebacker Kenny Dyson) in return. Josh Oliver is going on injured reserve after surgery to repair a torn biceps, and the injury could be season-ending. The Vikings are a little thin at tight end behind T.J. Hockenson and Gavin Bartholomew, though they could elevate Cam Grandy from the practice squad for added depth. Edge defender Kyle Van Noy was officially signed to the active roster after using up his three practice squad elevations, and the 13th-year man out of BYU has been a pleasant surprise for the Vikings so far. One move not listed but reported by Jordan Schultz was the signing of former Saints running back Devin Neal. Sources: The #Vikings are signing former #Saints RB Devin Neal to a contract. Just 23 years old and a 5th-round pick last year, Neal totaled 310 yards and 2 TDs as a rookie. He joins a Minnesota team that has been seeking RB depth. pic.twitter.com/Ouup84YB0i — Jordan Schultz (@Schultz_Report) September 29, 2026 Neal was drafted as a possible Alvin Kamara replacement in the sixth round last season and did find his way into 10 games, rushing 57 times for 206 yards and two touchdowns while adding 17 receptions on 19 targets for 104 yards. Neal was a dynamic dual-threat out of the Kansas backfield in college, rushing for 1,000 yards in three straight seasons from 2022-24 while also adding at least 20 receptions in each of those seasons. The second-year back was waived off New Orleans’ injured reserve list in early September as part of an injury settlement, four days after he was placed on IR with the injury in the first place. With Jordan Mason on injured reserve, Aaron Jones Sr. banged up and averaging just 3.9 yards per carry and Demond Claiborne still in the early stages of his rookie season, it’s not surprising to see the Vikings cast a look for help in the backfield. Neal had some steam as a riser in the pre-draft process, and he’ll now battle DeeJay Dallas for reps in a surprisingly thin Vikings backfield. full_text: MIAMI GARDENS, FL - OCTOBER 16: Justin Jefferson #18 of the Minnesota Vikings catches a pass over Xavien Howard #25 of the Miami Dolphins during the third quarter of an NFL football game at Hard Rock Stadium on October 16, 2022 in Miami Gardens, Florida. (Photo by Kevin Sabitus/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Minnesota Vikings return to U.S. Bank Stadium in Week 4 after a couple of weeks on the road as they host the Miami Dolphins in their first interconference matchup of the 2026 NFL season. The Vikings have gotten off to a 3-0 start on their season, with their most recent win coming over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers last week on the road as they brought home a 23-16 win. Kyler Murray made his return at quarterback, but Justin Jefferson went out after the first drive of the game with an ankle injury and did not return. The Minnesota offense struggled for much of the afternoon, but thanks in large part to the defense and the special teams, they brought a victory back to the Twin Cities and will look to keep their undefeated start going this Sunday. Miami, on the other hand, has gotten off to a rough start to their 2026 campaign, dropping their first three games. The Dolphins, led by new quarterback Malik Willis, have yet to top 13 points in any of their three games this season and have seen all three losses come by double digits. Adding to their woes is the loss of their best offensive player, running back Devon Achane, who suffered a torn ACL in their Week 3 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs and will miss the remainder of the season. The three teams the Dolphins have played this season (the Las Vegas Raiders, the San Francisco 49ers, and the Kansas City Chiefs) are all 3-0 going into Week 4, as are the Vikings. Minnesota is a significant favorite going into Sunday’s game, with the line already swelling to the Vikings being a 10.5-point favorite. Jefferson’s status is unknown at this point, as an MRI showed that he avoided any serious damage and he could be a game-time decision on Sunday afternoon. At the very least, we may not know his status until the final injury reports come out on Friday afternoon. Kickoff for this Sunday’s game is set for 3:05 PM Central, which willl again put it into the late window of NFL action, and the game will be carried by the FOX family of networks. We will be putting all of our stories about this week’s game in this stream for you to find more easily, so keep your eyes right here for all the latest. title: Vikes Views: Nincompoop of the Week – Week 3 Vikings at Buccaneers
summary: Your Minnesota Vikings went on the road to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-16. 3-0 never felt so unsatisfying, so if you’re not done complaining yet, let’s talk about who was terrible this past Sunday. Kyler Murray Murray being on this list might be a little harsh, but it’s the NFL. Murray’s start to his […]
full_text: MINNEAPOLIS, MINNESOTA - SEPTEMBER 13: General manger Nolan Teasley of the Minnesota Vikings looks on before a game against the Green Bay Packers at U.S. Bank Stadium on September 13, 2026 in Minneapolis, Minnesota. (Photo by Stephen Maturen/Getty Images) | Getty Images Your Minnesota Vikings went on the road to defeat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, 23-16. 3-0 never felt so unsatisfying, so if you’re not done complaining yet, let’s talk about who was terrible this past Sunday. Kyler Murray Murray being on this list might be a little harsh, but it’s the NFL. Murray’s start to his Minnesota tenure has not been ideal. The Buccaneers should’ve been put away long before they were and it’s the offensive incompetence in Minnesota that kept them in the game. I’m not ready to give up on Murray after one full game as the starter, but . his start to his Minnesota tenure hasn’t exactly inspired confidence. Vikings Offensive Line The Vikings’ OL did not do Kyler any favors on Sunday. The offensive tackles might have been the weakest spots on the line. Christian Darrisaw allowed a sack and committed a holding penalty. O’Neill couldn’t block anyone in the run game. Tampa’s defensive line is good, but they’re not that good. Keith Carter’s squad is going to have to regroup after a rough performance. Josh Metellus The Vikings allowed quite a few chunk plays on Sunday and it seemed Metellus was at the center of it. He seems to be struggling to find his place on this defense. Metellus has been a weak spot on the defense all three weeks so far. Theo Jackson At some point, potential has to turn into production. Jackson has been given a larger role in the defense this season and continues to be the player opposing offenses seem most interested in testing. Missed tackles, bad angles, and almost zero impact plays from Jackson. Nolan Teasley I am not the biggest J.J. McCarthy fan in the world, but he has shown some promise. He wasn’t completely awful, and he’s still very young. The Vikings have no clear long-term direction at quarterback right now, and it seems silly to pass up any potential solution for a fifth-round draft pick. Teasley’s first major move feels like a gamble the Vikings didn’t need to make. There are too many quarterback injuries around the league and too much uncertainty within the organization to move on from a former first-round pick for a Day 3 selection. From where I sit, the Vikings should have gotten more in return or held onto McCarthy a little longer. It’s the Nincompoop of the Week, it’s not that serious, it’s just football.
author: Craig Williams

title: Vikings 3-0: J.J. McCarthy Traded, Kyler Murray Wasn’t the Problem, Defense Is Record-Breaking
summary: Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Giants for a fifth-round pick; Forness breaks the bust label, All-22 on Kyler Murray, and O’Connell’s second-half collapse. — Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano of The Real Forno Show (a Vikings 1st & SKOL production) opened with the news that Minnesota dealt 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy to the New York […]
full_text: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: TAMPA, FL - SEPTEMBER 27: Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray (1) prepares to throw before a game between the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Minnesota Vikings, Sunday, September 27, 2026 at Raymond James Stadium in Tampa, Florida (Photo by Ricky Bowden/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Vikings trade J.J. McCarthy to Giants for a fifth-round pick; Forness breaks the bust label, All-22 on Kyler Murray, and O’Connell’s second-half collapse. — Tyler Forness and Dave Stefano of The Real Forno Show (a Vikings 1st & SKOL production) opened with the news that Minnesota dealt 2024 first-rounder J.J. McCarthy to the New York Giants for an unconditional fifth-round pick. Forness said the lack of escalators “really tells you where the value was in the trade market,” comparing it to Antonio Brown’s modest return at his peak. He argued the move “does right by McCarthy” by sending him to a team that once considered him at No. 6 and now needs a quarterback after Jackson Dart’s knee injury. Multiple matching reports from Alec Lewis and others about process inconsistency and off-field “eccentric” traits, Forness said, put McCarthy below the “hot crazy line”: talent existed, but “the play wasn’t good enough to match some of the behind the scenes stuff.” He called McCarthy “probably the biggest bust in Vikings history outside of maybe Demetrius Underwood,” while wishing him well as a backup to Jameis Winston. The hosts then turned to Sunday’s ugly offensive tape versus Tampa Bay. Forness, after watching All-22, insisted “Kyler Murray was not bad” even if stats looked poor. Early chunk plays (dagger to Justin Jefferson, corner and post to Jordan Addison) worked; the second half collapsed because Todd Bowles’ heavy fronts and deep linebackers clogged the intermediate windows Kevin O’Connell’s scheme lives on. “O’Connell got his ass absolutely handed to him by Todd Bowles,” Forness said, citing missing mesh, shallow crosses, and spacing concepts that could have baited linebackers. Protection was mostly clean (fastest sack 5.3 seconds), three batted balls were not height-related, and miscommunications with T.J. Hockenson and Addison were chemistry issues seen with prior quarterbacks. The defense, meanwhile, is “historic”: Forness cited a ~71% blitz rate on Baker Mayfield dropbacks and called it the highest ever recorded. Key Points: McCarthy traded Monday for a raw fifth-rounder; talks accelerated after Dart’s injury. No conditions surprised Forness; market simply wasn’t there once the league knew Minnesota was done. Giants offer a fresh start with John Harbaugh familiarity and Joe Schoen’s prior interest. Murray’s first-half 5-of-8, ~100 yards, TD vs. second-half drought blamed on play-calling, not the QB. Worst offensive success rate in 20 years; defense’s unique, repeatable blitz packages are the bright spot. Fifth-rounder may be flipped for a tight end (Josh Oliver torn bicep) or running back depth. Next: home vs. Dolphins and Malik Willis; Jefferson’s MRI “looked good.” Listen: Or on your favorite podcast aggregator. Watch: The Vikings sit 3-0 with an elite defense and an unresolved quarterback future. Forness’s All-22 take will fuel debate all week. Listen to the full Real Forno Show for the unfiltered tape study, trade context, and what O’Connell must fix before Sunday. Fan with Us!!! Tyler Forness @TheRealForno of Vikings 1st & SKOL @Vikings1stSKOL and A to Z Sports @AtoZSportsNFL , with Dave Stefano @Luft_Krigare producing this Vikings 1st & SKOL production, the @RealFornoShow found at the @BleavNetwork . So here’s questions for you: What would you have done with McCarthy—and do you buy that Murray wasn’t the problem? Are you buying the historic defense as a legitimate Super Bowl foundation, or do the offensive concerns worry you more than the 3-0 record suggests?
author: David Stefano

title: Vikings Autopsy: Daily Norseman Week 3 Postgame Roundtable (A 23-16 win over the Buccaneers)
summary: Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 3 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off a nail-biter in Tampa, beating the Bucs 23-16, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 3-0. Where does the offense go from here? Ostensibly…up, right? How quickly can the Vikings have a Brinks […]
full_text: TAMPA, FLORIDA - SEPTEMBER 27: Kyler Murray #1 of the Minnesota Vikings passes during the game against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Raymond James Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Tampa, Florida. (Photo by Mike Ehrmann/Getty Images) | Getty Images Hello everyone, and welcome to the Week 3 Minnesota Vikings postgame roundtable here at Daily Norseman. The Vikes are coming off a nail-biter in Tampa, beating the Bucs 23-16, and remain alone atop the NFC North at 3-0. Where does the offense go from here? Ostensibly…up, right? How quickly can the Vikings have a Brinks truck backed up to Brian Flores’ house with a lifetime contract and ALLLLL the money? Let’s talk to it: Question 1: Let’s freestyle for a minute — get your initial thoughts out about the Vikings beating the Bucs in Week 3, 23-16. Brandon Warne : I feel like a broken record, but damn….it wasn’t pretty. But at the end of the day, a win is a win, and it still kinda feels like a Black-and-Blue Division win against the Bucs, even if there isn’t an NFC Central anymore. Anyone else agree? No? The offense remains spotty, but I think I’m less worried about it than I usually would be given a few factors that I’ll get into as we progress here. Nobody in the NFC North has looked flawless, and if you weren’t feeling great about beating the Packers, who lost to the Falcons, maybe it feels a bit better to know the boys beat the Bears, who took down the mighty Eagles on Monday Night Football. Christopher Gates : Thank goodness for Brian Flores, because if that guy wasn’t running this defense and doing absolutely maniacal things to opposing offenses, I don’t know where this team would be right now. The offense is, honestly, a bottom-three offense in the NFL for any number of reasons, but this defense keeps dragging the team to victories somehow. It’s obviously not sustainable over the long term, but it will work against teams like the Buccaneers that are also having issues on offense. They’ll need to pick it up at some point. Are they capable of it? Ehhhhhhhhhhhh… Warren Ludford : It was a win on the road, so that was great, but it’s frustrating that the offense isn’t playing better. Losing Justin Jefferson after the first drive was more of a game-planning loss than people think. Not only did the Vikings lose their best player on offense, but they also had a game plan built around running the passing game through Jefferson. So, when he was lost after the first drive, receivers had to be given different roles, and perhaps different plays, etc., and they had to improvise plays they hadn’t practiced during the week, etc., etc. If Jefferson was out all week, they could have come up with a game plan without him, but losing him after the first drive forced them to improvise the rest of the game with stuff the receivers hadn’t practiced. The Bucs eventually doubled Addison too, and the other receivers didn’t get open much, and there isn’t any chemistry between Murray and them. The Bucs defense is pretty good too, but being down Jefferson (and Jordan Mason) has had an effect. Craig Williams : Why is it that when this team starts a season great, it never feels good? The offense is obviously worrisome. They also gave up a few big plays on defense. A better team would’ve beaten the Vikings on Sunday. Shawn C. : Fortunate. But 3-0 is 3-0. But make no mistake: this team has a definite ceiling with the current offense; I don’t care if our defense ends up being the 1985 Bears. It must get fixed. The passing game is anemic by 1970s standards. Sam Buegler : A win is a win is a win, but oof. That was not a fun watch. Brian Flores, I will personally make sure you never have to buy a drink in Minnesota again, even if it bankrupts me. ————— Question 2: Who was your Vikings MVP? BW : I have the benefit of reading everyone’s answers before my own, so how about I go off-script just a little bit…let’s give some love to Johnny Hekker. Sure, he has some name value — inasmuch as a punter can in this day and age outside of Pat McAfee — but to come off the street and punt eight times, average more than 46.0 yards per boot with a couple inside the 20 and a long of more than 60 yards? In a day where the offense was playing like the conditions were similar to a week earlier, I think that has a ton of value. CG : Who else but Will Reichard? It’s strange not to have an overwhelming sense of dread every time a Minnesota Vikings kicker takes the field, but Reichard has become so automatic that seeing him trot out onto the field is almost comforting at this point. I’m sure there’s absolutely no chance expressing that sentiment will come back to bite me later in any way, shape, or form. Honorable mention to Myles Price, who finally managed a long return and didn’t have it called back by a ridiculous penalty. WL : I’ll say Will Reichard, although Myles Price or Jordan Addison are contenders too. Reichard had 11 points total, including two field goals from 50+, which made the difference. CW : Vikings MVP Will Reichard always comes through and was perfect again. The 56-yarder was massive. Eric Wilson had a great day and was saved by a no-call on a facemask. SC : Could be a handful of players on defense, but I’ll go with Myles Price, as he continues an early-season All-Pro trajectory, and his touchdown won the game for the Vikings. SB : Reichard. He is the definition of consistency no matter what, and he just proves it again and again. Price also housing the punt was something we have been waiting for, and it was so nice to finally see it happen. But nailing three kicks and a few extra points again forces my hand in giving it to Will the Thrill. ————— Question 3: Who was your Vikings LVP? BW : I have a hard time saying anyone else other than Kyler Murray, though I think his performance on the Josh Freeman scale is still only like a 40/100. His accuracy was scattershot, and his wheels saved him from perhaps an even worse day than it already was, but it was functionally his first/only full game with the team on the heels of suffering a concussion early in Week 1. Lord knows we all deserve some grace, but if Murray still looks like this in a couple weeks…we’ve got problems. CG : It’s Kyler Murray. Yes, it’s one game, and Justin Jefferson got hurt and this and that and whatever. I was told Murray was the “veteran presence” who would help elevate Kevin O’Connell’s offense to the level we saw with Sam Darnold or Kirk Cousins behind center. All I saw was a guy with happy feet, even when the offensive line gave him plenty of time, who seemed scared to use the mobility that was supposed to separate him from other potential options the Vikings had at the position. He was awful on Sunday, no two ways about it. WL : I’ll go with Josh Metellus. It looked like he gave up the long TD to Ted Hurst, which was big for the Bucs, who otherwise couldn’t generate many points. He’s been the weak link in the secondary so far this season- and that was predictable. CW : Kyler Murray looked bad in his debut. The OL also struggled. The entire offense outside of Addison, I guess, would be my answer. So KOC? SC : Kyler Murray. I do think the loss of Justin Jefferson early threw the entire game plan out of whack, but his overall performance was still poor. The numbers are what the numbers are. I expect improvement over the next two weeks. I mean, there has to be, right? SB : The Vikings’ rushing attack. Aaron Jones had a few good runs, but otherwise no one could get anything going. Dallas and Claiborne combined for three yards. We need to bring in another back, or find a new way to get someone other than Jones going, because we can’t work him the way we did last week. It’s unsustainable. ————— Question 4: Where do you stand on Kyler Murray right now? BW : As I said earlier, I’m still cautiously optimistic. If Murray still looks like this in a few weeks, it’s time to start watching some college football to see who we like in the upcoming draft. My early thought? It’s a solid…

title: Examining the roster ties between Patriots, Bills ahead of Week 4
summary: The connections between the coaching staffs range from Bo Hardegree and Trace McSorley to Doug Marrone, Todd Downing and Scott Booker. But there’s additional familiarity to account for on the field. Between the active rosters, practice squad and reserve lists, a pair of former New England Patriots and a handful of former Buffalo Bills find […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Reggie Gilliam #44 of the New England Patriots runs off of the field at half time during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The connections between the coaching staffs range from Bo Hardegree and Trace McSorley to Doug Marrone, Todd Downing and Scott Booker. But there’s additional familiarity to account for on the field. Between the active rosters, practice squad and reserve lists, a pair of former New England Patriots and a handful of former Buffalo Bills find themselves in the fold for the AFC East opener. Here’s a glance through those ties ahead of Sunday’s 1 p.m. ET kickoff at Highmark Stadium. BUFFALO Brock Lampe, fullback — Lampe joined the practice squad in Orchard Park midway through September. That was the next move after reverting to injured reserve and reaching an injury settlement with the Seattle Seahawks in the preseason. The 23-year-old fullback out of Northern Illinois originally entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent in 2025. He did so in Foxborough. After spending his rookie season on injured reserve due to a leg injury, Lampe was waived by the Patriots heading into training camp in July. Trent Sherfield Sr., wide receiver — Sherfield signed to New England’s practice squad leading up the divisional round last January. After being released on the eve of the AFC title game, he re-signed ahead of Super Bowl LX. The 30-year-old wide receiver was not retained on a futures contract in February. But Sherfield stayed in the division with the Bills and subsequently joined the practice squad at its formation. Since going undrafted in 2018, the Vanderbilt alum has handled 2,684 snaps on offense and 1,804 snaps on special teams. His career stretches 124 games, including 14 starts, along with 89 receptions for 1,034 yards and six touchdowns. The veteran has also spent time with the Arizona Cardinals, San Francisco 49ers, Miami Dolphins, Minnesota Vikings and Denver Broncos. NEW ENGLAND Reggie Gilliam, fullback — As the new league year opened in March, the Patriots closed in on a three-year deal with Gilliam. The 29-year-old fullback has since notched one reception and two starts for New England while splitting his snaps between the offense and the kicking game. Buffalo marked the first NFL stop for Gilliam. Signed as an undrafted free agent in 2020, the former second-team All-MAC selection out of Toledo went on to appear in 94 games and make a dozen starts during his Bills tenure. Gilliam had a hand in 153 yards and two touchdowns from scrimmage across 25 touches. He also had a hand in 29 tackles, two forced fumbles, one fumble recovery and AFC Special Teams Player of the Week honors. Mack Hollins, wide receiver — The Patriots signed Holins to a two-year contract in 2025 and altered the incentives in the agreement entering 2026. The 33-year-old wide receiver has made 15 starts for New England in the regular season along with 58 catches for 706 yards and two touchdowns. Before arriving at Gillette Stadium, he started 13 games as a member of the Bills in 2024. Hollins’ lone campaign with the previous AFC East champions included a team-high five touchdown receptions. Entering the NFL in the fourth round of the 2017 draft at No. 118 overall, the North Carolina Tar Heel earned a Super Bowl LII ring as a rookie with the Philadelphia Eagles and has also been a Miami Dolphin, Las Vegas Raider and Atlanta Falcon. He finds himself 130 games, 220 catches, 2,775 yards and 17 touchdowns in. Greg Van Roten, guard — After visiting Foxborough in August, the 36-year-old Van Roten returned to sign a one-year deal following the preseason opener. He started at right guard last week with incumbent Mike Onwenu on injured reserve due to a broken ankle, yet exited with a thigh injury before halftime and has since landed on IR, as well. A veteran of 147 games, including 106 starts, the former All-Ivy League selection out of Penn began his career as an undrafted rookie in 2012. Van Roten has since made stops with nine different NFL organizations, plus the CFL, in a career approaching 7,000 offensive downs. For the 2022 Bills, he appeared in 16 games and got the nod for four starts. DaQuan Jones, defensive tackle — The Patriots signed Jones to the 53-man roster in September after the 34-year-old defensive tackle was hosted on a visit in August. On a one-year deal now, he had spent the previous four campaigns in the fold for the Bills. Standing 169 games into a career that got underway in the fourth round of the 2014 NFL draft at No. 112 overall, the Penn State product has started 161. His run in the league spans 374 tackles, 20 sacks, four forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries, one interception and one touchdown. Prior to finding his first AFC East home as a free agent in 2022, Jones made stops with the Tennessee Titans and Carolina Panthers. Mitch Wishnowsky, punter — New England promoted Wishnowsky to the 53-man roster after he served as a standard elevation twice in as many weeks to begin the regular season. The 34-year-old joined the initial practice squad as Patriots punter and holder Bryce Baringer landed on injured reserve in August. Before then, Wishnowsky had spent the majority of 2025 with Buffalo and was released at the cutdown deadline following the preseason. The former Ray Guy Award winner by way of Australia, Santa Barbara City College and the University of Utah originally entered the NFL with the 49ers in the fourth round of the 2019 class at No. 110 overall. Through 108 games, he has amassed 358 punts for 16,288 yards and a long of 74, good for an average of 45.5 yards per and 40.9 net yards per.

summary: The New England Patriots brought in a pair of free agents on Tuesday. The Patriots have two open spots on their 53-man roster and another on their practice squad at the moment. Dimukeje, […]
full_text: The New England Patriots brought in a pair of free agents on Tuesday. Outside linebackers Victor Dimukeje and Eric Watts were in town for a tryout, even though neither ended up getting signed just yet. The Patriots have two open spots on their 53-man roster and another on their practice squad at the moment. Dimukeje, 26, entered the NFL as a sixth-round draft choice out of Duke in 2021. He started his career with the Cardinals and appeared in 55 games for the organization over four seasons. A four-unit special teamer and part-time edge rusher, he registered a combined 67 tackles and four sacks. He joined the Giants in 2025 but was limited to only five games due to injuries; his stint with the 49ers this summer ended earlier this month, when the 6-foot-2, 250-pound defender was released with an injury settlement. Watts, 25, played college football at UConn before entering the NFL as a rookie free agent in 2024. He started his pro career with the Jets, for whom he played 18 games over two seasons and registered 23 tackles. The 6-foot-5, 277-pounder was let go by the organization in August with an injury settlement. The Patriots currently have four edge defenders on their roster and two others on the practice squad, but only three of them saw action during last week’s loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas played a bulk of New England’s defensive snaps , with Jose Ramirez checking in late during the 35-6 blowout. Dre’Mont Jones missed the game with a shoulder injury while neither Xavier Holmes nor Benton Whitley were promoted from the practice squad. Harold Landry and Quintayvious Hutchins are on the PUP and injure reserve lists, respectively, and eligible to return after Weeks 4 and 6. The 1-2 Patriots will travel to Buffalo on Sunday to take on the undefeated Bills for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

title: Patriots Power Rankings: Pats, Maye ‘a mess’ stumbling into Week 4
summary: Read ‘em and weep. I’m not going to argue with the negative commentary, and there’s not much anyone can say – even the optimists, that will put a stop to it. New England will continue to be the NFL’s favorite punching bag until they get a win or at least improve their play. Mistake-free football, […]
full_text: Read ‘em and weep. I’m not going to argue with the negative commentary, and there’s not much anyone can say – even the optimists, that will put a stop to it. New England will continue to be the NFL’s favorite punching bag until they get a win or at least improve their play. Mistake-free football, not turning the ball over, maybe score an offensive touchdown that doesn’t get negated by a penalty… any of these would help. This Sunday the Patriots head to Buffalo to take on the undefeated, division-leading Bills. The home team is favored by 6.5 points, which seems low to me. I’m in this for the season and always believe the Pats can win, right up until they show they can’t. New England hasn’t shown yet that they can play a clean game. Add to that the many, many injuries and I can’t say with any confidence that I think they can win. Hope they do, but we’ll see. I’ll be happy with a good game. GO PATS!! Around the AFC East: Buffalo Bills (3-0) vs. New England Patriots (1-2) New York Jets (1-2) at Chicago Bears (2-1) Miami Dolphins (0-3) at Minnesota Vikings (3-0) AFC Matchups: Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) at Las Vegas Raiders (3-0) Pittsburgh Steelers (2-1) at Cleveland Browns (2-1) Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) at Cincinnati Bengals (2-1 Baltimore Ravens (2-1) vs. Tennessee Titans (0-3) Denver Broncos (2-1) at San Francisco 49ers (3-0) Indianapolis Colts (1-2) at Washington Commanders (1-2) Houston Texans (0-3) at Dallas Cowboys (1-2) Los Angeles Chargers (0-3) at Seattle Seahawks (2-1) 14th – Vinnie Iyer (Sporting News): The Patriots’ offense is missing A.J. Brown as Drake Maye keeps making critical turnovers trying to force the issue in the passing game. Those struggles are putting too much on the running game and defense to win games . [-7] 15th – Nate Davis (USA Today): Copious problems here, notably QB Drake Maye’s. Probably doesn’t help that WR Romeo Doubs has been permitted to wear Rob Gronkowski’s No. 87 . [-8] 16th – NFL Nation (ESPN): Fantasy surprise: QB Drake Maye. Maye had an ADP of 61.2, which ranked him fifth among QBs. But he has just one TD pass while throwing six interceptions, bringing him to 15 turnovers in seven games since the start of last season’s playoffs. Maye has yet to put up double-digit fantasy points in a game this season. He badly misses WR1 A.J. Brown (on IR with a high ankle sprain), and when the running game struggles to gain traction (as it did this past Sunday), things get shaky quickly . — Mike Reiss . [-10] 16th – Ian Glendon (Full Press Coverage): This is the danger of early trust. New England’s defense looked like a foundation after Week 2, then Jacksonville dropped a 35-6 reminder that the Patriots are not ready to live near the top ten yet. One ugly loss does not erase the roster, but it absolutely changes the temperature . [-9] 17th – Pete Prisco (CBS Sports): They have a Drake Maye problem right now. When does he turn it around? He isn’t playing good football, and it’s bleeding over to the rest of the team . [-3] 17th – Ralph Vacchiano (FOX Sports): Remember when everyone thought Mike Vrabel and Drake Maye were going to start another New England dynasty? Yeah, those were fun times … eight months ago. Since then, Maye has gone from near-MVP to turnover machine. And still, it’s hard to say who’s dragging the defending AFC champs down more: him or head coach Mike Vrabel. They can’t run, their defense was a sieve this past weekend against Jacksonville, Maye is a mess … and the defending AFC champs could be finished if they lose in Buffalo this weekend . Stat To Know : Drake Maye is the first quarterback since 2007 with only one passing touchdown and at least six interceptions through his first three games of a season . [-6] 20th – Conor Orr (SI): We spent the entire playoff run telling Mike Vrabel miracle healer stories (guilty as charged). Well, his quarterback is pressing, making throws out of frustration and abandoning the flow of the offense. It’s time for that Mike Vrabel to show up for Drake Maye . [-5] 20th – Mike Florio (ProFootballTalk): There was blood on the ball; now there’s blood in the water . [-6] 22nd – Frank Schwab (Yahoo! Sports): Drake Maye’s struggles are now alarming. He leads the NFL with six interceptions and has a lost fumble, too. He’s 28th in adjusted EPA per play after leading the league in that category last season. There aren’t many instances of a quarterback who nearly won MVP in his second season falling this far in his third season, without some major injury involved. … The Patriots on the whole look bad. They lost 35-6 to the Jaguars and now just have a narrow home win against the Steelers carrying their résumé . [-11] 31st – Nick Shook (NFL): Save for the defensively driven victory in Week 2, the Patriots have been a mess and have a major problem at quarterback. Drake Maye looks completely lost, and judging by the tone of his postgame press conference on Sunday, he might not find his way back onto New England’s intended route for some time. Mike Vrabel was right when describing his concern level as “very high” afterward. There are problems everywhere for the defending AFC champions and a simple solution isn’t in sight . [-13] AVG RANK: 18.8 [-7.4]

title: Patriots vs. Jaguars position grades and film review from Week 3
summary: A blowout. A rout. A drubbing. No matter how you want to label it, the New England Patriots’ defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a lopsided affair. While the team of head coach Mike Vrabel did have its chances to keep this a close game, it kept find a way to shoot itself in the […]
full_text: A blowout. A rout. A drubbing. No matter how you want to label it, the New England Patriots’ defeat against the Jacksonville Jaguars was a lopsided affair. While the team of head coach Mike Vrabel did have its chances to keep this a close game, it kept find a way to shoot itself in the foot on offense, defense and special teams. The final score of 35-6 is not a coincidence but a fair reflection of both teams’ performances in Week 3. Needless to say, and like we already discussed previously , most of the Patriots’ was quite bad. And after watching the tape, we are ready to put some grades on their second loss of the year. Don’t expect many good ones, though. Patriots film review from NFL Week 3 Quarterback: Questions about Drake Maye’s shoulder aside, the biggest issue that keeps plaguing him appears to be a mental one: once things start trending downwards, he finds himself in a spiral he can’t get out of. The result is a quarterback looking for plays that aren’t there to be made, and one actively making bad ones worse. Sure, his supporting cast is not necessarily playing its best football at the moment either — in part due to injuries — but Maye himself is not looking like the MVP runner-up he was last season either. Against the Jaguars, he had three more bad turnovers and despite Josh McDaniels relying on some of the Patriots’ most basic concepts to get the pass game going finished with an EPA of -0.44. It was his seventh straight game with a negative expected points number, and another one where the good moments were dramatically outshone by the bad ones. As for Tommy DeVito, he did have a 20-yard completion to Romeo Doubs but overall looked like the backup he is. | Grade: D This is a throw Drake Maye makes with his eyes closed last year. Not even close now. pic.twitter.com/WGk6tAjPCY — Michael Hurley (@michaelFhurley) September 28, 2026 Running back: Congratulations Corey Kiner on the longest carry by a Patriots running back on Sunday: your 7-yarder after Drake Maye was pulled takes the crown. That very much is all you need to know about New England’s run game versus the Jaguars. It was bad. A large part of it was the blocking (the three RBs gained only 10 combined yards before contact on the day) and a lack of schematic diversity (you can only run duo so much). The backs themselves also left some to be desired, however, with TreVeyon Henderson’s lack of vision and Rhamondre Stevenson’s uneven creativity both exacerbating the other problems. And it wasn’t like Jacksonville sold out to stop the run, either; New England was unable to run into relatively light boxes all day. | Grade: C – Wide receiver: There was some good and some bad from the wide receiver position. Mack Hollins continues to show a good rapport with Drake Maye, including on a well-timed 21-yard pickup on a curl route to convert a 3-and-5 on the opening drive; however, his fourth-quarter taunting penalty to turn 4th-and-1 into 4th-and-16 was as unnecessary as they get. DeMario Douglas had a 38-yard pickup in the second quarter and nearly connected with Maye on another big play later in the drive, but he still has not developed into the volume target you would want. His timing with Maye is simply off at times while his routes appear to be just a tad too imprecise for a steady down-to-down role. Speaking of which, Romeo Doubs has not provided that either and continues to be quiet as the supposed main man with A.J. Brown out. Kyle Williams and Efton Chism are non-factors, with the former’s lack of production particularly frustrating: he very much remains a one-trick pony whose one trick doesn’t look so powerful outside of preseason and who could have fought his way back to the ball on Maye’s second INT. Chism, meanwhile, was in no position to catch Maye’s first pick, but does deserve credit for salvaging the blown-up double pass in the second quarter by hitting Hollins for 16. | Grade: C- Tight end: It was a rough outing for a Patriots tight end group missing its secondary option, third-round rookie Eli Raridon. Hunter Henry was the clear No. 1 again, but he and Maye connected only once all game for a modest gain of 5 yards. His ability to beat zone coverage is still solid but the ball is simply not finding him as readily as it did a year ago. His blocking, meanwhile, is an issue — something that is also true for Cameron Latu, whose role on the team very much could come into question once players start returning from the injury lists. He did little as a run blocker (in fact, his presence very much might alert teams to what a play is going to be), had one penalty each on offense and special teams (and could have had a third had the officials not missed a face mask call in the first quarter), and was replaced by rookie Tanner Arkin down the stretch. | Grade: D Offensive line: Let’s start with the positives, namely the left side of the line. Will Campbell continues to look promising, while Alijah Vera-Tucker had possibly his best game yet next to him. The further right we go, the more problematic things get. Jared Wilson did bounce back as a pass blocker but failed to generate an adequate push in the run game; the right guard position lost their Mike Onwenu replacement, Greg Van Roten, in the first half and replaced him with first-timer Walter Rouse. It proved to be a downgrade from a downgrade both in the run game and in pass protection. Then, there was Morgan Moses, who looked as old as he ever has since joining the team last year. Maybe it was the foot injury he was dealing with heading into the game, but the veteran right tackle simply wasn’t right before getting replaced by rookie Caleb Lomu — who was shaky himself — in the late third period. | Grade: C- Defensive line: The Patriots are missing Khyiris Tonga, and unless DaQuan Jones can fully replace him are in a vulnerable position along their interior defensive line versus the run — that is one of the big takeaways from Sunday’s game. Cory Durden and Joshua Farmer simply do not have the size and raw power to consistently hold the line from the nose, and if Milton Williams and Christian Barmore have quiet days for whatever reason the interior is suddenly not as stout as it should be. One positive, however, was the play of young edges Elijah Ponder and Gabe Jacas: despite a heavy workload at an injury-ravaged position, they logged seven combined quarterback disruptions and were the most consistent source of pressure on the day. They were still a bit hit-or-miss with their assignments both against the run and the pass, but they are fairly low on the list of problems right now. | Grade: C+ If you're looking for silver linings, #Patriots second-rounder Gabe Jacas might be a demon. Give him some 1-on-1 pass rush moves and we'll really be cooking. pic.twitter.com/LYT7Oyub2K — Evan Lazar (@ezlazar) September 28, 2026 Linebacker: Robert Spillane and Christian Elliss were among the best players on the field last week against the Steelers, but their impact was far less pronounced in Jacksonville. Elliss was solid again particularly coming downhill, but Spillane was a bit more inconsistent, His tackling (two misses) and spot-drops into coverage were especially uneven. Trevor Lawrence completed 11 of 14 downfield throws over the middle of the field — wisely staying away from the perimeter — and the linebacker’s ability to defend his zones was part of the reason for his success. The second level wasn’t bad per se, but it will continuously be challenged by opposing offenses if they see matchups they like. | Grade: C Cornerback: Pay no attention to his PFF grade, Christian Gonzalez was again very good against the Jaguars. His only blemish was slipping on a third-down pass to Jakobi Meyers while coming out of his back-pedal, resulting in a 14-yard pickup. Other than that, he was excellent again in man or zone looks — prompting the Jaguars to simply look elsewhere for most of the day. This meant a busy day for Carlton Davis and Marcus Jones, who…

title: What placing Greg Van Roten on injured reserve means for the Patriots
summary: The New England Patriots’ offensive line depth has taken another hit. One week after losing right guard Mike Onwenu, his replacement in the starting lineup has been placed on injured reserve as well: Greg Van Roten will miss at least the next four games due to the thigh injury he sustained during Sunday’s blowout loss […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ offensive line depth has taken another hit. One week after losing right guard Mike Onwenu, his replacement in the starting lineup has been placed on injured reserve as well: Greg Van Roten will miss at least the next four games due to the thigh injury he sustained during Sunday’s blowout loss in Jacksonville. Let’s assess what the move means for the Patriots and their offensive line. More turnover at right guard The Patriots entered the 2026 regular season with the ever-reliable Mike Onwenu as their starting right guard, but he suffered a broken ankle during the team’s Week 2 win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. This bumped Van Roten — a training camp signing — into the top spot between center Jared Wilson and right tackle Morgan Moses. Van Roten, who had played every single offensive snap for the New York Giants in 2024 and 2025, lasted only 64 snaps as Onwenu’s replacement. This forced the Patriots to move third-stringer Walter Rouse, himself a trade acquisition in late August, into the top lineup versus Jacksonville. The results were as expected: Rouse, who had not played even a single regular season right guard snap before Sunday, struggled. With Van Roten now out, however, there is a scenario that he again sees extensive snaps this coming week versus the Buffalo Bills. Whether the team starts him or veteran Ben Brown, the situation is anything but ideal. Losing not one but two starting right guards in back-to-back weeks is a blow to an offense already running on fumes. Two realistic replacement options Between the 53-man roster and practice squad, the Patriots have six interior offensive linemen available at the moment. Beyond the aforementioned Ben Brown and Walter Rouse, they also have two on the practice squad: 53-man roster (4): Alijah Vera-Tucker (75 | LG), Jared Wilson (55 | C), Ben Brown (77), Walter Rouse (72) Practice squad (2): Jake Kubas (63), Xavier Newman-Johnson (64) IR (2): Mike Onwenu (71), Greg Van Roten (70) Theoretically, the Patriots could also use rookie Caleb Lomu to bolster their depth inside; the first-round draft pick did see some guard snaps in practice over the summer. However, his main focus has been at offensive tackle, and with RT Morgan Moses nursing an injury it seems unlikely the team will move him insight until its hand is truly forced. Realistically, this leaves Brown and Rouse as the replacement candidates for Van Roten (and by extension Onwenu). While the latter filled that role versus the Jaguars, it would not be a surprise if the former was the pick against the Bills in Week 4: Brown, who missed time earlier this year due to an ankle injury suffered in preseason, started the summer as the No. 4 interior offensive lineman and possesses a level of experience in the system that the third-year man Rouse simply does not have. Two open spots The Patriots did not announce any follow-up moves to placing Van Roten on IR. This means that as of Tuesday afternoon, they are down to 51 players on their active roster; they still have not filled the spot created when rookie outside linebacker Quintayvious Hutchins was sent to injured reserve last week. New England does have some candidates to take those spots, either from the practice squad or its current injury lists. Five players, after all, are set to become eligible to return from their respective injury lists after Week 4: OT Marcus Bryant, ED Harold Landry, LB Khalil Jacobs, S Brenden Schooler, and P Bryce Baringer. The team keeping the spots open until then and trying to use practice squad promotions to bolster the game day team against Buffalo on Sunday is not entirely unreasonable. 17th player on IR The Patriots were relatively healthy during their 2025 Super Bowl season, but this year so far has been a challenge. Going back to the offseason, they have now placed 17 different players on injured reserve. Out of those, 11 remain on the list as of today (i.e. have not been let go with a settlement): IR (11): RB Myles Montgomery (39 | season-ending), WR A.J. Brown (1), WR Jeremiah Webb (29 | season-ending), TE Julian Hill (80 | season-ending), OT Marcus Bryant (52), RG Mike Onwenu (71), OL Greg Van Roten (70), ED Quintayvious Hutchins (45), LB Khalil Jacobs (59), S Dell Pettus (24), P Bryce Baringer (17) The most prominent names on the list are starting receiver A.J. Brown, who is eligible to come back in two weeks, as well as the aforementioned Mike Onwenu. Punter Bryce Baringer can be reactivated after Week 4, while third safety Dell Pettus can come back after Week 6.

title: Patriots place veteran guard Greg Van Roten on injured reserve
summary: Another loss has been taken in the New England Patriots’ trenches. The organization officially placed Greg Van Roten on injured reserve Tuesday afternoon, sidelining the veteran offensive lineman for a minimum of four games. Van Roten, 36, started at right guard against the Jacksonville Jaguars after incumbent Mike Onwenu sustained a broken ankle and landed […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WA - SEPTEMBER 09: Greg Van Roten #70 of the New England Patriots walks off of the field at half time during an NFL football game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on September 9, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Another loss has been taken in the New England Patriots’ trenches. The organization officially placed Greg Van Roten on injured reserve Tuesday afternoon, sidelining the veteran offensive lineman for a minimum of four games. Van Roten, 36, started at right guard against the Jacksonville Jaguars after incumbent Mike Onwenu sustained a broken ankle and landed on injured reserve the week prior. But in the second quarter of what became a 35-6 loss at EverBank Stadium, the second-stringer exited for the blue medical tent and was announced as questionable to return because of a thigh injury. No return followed. August trade acquisition Walter Rouse stepped in to play the final 41 offensive snaps of the Sunday runaway. The 6-foot-3, 305-pound Van Roten visited Foxborough as a free agent amid training camp. And after previous top backup interior lineman Ben Brown sustained a multiweek injury in the preseason opener, a one-year deal was reached. A veteran of 147 games, including 106 starts, Van Roten began his career as an undrafted rookie with the Green Bay Packers in 2012. Over the years since then, the former All-Ivy League offensive tackle out of Penn has been a member of nine different NFL clubs in addition to the CFL’s Toronto Argonauts. In 2024 and 2025 with the New York Giants, he posted consecutive wire-to-wire seasons with 100 percent of the offensive snaps. New England now stands with two vacant spots on the active roster after losing multiple players to IR before falling to 1-2. In additional movement, the Patriots released linebacker Riley Wilson from the practice squad on Tuesday, opening a spot among the 17-man group. Wilson, 24, signed as an undrafted free agent ahead of training camp in July. The 6-foot-1, 226-pound off-ball rookie was waived and retained on the initial practice squad after going unclaimed at the 53-man roster deadline. A former transfer from Hawaii to Montana, he finished his collegiate career at Arizona last fall. Altogether, Wilson appeared in 52 collegiate games and totaled 193 tackles, 16 sacks and two interceptions. The Buffalo Bills host the previous AFC East champions at Highmark Stadium on Sunday. Kickoff is set for 1 p.m. ET.

title: Patriots injury analysis after Jaguars loss in Week 3
summary: The New England Patriots’ third game of the 2026 season was an abject disaster. The offense was all sort out of sync, the defense played its worst football in two years, and special teams didn’t make many positive contributions either. To make matters worse, the team sustained multiple injuries. While not quite as dramatic as […]
full_text: The New England Patriots’ third game of the 2026 season was an abject disaster. The offense was all sort out of sync, the defense played its worst football in two years, and special teams didn’t make many positive contributions either. To make matters worse, the team sustained multiple injuries. While not quite as dramatic as the Week 2 win over Pittsburgh, the 35-6 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars was still a bad one from a health perspective. For a 1-2 team already reeling, the hits just keep coming. Patriots injury analysis: NFL Week 3 RT Morgan Moses: The veteran right tackle was a limited participant in practice all week but eventually made the trip to Jacksonville without a game designation. That said, he did not look his best on the field from the first drive on. Moses hobbled on several occasions and was pulled from the game for rookie Caleb Lomu in the late third quarter. CB Christian Gonzalez: The Patriots’ best player had his shoulder checked out after a physical third-down tackle in the first quarter. No injury was announced by the team and no time missed by Gonzalez. C Jared Wilson: Wilson played all 51 snaps alongside quarterback Drake Maye, and he did so despite suffering a cut on his right middle finger early in the game — the second time an injury like that happened this season after Week 1 versus Seattle. According to Maye, the bleeding might have contributed to his fumble in the first quarter. DT Christian Barmore: Barmore was announced as questionable to return early in the second quarter and did leave for the locker room due to a shoulder issue. He did return to the sideline shortly thereafter and reentered the game later during that period without showing any obvious limitations. RG Greg Van Roten: Already starting in place of an injured Mike Onwenu, the Patriots’ right guard was slow to get up after a third-down play in the second quarter. He headed into the blue medical tent to have his thigh checked out and was announced as questionable to return. He never did, with third-stringer Walter Rouse finishing the contest in Van Roten’s place. CB Carlton Davis III: Making his comeback after missing the previous game with a neck injury, Davis remained down on one knee after a sideline tackle in the third quarter. He was checked out by the training staff, but walked off under his own power and into the medical tent. He eventually returned on the next series after missing a total of five defensive plays. LT Will Campbell: One of the few Patriots to perform at an adequate level on Sunday, Campbell was slow to get up after a short run in the late fourth quarter. He limped back to the huddle, stayed in the game, and finished with a 100% playing time share and no injury ever being announced. OL Ben Brown: One play after Campbell, Ben Brown showed some discomfort following a short catch-and-run. The backup center also remained in the contest and showed no obvious limitations before the final whistle. What this means for the Patriots If we look at the Jaguars game and the Patriots’ injury situation coming out of it from a “glass half full” perspective, we can say that only one player — Greg Van Roten — was truly unable to finish the contest. The others suffered some bumps and bruises, but seemingly nothing that should be considered a long-term concern. However, where there is a glass half full, there also is a glass half empty. And if we use that point of view, we see a Patriots team that a) saw even more players get banged up, and b) is now down to its third-string right guard. After Mike Onwenu was lost to a fractured ankle in Week 2, Week 3 saw his replacement leave before the half only to be replaced by a late-August trade pickup who had played zero regular season snaps at the position since entering the NFL in 2024. Walter Rouse very well might turn into a serviceable player at some point, but the progression from Onwenu, to Van Roten, to him is still one downgrade after the other. Maybe Van Roten will be able to get back in time for the upcoming game against the Buffalo Bills [ Update : He has been placed on injured reserve] . Even so, the right guard spot — and the right side of the O-line in general given Morgan Moses’ own issues — is a problem right now. The first indication of may or may not be available for Week 4 will come on Wednesday, first at practice and then via the injury report. The Patriots will visit the 3-0 Bills on Sunday for a 1 p.m. ET kickoff.

title: Mike Vrabel wants Drake Maye to ‘relax’ to get back on track
summary: A 1-2 start to the 2026 season has left many questions for New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel to try and answer. The biggest? Getting Drake Maye back on track. Through three games, Maye has thrown six interceptions in addition to losing a fumble. Decision-making seems to be the biggest issue early on for […]
full_text: A 1-2 start to the 2026 season has left many questions for New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel to try and answer. The biggest? Getting Drake Maye back on track. Through three games, Maye has thrown six interceptions in addition to losing a fumble. Decision-making seems to be the biggest issue early on for the quarterback, who was pulled in the fourth quarter of Sunday’s 35-6 blowout loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars. “I think quarterbacks want to make plays. I think they want to throw touchdowns. I think sometimes when Greg and I go golfing, we really want to make a good score, right? Sometimes we’re so focused on it, we try to choke the life out of the golf club, and we’re squeezing it so damn tight that the ball has no choice but to go sideways,” Vrabel said Monday morning on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show . “We need to stop trying to choke the life out of every single play. We need to relax. We need to settle in and go play football and not try to force things that aren’t there.” Later in the day, Vrabel was asked how he goes about addressing that issue while also raising Maye’s confidence level. “Confidence comes from your preparation, and it comes from going out there. I can’t manufacture confidence. I can’t just say, ‘Hey, be confident.’ You have to practice. You have to hit those plays in practice, and you have to feel good about it,” Vrabel said. “Sometimes you want to do something so badly. It’s like the tighter you hold the golf club, the more crooked it goes when you hit it. We just have to be able to make sure that we’re on the same page, that everybody knows what is expected of them, have a few details and then go play football.” Following Sunday’s game, Maye said there was nothing wrong with his right shoulder that was injured in last year’s AFC Championship Game. However, the quarterback didn’t say there weren’t lingering effects from the hit. Vrabel, meanwhile, said he was not aware of any ongoing injury concerns before adding he doesn’t “anticipate that being an issue going forward.” Now, with the head coach looking for answers ahead of next Sunday’s showdown with the Buffalo Bills, Vrabel was asked if simplifying the offense is necessary. “When you have games like that throughout the entire team – how do you fix some things? You get back to the basics,” Vrabel said. “Again, we want to continue to impress upon the importance of what our identity is. We still have to build it. You have to put it out there. Before you can protect something, you have to build it. And we have to get back to the basics. “So, some of that is, do you do less and try to do it better? Or do you go and you try to scheme up a bunch of stuff and hope you hit it? I think at the end of the day, there’s a great balance. I thought we had a couple of good scheme plays and we didn’t hit them. They made it and we didn’t. … So, I think to your question, you never want to go into a game when a guy is unsure, right? But how much we do, we’ll look at that, and we’ll look at everything that we can do to help us win here on the road.”

title: Are the Saints actually a couple bad calls away from being 3-0?
summary: The New Orleans Saints are 1-2 after three weeks, but is it true they are a few officiating decisions away from being 3-0? That is the latest overreaction worth exploring after another frustrating loss. New Orleans has now been on the wrong side of controversial calls in both of its losses this season. The latest […]
full_text: The New Orleans Saints are 1-2 after three weeks, but is it true they are a few officiating decisions away from being 3-0? That is the latest overreaction worth exploring after another frustrating loss. New Orleans has now been on the wrong side of controversial calls in both of its losses this season. The latest came Sunday against the Las Vegas Raiders, when a fourth-quarter sack-fumble by Tyler Shough was upheld on replay, while the Raiders got three extra chances to punch the ball in the endzone due to questionable penalties. That does not necessarily make the officiating the reason New Orleans lost either game. It does, however, make the Saints’ 1-2 record more interesting. Against Detroit, New Orleans had opportunities to win despite the controversial ruling. The same was true against Las Vegas. The Saints led the Raiders 27-16 in the second half and appeared to be in control before everything unraveled. New Orleans turned the ball over on all four of its fourth-quarter possessions, including two lost fumbles and an interception. Las Vegas turned those mistakes into points and rallied for a 35-27 victory. That is where the “couple bad calls away from 3-0” argument becomes complicated. There is no denying that officiating has been a major storyline in the Saints’ two losses. But New Orleans has also had chances to put those games away and failed to do so. Sunday was the clearest example. The Saints’ offense was extremely efficient for most of the afternoon. Shough threw four touchdown passes, Chris Olave had nine catches for 107 yards, and New Orleans converted 9-of-15 third downs while going 4-for-4 in the red zone. Yet they couldn’t finish the game with a win. So, yes, the Saints could reasonably argue that officiating has affected their record. But saying they’re simply 3-0 without the poor officiating would ignore the opportunities they’ve had to win these games themselves. And perhaps that’s what makes this an interesting overreaction. New Orleans may not be as far away from a 3-0 start as its record suggests. But the Saints still have to prove they can finish games when the opportunity is there.

title: State of the NFC South: Week 3 recap
summary: Just when you think you know how the division is going, almost nothing goes as everyone expected. Tampa Bay Buccaneers It’s not crazy to say that Bucs HC Todd Bowles could be fired after Week 4. This team has been one of the biggest disappointments in the NFL, and their performance against the Minnesota Vikings […]
full_text: NEW ORLEANS, LA - SEPTEMBER 27: Tyler Shough #6 of the New Orleans Saints warms up before kickoff against the Las Vegas Raiders prior to the NFL football game atCesars Superdome on September 27, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images Just when you think you know how the division is going, almost nothing goes as everyone expected. Tampa Bay Buccaneers It’s not crazy to say that Bucs HC Todd Bowles could be fired after Week 4. This team has been one of the biggest disappointments in the NFL, and their performance against the Minnesota Vikings was bad. The score showed a 7-point game in the end, but the Bucs made mistakes, and Baker Mayfield struggled. Speaking of Mayfield, near the end of the game, he injured his finger, which looked really bad. Next week, the Bucs play the Packers, so they could win, but it’s doubtful. Carolina Panthers Speaking of shock, the Panthers lost to the Cleveland Browns. First thing, this means the Browns are 2-0 against the NFC South so far. May spell bad news for the rest of the division, but going away from that, let’s focus on this game. The Panthers’ defense didn’t do enough against a Browns offense they should have handled. It doesn’t help that star CB Jaycee Horn went down with an injury and will be out for most of the season. The offense was also very disappointing and looked nothing like their first two weeks. A performance to forget. Atlanta Falcons Somehow, the Falcons are the only winners of the week. After Michael Penix returned, all eyes were on their QB situation, and he did well in his first game. The real hero was Bijan Robinson, who completely controlled this game for Atlanta and gave the Packers zero chance of winning. Could this win be the Packers just being a mess? I actually don’t think so. If Atlanta won by 3 points, then I would say that’s the case, but the Falcons won 35-14. We are going to see up close what this Falcons team really is, because Atlanta is playing the Saints this week. New Orleans Saints And now, a rant I have been waiting for. The Saints’ loss to the Raiders was one of the most frustrating losses since the Drew Brees/Sean Payton era. This game should have been won by New Orleans, and that fourth-quarter collapse was embarrassing. It was really one of the first times the Saints faced adversity while winning, and just like the Ravens last week, they couldn’t recover. The refs had a hand in making that happen, and some of those calls/no calls were truly mind-boggling, but this team had chances to overcome these, and they couldn’t. It sucks for everyone because I do think many of the Saints’ early weaknesses were fixed in this game. The run game was much better, Taliese Fuaga’s blocking improved, the Saints started fast, the run defense played really well, and the playcalling was exceptional at times. Momentum is a killer, and the Saints fell victim to it. Travis Etienne’s injury is extremely worrying, and the Saints must bring in an RB ahead of this week’s game, but I also think the pass rush needs more talent. This defense had its worst game so far in 2026, and the pass rush behind Chase Young was completely missing. The Saints won’t be able to survive with these two units where they are right now. NFC South standings: Carolina Panthers (1-2) New Orleans Saints (1-2) Atlanta Falcons (1-2) Tampa Bay Buccaneers (0-3)

title: The Good, the Bad, and the Ugly from the Saints loss to the Raiders
summary: The Good: Tyler Shough The Saints quarterback threw 4 touchdowns for the first time in his career on Sunday and continued his strong start to the season against the Raiders. Shough found tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant twice each in the end zone and found Chris Olave nine times for 107 yards. Shough […]
full_text: The Good: Tyler Shough The Saints quarterback threw 4 touchdowns for the first time in his career on Sunday and continued his strong start to the season against the Raiders. Shough found tight ends Juwan Johnson and Noah Fant twice each in the end zone and found Chris Olave nine times for 107 yards. Shough did throw a costly interception in the 4th quarter but up until that point he had played a great game. The offensive line started to get beat in the fourth quarter which also led to a “fumble” by Shough which started the comeback for Vegas, but all things considered the Saints QB was not the biggest reason this game went awry in the fourth quarter and overall had a pretty good game. The Bad: Pass Defense The Saints allowed Raiders QB Kirk Cousins to complete 22/33 passes for 248 yards and 3 TDs with no interceptions. Brock Bowers returned for Las Vegas and had an immediate impact catching 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Chase Young had two sacks, but outside of Young no one on the Saints has been able to consistently put pressure on the QB this year, as no one else on the team has more than 1 sack so far. The defense couldn’t get the stops they needed to at the end of the game, as after taking a 27-16 lead the Saints allowed 19 straight points to the Raiders on three drives which all lasted just 6 or fewer plays. The Ugly: Turnovers The last four drives of the day for the Saints all ended in turnovers, three of which were fumbles and one interception. Shough fumbled twice, but the offensive line did not do him any favors on either and also got beat on the interception he threw. The first fumble came on a play that looked more like a forward pass than the one called back in Detroit in Week 1. The NFL is going to have to explain in detail the difference between the two plays, as right now it looks like their rules are not being enforced consistently by their officiating crews. The bad call by the refs completely derailed the game, as instead of potentially going up two scores the Saints fell behind thanks to the officials ruling the Shough play a fumble. Call it a fumble if you want, but if that was a fumble than so was the play in Detroit, and all we want is a little consistency and also some accountability if the refs miss a call that potentially changes the outcome of a game. The refs were not the sole reason or even the biggest reason the Saints lost however, as the offensive line was completely overwhelmed in the fourth quarter. There are many things that were ugly about this game, but the ultimate result of them was the Saints just giving the ball back to the Raiders when they had multiple chances to take the lead or tie in the final frame. The offensive line could be a problem going forward without Kelvin Banks Jr., but hopefully they will get it figured out as the Falcons come to town off their first win in a Monday night showdown next week.
