title: NY Giants news: OBJ released, J.J. McCarthy fit, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants prepare to stay atop of the NFC East. Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4 | ESPN.com I think … J.J. McCarthy will save neither himself nor the Giants. In New York, McCarthy will get more spread looks […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to as the Giants prepare to stay atop of the NFC East. Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4 | ESPN.com I think … J.J. McCarthy will save neither himself nor the Giants. In New York, McCarthy will get more spread looks and RPOs from the gun. Does he have the poise, field vision and accuracy to create explosive plays in that passing game? I’m dubious … but I am interested. The offensive line in New York is far better than the banged-up line the Vikings had for McCarthy in 2025. McCarthy is a slippery mover who should be involved in the option running game, though he needs to protect himself from hits, as he has collected far too many knocks over his short time in the league. I can see Matt Nagy and Greg Roman, the two primary offensive designers in New York, coming up with good, risk-averse game plans that dramatically lower McCarthy’s time to throw (3.22 seconds last season, 14th longest for a QB since 2010) and minimize his opportunities for post-snap decisions. The Vikings were finished with J.J. McCarthy. So why did the Giants want him? | The Athletic A bevy of injuries prevented him from staying on the field enough to develop further. Wonky footwork didn’t allow him to pass the ball with enough accuracy to move the Vikings offense. Off the field, his day-to-day habits, even inside the Vikings’ building, made it difficult for the staff to know what type of mindset they’d be coaching each week. Even though McCarthy played in a pro-style system at Michigan, he often seemed more comfortable flowing out of the pocket. The Vikings worked hard to ingrain him within their complex rhythm-and-timing-based system. During the back half of last season, McCarthy found success, saying that he stopped fixating on the fundamentals and processes and played free. Maybe Giants offensive coordinator Matt Nagy’s offense, which contains some simpler RPO-style concepts that were a part of the game plan with Dart, will allow McCarthy to think less and let his athleticism take over. Giants Trade For J.J. McCarthy: What Does It Mean For Present, Future Of QB Room? | FOX Sports Make no mistake, this is Dart’s team. The Giants love him and his potential. Even Harbaugh, who wasn’t around when the Giants traded back into the first round to get him in 2025, fell in love with Dart quickly. He made it clear that Dart was a big selling point when he took the Giants job. There are almost no scenarios where he doesn’t enter camp with his old starting job. Once McCarthy is up to speed on the playbook, probably in a couple of weeks, Winston will have to watch his back. His hold on the job could very much be week-to-week. Some of that is because of how one team source described the Giants’ interest in McCarthy: “He’s just a better fit for what we want to do. He’s athletic. He’s much more like Dart than Winston is. He may not be better, but he’s a better fit.” Giants ’ J.J. McCarthy gamble shows they’re not giving up after Jaxson Dart’s injury | SNY.tv Schoen and Harbaugh could easily stick to their guns. Ride through with Winston no matter what. McCarthy seems to be an admission that they misvalued Winston’s worth. If they didn’t trust Jake Haener, elevated from the practice squad, as a backup, there were options in free agency (Jimmy Garoppolo) or practice squads (Josh Johnson) who were more than capable of riding out a game. This aggression for McCarthy (the Vikings would not accept a sixth-round pick in compensation) is a two-fold covering: Both if Winston goes down, or if they’ve seen enough of the 32-year-old and believe they need a switch. The expectation, talking to league sources, is that the Giants do not give up a fifth-round pick unless they plan to play McCarthy in the near future. #BaldyBreakdown of Arvell Reese "From the opening drive of the game, Arvell Reese was a factor" pic.twitter.com/m3AshxlDvh — New York Giants (@Giants) September 29, 2026 Arvell Reese nominated for Pepsi Rookie of the Week | Giants.com Arvell Reese has been nominated for Pepsi Rookie of the Week following the Giants’ 12-7 victory over the Titans in Week 3. The linebacker was everywhere against Tennessee as he finished with a game-high 13 tackles (10 solo), including one tackle for loss, and a pass defensed. The rookie linebacker also performed well in coverage, according to Pro Football Focus. Reese surrendered just three receptions for 14 yards against the Titans, which earned him a passer rating against of just 79.2. In addition to his dominant performance on defense, Reese also made an open-field tackle on Jordan Stout’s 74-yard punt. Yannick Ngakoue says he’s ‘ willing and able ’ if Giants come calling | USAToday.com Veteran pass rusher Yannick Ngakoue has attempted to put himself on the New York Giants’ radar days after Brian Burns suffered a season-ending torn ACL in Sunday’s win over the Tennessee Titans. When a Giants fan suggested the team call the free agent and loop in head coach John Harbaugh, Ngakoue answered with three words: Willing and able. title: Survey – When will we see J.J. McCarthy at quarterback for the Giants?
summary: It was widely expected that the New York Giants would make a move for a quarterback once it became known that starter Jaxson Dart would need season-ending knee surgery. What wasn’t expected was that the Giants would make a trade for a quarterback, and it was very unexpected that they’d make a trade with the […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images It was widely expected that the New York Giants would make a move for a quarterback once it became known that starter Jaxson Dart would need season-ending knee surgery. What wasn’t expected was that the Giants would make a trade for a quarterback, and it was very unexpected that they’d make a trade with the Minnesota Vikings for J.J. McCarthy . But trade they did, and now McCarthy is a Interestingly, John Harbaugh said after the trade that it was the Giants’ front office that first floated the idea of trading for the 2024 10th overall pick, and not the other way around. But still, Harbaugh was very familiar with McCarthy, both from following Michigan when Jim Harbaugh was leading them to the National Championship, and with conversations with his brother. Familiarity is one piece of the puzzle, and so too is the fact that McCarthy shares a number of traits with Dart. In hindsight, the move does make sense. Excitement over the trade aside, John Harbaugh confirmed on Monday that Jameis Winston remains the Giants’ starting quarterback for the foreseeable future. But just how long a leash does Winston have? He has not played well since taking over as QB1 following Dart’s injury. It’s possible that his play can be chalked up to being uncomfortable in a jury-rigged gameplan against the Los Angeles Rams and the miserable conditions this past week against the Tennessee Titans. But the Giants aren’t giving up on the 2026 season despite losing Dart and now Brian Burns . That already has people speculating on when we could see McCarthy on the field as QB1 for the Giants. So we put that question to you, the Giants fans. When do you think McCarthy will take over and assume the starting job? A) Never. Jameis will rebound and hold be the starter through the end of the season. B) In two to three weeks. Jameis is on a short leash and gets pulled if he continues to struggle against the Arizona Cardinals, Washington Commanders, or New Orleans Saints. C) Over the bye week. The Giants will give McCarthy time to settle in and learn the system before turning the offense over to him. D) In December. The Giants have a tough run from November 22nd through December 13th, with the Jaguars, Colts, 49ers, and Seahawks. They’ll let McCarthy play after that. title: NY Giants add 2 WRs to roster after releasing Odell Beckham, putting Brian Burns on IR
summary: The New York Giants made the previously-reported release of Odell Beckham Jr. official Tuesday afternoon. They also placed edge defender Brian Burns on injured reserve with the torn ACL he suffered in Sunday’s victory over the Tennessee Titans. To fill those roster spots, the Giants signed two wide receivers off their practice squad. Added to […]
full_text: Braxton Berrios | Getty Images The New York Giants made the previously-reported release of Odell Beckham Jr. official Tuesday afternoon. They also placed edge defender Brian Burns on injured reserve with the torn ACL he suffered in Sunday’s victory over the Tennessee Titans. To fill those roster spots, the Giants signed two wide receivers off their practice squad. Added to the 53-man roster were Braxton Berrios and Charlie Jones . Berrios was out of practice squad elevations after being brought up for the first three games of the season. Berrios has returned two punts for an average of 6.0 yards, and five kickoffs for an average of 27.6 yards. He has played 22 snaps at wide receiver, but has yet to be targeted. Jones, 27, was signed to the practice squad on Sept. 1. A 2023 fourth-round pick by the Cincinnati Bengals, he played in 33 games over three seasons for Cincinnati with eight receptions. Like Berrios, Jones’ primary contribution came as a returner for the Bengals. In his career, he has returned 50 punts for an average of 9.2 yards, and 47 kickoffs for an average of 27.3 yards. The Giants bypassed signing veteran linebacker Malik Harrison , who is also out of practice squad elevations, to the 53-man roster. Perhaps that is an indication the Giants may not be done shuffling the roster before they face the Arizona Cardinals this Sunday at MetLife Stadium. The Giants also bypassed signing edge defender Trace Ford off the practice squad as a replacement for Burns.

The most common grade was a ‘B’, with 36% of voters giving GM Joe Schoen and head coach John Harbaugh that score for acquiring the 23-year-old McCarthy from the Minnesota Vikings in exchange for a fifth-round pick. full_text: New York Giants wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr. | Getty Images The New York Giants are releasing wide receiver Odell Beckham Jr., per reports from Mike Garafolo and Ian Rapoport . The Giants signed Beckham, 33, for the second time this summer along with fellow veteran receivers Braxton Berrios and JuJu Smith-Schuster. Beckham was solid but unspectacular in his return to the Giants. He was able to consistently work open in the preseason, but the ball never really found him in games. He proved to still be a fan favorite once the regular season started and received ovations from the home, but rarely even saw the field. Instead, the former star had been reduced to a decoy and downfield blocker on the few snaps he did receive over the first three games of the season. In releasing Beckham, the Giants are now only carrying three wide receivers on their 53-man roster: Malik Nabers , Darnell Mooney , and rookie Malachi Fields . The move to release Beckham comes as Berrios, the Giants’ primary returner, has exhausted his elevations from the practice squad. full_text: EAST RUTHERFORD, NEW JERSEY - SEPTEMBER 27: Jevon Holland #8 and Jordan Stout #15 of the New York Giants celebrate the 12-7 win against the Tennessee Titans as they leave the field at MetLife Stadium on September 27, 2026 in East Rutherford, New Jersey. (Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images) | Getty Images Given the awful weather conditions at MetLife on Sunday for the Giants’ 12-7 victory over the Tennessee Titans, analysis of the performance of any Giants player or unit is at best of limited use. The fact that the Giants’ best defensive player, Brian Burns, is now out for the season with what looks like an ACL tear, following on the gut punch of losing their best offensive player, Jaxson Dart, to his own knee injury the week before, seems like a classic “only the Giants” sequence of events. That said, the Giants are 2-1, their best record after three games since 2022, and tied for first place in the NFC East. The only point is that as ugly as Sunday’s game was, the Giants found a way to come out with a win, something they haven’t done much of the past few years, and the season goes on even if you’re not as excited about it as you were two weeks ago. The Giants will play 14 more games, so we might as well look at who is and is not playing well to see where hope for the future lies. PFF grades Here are the PFF grades for the offense: Jameis Winston had a rough outing (47.3 passing grade), but he gets a mulligan because of the conditions. He’ll have to do better in the coming weeks…if the coaching staff is willing to open up the offense a little bit when the weather cooperates, and if he doesn’t take a seat with the acquisition of J.J. McCarthy. Strangely, Jameis graded better under pressure (66.8) than when kept clean (41.6). The reason was because his one “big-time throw” came when he was flushed from the pocket because Jermaine Eluemunor’s man beat him, and he threw downfield just before being hit to the Giants’ big deep threat…Cam Skattebo . His one turnover-worthy play came from a clean pocket. The offensive line was a mixed bag. Eluemunor and Andrew Thomas both pass-blocked pretty well overall, although Eluemunor drew two penalties. Sisi Mauigoa had a clean game, and Jon Runyan pass-blocked well other than drawing one flag. The real problem was John Michael Schmitz, who is both overmatched in pass blocking against big physical defensive linemen and sometimes makes curious decisions about who to block. The rest of the offense was just a collection of average and slightly below-average performances, as befits the weather conditions. Isaiah Likely drew the lowest grade because he only caught 2 of 5 targets and had a drop. Moving on to the defense: Arvell Reese had clearly his best game as a Giant, grading 84.6 overall with 80+ grades each in run defense, tackling, and pass coverage. Reese had eight tackles and an assist, five of them “stops” (unsuccessful running plays). He did give up three receptions in four targets but for only 14 yards total and only 2 YAC. D.J. Reader also graded elite overall, with at least average grades in every category and very good grades in run defense and pass rush (a QB hurry from an interior defensive lineman!). For a change, the Giants’ secondary graded pretty well overall. Unsurprisingly, Jevon Holland was the star of the show because of his game-saving interception, but Dru Phillips and Jason Pinnock also graded well, notably for Phillips in coverage as well as run defense, and Greg Newsome graded very good in coverage. Of the other DBs, I was surprised to see Colton Hood get a grade as high as 57.9 in coverage, considering that Cam Ward targeted him all game, completing six of seven passes thrown his way plus the only touchdown of the game. Ar’Darius Washington was the lowest graded Giant on defense, because of the two catches in two targets he gave up for 22 yards including 13 YAC. Otherwise the defense graded in the average category overall, with the occasional bright spot. For example Abdul Carter got a 70.9 in pass rush despite getting no pressures. This suggests that he beat his blocker sometimes but didn’t get to Ward in time to affect his throw. Ward’s 2.47 s average time to throw yesterday indicates that he was getting the ball out quick. More on that below. Advanced metrics Like you, I am dismayed about the Giants’ lack of an effective pass rush. There may be multiple reasons – the lack of a big physical bull-rushing edge defender; a lack of creativity from Dennard Wilson with twists, stunts, blitzes to get free rushers; or the Giants’ edge defenders are just overrated. Here’s one thing, though, that shouldn’t be overlooked: The Giants have faced the second most quick passes 2.4 seconds or faster) in the NFL through three weeks (pre-MNF). Something to think about regarding pass rush dismay. Only the Vikings have had more, the most blitz-happy coach in football by a mile. 58 of 101 pass attempts… — David Syvertsen (@Ourlads_Sy) September 28, 2026 Of course if you have defensive backs who tightly cover receivers it’s not so easy to get rid of the ball completely. A good DB is an edge rusher’s best friend. In fairness, though, the Giants’ DBs were not terrible Sunday overall, as I indicated above from the PFF grades. Here’s an objective metric, QB EPA/play, that tells us several things of interest to Giants’ fans (click on the figure to see the full list; the QBs of interest are near the bottom): QB EPA/Play by Week 1. Brock Purdy (Week 2): 0.99 EPA/Play 2. Brock Purdy (Week 3): 0.84 EPA/Play 3. Jaxson Dart (Week 1): 0.73 EPA/Play 4. Trevor Lawrence (Week 1): 0.72 EPA/Play pic.twitter.com/mn1vhHKoQR — SFdata9ers🏈📊 (@sfdata9ers) September 28, 2026 First, take a moment to lament the Dart injury; he led the NFL in EPA/play in Week 1. For this week, though, go to the bottom of the chart. Cam Ward is ranked No. 30 for the season. His -0.15 EPA/play yesterday was among the lowest in the NFL, though the weather may have had something to do with that. Unfortunately just a few spots below Ward is Jameis Winston at -0.14, just about as bad. That said, it beats Jameis’ -0.45 against the Rams. Oh how quickly they forget, though. Here are EPA/play rankings from weeks 6-12 last year: Jameis Winston was the best QB last year from weeks 6-12 JJ McCarthy was the worst QB last year from weeks 6-12 https://t.co/h8VN4ZFRzA — Doug Analytics (@Doug_Analytics) September 28, 2026 This suggests several hypotheses, more than one of which might be correct: Jameis and Dart being No. 1 and No. 3 during that period means they played really well The fact that Jameis is so low in EPA/play this year is due to the fact that in his two starts he had to face a ferocious Rams defense (not that it looked great against Denver) with the Giants already behind and then had to play in windy, rainy conditions in his second start The fact that Jameis is so much worse this year than last is due to the Brian Daboll-Mike Kafka passing offense being much better designed than this year’s Matt Nagy-Brian Callahan passing offense. J.J. McCarthy being dead last on the list does not suggest that he will be an improvement over Jameis. Choose whichever explanation(s) you like. Here’s another take on quarterback performance, looking at how EPA/play compares to PFF passing grade: *Week 3 only* PFF grading & efficiency (EPA/play), through SNF pic.twitter.com/vTXPRoOIMG — Kevin Cole (@KevinCole___) September 28, 2026 PFF doesn’t always agree with EPA/play, but there is a definite positive correlation, and for Jameis yesterday they are in good agreement – he was below average (as was Ward). Take solace, though, because Drake Maye’s carriage has suddenly turned into a pumpkin this season. How well did the Giants play overall on offense and special teams yesterday (again, click on the figure to see the full list)? title: NY Giants QB J.J. McCarthy: Film shows lots of good … and bad
summary: The New York Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round pick for quarterback J.J. McCarthy on Monday. The 2024 10th overall selection missed his rookie season due to a torn right meniscus. He also missed five games in 2025 with a high ankle sprain and one game with a concussion.  The 6-foot-3, 219-pound 23-year-old signal caller threw […]
full_text: J.J. McCarthy | Getty Images The New York Giants traded a 2027 fifth-round pick for quarterback J.J. McCarthy on Monday. The 2024 10th overall selection missed his rookie season due to a torn right meniscus. He also missed five games in 2025 with a high ankle sprain and one game with a concussion. The 6-foot-3, 219-pound 23-year-old signal caller threw for 1,632 yards with a 57.6% completion rate last season. He threw 11 touchdowns and 12 interceptions, with a 7.3% big-time-throw rate and a 4.8% turnover-worthy play rate. The Vikings dropped 17 of his passes, and he rushed for 181 yards with four touchdowns and six fumbles. McCarthy was relegated to third string after the Vikings signed Kyler Murray and had Carson Wentz to the roster. What McCarthy offers McCarthy’s film was frustrating. There’s no denying his athletic ability and how his legs will be an asset in Matt Nagy’s scheme, but his mechanics, accuracy, and decision-making were maddening at times. McCarthy air-mailed several throws, threw awkwardly from clean pockets and made easy completions much harder than they had to be. His accuracy issues, though, could be attributed to wild mechanics. However, he had several WOW-type plays throughout his bad season, and his throws – when his footwork was correct – had improved accuracy. McCarthy showed impressive velocity throughout his tape. He ripped several far hash throws and there were plays where he navigated the pocket well and delivered good throws, while using his eyes well: via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY The play above against the Giants is an elite pass to Justin Jefferson (18) against tight coverage. There was one place that the football could have been delivered to ensure that Jefferson caught the ball, and McCarthy delivered it. Below is another play-action rip that resulted in a touchdown: via GIPHY We see the heavy personnel, under-center, play-action use against Dallas. Plays like this – where McCarthy threw on the run off a bootleg – are plays that easily fit into what Nagy and Greg Roman will ask of McCarthy if/when he sees the field. I wish I could say, however, that McCarthy was generally accurate throwing on the run, but McCarthy had some very poor throws while on the move last season; we’ll see that later. McCarthy had a dim flash of touch passes throughout his tape, which was an issue of his at Michigan. His passes were delivered on a line too often, making the catch more difficult for the receivers. But plays like this one below, where McCarthy used touch, did pop up every now and again, which was encouraging: via GIPHY via GIPHY McCarthy is comfortable throwing over the middle of the field. Of throws inside the numbers of 20-air yards or less, McCarthy finished 31 of 59 ( 53% ) with a positive EPA. Again, he flashed high-level throws, carving through zone coverage while showcasing good arm talent, but these throws were coupled with good footwork; unfortunately, it wasn’t consistent throughout his tape, but here are some throws that highlight his ability to throw over the middle of the field: via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY Off play-action, McCarthy rips a pass to T.J. Hockenson (87). Watch how McCarthy steps into the pocket with trust and just delivers the concept after hitching up. This was an exceptional play by McCarthy. McCarthy again looked poised against Dallas, throwing this seam ball to Hockenson against bailing middle-hook zone defenders: via GIPHY McCarthy hit the receiver in stride on third down against a trailing man defender, just in front of the safety: via GIPHY Here’s another successful play against the Giants off play-action where McCarthy pump fakes to displace the Giants before delivering a completion to Jordan Addison (3). via GIPHY McCarthy also had several high-level back-shoulder throws away from defensive leverage. The play against the Giants was very impressive, for it was a back-shoulder toward the middle of the field with Dexter Lawrence (97) in his face, while the other two come from completely clean pockets: via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY McCarthy is a threat with his legs; he rushed for 894 yards through three seasons at Michigan, with an average of six yards per carry. He also averaged 3.07 yards after contact through college. He wasn’t used on a ton of designed rushes with Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings last year, but I expect that to change with the Giants. Here are a few quarterback scrambles that showcase his speed and movement skills: via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY Then there’s McCarthy’s ability to throw on the run; there were some good one, like these… via GIPHY via GIPHY Reasons for concern …Then there are plays with McCarthy on the move where he is wildly inaccurate: via GIPHY via GIPHY The mechanics and accuracy issues are married, and correctable, which is excellent for both McCarthy and the Giants, but it was certainly a problem in 2025 for the Vikings. via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY McCarthy also used suspect decision-making through the 2025 season. There were several plays where it seemed like he negligently forced the issue: via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY via GIPHY Final thoughts The Giants acquired a talented young quarterback with tools that MUST be ironed out. McCarthy is mobile, has good velocity, and has made high-level throws at the NFL level, but WOW, did he make mistakes throughout his 2025 season. That said, I believe the Giants can leverage his tools; his mobility will be an asset and will be used more often in Roman’s rush scheme, but McCarthy’s lower-body mechanics and decision-making must improve. This trade is a new start for McCarthy, and it gives the Giants an interesting insurance option behind Winston. I get it.

title: NFL power rankings: Nick’s picks for how teams stack up before Week 4
summary: No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (1st) SAME Somehow, the Buffalo Bills turned the football over five times and still WON THE GAME! Of course, it was against the Chargers, who are currently — and historically — allergic to winning, but James Cook’s 154 yards on the ground helped give Buffalo the 24-16 win, and they […]
full_text: Brock Purdy | Getty Images No. 1 — Buffalo Bills (1st) SAME Somehow, the Buffalo Bills turned the football over five times and still WON THE GAME! Of course, it was against the Chargers, who are currently — and historically — allergic to winning, but James Cook’s 154 yards on the ground helped give Buffalo the 24-16 win, and they remain at the top of the standings here. No. 2 — San Francisco 49ers (5th) 📈 3 spots Brock Purdy and the 49ers are one of the hottest teams in football. Purdy went for 297 yards and four touchdowns against an inferior Cardinals team, who pushed the 49ers in the 36-30 game. Still, through all the injuries, the 49ers remain a top team in the NFL. No. 3 — Kansas City Chiefs (7th) 📈 3 spots The Chiefs went into Miami and easily handled the Dolphins. Patrick Mahomes was efficient (20 of 24 for 246 yards with two touchdowns), and Rashee Rice finally got going with seven catches for 88 yards. Miami offered little resistance in the 24-10 win, and the Chiefs are one of the four undefeated teams that remain in the NFL. No. 4 — Seattle Seahawks (2nd) 📉 2 spots Seattle goy Sam Darnold back from his hip injury, but Washington did an excellent job harrassing the Seahawks all game. Darnold finished with 379 passing yards and four touchdowns, but Marcus Mariota did enough to give the Commanders a 33-31 home victory. No. 5 — Los Angeles Rams (3rd) 📉 2 spots The Rams drop to 1-2 but remain in the top five. Massive credit to the Broncos, who appeared dead for much of the game but battled back with 30 second-half points. Matt Stafford finished with 390 yards passing and two touchdowns, but the Rams’ game plan shifted after a Terrance Ferguson injury, and they were without Puka Nukua, who they hope will return soon. No. 6 — Baltimore Ravens (7th) 📈 2 spots Tyler Loop! The Ravens and Dallas were headed to overtime after Dak Prescott led the Cowboys down the field on a last-minute drive to tie the game with a field goal. Unfortunately for Dallas, Lamar Jackson found Zay Flowers for 27 yards, which set up a 56-yarder from Loop for a big road victory over Jerry Jones’ Cowboys. No. 7 — Minnesota Vikings (11th) 📈 4 spots The Vikings have moved eight spots up in the rankings over the last two weeks. They’re undefeated, but sit seventh in the rankings; this is because of my discomfort with Kyler Murray, who missed Week 2 with a concussion. The Vikings’ defense, led by Brian Flores, is playing amazing football, and they beat up on the Buccaneers, 23-16. Still, the offense isn’t going to be bailed out by the strong defense every week; the team must become more complementary. No. 8 — Denver Broncos (14th) 📈 2 spots The Broncos defeated a very good Rams team at home with second-half resilience. The win was similar to their win over the Giants last year, where they scored 30 points in the fourth quarter; they did that in the second half, and the Broncos’ defense slowed down Matt Stafford when it mattered most. No. 9 — Chicago Bears (12th) 📈 3 spots Chicago dismantled the Philadelphia Eagles with 38-year -old journeyman quarterback Case Keenum. Ben Johnson continues to prove why he’s an offensive wizard, and he unlocked the potential of Luther Burden III in the game. Kalif Raymond finished with six grabs for 90 yards and a touchdown, as Philadelphia was held to seven points and 248 total yards. Impressive win against a struggling, now 2-1 Eagles team. No. 10 — Cincinnati Bengals (4th) 📉 6 spots The Bengals gave up 292 yards and three touchdowns to Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers. After two strong weeks of defensive football, the Bengals’ defense struggled to stop Rodgers and Jaylen Warren, who rushed for 127 yards. Cincinnati will be okay, but this was a tough loss. No. 11 — Jacksonville Jaguars (13th) 📈 2 spots The New England Patriots are spiraling right now, and Jacksonville took advantage of that fact in Week 3. Jacksonville beat up on the Patriots, 35-6, with Drake Maye looking very bad, finishing 14 of 25 for 199 yards with a pair of interceptions. Jacksonville got back on track against the AFC champs from last season. No. 12 — Detroit Lions (15th) 📈 4 spots Detroit was pushed by the New York Jets, but they found a way to win late in the 31-24 game against a feisty Jets team. Jaymeir Gibbs finished with 99 yards and a pair of touchdowns on 20 carries, and the Lions sit at 2-1. No. 13 — Philadelphia Eagles (9th) 📉 4 spots The Eagles are a 2-1 team that does not inspire much hope. Jalen Hurts still has his flaws as a passer, and they were just embarrassed in primetime by the Chicago Bears. Things do not get much easier for the Eagles, as they host the Rams next Sunday and then travel to London to play the Jaguars. No. 14 — Las Vegas Raiders (24th) 📈 10 spots The Raiders are undefeated! And they just went into a hostile New Orleans environment and defeated the Saints 35-21. Brock Bowers’ return was exciting, as the young tight end caught 10 passes for 116 yards and a touchdown. Kirk Cousins is doing enough to put the Raiders into advantageous situations, as they sit undefeated. No. 15 — Dallas Cowboys (14th) 📉 1 spot I hate having the 1-2 Dallas Cowboys this high, especially with their suspect defense through three weeks. But I know how explosive their offense can be with CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. Plus, their rushing attack is getting going, and they’ll be getting Tyler Smith back soon. The defense remains an issue, of course, but Dallas stays put at 14. No. 16 — Pittsburgh Steelers (22nd) 📈 5 spots I didn’t expect to see Aaron Rodgers dial back the clock against a Bengals defense that tormented the Buccaneers and Texans in their first two matchups. The Steelers’ defense remains their strength, but competent quarterback play makes them a threat, so they are in the top-fifteen. No. 17 — Indianapolis Colts (20th) 📈 3 spots The Colts finally got their first victory against the Houston Texans on a last-second field goal. Indianapolis struggled to do much against a very good Texans defense, but they found a way to get a valuable win and send the Texans to 0-3. No. 18 — Houston Texans (17th) 📉 1 spot I don’t like having the 0-3 Texans this high, but I feel better about their position — specifically with their defense — than I do with the remaining teams, including the injured Giants, so here we are. Houston pushed Buffalo and the Colts to near victories; they must get more out of their offense and learn to secure wins, but they’re better than their 0-3 record would indicate. No. 19 — New York Giants (21st) 📈 2 spots The Giants are 2-1 and handled their business in a sloppy noreaster against the Tennessee Titans. New York has issues with Jameis Winston; the trade for J.J. McCarthy may eventually solve that problem, but the Giants are beat up on both sides of the ball. However, Jordan Stout is a stud. The Giants can still compete for this NFC East with their current injury situation, and I expect better play out of Jameis Winston, although I’m relieved they’ll have another viable option. No. 20 — Washington Commanders (26th) 📈 6 spots Washington pulled off one of the season’s more impressive wins, defeating the Super Bowl champions 33-31 at home. Perhaps it was Sam Darnold jitters, or the dreaded one-o-clock start for a West Coast team — I’m not sure — but it does seem like Washington’s defense has improved, and Marcus Mariota did enough against Mike Macdonald’s talented defense No. 21 — New Orleans Saints (18th)📉 3 spots Las Vegas just might be a much better football team than many anticipated, and the Saints found that out firsthand. Tyler Shough played well, throwing four touchdowns with 255 yards passing. Still, the Raiders forced four turnovers and the Saints lost running back Travis Etienne to injury. New Orleans is a quality 1-2 team, but they’re still young and learning themselves. No. 22 — Carolina Panthers (20th) 📉 2 spots The Panthers suffered a tough loss to the now 2-1 Browns. title: NY Giants news: Brian Burns out for the year, Giants acquire J.J. McCarthy, more
summary: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know the day after the Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthy and lose Brian Burns for the year. NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants | ESPN.com Giants grade: C. But the Giants’ front office should look in the mirror over […]
full_text: Good morning, New York Giants fans! Here are the stories you need to know the day after the Giants acquire QB J.J. McCarthy and lose Brian Burns for the year. NFL trade deadline grades: J.J. McCarthy to the Giants | ESPN.com Giants grade: C. But the Giants’ front office should look in the mirror over its bungling of the Winston situation. It’s not unreasonable for the Giants to be aggressive in finding a better replacement given how much time is left in the season. But they clearly shouldn’t have signed Winston to an extension right before the season if this is how they feel about him! Even though Murray is a free agent at the end of this season, McCarthy’s ship had already sailed in Minnesota after he couldn’t beat out Wentz. If he wasn’t going to be the Vikings’ backup quarterback, his value would likely have continued to drop. To get a fifth-round pick while saving a few million across his remaining 2026 and 2027 compensation (not nothing!) makes sense. They have uncertainty at quarterback in 2027, yes. But that was true whether McCarthy was there or not. McCarthy throws against Dallas, Washington So many cutups against the Cowboys and Commanders. Yeah I’m all in. LETS RUN IT @jjmccarthy09 pic.twitter.com/whFFmwj8Ep — Anthony (@AnthonyGros13) September 28, 2026 Giants made the one QB trade that offered hope, even if it doesn’t guarantee anything | Yahoo Sports! Yet it at least has a chance to work, which is likely better than you can say about the other options the Giants had. Most of them were short-term rentals. Most of them were older and more experienced, but there was a reason they were either unemployed or available by trade. That’s a reminder of where McCarthy was prior to the trade: the third QB option on a team that ranks last in the NFL in total yards, pass yards and first downs. It should also serve as a warning for any Giants fans counting on this saving their season. Giants to waive QB Jake Haener, intend to re-sign him to practice squad | Pro Football Talk With the Giants trading for J.J. McCarthy, the club will make another roster move to keep just two quarterbacks on their 53-man roster. Per Mike Garafolo of NFL Network, New York will waive Jake Haener but intend to re-sign him to the team’s practice squad. Haener was promoted to the active roster on Saturday after Jaxson Dart suffered a long-term knee injury last Monday night. Haener, 27, joined the Giants in August after spending some time with the Chiefs during the offseason program. QB Report Cards for 2026 NFL Week 3 | Bleacher Report Grade: D. Jameis Winston didn’t do enough for the New York Giants to beat the Tennessee Titans. That’s OK. He didn’t to. The Giants benefited from a ground-and-pound approach, a strong defensive effort and multiple Titans mistakes. Tennessee didn’t pieced together a drive longer than three plays until the team’s seventh offensive possession. Winston simply needed to avoid a significant mistake, which he did. Will the Giants trick themselves in the wake of Jaxson Dart’s injury? | The Athletic The concerns following the Giants entering the season — the availability of Dart, Cam Skattebo and Malik Nabers, plus the maturity of Dart/Skattebo — were mostly realized in less than two games. But the key questions that followed the Giants into this season will follow them into 2027 as well. They should not assume those questions will be answered to their liking. The evidence so far suggests some of the team’s biggest bets carry even greater risk. Harbaugh on losing Dart, Burns "We got our quarterback one week and probably our top defensive player the next week is shocking. But you've got to overcome the shock" John Harbaugh talks about the loss of Brian Burns for the season pic.twitter.com/xgLv0pjVnV — SNY Giants (@SNYGiants) September 28, 2026 Giants in survival mode after losing the irreplaceable Brian Burns for the season | SNY.tv If New York’s quarterback was the team’s most important offensive player, Burns held that role for the defense. He is a monster on the field, evident by his 16.5 sacks a season ago. He’s an elite edge rusher and solid against the run, but more than anything, the heart-and-soul and emotional leader of that side of the ball. So many players treat this as a job – justifiably so. Burns took everything that happened on the field to heart. When the Giants blew a late lead to the Broncos last season, it was Burns who sat in his locker stall after the game, in full game uniform, crying. Teammates gravitate toward that level of emotion, care. It’s why they elected him captain the last two years. Jason Pierre-Paul pitches Giants reunion after crushing Brian Burns injury | New York Post The 37-year-old — who played three games for the Buccaneers last season after being away being away from football for nearly two years — tagged the Giants in a post on X that said, “@Giants what’s up.” Pierre-Paul signed with the Bucs’ practice squad in December 2025, and was activated for three games late in the season. Rookie was a force on Sunday Arvell Reese was flying around the field against Tennessee. 12 TKL, 9 SOLO, 1 TFL, 1 PD vs Titans The rookie linebacker continues to flash as one of the most exciting young pieces on New York’s defense. https://t.co/UMG5nOAliR pic.twitter.com/5Zx9aA1QRV — Football Performances (@NFLPerformances) September 28, 2026 Giants’ Arvell Reese on Week 3 performance: I had a ‘chip on my shoulder’ | USAToday.com New York Giants rookie linebacker Arvell Reese responded to a disappointing performance last week with a game-high 13 tackles on Sunday against the Tennessee Titans. “After a loss, you always want to self-reflect and see what you could be doing better,” Reese said. “So I just self-reflected on that and came out this weekend with a chip on my shoulder. title: New York Jets News: Geno Smith is Having a Historic 2nd Act
summary: The New York Jets are 1-2, and that stinks, but I have something to cheer you up. Geno Smith is delivering a level of quarterback play that we have literally never seen before. It probably isn’t getting attention from the rest of the NFL because of the Jets’ not-so-great record, but it totally deserves more […]
full_text: Sep 27, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith (7) runs with the ball aginst Detroit Lions linebacker Derrick Barnes (55) at Ford Field. Mandatory Credit: David Reginek-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The New York Jets are 1-2, and that stinks, but I have something to cheer you up. Geno Smith is delivering a level of quarterback play that we have literally never seen before. It probably isn’t getting attention from the rest of the NFL because of the Jets’ not-so-great record, but it totally deserves more love from anyone who watches the sport. “As far as I can tell, Geno Smith is the first Jets QB to EVER open the first three games of a season with 700+ passing yards 4+ TDs 0 interceptions 70% completions,” Zack Rosenblatt of The Athletic wrote. Smith currently leads the league in completion percentage (75.5%) and is top-five in quarterback rating this season. It’s a shame that we’re 1-2 because no one could have predicted that we’d get this insane Smith renaissance season in 2026. Smith has been efficient, has been protective of the football (only one turnover through three games), and is starting to click with his array of playmakers. Jets fans, we are freaking scoring points. The rushing attack admittedly leaves much to be desired right now, which is super disappointing, BUT the Jets are 13th in offensive yards per game, 11th in passing yards per game, and 17th in scoring. The good news is it should only continue to get better. There are several players on offense that we’re waiting to return to the lineup, and as this unit plays more together, they will continue to gel. Mandatory Credit: Brad Penner-Imagn Images | USA TODAY Sports via Reuters Con This is an uncomfortable conversation. Olu Fashanu was supposed to be the steal of steals in the first round of the 2024 NFL Draft. He was supposed to be the blindside protector for the next decade, and maybe he still will be, but this most recent showing was perhaps the worst of his career. The former Penn State product allowed 2.5 sacks and five quarterback pressures against the Detroit Lions in Week 3. He now leads the league in sacks allowed (four). You may be saying to yourself or screaming at the computer, but Paul, this is one game; aren’t we overreacting here? But that’s the thing: this isn’t just one game. This season, he is the 20th, 36th, and 15th ranked offensive tackle in overall grade, pass block grade, and run block grade, per Pro Football Focus. Last year there were signs of struggle. In those same categories, he ranked 39th, 27th, and 65th in overall grade, pass block grade, and run block grade among qualifying offensive tackles. If this were only one game, you could chalk it up to that. This has become a pattern. Fashanu has been bullied by superstars and random players (I’m looking at you D.J. Wonnum) alike. He hasn’t been consistently bad, but he hasn’t been consistently good either. Next offseason, the Jets have to decide on his fifth-year option. title: Eagles-Bears snap counts
summary: The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE DEFENSE SPECIAL TEAMS DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Mac McWilliams INACTIVE: Hollywood Brown, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, A.J. Epenesa, Fred Johnson, Dallas Goedert
full_text: PHILADELPHIA, PENNSYLVANIA - AUGUST 28: Andy Dalton #14 of the Philadelphia Eagles walks off the field after a preseason game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Lincoln Financial Field on August 28, 2026 in Philadelphia, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images The official snap counts from the Philadelphia Eagles’ Week 3 loss to the Chicago Bears are in. Let’s take a look and run through some analysis. OFFENSE Only 50 snaps for the offense is low. So low that it tied their season-low for offensive snaps in a game last year, which came in a win over the Minnesota Vikings. Jalen Hurts was pulled from the game by the concussion spotter. Those four snaps he missed turned out to be pretty important since Andy Dalton came in and threw a terrible interception into the end zone for a touchback. Dontayvion Wicks was once again the clear WR2. He was second in wide receiver snaps and targets. Saquon Barkley looked pretty spry out there despite playing with a collar on after suffering a stinger injury last week. Good to see his playing time wasn’t really limited. Makai Lemon’s snap count percentage was a season-high, slightly up from the 63% mark he was at in each of the first two weeks. Johnny Mundt was the Eagles’ top tight end with Dallas Goedert out. Not really an ideal configuration. Zach Ertz was limited to a relatively small role in his first game back with the Eagles. He was still TE2 ahead of E.J. Jenkins, though, in terms of total playing time. Will Shipley was RB2 over Tank Bigsby, who fumbled on one of his two snaps played. That giveaway isn’t going to help Bigsby get more snaps. With Hollywood Brown inactive, Elijah Moore made his Eagles debut in this game. He was not targeted and he did not help out on special teams at all. Darius Cooper looked good in Week 2, including when he made the game-winning touchdown grab. His reward? The fifth-most playing time of any Eagles receiver (behind Moore, who was previously a healthy scratch behind six active receivers in each of the first two games) … and zero targets. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯ Markel Bell made his NFL debut on offense in a six offensive linemen package. DEFENSE Cooper DeJean and Quinyon Mitchell are the only Eagles defenders to not miss a snap so far this season. Jalen Carter’s snap count percentage has dropped each week this season (94% to 77% to 71%) while he continues to play through a wrist injury that’s causing him to wear a cast. Jordan Davis logged his highest snap count percentage of the season. He was ahead of Moro Ojomo for the first time this year. Byron Young saw a lot more playing time than he usually does. Guess the Eagles are trying to use him more to help lighten the load of the players ahead of him. Ty Robinson also saw a bigger role than normal to have the Eagles significantly utilize five DTs. Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II rotated as at the safety next to Andrew Mukuba in nickel defense packages. When you have two safeties playing at one spot, you might just have none. Here’s a positive for the defense on what was otherwise a pretty bad night: Jonathan Greenard looked good in his debut. He logged two pressures (including one QB hit), a forced fumble, and a stop in just 18 snaps played. The Eagles need to hope he’s able to handle an increased workload sooner than later. Jeremiah Trotter Jr. saw a little action on defense for the first time this season. SPECIAL TEAMS Chance Campbell saw some special teams action in his Eagles debut and first regular season action since 2023. Quiet night for Jake Elliott, who did a single kickoff and a single extra point. Micah Morris played a single special teams snap in his first-ever NFL game. DID NOT PLAY ACTIVE: Mac McWilliams INACTIVE: Hollywood Brown, Tanner McKee, Cole Payton, A.J. Epenesa, Fred Johnson, Dallas Goedert McWilliams was active but did not play a snap for the first time this season. Goedert, Brown, and Johnson were ruled out due to injury. McKee was the emergency third quarterback once again. He should really be QB2. Dalton shouldn’t be on the team. With Greenard returning to the field, Epenesa was a healthy scratch as the fifth edge rusher.

title: Eagles Film Review: This team looks like they are running two separate offenses
summary: This was a deeply disappointing offensive performance. There were positives on film, and I do not want to ignore them. However, those positives existed within an offense that still doesn’t fit together. Right now, the Eagles look like they are running two separate offenses. They have a shotgun passing game and an under center running […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Montez Sweat #98 of the Chicago Bears sacks Jalen Hurts #1 of the Philadelphia Eagles during the third quarter of the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Patrick McDermott/Getty Images) | Getty Images This was a deeply disappointing offensive performance. There were positives on film, and I do not want to ignore them. However, those positives existed within an offense that still doesn’t fit together. Right now, the Eagles look like they are running two separate offenses. They have a shotgun passing game and an under center running game. Those two worlds barely connect. The Eagles ran for 107 yards on 19 attempts, but that success didn’t produce the explosive play-action passes it should. The numbers were ugly. The Eagles finished with 14 first downs and 248 net yards. They went 2-for-9 on third down, 0-for-5 on third-and-long, and 0-for-2 on fourth down. They reached the red zone twice and came away empty once. Andy Dalton’s interception was the single biggest win-probability swing of the game. We will get into that because I’m still angry… For me, the biggest problem was pass protection, particularly against pressure. I’m saying pass protection rather than offensive line play. Cam Jurgens had a poor game in pass protection, but the recurring free rushers were not simply five linemen losing individual blocks. The Eagles repeatedly looked confused about who they wanted to block and which defender they were prepared to leave free. That is a schematic and coaching problem first. Jalen Hurts was largely fine for three quarters before his play deteriorated once the Eagles fell behind by 20. The quarterback was not the main reason this offense failed. Offense It all started so well. The Eagles used pistol, paired the backfield action with a fake toss, and created an easy completion to Makai Lemon. Pistol gives the offense access to a downhill run action without forcing Hurts to turn his back completely on the defense. The fake moved the Bears in the wrong direction, and Lemon came open with ease. The frustrating part is that the Eagles used it once. One snap doesn’t mean pistol is the answer to everything, but this offense needs formations that connect the running game to the passing game. This did exactly that. Maybe use it again? Try running out of pistol next week and see if we can get something going? Eagles' Offense All22 vs. Bears. Sigh. 1) It all started so well. We used Pistol (ONCE !), and it produced this. The benefit is that Hurts doesn't have to turn his back on the defense. The fake toss gets the Bears to flow the wrong way and enables the easy throw to Lemon. Maybe,… pic.twitter.com/cOtyK5Jh4K — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 29, 2026 The outside zone running game was one of the clearest positives. It’s been bad through two weeks, but it was significantly better this week. The Eagles attacked the left side of the Bears’ defense, as I suggested they should in the preview, and created real movement. Jurgens and Drew Kendall produced some excellent combination blocks, and Kendall once again looked comfortable climbing and finishing at the second level. He looks like he might belong as a starter this year, but it’s still early days. Barkley finished with 82 yards on 15 carries, and the run blocking was significantly better than in the first two weeks. The Bears’ run defense is not good, so I am not ready to declare every issue fixed. But the execution was better, and the Eagles found something they could lean on throughout the game. The maddening part is what did not come next. If a defense is flowing hard toward outside zone to the left, the natural counter is boot action with Hurts moving back to his right. The run game should create that throw. It never really did. That is the central problem with this offense. A successful run should make the next pass easier. Here, the run game existed in isolation. There was no sense that one concept was setting up another. 2) One big positive was the outside zone running game, which finally got going. The team also produced some excellent blocks in the run game. Kendall looked good again (I mean, what a finish here!), and they attacked the left side of the defense, as I said they should in the… pic.twitter.com/km30VsjcjY — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 29, 2026 This is why the pass protection has to be the Eagles’ first priority this week. Under center, play-action cannot function if Hurts turns his back to sell the fake and immediately finds an unblocked defender in his face when he turns around. The routes have not reached their useful point, the back is still following the fake, and the quarterback has no clean platform to throw. It doesn’t matter whether the play design created an open receiver if the protection doesn’t give Hurts enough time to see him. Not every pressure came from the same error. Some snaps raised a protection-count question. Others exposed a problem with the play’s construction. Even if the line blocked the defenders they were assigned, who was responsible for the linebacker attacking the space vacated during the fake? This was a consistent issue, and when the same broad issue appears repeatedly, the coaches need to provide a dependable rule that everyone understands. The Eagles have several possible answers. If they want a long fake and a deep crossing route, they can keep a tight end or second back (fullback, anyone?) in protection and accept having fewer receivers in the pattern. They can shorten the fake and ask the back to scan inside before releasing. They can change the slide toward the likely A-gap pressure, move Hurts’ launch point, or build in an immediate throw behind the linebacker as soon as Hurts completes his turn. There is no single magic solution. The unacceptable option is to keep combining a long-developing fake and route concept with protection that acts like the ball should already be gone. My preferred answer is to split the under-center play-action package in two. Use sturdier protection when you want the deep crosser. If the back is going to sell the fake and release, give Hurts a route he can throw immediately when he turns around. Right now, the Eagles are asking the protection to survive longer than the backfield action allows. That mismatch is killing good concepts before they can develop. "The food at this place is really terrible…and such small portions!" #Eagles have run the fewest under center play action plays in the NFL through 3 weeks, and have been terrible at it when they have, with a league-low 25% success rate. pic.twitter.com/lClDbJWrwL — Deniz Selman (@denizselman33) September 29, 2026 This also feels uncomfortably familiar. Before Kellen Moore, the Eagles too often appeared to treat Hurts creating outside structure as their answer to pressure. Moore improved that area. Now it feels as though the offense is drifting back toward ‘Hurts must create’ as the protection plan. That cannot be the solution. The Eagles ran under center play-action 3 times in this game, and every time Hurts didn’t stand a chance. That’s a nightmare. 3) One answer for why they don't do it is pass protection. I truly believe pass protection in this game stopped the offense from succeeding, in particular from under center. There are too many plays where unblocked defenders come free on Hurts, or he doesn't have the time to look… pic.twitter.com/w8SqkqqmGt — Jonny Page (@JonnyPage9) September 29, 2026 The Eagles have had some success with Mesh Rail this season, and this is another good example. I have already seen screenshots of Dontayvion Wicks standing open on the right side, followed by criticism of Hurts for not throwing him the football. Ignore those screenshots; they aren’t worth engaging with. Hurts is reading the left side. The beauty of Mesh is that the crossing receiver eventually enters the quarterback’s line of vision from the opposite side, so Hurts does not have to read…

title: Eagles rookie report card from the Bears game
summary: The Eagles dropped to 2-1 after a flat showing on Monday Night Football against the Bears. It was a depressing loss to say the least, and there’s blame to go around for the Eagles lack of juice. The team only had one rookie make any meaningful contributions.  Makai Lemon: C- I am just as perplexed […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Makai Lemon #9 of the Philadelphia Eagles looks on prior to the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Eagles dropped to 2-1 after a flat showing on Monday Night Football against the Bears. It was a depressing loss to say the least, and there’s blame to go around for the Eagles lack of juice. The team only had one rookie make any meaningful contributions. Makai Lemon: C- I am just as perplexed as the rest of you. On one end, Makai Lemon’s numbers have improved every week this year, but the bar is really low. He went from negative five yards in the Washington game, to 14 yards in Tennessee and then he put up 29 in the game last night. Lemon had a nice catch downfield in the first half where he broke some tackles and picked up yards after catch. And he had another similar catch later in the game. But Sean Mannion once again insisted on using Lemon on a bizarre screen attempt that lost yardage. Funny enough, Lemon picked up three yards on that play after the catch, but the play was so far behind the line that it still lost three yards. On the season, Lemon has seven catches for 38 yards, averaging 5.4 yards per reception. Lemon has been targeted on three screens this season that have lost 11 total yards. On the rest of his receptions, he has 49 yards on four catches. I don’t really understand why Mannion keeps running these screens. I don’t mind Lemon lining up in the backfield to create mismatches, but the Eagles have not established a strong screen game yet and don’t seem to have the personnel to block for it. Maybe it improves, but it’s head-scratching every time it happens. Other Observations I hate to say it, but Cam Jurgens is unplayable. I’d have to guess there is a health thing that is limiting him, or perhaps it’s the move to left guard, but it’s hard to watch him struggle out there. While Willie Lampkin is the next in line to get guard snaps, you have to wonder if Micah Morris or even Markel Bell will see any time on the starting line this season. The Eagles need Eli Stowers to make an impact when he comes off injured reserve. The Zach Ertz thing feels good, but it’s hard to see him making a real impact this year. E.J. Jenkins and Johnny Mundt are not filling in well as blockers or pass catchers. While the hope should be Dallas Goedert makes a triumphant healthy return in a few weeks, Philly needs more from its second-round pick sooner than later.

title: Jalen Hurts talks concussion evaluation from Eagles-Bears game
summary: The Eagles struggled on Monday night against the Bears — on offense and on defense — and quarterback Jalen Hurts took responsibility post-game for not playing up to his standard. He said, all-in-all, there was a theme of negative plays and they need to keep building continuity in what they’re doing. Hurts also noted that […]
full_text: The Eagles struggled on Monday night against the Bears — on offense and on defense — and quarterback Jalen Hurts took responsibility post-game for not playing up to his standard. He said, all-in-all, there was a theme of negative plays and they need to keep building continuity in what they’re doing. Hurts also noted that all the things that get them behind the sticks, are things they can control, so they need to get to work to fix those. The quarterback acknowledged that a lot of people are going to spend the week picking apart the game and asking about individual plays, which he thinks is understood and appropriate, but as a leader of the team, he thinks that many of the concerns are bigger picture. Still, he’s confident that they just need to keep working their process and continue to find themselves on offense. “We just got to take this brick-by-brick. This is an opportunity to learn from, but we have to choose to learn from it. That was my message to everyone. Nobody’s gonna wait on us to do the things we need to do, so we all just need to dedicate ourselves to this, and keep pushing forward.” Here’s what the QB had to say: On his possible concussion Hurts said that he felt like he could still play immediately after the late-hit, and didn’t feel like he had any kind of head injury. “I just went through my normal evaluation. They felt that I need to do the standard SOP for protocol.” The QB noted that he was still waiting for the results when he was on the sideline and Andy Dalton was playing his third snap. “Just waiting for the thumbs up. I felt fine, we already checked it. I don’t know the extent of the process. Obviously, wish we could have expedited things, I know I felt fine.” He reiterated that he was in a place mentally and physically that he was able to return to the field and continue playing, and hopefully they can learn from this situation, but it’s not something they really can plan for. Still, he accepted that there is a process he had to go through based on what they saw, and he didn’t want to put too much blame on that time he was out. On the TD before halftime “We went in to attempt to clock the ball. I didn’t think we’d have enough time to clock it. So, we’re pretty good at the quarterback sneak.” On punting on 4th-and-1 “Competitively, I’m always gonna want to go for it. I always trust Coach [Sirianni] to make the right decision in these situation. I just sung his praises this past week and how he’s been managing those situations. So, there’s no difference with that. Win some, you lose some, obviously there’s always something we can learn from.” On his INT “That’s one of those plays I say I didn’t play to my standard in situational football — 4th-and-5, they did a really good job defensively of showing all-out blitz and getting out of it. I think, really, [they] played aggressive defense, tried to set the terms of the game a little bit, and that’s something we got an opportunity to combat. But, on that play specifically, just was trying to get the ball to 6 [DeVonta Smith], spot route. Felt like we could find a void in the zone. His eyes didn’t turn the way I thought they were, [I] gave one up. And, had Makai [Lemon] right there to the field on a hitch route I could’ve taken. So, not to my standard at all.“

title: Eagles News: Outcoached by the Bears
summary: Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Ben Johnson is obviously more accomplished than Nick Sirianni. But, be honest, did you find yourself jealous of how the Bears’ head coach gave his team an edge last night? All while the Eagles’ head coach struggled to maximize what he […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: (L-R)Head coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles congratulates head coach Ben Johnson of the Chicago Bears after the game at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Michael Reaves/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to The Linc, the daily Philadelphia Eagles links roundup at Bleeding Green Nation! Ben Johnson is obviously more accomplished than Nick Sirianni. But, be honest, did you find yourself jealous of how the Bears’ head coach gave his team an edge last night? All while the Eagles’ head coach struggled to maximize what he could control to help his team win? Or is that just me? Let’s get to the Philadelphia Eagles news and links … Roob’s Instant Observations after Eagles embarrass themselves against Bears – NBCSP This was a game where the Bears’ coaches thoroughly out-coached the Eagles’ coaches. Ben Johnson had a masterful plan to neutralize the Eagles’ defense, keep them off balance, keep them guessing, confuse them and render them utterly ineffective. He completely out-coached Vic Fangio and that’s not something you see very often. And Bears defensive coordinator Dennis Allen had a perfect plan to stifle the Eagles’ offense and take away everything Sean Mannion wanted to do and render Jalen Hurts ineffective. And Nick Sirianni just didn’t have his team prepared. What’s really discouraging is that the Bears made all the halftime adjustments. The Eagles had some good momentum with the touchdown just before halftime, but the Bears outscored them 17-0 in the second half, outgained them 199-62 and held the Eagles to just three first downs. The Eagles have been outplayed in the second half in all three games, getting outscored by a total of 40-20 and outgained 563-334. That’s alarming. The Eagles didn’t just get outplayed. They got out-coached. Eagles-Bears takeaway: Lackluster play catches up with the Birds in Chicago – BGN You could feel this game coming. In Week 1, the Eagles struggled to beat the Commanders in Washington 24-22. They followed it up with a last-second, 24-20 victory on the road against the Titans, who finished with the NFL’s second-worst record a season ago. The defense had put together two lackluster performances against weaker opponents. The offense was bailed out by Jalen Hurts playing hero ball. And so last night’s 27-7 shellacking at the hands of Ben Johnson’s Bears in Chicago shouldn’t have been too surprising. Hopefully, it’s a wake-up call. Against an opponent superior to the two they played previously, Hurts couldn’t paper over the offensive line’s continuing and worrisome struggles, and the defensive line’s inability to pressure the quarterback continued despite the return of Jonathan Greenard. Meanwhile, the secondary suffered breakdowns throughout the game and allowed a third-string QB who they beat in the… checks notes… 2017 NFC Championship Game put up a 110.8 rating against them. Eagles Downed: Bears BEAT UP Jalen Hurts, Eagles D in Ugly MNF Loss – PHLY Eagles Post Game Show Case Keenum exacted his revenge on the Eagles with a spotlight game in the twilight of his career as the Eagles defense looked sloppy and ill-prepared while Jalen Hurts threw a second-half interception, Nick Sirianni forgot to try to win the game and Andy Dalton did what Andy Dalton has done since joining the Eagles. The Eagles fell to 2-1 with the Los Angeles Rams on deck next Sunday. Super Bowl champion Vinny Curry, Miles Johnson, Brandon Lee Gowton and Bo Wulf react to the game, with insight from Fran Duffy and EJ Smith, live on the scene in Chicago. Bears show resilience in primetime win over Eagles – Windy City Gridiron Coming into Monday night after a 9-3 loss to the Vikings, with third-string quarterback Case Keenum thrust into a starting role, the Bears had several question marks around them in Week 3. They answered those questions in about as decisively as you could possibly imagine. The Bears trounced the Eagles 27-7 on Monday night, excelling on both sides of the ball in a win to improve their record to 2-1 for the season. Keenum looked impressive in his first start since 2023, and Chicago got back on its feet to get back into the win column. In a game where many doubted the Bears, they bounced back and showed the nation what they’re capable of. Here are some of my takeaways from Monday’s victory. Case Keenum went from forgotten QB to Bears hero on Monday Night Football – SB Nation Keenum completed 24-of-34 passes for 247 yards and a pair of touchdowns on a night where everyone, including Eagles defensive coordinator Vic Fangio, expected the Bears to run the football as much as possible to help their third-string quarterback. While the Bears struggled to get the running game going until late, and Johnson even spoke about the need to run the football during a halftime interview with ESPN, Keenum kept slinging it. And slinging it well. His first touchdown pass, an underneath shovel pass to Luther Burden, came as a result of an incredible individual effort from the wide receiver and his teammates, as he bullied his way into the end zone after being initially stopped well short of the goal line. Keenum’s second touchdown pass, however, had a higher level of difficulty. Handing out 10 awards from the Eagles-Bears game – PhillyVoice 3) The ‘Again… WHY?!’ Award ⁉️: Andy Dalton. I’ll never understand what the Eagles see in Andy Dalton. He has had a long NFL career that he should be proud of, but physically, he’s going to be 39 in October and there’s simply no upside there at all. He had some really bad tape last season, and at this stage of his career he doesn’t have a strong arm and he’s not a threat as a runner. When he was at his best during training camp, he got the ball out quickly and on time. When he was at his worst, his physical flaws were obvious. Whatever you may think of Tanner McKee — some fans like him more than others — he’s better than Dalton. In fairness, Dalton was put into a difficult situation. He was being asked to close out a long drive with a TD. Of course, that should really be the benefit of a player in his 16th NFL season — that he has seen it all and is just ready for those moments. But, for those of us who watched training camp all summer, the INT wasn’t much of a surprise. Windy City Heat – Iggles Blitz Vic Fangio is a brilliant defensive coach, but either he doesn’t have the right players or he didn’t have the right plan. Chicago’s offense had open receivers way too often on Monday night. Keenum wasn’t sacked and the Eagles were only credited with 3 QB hits. This defense has been disappointing in all three games so far. This was the first game where you can argue that they were flat out bad. Jalen Hurts looked terrific last week and got us all excited. He stunk up the joint on MNF. He missed some easy throws. He didn’t look comfortable in the pocket. He made some bad reads and forced the ball into coverage. Discouraging performance. Sean Mannion did a solid job in the first half, but then made some awful calls in the second half. You can see the huge gap between a guru like Ben Johnson and a noob like Mannion. Nick Sirianni didn’t have a great performance either. He made some questionable decisions. The Early Bird: Nick Sirianni’s fourth-down balk, Eagles defensive woes underscore a ‘true team loss’ to Bears – PHLY Eagles None of this is to say that Sirianni’s decision alone lost the Eagles the game at Soldier Field. Sirianni aptly characterized it as a “true team loss,” underscored by both the Eagles defense and offense turning in one of the worst performances each group has had over the last several seasons. “We all have to own that loss right there,” Sirianni said. “I don’t think anybody coached well. I don’t think anyone played well. It was a true team loss. And when it’s a true team loss, I have to look at myself first. We weren’t ready to coach, we weren’t ready to play. And that ultimately starts and ends with me.” Offensively, this…
