title: Eagles-Bears takeaway: Lackluster play catches up with the Birds in Chicago
summary: You could feel this game coming. In Week 1, the Eagles struggled to beat the Commanders in Washington 24-22. They followed it up with a last-second, 24-20 victory on the road against the Titans, who finished with the NFL’s second-worst record a season ago. The defense had put together two lackluster performances against weaker opponents. […]
full_text: CHICAGO, ILLINOIS - SEPTEMBER 28: Head Coach Nick Sirianni of the Philadelphia Eagles gestures during the fourth quarter of the NFL game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field on September 28, 2026 in Chicago, Illinois. (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images You could feel this game coming. In Week 1, the Eagles struggled to beat the Commanders in Washington 24-22. They followed it up with a last-second, 24-20 victory on the road against the Titans, who finished with the NFL’s second-worst record a season ago. The defense had put together two lackluster performances against weaker opponents. The offense was bailed out by Jalen Hurts playing hero ball. And so last night’s 27-7 shellacking at the hands of Ben Johnson’s Bears in Chicago shouldn’t have been too surprising. Hopefully, it’s a wake-up call. Against an opponent superior to the two they played previously, Hurts couldn’t paper over the offensive line’s continuing and worrisome struggles, and the defensive line’s inability to pressure the quarterback continued despite the return of Jonathan Greenard. Meanwhile, the secondary suffered breakdowns throughout the game and allowed a third-string QB who they beat in the… checks notes… 2017 NFC Championship Game put up a 110.8 rating against them. Giants vs. Eagles will be played on the fifth anniversary of the Vikings vs. Eagles NFC Championship game. 38-7. pic.twitter.com/0kRenhPCOK — Brenden Deeg (@BrendenDeeg_) January 18, 2023 Yup, that was the same Case Keenum throwing for 247 yards, 2 TDs and no interceptions against a Vic Fangio unit that garnered a whole lotta hype in training camp. They’ve given up an average of 23.0 points per game through three outings, 16th in the NFL. They have three sacks thus far and have yet to force a turnover, sitting -5 in the turnover differential. Per Sumer Sports , the Birds are 23rd in EPA/play and 20th in success rate. The safeties and linebacking corps haven’t looked good through three games. Drew Mukuba, Marcus Epps and Michael Carter II have missed tackles and blown assignments. Nakobe Dean’s absence has been felt, with Jihaad Campbell so far failing to replicate his predecessor’s performance. But the real issue stems from the defensive line, who quite simply, hasn’t delivered on their preseason promise. A lot of money has been invested on the defensive line. Jalen Carter signed a 4-year, $152 million contract extension with $107 million in guaranteed money this off-season. Jordan Davis got a 3-year, $78 million deal with $64 million guaranteed. Jonathan Greenard received a 4-year, $98 million extension after his trade from Minnesota, and Jalyx Hunt will likely be the next lineman to follow with a similar mega-deal. Greenard just this week returned to the field following two weeks on the injured list, so it’s unfair to expect peak performance from him as of yet, but there is little excuse for everyone else. Moro Ojomo and Nolan Smith, two young players looking to secure big deals of their own, have been largely silent. One has to think Fangio’s guys will figure this out and get it together, but there is absolutely no excuse for getting shredded in a prime time NFL game by Case Keenum in the year 2026. A defense some believed would be one of the five best units in the sport has been middling through their first three games, and the onus is on the defensive line to make life difficult for opposing coordinators. On the offensive side, preseason concerns about the O-line were well-founded. Landon Dickerson’s inability to return to full health was less than ideal. Fortunately, last year’s 5th-round pick Drew Kendall has held his own thus far at center. The rest of the line has struggled. Tyler Steen has been abysmal at right guard to start the season. Cam Jugens, who shifted from center to left guard with Dickerson out, can’t find any consistency. And Jordan Mailata, one of the highest-priced vets on the team, has simply not been the same player since the 2024 Super Bowl season. Lane Johnson has been fine at right tackle, but he can’t do it all alone. On 1st-and-goal from just outside the one yard line in the 2nd quarter, the offensive line couldn’t generate enough push or open up a single lane to allow Barkley to run the ball into the end zone for the tying score. Instead, they forced Sean Mannion to try a pass play on 3rd-and-goal from the 2 with Andy Dalton, who threw an interception in the end zone. A 95-yard drive ended in no points as a result. Sure, Dalton is terrible, should not be on the roster and should not have been asked to throw a pass in that situation. But the O-line’s inability to get Barkley in the end zone on first and second downs shouldn’t be ignored, either. In the first half against the Bears, the line looked like it was figuring things out. Saquon Barkley broke off some big runs and the running game looked good. Barkley ran for 73 yards on 11 carries before halftime and then came out and rushed four times for nine yards in the second half. Jalen Hurts’ pass protection was OK, but some killer penalties and poor execution on 1st and 2nd downs put him behind the sticks most of the night, resulting in an ugly performance in which he threw for just 153 yards with two turnovers. He was shut out in the 2nd half. He was not helped by his coaching staff. Nick Sirianni’s decision not to go for it on 4th-and-1 near midfield in the 3rd quarter trailing 20-7 reeked of a lack of confidence in his unit. After the game, Sirianni, the team’s CEO head coach who says he specializes in his decision-making in just these kinds of game situations, admitted he made a mistake. He then went for it on 4th-and-5 later in the 4th quarter, after the game had largely been decided. None of it made sense. Play-caller Sean Mannion continues to call screen passes behind the line to Makai Lemon, and receivers weren’t schemed open this week. It had been a bumpy first two weeks for the Eagles, but they had persevered and managed to pull out two victories against lesser opponents/coaching staffs. Against Ben Johnson’s Bears, they did not receive similar fortune. Things won’t get any easier when Matthew Stafford comes to Philadelphia this week, looking to exact revenge in his own personal house of horrors. The Rams, 1-2 to start the season, will be out for blood. Then it’s on to Jacksonville to face a Jaguars team that has given up the fewest points in the league through the first three weeks. If they play like they did last night in Chicago, the Eagles will be staring at a 2-3 record two weeks from now.
author: John Stolnis

title: Steelers-Browns preview: What to expect from Cleveland’s offense, defense in Week 4
summary: The Steelers and Browns will meet on Thursday Night Football to open the NFL’s Week 4 — and who would’ve thought the winner will take the lead in the AFC North? Both Pittsburgh and Cleveland, with new head coaches, have endured some early-season struggles to emerge with a 2-1 record to open 2026. Now, it’s […]
full_text: Sep 20, 2026; Tampa, Florida, USA; Cleveland Browns linebacker Carson Schwesinger (49) reacts after they beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers during the second half at Raymond James Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kim Klement Neitzel-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Steelers and Browns will meet on Thursday Night Football to open the NFL’s Week 4 — and who would’ve thought the winner will take the lead in the AFC North? Both Pittsburgh and Cleveland, with new head coaches, have endured some early-season struggles to emerge with a 2-1 record to open 2026. Now, it’s a short-week divisional game — both teams will be vying for yet another gritty win on Thursday night. What to expect from the Browns’ offense Rushing YPG: 87.7 (29th) Passing YPG: 178.3 (28th) PPG: 18 (24th) RB : The Browns offense, much like the team as a whole, is in a weird spot right now. Stuck with quarterback Deshaun Watson for another season and enduring a 34-10 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars in Week 1, it looked like Cleveland’s season was over right about when it began. But although the overall metrics still aren’t great, Cleveland has managed to put together just enough offensive production to enjoy a two-game winning streak entering Week 4, with a 23-19 win over the Buccaneers and a 21-18 win over the Carolina Panthers in the last two weeks. The Browns are one of three AFC North teams to have a new head coach in 2026, with former Ravens offensive coordinator Todd Monken taking on the role while also being Cleveland’s play caller. Under Monken, Cleveland has used some of his signature heavy-personnel tendencies (tight formations, a healthy dose of fullback Michael Burton), but are a primarily 11 personnel operation. According to NFL Pro, Cleveland currently uses it 64.7% of the time, while Monken’s highest 11 personnel rate in Baltimore was 47.2% in 2023. Some of that willingness to use more receivers has come from the Browns retooling the position group in the draft with the additions of Texas A&M’s KC Concepcion and Washington’s Denzel Boston. Concepcion, playing primarily in the slot so far, certainly hasn’t been bad, but he and Watson have struggled to connect despite the rookie seeing a number of snaps and targets. But with incredible quickness and primary usage in the short game, he remains a yards after catch threat. Wide receivers with 20+ targets and <81 receiving yards through the first three weeks of the season, since 2000. KC Concepcion joining a distinguished line of Browns pass catchers. pic.twitter.com/1tSCq2D3WR — Benjamin Solak (@BenjaminSolak) September 29, 2026 However, the budding star on the Browns offense to start the season is Boston, who has emerged as a legitimate Offensive Rookie of the Year candidate through three games with nine catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns. The big-bodied wideout is a smooth mover with great hands who has developed good chemistry with Watson in the intermediate passing game. Denzel Boston getting constant chunks already through 2 games as an NFL player. all the explosive reception leaders right now are strong pass catchers that can run through contact on intermediate throws. pic.twitter.com/qAgdtwiJEy — Nate Tice (@Nate_Tice) September 20, 2026 While the Browns are primarily a short passing game (Watson averages just 6.6 yards per attempt), Monken’s passing concepts emphasize in-breakers that find spots in zone, and motion before the snap and into the routes to give receivers some early momentum. That’s created some easy completions; per NFL Pro, the Browns’ 4.5 yards of separation per target is the best mark in the league. Cleveland’s 71 yards after the catch over expected is also the NFL’s seventh-best mark. Still, Watson hasn’t always been able to take full advantage of his talented group of pass catchers, which also includes young tight end Harold Fannin Jr. The Browns have SEPARATORS. KC, Boston, & Jerry completely dominated their defenders. Boston with the sudden snap down, KC stemming inside & winning with violent hands over top, & Jerry attacking leverage and getting the DB turned around with the rocker step. pic.twitter.com/mKN1sZX59V — Cam White (@RouteUniverse9) September 30, 2026 We have got to find a way to hit KC on this basic. Would have been a gigantic play. pic.twitter.com/zPMo8fQg5o — Cam White (@RouteUniverse9) September 30, 2026 While Watson has a 4-0 touchdown/interception ratio over the last two games, he had at least two almost-interceptions and a number of other misses against the Panthers in Week 3. Still, Watson hasn’t lost all the traits that used to make him a productive passer in the NFL. He can be a bit of a one-speed thrower but still possesses a powerful arm. He’s also been impressively mobile at times in 2026, even if his throwing off-platform comes with highs and lows. that's ✌️ scores on the day for Harold! #CARvsCLE on FOX pic.twitter.com/gYzHTbpmYR — Cleveland Browns (@Browns) September 27, 2026 Still, Watson has already amassed 105 rushing yards on the season. And according to NFL Pro, while he’s faced 12 unblocked pressures this season — good for third-most in the NFL — he has not been sacked on any of them. He’s done a good job of slipping by rushers in the pocket. Watson has had to scramble more because the Browns offensive line remains a work in progress. Through three weeks, Cleveland has allowed the eighth-highest pressure rate (39.4%) and the third-worst sack rate (9.8%). The running game has been similarly unsteady. Cleveland has the sixth-worst rushing success rate in football (33.3%), with the offensive line often looking uncoordinated, especially on the team’s zone concepts. Running backs Quinshon Judkins and Raheem Sanders are hard-nosed, downhill backs, but haven’t always been able to get a runway through three weeks. Like I said bad blocking on the perimeter You have to either seal or drive out the overhang in wide zone Fannin gets good pop but doesn’t replace his hands Howard takes a very slow left step & the double with Barber isn’t tight Front side is washed and no where to cut back pic.twitter.com/kMYag1yRe0 — Mac🦬 (@tha_buffalo) September 25, 2026 I wouldn’t expect those line troubles to be fixed on a short week ahead of Thursday Night Football. Tackle Tytus Howard (knee) and guard Teven Jenkins (back) were limited in Tuesday’s practice, while center Elgton Jenkins did not participate in concussion protocol. And while healthy, both guard Zion Johnson and rookie tackle Spencer Fano have been shaky at times early in the season. This is a flawed Browns offense, and Pittsburgh should be able to find some success if its pass rush can consistently win against a struggling Cleveland line and force mistakes from Watson. Still, Watson and the Browns’ developing group of offensive weapons have managed to get the job done in recent weeks, with Watson tossing a go-ahead touchdown in each of the team’s last two games to earn a win. Sure, “the Browns is the Browns,” but that doesn’t mean there aren’t some exciting players in this offense. What to expect from the Browns’ defense Rushing YPG Allowed: 120.3 (23rd) Passing YPG Allowed: 224.0 (18th) PPG Allowed: 23.7 (18th) RP : Much like the Steelers, the Browns defense has undergone some significant transformation since these teams last met. The headliner here, of course, is that the team traded away perennial All-Pro Myles Garrett during the offseason. But Cleveland also has a new coaching staff, which means this defense is no longer the blitz-happy unit it was for the past three seasons under Jim Schwartz. Instead, the Browns have a first-time coordinator in Mike Rutenberg. So far, Rutenberg and the Browns are blitzing far less. In the three seasons under Schwartz, the Browns’ blitz rate never dipped below 28.2% in any given year. In 2026, the Browns are blitzing at a 23.3% clip, the ninth-lowest figure in the NFL. And yet, the Browns appear to be having even greater success than they did just a year ago. Last season,…

title: Jerry Jones hints that Cowboys have interest in Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr.
summary: Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones confirmed the team is exploring potential roster additions, and Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. appears to be among the names connected to the Cowboys. Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Jones said Dallas currently has “conversations going on” regarding ways to upgrade its roster. When Porter’s name was brought up […]
full_text: (Photo by Stacy Revere/Getty Images) | Getty Images Dallas Cowboys owner Jerry Jones confirmed the team is exploring potential roster additions, and Pittsburgh Steelers cornerback Joey Porter Jr. appears to be among the names connected to the Cowboys. Speaking on 105.3 The Fan, Jones said Dallas currently has “conversations going on” regarding ways to upgrade its roster. When Porter’s name was brought up during the appearance, Jones declined to specifically address the Steelers cornerback, citing NFL tampering rules. Cowboys owner Jerry Jones on @1053thefan said there are “conversations going on” right now to potentially upgrade their roster. He wouldn’t specifically comment on Steelers CB Joey Porter Jr. to avoid tampering — Jon Machota (@jonmachota) September 29, 2026 The decision not to discuss Porter directly does not necessarily confirm that the Cowboys have made an offer or are actively negotiating for him, but his name has emerged in connection with Dallas as the team evaluates options. Dallas has reason to explore additions to its secondary. The Cowboys have dealt with several injuries in the defensive backfield, including P.J. Locke being placed on injured reserve and Jalen Thompson dealing with a hamstring injury. Those absences have reduced the team’s depth and forced Dallas to make roster moves, including elevating players from its practice squad. Porter remains under his rookie contract and has dealt with a contract situation and reported back injury that has limited his availability, adding another layer to any potential trade discussion. For now, Jones’ comments stop short of confirming Dallas’ interest in Porter. But with the Cowboys actively exploring ways to improve their roster and Porter’s name circulating in trade discussions, the Steelers cornerback is a player worth monitoring as the situation develops. title: Steelers’ Jalen Ramsey hopes to play vs. Browns despite broken wrist
summary: Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey revealed to media members Tuesday that he has a broken wrist, ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported Tuesday. Still, he hopes to play in the Steelers’ Week 4 matchup against the Cleveland Browns despite less recovery time than usual due to the Thursday night kickoff. “It’s just going to be about seeing […]
full_text: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 27: Jalen Ramsey #5 of the Pittsburgh Steelers looks on against the Cincinnati Bengals during an NFL football game at Acrisure Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Steelers defensive back Jalen Ramsey revealed to media members Tuesday that he has a broken wrist, ESPN’s Brooke Pryor reported Tuesday. Jalen Ramsey said today that his wrist is broken. On playing vs. Cleveland: "It's just going to be about seeing if I'm able to protect it and also still be myself in a good enough capacity where I feel like if I go out there, I won't be letting any of my teammates down." https://t.co/lzzMfF3OOR — Brooke Pryor (@bepryor) September 29, 2026 Still, he hopes to play in the Steelers’ Week 4 matchup against the Cleveland Browns despite less recovery time than usual due to the Thursday night kickoff. “It’s just going to be about seeing if I’m able to protect (my wrist) and also still be myself in a good enough capacity where I feel like if I go out there, I won’t be letting any of my teammates down,” he said Tuesday, via Pryor. Ramsey played every Steelers defensive snap last week against the Cincinnati Bengals. PennLive’s Nick Farabaugh reported on Tuesday that Ramsey suffered the broken wrist on the Bengals’ first drive. “I’m going to give everything to try to (play). I have to be able to protect it. It’s a real injury, a broken wrist. I can’t really do anything about it,” Ramsey said via Farabaugh. The veteran defensive back was seen in a sling earlier in the week, but switched to a wrist brace in Tuesday’s walkthrough practice. While Pittsburgh has only estimated practice participation thus far this week, Ramsey has been listed as limited on both Monday and Tuesday. Ramsey plays an important role in an already shorthanded Steelers secondary, seeing reps at both nickel cornerback and safety. Starting safety DeShon Elliott is on injured reserve for at least one more game, while cornerback Joey Porter Jr. has yet to play this season amid reported back and conditioning issues as well as a contract dispute. If Ramsey can’t go on Thursday, the Steelers will have some questions to answer at nickel cornerback. Cornerback Brandin Echols has started the week with two limited practices in concussion protocol, while the team’s next in line at slot corner, practice squad defender Doneiko Slaughter, has already been promoted to the active roster the maximum three times this season. If the Steelers want to play Slaughter on Thursday, the team will need to officially sign him to the 53-man roster and cut another player to make space.

title: Steelers Week 3 grades in win over Bengals
summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers did a complete 180 from their performance in Week 2 and saw their offense come to life against the Cincinnati Bengals in a 30-27 win. As they get ready for the Cleveland Browns on a short week, we give you our Week 3 grades as the Steelers improved to 2-1. QB Aaron […]
full_text: (Photo by Joe Sargent/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Steelers did a complete 180 from their performance in Week 2 and saw their offense come to life against the Cincinnati Bengals in a 30-27 win. As they get ready for the Cleveland Browns on a short week, we give you our Week 3 grades as the Steelers improved to 2-1. QB Aaron Rodgers ​ Jarrett Bailey: Rodgers looked as good as he ever has in a Steelers uniform. He finished the week tied for eighth in EPA per play among quarterbacks, and nearly topped 300 yards with three touchdowns. Had a pass not bounced off Roman Wilson’s hands for an interception, his stat line would have been as close to perfect as it can get. Great bounce back from Rodgers and the offense. Grade: A Joey Bray: Was it the cleanest game from Aaron Rodgers? No, but it was easily one of the better performances we have ever seen from the veteran quarterback in a Steelers uniform. Again, Rodgers was let down by his receivers, who left a few completions on the field. Despite all of the miscommunications and trouble snapping the ball on time, Rodgers threw for nearly 300 yards and three touchdowns. This is the type of performance you should be hoping for every week from your 42-year-old quarterback. Grade: A ​Offensive Line ​ Jarrett Bailey: The Steelers had over 400 yards of offense on Sunday, and that was in no small part due to the upgraded play on the offensive line. Brock Hoffman and Max Iheanachor made their respective first starts of the season, and instantly provided more time for Rodgers to throw and opened more lanes for Jaylen Warren to run through. While we can’t expect them to be perfect each week, this was as close to perfection as it gets. Grade: A+ Joey Bray : It cannot be overstated just how much the offensive line play opened up the Steelers offense in Week 3. Rookie first-round pick Max Iheanachor got his first career start at right tackle, while veteran Brock Hoffman took over for Spencer Anderson at right guard. Both played well, and you could see the difference in the offense this week. Both the running and passing game both saw season highs in terms of production while the offense scored 30 points after scoring just 16 points through the first two weeks. While it’s still hard to imagine we see the offense put up 30 points every week, the changes to the offensive line seem to have made a massive impact on the offense. Grade: A+ ​RB Jaylen Warren ​ Jarrett Bailey: Warren had a career day, putting up a career-best 176 yards from scrimmage. Had his run of north of 80 yards not been taken away due to a ticky-tack penalty, we could be talking about Warren topping 200 yards on the ground. Keep feeding No. 30. Grade: A Joey Bray : This was one of the very best games that Jaylen Warren has played in the NFL. Warren averaged 7.5 yards per carry and had an 84-yard run negated due to a holding call. He also should have at least ten more yards and a touchdown to his total if he weren’t caught by the turf monster. The speedy back had to carry the load with the absence of Ric Dowdle, and proved that he deserves a larger slice of the pie even when Dowdle is back healthy. Grade: A+ WR Roman Wilson Jarrett Bailey: It’s constantly one step forward and another step back for Wilson. He was sprung open for a touchdown on the opening drive, and then had a pass bounce off his hands for an interception later on in the game. Germie Bernard needs more looks. Grade: C+ Joey Bray : Man, I really thought I was going to be able to talk nicely about Roman Wilson after his 38-yard touchdown on the opening drive of the game. However, Wilson is responsible for Rodgers’ interception as the ball bounced right off the hands of the young receiver. Wilson was left on the bench for a good majority of the second half as rookie second-rounder Germie Bernard saw the field more. The inconsistencies of Wilson continue to outshine any bright spot he creates. He continues to be a frustrating player to evaluate. Grade: C ​Pass Defense ​ Jarrett Bailey: I’m not going to crush the Steelers’ secondary. When you face an elite quarterback and two high-caliber receivers, you’re going to give up yards. Burrow was getting the ball out quickly, and both Chase and Higgins had good days picking apart the consistent zone looks from the Steelers. They need to be better as a unit, but it also felt like the plan was to be a bend don’t break defense against an elite passing attack. Grade: C- Joey Bray : I have a tough time being super hard on the secondary considering they are down two of their best players in Joey Porter Jr. and DeShon Elliott. That being said, this was their worst showing of the season. Joe Burrow started the game 14/14 and had a solid game overall. The Bengals, of course, have one of the best receiver duos in the league, which poses its own set of challenges for the Steelers each time they play Cincinnati. It was another zone coverage-heavy game for the defense who was picked apart by an elite quarter and a duo of elite receivers. Grade: D ​Special Teams ​Jarrett Bailey: Sunday felt like a vintage Steelers win, largely due to their luck and playmaking on special teams. A roughing the kicker call on Cam Johnston extended a drive that led to a DK Metcalf touchdown. A muffed punt was then recovered by Ben Skowronek and set up a Chris Boswell field goal, of which he went 3-for-3 on the day. A great day for the special teams. Grade: A Joey Bray : After missing a field goal in each of the first two games, Chris Boswell went 3-for-3 on field goals. Cam Johnston appeared to get hit during a punt but bounced back and turned in a solid performance. Kaden Wetjen has yet to make any impact plays as a return man, but it could only be a matter of time before he breaks one loose. Grade: A Let us know what you think in the comments . summary: In devastating news for the Miami Dolphins, star running back De’Von Achane suffered an ACL tear against the Kansas City Chiefs. full_text: In devastating news for the Miami Dolphins, star running back De’Von Achane suffered an ACL tear against the Kansas City Chiefs. He’s obviously out for the season, as one of the few reasons to even watch the Dolphins on purpose won’t be back until 2027. And so the search begins for running back depth, and the Dolphins have brought in a couple of former Seahawks running backs for tryouts. Kenny McIntosh and Damien Martinez, seventh-round picks in 2023 and 2025 respectively, were among four running backs Miami worked out. Don’t believe me for some reason? Here’s the official NFL transaction wire, which has no choice but to be truthful. Unlike Martinez, McIntosh did make Seattle’s active roster as a rookie and even had a minor role in Seattle’s offense in 2024. Unfortunately, injuries limited his playing time in 2023 and he missed all of 2025 with an ACL tear suffered in training camp . McIntosh was waived earlier this summer during training camp and has not signed with a new team despite visits with several teams , including Klint Kubiak’s undefeated Las Vegas Raiders. Martinez, who finished his collegiate career at the University of Miami, had some intrigue as a Day 3 running back. He underwhelmed throughout camp and preseason and found himself on the outside looking in for roster cuts. Seattle briefly kept Martinez on the practice squad before releasing him early in September. Martinez remained a free agent until the Green Bay Packers added him in December to their practice squad. He competed for a roster spot this preseason, only to again be let go but this time not immediately signed to a practice squad. So if you’re wondering what Martinez and McIntosh have been up to in recent times, there’s your answer.

title: Seahawks vs. 49ers gets more national coverage thanks to NFL Week 5 schedule change
summary: Despite a disappointing loss to a last-place team in Week 3, the Seattle Seahawks are moving on up in the world. The National Football League made a scheduling change to move the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears from the featured 1:25 pm PT slot to 10 am PT on FOX. This means that the […]
full_text: Despite a disappointing loss to a last-place team in Week 3, the Seattle Seahawks are moving on up in the world. The National Football League made a scheduling change to move the Green Bay Packers and Chicago Bears from the featured 1:25 pm PT slot to 10 am PT on FOX. New from @nfl345 pic.twitter.com/VIwnMlGPqT — Brian McCarthy (@NFLprguy) September 29, 2026 This means that the Seattle Seahawks and San Francisco 49ers will be the lead late doubleheader game on FOX, as opposed to playing second fiddle to Bears-Packers and getting significantly less national distribution. This comes in part because Caleb Williams is expected to miss multiple weeks, and the Packers have dropped 2 out of their first 3 games. With this change, the Seahawks will draw the commentating team of Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady. It’ll be an NFC West affair, with the Niners leading the division with a 3-0 record, and the Hawks trailing at 2-1. FanDuel Sportsbook has the two teams both inside the top 10, in terms of best Super Bowl odds, with SF tied for 3rd-best (with the Baltimore Ravens) at +950, and Seattle sitting at 5th with a +1000. This high-profile clash is colored with the recent Super Bowl win by the Seattle Seahawks in the 49ers’ own stadium back in February. The two teams will meet in Seattle for their first game of the series in the 2026 season. Will it be a 3-part story, as it was last year? The Seahawks will hope to gain a major foothold against their nemesis in front of a larger segment of the country and keep the good times rolling after crushing them in the playoffs last year, 41-6. It’s a new season and new stakes, so this game will be one to have your popcorn ready for.

title: Snap Reactions: What playing time says about Seahawks depth chart at skill positions
summary: The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks went on the road in Week 3, facing off against the Washington Commanders, losing for the first time since Week 12 of the 2025 season. While the final score was close, between an ineffective running game and three turnovers that led to 21 points for the commanders, it’s […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Jadarian Price #8 of the Seattle Seahawks runs the ball against the Washington Commanders during the first quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Scott Taetsch/Getty Images) | Getty Images The defending Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks went on the road in Week 3, facing off against the Washington Commanders, losing for the first time since Week 12 of the 2025 season. While the final score was close , between an ineffective running game and three turnovers that led to 21 points for the commanders, it’s a game the Seahawks will look back on and feel they should have won. On the offensive side of things, Seattle had a solid day outside of turnovers. The run game certainly was not where the team or fans would like it to be, but Sam Darnold showed once again that he is capable of leading an offense even when the run game isn’t working. The offensive snap counts are very interesting for several reasons. Likely the most talked about snap counts on the offensive side of the ball is at right guard, where there was a clean 60/40 split for snaps between Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens. Perhaps more interesting, though, is what the snap counts say about other position groups. Tight end is unquestionably A.J. Barner and then a huge gap before either of Eric Saubert or Elijah Arroyo, both of whom finished with 18 offensive snaps. At receiver All-Universe Jaxon Smith-Njigba is the unquestioned leader of the group, with Cooper Kupp and Rashid Shaheed seeing similar snap counts to the 2025 season. Tory Horton wouldn’t be expected to see a huge amount of work as he continues working his way back into things, but it bears watching whether he earns more snaps in the coming weeks. Another position that bears watching is running back, where former undrafted free agent George Holani and former undrafted free agent Emmanuel Wilson both outsnapped 2026 first round pick Jadarian Price. Similar to Horton, Price wouldn’t necessarily be expected to have a huge workload after leaving the Week 2 win over the Arizona Cardinals due to injury, so at least at this point being outsnapped by more veteran players is likely less of a concern than ball security. On the defensive side of the ball, there weren’t a whole lot of surprises. Nick Emmanwori played 36 defensive snaps in his second game back on the field following surgery in the offseason, while Nehemiah Pritchett played just over half of the defensive snaps in the game. That is noteworthy for Pritchett in that it marks the third time in three games that he has played more than fifty percent of defensive snaps, something he had only done twice in his career prior to this season. And when it comes to special teams, just as it has been in recent seasons, it’s Brady Russell’s world and everyone else just lives in it. Russell led the Seahawks with 28 special teams snaps, while Mike Morris was second at 24 in his first regular season action of the year. Tyrice Knight, Patrick O’Connell and Chazz Surratt all logged 23 special teams snaps to round out the top five for the team. And now it’s on to a second consecutive matchup against a winless opponent, as the Los Angeles Chargers bring their 0-3 record to Lumen Sunday afternoon in search of their first win of the season.

title: 3 questions to think about following Seahawks loss to the Commanders
summary: We’ve had well over 24 hours to digest the Seattle Seahawks daring to lose a regular season football game for the first time in 10 months. They were not at their best against the Washington Commanders and paid a heavy price, losing 33-31 despite comfortably out-gaining Washington on the afternoon. Turnovers will kill you no […]
full_text: LANDOVER, MARYLAND - SEPTEMBER 27: Jeremy Reaves #39 of the Washington Commanders attempts catch against Rashid Shaheed #22 of the Seattle Seahawks during the fourth quarter at Northwest Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Landover, Maryland. (Photo by Patrick Smith/Getty Images) | Getty Images We’ve had well over 24 hours to digest the Seattle Seahawks daring to lose a regular season football game for the first time in 10 months. They were not at their best against the Washington Commanders and paid a heavy price, losing 33-31 despite comfortably out-gaining Washington on the afternoon. Turnovers will kill you no matter how great you area. Myself and Bryce Coutts dissected the game on The Hawks Eye podcast on Monday, and there were a few questions Bryce posed that I think we should pose or at least repurpose to Field Gulls readers. Did the Seahawks make a mistake by not keeping Cody White? Dareke Young left as a free agent to the Las Vegas Raiders, while Jake Bobo had an unfortunate ACL tear in training camp. Cody White stayed on the Seahawks roster throughout preseason and lost out on a roster spot to Montorie Foster Jr, training camp and ‘Hard Knocks’ star. As Mike Macdonald laments the lackluster special teams , Bryce and I wondered aloud ( at 12:13 of the video ) if the Seahawks should’ve kept one of their established special teams standouts. Foster has not played in the last two games, which means the Seahawks don’t have any reserve wide receivers on kick or punt coverage duties. Bryce : “On specials, Cody White was a factor. You lost Dareke Young as a gunner, Irv Charles hasn’t been able to go, Montorie Foster hasn’t given you anything on specials, and your specials have been atrocious. I feel if Cody White was able to be on here, at least you would’ve gotten something out of him on specials because he was one of the better gunners and kick cover guys.” Young, Bobo, and White all being gone is a lot of ST snaps to replace just at the WR position. If Foster isn’t providing anything right now, should Seattle have made more of a push to keep White and try and stash Foster on the practice squad? I think Emmanuel Henderson and Ricky White III should be considered special teams options as the season progresses, along with Irv Charles. Should the Seahawks keep rotating at right guard? Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens split snaps for the second week in a row. I outlined on the show (at 22:02 and 44:26 ) that I am not interested in a midseason competition for backup right guard. Either Haynes should get all the snaps or Stephens gets all the snaps. The fact that Haynes is once again in split duties like he was as a rookie is either a sign that they don’t trust his conditioning or there is something that is lacking in Haynes’ game that makes the coaching staff not want to play him a full game. Bryce : “How much do the Seahawks in the run game miss Anthony Bradford right now? Because he can move people. This is where that rotation with Christian Haynes and Beau Stephens has to get solved. They got to find someone that can move somebody in the run game. They’re not getting as much push as they should off that right side.” Mookie : “I think they had eight carries for -1 running on the right side. That tells you all you need to know, where [Abe] Lucas hasn’t been at his best, and even if Haynes and Stephens are playing to a draw, you want them to actually put people a couple of yards beyond the line of scrimmage, and that’s just not happening. I want them to drop the rotation. Either Haynes is ready for a full game or you start Beau Stephens. My hang-up with this is they did the same rotation thing with Haynes and Bradford when Haynes was a rookie. The fact that we’re still doing this: either Haynes has some sort of conditioning problem that they don’t want to talk about, or they really don’t want to commit to Haynes for a full game for what ever other reason.” Until Anthony Bradford is back, I don’t think there’s any benefit to rotating your offensive line at any position. Is Rashid Shaheed actually a good fit in the Seahawks offense? We’re three weeks into the season and Rashid Shaheed has six catches for 53 yards on 12 targets. Not exactly dazzling numbers for a player who signed a $51 million contract in free agency. Tory Horton barely played on Sunday and had three catches on as many targets for 48 yards. The season is still young and Shaheed’s chemistry has been primarily with Sam Darnold, whom he’s only played with for barely over the equivalent of a full game this month, but does it look like Shaheed actually makes sense for Seattle’s receiver group? It’s been a disappointing start to the season for Shaheed, who was on an 80+ catch pace with the New Orleans Saints before he was traded to Seattle . Perhaps there is a benefit to being a bigger fish in a small pond (albeit one where the biggest fish is Chris Olave), and Shaheed on a more stacked team could get lost in the shuffle. We get into this at 25:35 . Mookie : “So far it’s just JSN, it’s Kupp, and the fact that Horton had more catches than Shaheed in far fewer snaps is not great for Rashid. I’m wondering about his fit as a blocker, his ability to separate in certain route combinations—just because you’re fast doesn’t mean you can separate consistently at an NFL level. There’s a lot to think about here, it’s the only sour point for me in what was the most varied passing game to date under Brian Fleury.” Watch the full episode below! We also review Sam Darnold’s performance, how the defense performed, and whether it was a good decision by the coaching staff to sit Jadarian Price for fumbling again. Video

title: 49ers News: We’re on to Denver
summary: Brock Purdy has already earned my immense respect, and any accomplishment from here on out is gravy. Of all the things he has left to do before truly having a legacy… Super Bowl win, league MVP, other statistical accomplishments… he would become an actually immortal legend if he’s able to turn Dante Pettis into an […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - DECEMBER 9: Dante Pettis #18 of the San Francisco 49ers scores on a 1-yard touchdown recption during the game against the Denver Broncos at Levi's Stadium on December 9, 2018 in Santa Clara, California. The 49ers defeated the Broncos 20-14. (Photo by Michael Zagaris/San Francisco 49ers/Getty Images) | Getty Images Brock Purdy has already earned my immense respect, and any accomplishment from here on out is gravy. Of all the things he has left to do before truly having a legacy… Super Bowl win, league MVP, other statistical accomplishments… he would become an actually immortal legend if he’s able to turn Dante Pettis into an NFL wide receiver. I’m really curious to see how Dante has adjusted and evolved since his first stint. I was a believer initially, and I hated to see it all turn out the way he did. Maybe he’s gained an edge after bouncing around the league for a while. 49ers reuniting with former second-round pick Dante Pettis “During the 2025 season with the Saints, Pettis appeared in eight games, recording nine receptions for 127 yards and averaging 14.1 yards per catch. His most recent receiving touchdown came in 2024 with New Orleans.” 49ers practice and media schedule ahead of Week 4 matchup vs. Broncos “ Wednesday, September 30: 12:35 p.m. – Kyle Shanahan press conference 1:30 p.m. – Practice Thursday, October 1: 12:30 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 2:20 p.m.) – Raheem Morris press conference Following Morris – Klay Kubiak press conference Following Kubiak – Brock Purdy press conference Friday, October 2: 12:35 p.m. – Practice After practice (approx. 1:35 p.m.) – Kyle Shanahan press conference.” Brock Purdy, the NFL’s most underappreciated player “Another trait that gets lost in the Purdy discussion is his aggressiveness. Shanahan gives Brock plenty of “easy outs,” like a six-yard pass to George Kittle or a swing pass out of the backfield to Deebo Samuel. But that’s just not how Purdy is wired. More often than not, he’ll forgo gimme completions for a tight-window throw 15 yards downfield. It happens every week. It happened on his first dropback of the game to Mike Evans. It happened later on a backside throw to Kittle. He’s not interested in first-level routes. Where Brock has grown the most, even since last year, is his ability to manipulate defenders. You can only do this if you know the offense inside and out. Purdy has shown a knack for getting to the second and third progressions in the blink of an eye, but he’s holding defenders with his eyes to create bigger throwing windows. What’s been prevalent for two weeks in a row is Purdy manufacturing chunk plays against the blitz. It’d be easy for Brock to check the ball down and be content with a five-yard gain against five- and six-man rushes. But again, that’s not how he’s wired. He’s a swing-for-the-fences kind of quarterback. You think you can get over on him by bringing extra rushers? He’ll make you pay at the intermediate level. The beauty is that the throws are on time and fit within the structure of the offense.” 49ers minutia minute: Fred Warner, Osa Odighizuwa weathered career highs in snaps (paywall) “ Odighizuwa’s 71 snaps set a career high and nearly matched the number of snaps he played in the first two games combined (77). His previous career high was 64 snaps in Week 12 of the 2024 season, when he was with the Dallas Cowboys. Among the newcomers asked to play bigger roles Sunday, perhaps the biggest standout was Kareem, who logged the third-most snaps and finished with two quarterback pressures and three solo tackles. Givens, meanwhile, had an impressive 22.2 percent pass rush win rate on his nine rushes. To put that in perspective, Aaron Donald’s win rate so far this season is 21.4 percent.” Inside George Kittle’s 243-day recovery from torn Achilles “Milligan told Kittle about an athlete who came back from the same injury but had a huge difference in the size of his legs because he didn’t properly strengthen both of them before returning to field work. That athlete tore the ACL on his other leg in his first year back. Kittle bought in immediately. Within minutes of getting his cast off, he was doing pointed toe flexes. Once he shed his walking boot, Milligan instructed him on which inserts to put in his shoes, starting with 3.5 centimeters. The inserts got smaller as he progressed, down to the 0.75 ones he still wears. ….Most importantly, Kittle never lost sight of the importance of strengthening both legs. Using numbers collected from the 49ers, Milligan and Rojas knew how strong Kittle was before the injury. To ensure the legs stayed within 10% strength of each other, Milligan tracked his calf girth and put him on a strain gauge to measure his raw toe-push force against a weight room floor plate. As Milligan emphasized, the goal wasn’t just to get Kittle back on the field. It was to get him back as close to his normal level of performance as possible. That meant continuing to do the boring single leg heel raises or marble pickups for about 90 minutes to two hours every day over the course of 10 weeks…..Since there are only so many exercises you can do on the Achilles — calf raises off a wedge while standing, seated, with bands or with isolation holds — Rojas tried to challenge Kittle by forcing him to do it all from different angles to best simulate some of the sudden football movements. Some days, Rojas threw Kittle tennis balls. Other days, they chatted about life, trying to find ways to break the boredom. All the while, Kittle was deploying his secret weapon: the BFR. A BFR is, essentially, a tourniquet that Kittle strapped to his thigh to cut off the blood flow into the muscles he was working. It tricks the brain into thinking it’s taking on heavier loads than it actually is. According to Kittle, it’s a better method to work to failure when you can’t bear weight on the leg. In any Achilles recovery, the BFR is a suggested tool used a couple of times a week. Kittle used it twice every day. He also used the BFR as a recovery method, inflating it to 100% and then laying down for a few minutes so when he deflated it, the blood rushed back into the leg. “It’s really hard,” Rojas said. “It makes the easiest thing really challenging. It enabled us to push him hard from a muscular standpoint without putting a ton of stress on the Achilles that was healing … Him really pushing through some of that boring stuff and pushing that calf to fatigue is why he was able to get back so fast.” 49ers overreactions: Does Brock Purdy’s talent neutralize defensive injuries? “Of this much we are certain: The 49ers eventually will move their team headquarters and practice facility from its current location in Santa Clara. The organization is in the process of scouting sites that have more acreage for practice fields and office space. And, at least for optics, it is a good bet there will not be an electrical substation looming in the background of every video shot from their future location.”
author: Yinon Raviv

title: 49ers set to reunite with Dante Pettis following tryout
summary: The 49ers are set to reunite with Dante Pettis. San Francisco’s second-round pick in the 2018 draft was one of a host of wide receivers who tried out for the team on Tuesday following a rib injury to Mike Evans. And the Niners are giving Pettis a second chance with the team, with Jordan Schultz […]
full_text: September 22, 2019; Santa Clara, CA, USA; San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Dante Pettis (18) scores a touchdown during the fourth quarter against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Levi's Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Kyle Terada-USA TODAY Sports The 49ers are set to reunite with Dante Pettis. San Francisco’s second-round pick in the 2018 draft was one of a host of wide receivers who tried out for the team on Tuesday following a rib injury to Mike Evans. And the Niners are giving Pettis a second chance with the team, with Jordan Schultz reporting he will sign back with San Francisco. Pettis showed plenty of initial promise in his rookie season with the Niners eight years ago, finishing with 467 yards and five touchdowns, numbers that remain career-highs for the former Washington standout. His most memorable moment as a 49er came in the following season when he caught a game-winning touchdown in a Week 3 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers. But Pettis found opportunities to impress limited thereafter. He did not play in any of the final five games of the regular season or in the run to the Super Bowl that followed. He played in five games in the 2020 season before being waived. Since his departure, Pettis has had spells with the New York Giants, Chicago Bears and New Orleans Saints. He had a brief stint with the Buffalo Bills during training camp this year. Despite their injuries at the receiver position, the 49ers will hope to not have to rely on Pettis much. However, with his experience and knowledge of the offense, it is a reunion that makes sense for a team in need of greater depth in its pass-catching ranks.

full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in 49ers fans and fans across the country. How long will the Niners stay undefeated? For today’s SB Nation Reacts, we’re asking how long the 49ers can remain undefeated. It’s the NFL, and you never know what to expect week to week. Nobody expected the Falcons to beat the Packers by 21 points, or the Seahawks to lose outright to the Commanders with Sam Darnold returning. The Bears made the Eagles look lost. Anything can happen. We gave you every option up until the bye. This week’s game against the Broncos will be the best team the 49ers have played to date. Quarterback aside, the Broncos have a quality group of wide receivers, speed at running back, and a buttoned-up defense that’ll test the Niners in ways they haven’t been all season. The game is at Seattle in Week 5. The first road game in three weeks against a team that had the Niners number in the final month of 2025. The 49ers return home for a Monday night game against Washington. An emotional letdown after facing your rival is always a tricky spot in sports. From there, they travel to Atlanta to face a potentially pesky Falcons team, especially if Michael Penix continues to play with confidence. Will the undefeated streak continue through the bye? Are you feeling confident in the 49ers? As always, injuries are the topic when discussing the 49ers. They’ve taken care of business; despite suffering injuries, the offense is operating on a juggernaut level. Heading into Week 4, what’s your confidence level? title: 49ers make a change to the practice squad; try out Dante Pettis and Jerry Rice’s son
summary: The San Francisco 49ers announced they have released defensive lineman Vincent Anthony Jr. from the practice squad. This comes a day after signing Matthew Judon. That seems like a 1-for-1 swap, as the team was unlikely to elevate Anthony Jr. to the active roster. Here’s what Kyle Shanahan said about Judon on Monday: “I know […]
full_text: (Photo by Timothy T Ludwig/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers announced they have released defensive lineman Vincent Anthony Jr. from the practice squad. This comes a day after signing Matthew Judon. That seems like a 1-for-1 swap, as the team was unlikely to elevate Anthony Jr. to the active roster. Here’s what Kyle Shanahan said about Judon on Monday: “I know we had a workout with him over the weekend, so just to really get him in with the group on Wednesday, see where he’s at. Starting him out in individual drills, just seeing the type of shape and stuff he’s in, what he can learn in the scheme. Obviously, with our situation, hopefully we’ll get him caught up here real fast, and hopefully he’ll be an option to help us.” According to the NFL’s transaction wire, the 49ers worked out 5 different receivers and three defensive backs. We already went over Brady Boyd . Here are the other wideouts: Dante Pettis Brenden Rice Malik Turner Quentin Skinner That is Jerry Rice’s son. He grew up in my backyard here in Phoenix. Rice was a seventh-round pick from the 2024 NFL Draft. He’s listed at 6’3″, 210 pounds. Some fans figured Turner would be back on the roster sooner rather than later, given all the injuries. Skinner might be the only recognizable name. He went undrafted in the 2025 NFL Draft. He’s another tall wideout, listed at 6’5″, weighing 195 pounds. Quarterback Dorian Thompson-Robinson was listed on the transaction wire as the quarterback who had the tryout, but that’s more than likely the 49ers needing somebody to throw the wide receivers the ball. The other defensive backs, other than Sam Webb, were Cobee Bryant and Corey Ballentine. Bryant was with Raheem Morris in Atlanta last season. He played 93 snaps at cornerback for the Falcons as a rookie. Ballentine has been in the NFL since 2019, bouncing around between the Giants, Packers, and most recently the Cowboys last season.
author: Kyle Posey

title: 49ers work out former Jaguars wide receiver with Mike Evans banged up
summary: On Monday, San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided a few injury updates. Mike Evans’ rib injury “shouldn’t be long-term,” as the team evaluated him throughout the week. It’s unlikely that we’ll see Evans in Week 4, which means Brock Purdy and the offense will be missing the 6’5″ wideout who was objectively the […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images On Monday, San Francisco 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan provided a few injury updates . Mike Evans’ rib injury “shouldn’t be long-term,” as the team evaluated him throughout the week. It’s unlikely that we’ll see Evans in Week 4, which means Brock Purdy and the offense will be missing the 6’5″ wideout who was objectively the biggest threat in the passing game. The 49ers will work out wide receivers throughout the week. They can also elevate Brandin Cooks from the practice squad. You’re not going to ask 5’10” Brandin Cooks to do the same tasks as Evans, which is why it wouldn’t be surprising to see the Niners bring in bigger bodies at the position. Because for now, KhaDarel Hodge at 6’2″, 210 pounds is the closest body type to Evans on the roster. According to Aaron Wilson, the first wideout we know that the Niners are bringing in is Brady Boyd, listed at 6’1″, 195 pounds. Boyd was an undrafted free agent from the 2026 NFL Draft. He put on a show at Utah State’s Pro Day in March . Boyd had a 40″ vertical jump with a 10-foot-10 broad jump, and ran a 4.45 40-yard dash. His vertical jump would’ve been tied for sixth at the NFL Combine, and his broad jump would’ve been eighth — and three inches further than the 11th-placed De’Zhaun Stribling. Boyd played 83 offensive snaps for the Jaguars, and played four snaps on special teams in the preseason. Boyd only had five targets in the preseason, catching two of them for 23 receiving yards. He lined up at “X” and ran the type of routes you’d imagine somebody with his athletic ability would: high, intermediate crossing routes to stretch the field horizontally. So, it’s no surprise that the 49ers are interested. Boyd’s first reception was a 19-yard curl route, which tells you the defense needed to respect his speed (granted, this came against a cornerback who did not make the Saints roster). But his usage outweighs the result here, and it tells us what the 49ers are looking for. A small corner of the internet is begging for Jauan Jennings to return in a trade. The 49ers would not be able to operate offensively the way they have to begin the year with Jennings on the field. Players like Boyd and Cooks’ speed make a difference and open up the field. The Niners also worked out defensive back Sam Webb, per Wilson. Webb played 134 snaps across seven games for the Browns in 2025. He was targeted 12 times, allowed nine completions for 90 yards, and had a pass breakup. Webb was flagged for two penalties and also missed two tackles with Cleveland. Starters Renardo Green and Deommodore Lenoir were both in the concussion protocol in Week 3. This could be precautionary, or for down the line if there are injuries at cornerback.
author: Kyle Posey

title: Week 5 schedule flex impacts 49ers-Seahawks game
summary: The 49ers’ game with the Seattle Seahawks was already set to be one of the biggest of Week 5 of the NFL season. Now it will be subject to more eyeballs after the NFL made a change to the schedule that week. The league is bumping the Chicago Bears’ game with the Green Bay Packers […]
full_text: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - JANUARY 17: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers is pressured by DeMarcus Lawrence #0 of the Seattle Seahawks during the second quarter in the NFC Divisional Playoff game at Lumen Field on January 17, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Sean M. Haffey/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers’ game with the Seattle Seahawks was already set to be one of the biggest of Week 5 of the NFL season. Now it will be subject to more eyeballs after the NFL made a change to the schedule that week. The league is bumping the Chicago Bears’ game with the Green Bay Packers from the late window and into the 1:00pm ET time slot. That will mean the 49ers’ trip to the Pacific Northwest to face their NFC West rivals will be Fox’s featured game in the 4:25pm ET (1:25pm PT) slot, with the Detroit Lions’ clash with the Arizona Cardinals the only other matchup on the network being played at that time. The game will almost certainly be called by Kevin Burkhardt and Tom Brady, who were the announcers for the last meeting between the Niners and Seahawks, which saw San Francisco’s season ended with a 41-6 divisional round loss at Lumen Field. While that was a chastening evening for the 49ers, it was largely a case of a plethora of injuries being too much to overcome against a team backed by a ferocious defense. In the regular season, the 49ers have won their last four road games against the Seahawks. If they can stretch that streak to five games despite dealing with a significant number of injuries already at this point in the season, it will say much about the championship mettle of this 49ers team. Before focus turns to a renewal of acquaintances with Seattle, the 49ers will host the Denver Broncos in Week 4. CBS Sports’ Kevin Harlan and Trent Green will be on the call for that game.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Brock Purdy, the NFL’s most underappreciated player
summary: After three weeks, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is second in MVP odds on FanDuel Sportsbook. Obviously, a lot can change between now and the end of the season, but Purdy gaining recognition after only one national spotlight game where he wasn’t asked to do much is a good sign. Kyle Shanahan said Purdy […]
full_text: (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images After three weeks, San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy is second in MVP odds on FanDuel Sportsbook . Obviously, a lot can change between now and the end of the season, but Purdy gaining recognition after only one national spotlight game where he wasn’t asked to do much is a good sign. Kyle Shanahan said Purdy had a couple of great plays on Sunday, and those were just the ones he was asked about. To date, Purdy has double Josh Allen’s total EPA, and Allen sits in second place. His passing success rate is about four percentage points higher than the second-placed Lamar Jackson. A 9-to-1 touchdown-to-interception ratio isn’t too shabby. And Purdy isn’t dinking and dunking his way down the field. Thirty percent of his throws are intermediate, the fifth-highest in the league. Purdy has a $265 million contract. He wasn’t paid like an underrated player. However, he’s performing at an MVP level. His quarterback rating, which accounts for rushing, is less than seven points shy of perfect (93.8). His passer rating is 133.1—a number that would be difficult to achieve in three games of Madden. Again, it’s September, but the highest QBR in 2025 was 77.1, and the best passer rating was 113.5. You have to go back to 2007 — yes, that undefeated Patriots team — to find a quarterback with a higher EPA added on passing plays through the first three weeks of the season than Purdy. I’m not saying Purdy is going to throw for over 4,000 yards and 50 touchdowns, but that’s the pace he’s on. It’s even more impressive when you realize he’s not throwing to the wide receivers he was slated to throw to heading into training camp. And with the injuries on the other side of the ball, the 49ers will need Purdy to continue playing at a white-hot level to remain undefeated. Another trait that gets lost in the Purdy discussion is his aggressiveness. Shanahan gives Brock plenty of “easy outs,” like a six-yard pass to George Kittle or a swing pass out of the backfield to Deebo Samuel. But that’s just not how Purdy is wired. More often than not, he’ll forgo gimme completions for a tight-window throw 15 yards downfield. It happens every week. It happened on his first dropback of the game to Mike Evans. It happened later on a backside throw to Kittle. He’s not interested in first-level routes. Where Brock has grown the most, even since last year, is his ability to manipulate defenders. You can only do this if you know the offense inside and out. Purdy has shown a knack for getting to the second and third progressions in the blink of an eye, but he’s holding defenders with his eyes to create bigger throwing windows. What’s been prevalent for two weeks in a row is Purdy manufacturing chunk plays against the blitz. It’d be easy for Brock to check the ball down and be content with a five-yard gain against five- and six-man rushes. But again, that’s not how he’s wired. He’s a swing-for-the-fences kind of quarterback. You think you can get over on him by bringing extra rushers? He’ll make you pay at the intermediate level. The beauty is that the throws are on time and fit within the structure of the offense. Now, there have been enough exposures this season where either nothing was there, or the protection broke down, and Purdy had to save the day with his legs. If there were a “how many times this quarterback ran out of sacks” stat, I’d put money on Brock being in the top three. It’s why Purdy’s double-digit throwaway percentage in Week 3 should be viewed as a positive and a sign of maturation. Some aspects of Purdy’s game remain underappreciated. I’d argue that two of the areas, his accuracy and mobility, are two of the most important traits for a quarterback. When he does scramble, it’s with intent. The play where a touchdown was called back in Week 3 felt like Purdy was just buying time until the entire left side of the field cleared out, so he could gallop down the sideline. He’s fifth in rushing EPA, thanks to five first downs on only 10 rushing attempts. Purdy has the third-best rushing success rate for any quarterback. Aggression, mobility, and manipulation would mean squat if the quarterback isn’t accurate. We’ve seen Purdy hit receivers in the numbers and in stride. And it’s not just Mike Evans. I’m talking about KhaDarel Hodge and Jordan Watkins. Purdy is third in on-target percentage at 80.7%. Regardless of who he is throwing to, the ball is on the money. It’s all coming together for Purdy, who has taken a step forward at the quarterback position. This is why the 49ers paid him. They expect him to be great, and he has not disappointed.
author: Kyle Posey

title: The 49ers’ injuries aren’t sustainable, but Brock Purdy might make them survivable
summary: The 49ers dodged several bullets with their injuries in their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Having lost defensive end Nick Bosa to a calf injury last week week — with the star pass rusher likely looking at around a month on the sideline — the 49ers saw several other key players go down […]
full_text: (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) | Getty Images The 49ers dodged several bullets with their injuries in their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals. Having lost defensive end Nick Bosa to a calf injury last week week — with the star pass rusher likely looking at around a month on the sideline — the 49ers saw several other key players go down in a 36-30 defeat of their division rivals on Sunday. Mike Evans suffered a rib injury with two minutes left in the first half and was carted to the locker room, while the second half saw Trent Williams leave the game with a stinger and Dre Greenlaw sustain a quad injury. Yet the saving grace for the 49ers is that, following evaluation, none of those injuries are serious . Evans is day-t0-day with a rib strain, Williams should be ready by Thursday while Greenlaw will be managed throughout the week with a quad contusion. Still, there is an obvious sense of deja vu around the 49ers amid their excellent start to the season. The Niners are winning games despite a remarkable amount of injury adversity, just as they did in 2025. Yet with 16 players already on injured reserve, and with the 49ers electing not to put Bosa on IR in part because of concern about having enough spots to designate players to return, it is clear San Francisco is close to a tipping point with injuries. It is not sustainable for the 49ers to continue suffering injuries so consistently and keep winning. With tough games against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks on the horizon, fortunes for this injury-ravaged roster may soon change, and the harsh reality is that — even with this impressive start — it is difficult to envisage a roster in this shape seriously contending for the Super Bowl. In this situation last season, the 49ers’ decimated roster unsurprisingly hit a ceiling, and the result was 41-6 divisional round loss to the Seahawks that ended an admirable campaign. Still, for as much as the sheer scale of the injuries has presented significant challenges for San Francisco, outside of Ricky Pearsall, the 49ers have yet to lose a member their roster who could be considered a blue-chip player for the season. That is a crucial difference from 2025, when the 49ers lost Bosa and Fred Warner for the season within the first six weeks and also had to deal with a multi-week injury to quarterback Brock Purdy. And, though their current form amid the injuries doesn’t seem sustainable, the 49ers have hope that it can continue because of the play that is being sustained by two critical components of the offense. Purdy provides hope amid yet more adversity That Purdy’s performance against the Cardinals was arguably his worst of the season so far speaks to how well he is playing. Arizona succeeded in making life a lot more difficult for Purdy than either the Los Angeles Rams or Miami Dolphins did, and there were periods of the game in which the offense sputtered. Purdy did not put up the spectacular completion percentage numbers that defined the first two weeks, but the final stat line still made for very impressive reading. He completed only 55.6 percent of his passes against the Cardinals, but still threw for 297 yards and four touchdowns. Through three games, Purdy boasts a completion percentage of 72.3, has 789 passing yards and leads the NFL with nine touchdown passes while throwing just one interception. Purdy is also first in the NFL in success rate on passing plays (63.9%) and adjusted yards per attempt and adjusted net yards per attempt (both 11.1). He leads the NFL in passer rating (133.1) and QBR (93.8). In terms of Expected Points Added, Purdy’s EPA per play of 0.59 over the first three weeks ranks first of any quarterback since 2016, per Sumer Sports . BROCK PURDY TO MIKE EVANS EXTENDS THE LEAD @AZvsSF on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/ScREsrmsVw — NFL (@NFL) September 27, 2026 Put simply, Purdy is playing at an MVP level right now, with his standard exemplified by three standout plays in Week 3. His 23-yard touchdown pass to Mike Evans was a superb demonstration of the accuracy that has played a substantial role in his high completion percentage, while the sequence that effectively ended the game as a contest was an encapsulation of the upside he possesses as an athlete. Purdy was robbed of an early MVP moment when he saw a 35-yard scramble for a touchdown brought back because of what looked a harsh holding penalty against George Kittle. Two plays later, though, Purdy rolled out after a play-fake and found a wide-open Kittle for a 20-yard score to end Arizona’s comeback effort. Brock Purdy has put up an MVP performance through 3 weeks. Here are two MVP level plays that did not even count pic.twitter.com/y6UwKBxud5 — Gridiron Gold Mine (@GridironGoldM_) September 28, 2026 Asked if any quarterback is playing better than Purdy right now, Kyle Shanahan told his post-game press conference: “I’d be surprised, but I don’t study the other quarterbacks right now, so I don’t really know what anyone else is doing except for the guys that we go against. “I don’t get to see any of that, but I think it’s really hard to play much better than he’s playing right now.” All the numbers indicate you cannot play any better than Purdy is doing right now, but he is being supported by an offensive line that is doing an excellent job through three weeks. Indeed, despite concerns about the makeup on the interior O-Line and the injury to Williams on Sunday, the 49ers have still yet to give up a sack. Piss missile by Purdy on third-and-12 pic.twitter.com/nhDZWhvl2T — Ted Nguyen (@FB_FilmAnalysis) September 28, 2026 Per Pro Football Reference , the 49ers have allowed a pressure rate of just 13.5%, the best in the NFL. Pressures and sacks are a quarterback and offensive line stat, and those hugely impressive numbers reflect a quarterback with an elite understanding of how to move in the pocket and an oft-maligned O-Line making huge strides. The challenge for both Purdy and the O-Line is maintaining that kind of form as the difficulty level ramps up. Of course, there are going to be some down weeks for Purdy and the offensive line is obviously not going to go the entire season without giving up a sack. But the level of play at the quarterback position and in the trenches are primary reasons for hope for the 49ers that this year could be different, and that the injuries don’t necessarily have to limit what they can achieve. The defenses of both Denver and Seattle will severely test the 49ers up front and provide challenges to Purdy that he has yet to face through weeks. If Purdy and the O-Line can rise to these forthcoming challenges and perform at somewhere close to the standard they have each produced so far, then that would provide cause for expectations to rise significantly. San Francisco can’t afford for the injuries to keep piling up, and the 49ers desperately need Bosa back as soon as possible. But Purdy and those protecting him have to this point served as key differentiators from last season. As long as that remains the case, the 49ers have a chance of surviving their adversity and mounting a more serious challenge than their 2025 injuries allowed.
author: Nicholas McGee

title: Why didn’t George Kittle take a knee? Kyle Shanahan didn’t tell him to
summary: The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals Sunday 36-30 and as the Cardinals went to their onside kick in an attempt to win the game, one question entered my mind: What was George Kittle doing running that final touchdown into the end zone? The touchdown is nice. Especially when Brock Purdy scored one two […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CALIFORNIA - SEPTEMBER 27: George Kittle #85 of the San Francisco 49ers celebrates after scoring a touchown during the fourth quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi's Stadium on September 27, 2026 in Santa Clara, California. (Photo by Ezra Shaw/Getty Images) | Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers beat the Arizona Cardinals Sunday 36-30 and as the Cardinals went to their onside kick in an attempt to win the game, one question entered my mind: What was George Kittle doing running that final touchdown into the end zone? The touchdown is nice. Especially when Brock Purdy scored one two downs earlier with a near 50-yard scramble. Unfortunately that touchdown got nullified thanks to a holding call on none other than Kittle. Had Kittle taken a knee, the anxiety of the game possibly getting snatched from the 49ers would be nothing. The Cardinals had no timeouts, and the clock was well below the two-minute warning. A knee on the 1-yard line and the 49ers can run the clock out leading to the game ending 29-27, 49ers. Instead, we got this: Kittle extending the lead 📈 📺: FOX pic.twitter.com/iQXUbg6nGF — San Francisco 49ers (@49ers) September 27, 2026 Now look, no one is disputing the awesomeness of the touchdown itself, especially with the background behind it. That said, why not take a knee? Kittle had just the perfect opening to even go out of bounds. Stops the clock, but at least the 49ers can still tick the thing down, and the Cardinals can never take the field again. Kittle was just doing what he normally does. “Probably should have gone out of bounds,” Kittle told reporters after the game. “We could have just kneeled it out. But no one told me to, so that’s their fault, not mine.” The 49ers head coach shouldered responsibility for not delivering the memo: “That was on me,” Kyle Shanahan said. “I didn’t remind him in the huddle and I don’t expect him to be paying attention to the clock. But I definitely wish I did.” What resulted was the Cardinals trying to move down the field with a minute and change and electing to kick a 49-yard field goal on 2nd and 10 with 34 seconds left. 34 seconds is a sliver of time to get the obvious onside kick and then try to get it in the endzone proper. The plan didn’t work as the kicked ball rolled into the waiting arms of a Deebo Samuel. Leave it to George Kittle—or is it Kyle Shanahan—to leave us glued to the monitor until the very, very end.
author: Patrick Holloway

title: Kyle Shanahan explains why he was impressed with 49ers’ depleted D-Line in Week 3
summary: It’s no secret that the 49ers are extremely thin on the defensive line, and the pressure numbers from their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals reflect that. Per Pro Football Focus, the 49ers managed only 12 pressures of Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, getting home on two as Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White recorded sacks. […]
full_text: SANTA CLARA, CA - SEPTEMBER 27: Keion White #56 of the San Francisco 49ers sacks Jacoby Brissett #7 of the Arizona Cardinals during an NFL game on September 27, 2026 at Levi's Stadium in Santa Clara, CA. (Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images It’s no secret that the 49ers are extremely thin on the defensive line, and the pressure numbers from their Week 3 win over the Arizona Cardinals reflect that. Per Pro Football Focus, the 49ers managed only 12 pressures of Cardinals quarterback Jacoby Brissett, getting home on two as Ogbo Okoronkwo and Keion White recorded sacks. It was always likely to be tough sledding for the 49ers’ front from a pass-rushing perspective without Nick Bosa and rookie Romello Height, and with impressive rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton leaving the game with cramps in the second half. But, speaking in his Monday conference call, head coach Kyle Shanahan explained why he was more than satisfied with the performance of the Niners’ young and depleted D-Line. Said Shanahan: “By no means was it perfect, but I was real proud of how they played. They really competed their asses off. They were running to the ball, working real hard. I thought they did a good job throughout the game. I think they all kind of died out a little bit as the game went, just getting those plays up into the 80s and then losing Gracen to the cramps and stuff, which just took the numbers down some. But, we were able to change up our fronts throughout the game. We asked a lot of them and considering the circumstances for them, I thought it was a real successful game for them.” With Raheem Morris as the defensive coordinator, the 49ers have become more multiple up front. Morris frequently mixes in five-man fronts, and he presented the Cardinals with several different looks last Sunday, with his deployment of Fred Warner as an extra rusher proving successful in speeding up Brissett’s clock. While playing in a variety of different fronts, Osa Odighizuwa (82%), White (69%), Khalid Kareem (62%) and Okoronkwo (55%) all featured on over 50 percent of the defensive snaps. That is a huge mental and physical strain to put on a thin group and, in those circumstances, a return of two sacks and only 90 yards surrendered Jeremiyah Love on the ground represents a solid day from the 49er D-Line. It is not an effort Shanahan will want that group to have to put in regularly, and help is on the way with Height returning to practice following surgery on his broken hand, Matthew Judon being signed to the practice squad and Mykel Williams seeing his practice window opened after starting the year on the PUP list. Reinforcements are on the way ahead of more exacting challenges for the 49ers against the Denver Broncos and Seattle Seahawks in the next two weeks. However, those who held the fort on the defensive side of the trenches against Arizona can afford to hold their heads high.
