title: Titans QB Cam Ward is wasting this offensive line
summary: Remember when everyone was worried about the Tennessee Titans’ offensive line prior to the 2026 season starting? Fast forward past Week 3 and the tape has revealed an even more concerning revelation. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward is actually wasting a pretty good offensive line. Pro Football Focus has the Titans’ pass-protection unit ranked as No. […]
full_text: NASHVILLE, TENNESSEE - SEPTEMBER 20: Cam Ward #1 of the Tennessee Titans looks on prior to the national anthem of the game against the Philadelphia Eagles at Nissan Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Nashville, Tennessee. (Photo by Johnnie Izquierdo/Getty Images) | Getty Images Remember when everyone was worried about the Tennessee Titans’ offensive line prior to the 2026 season starting? Fast forward past Week 3 and the tape has revealed an even more concerning revelation. Sophomore quarterback Cam Ward is actually wasting a pretty good offensive line. Pro Football Focus has the Titans’ pass-protection unit ranked as No. 3 in the entire NFL , with a grade of 71.9. Through three weeks, Titans left tackle Dan Moore Jr. is the team’s only offensive lineman who has been assigned primary blame for a sack. Ward has been sacked on just five occasions through three games. Collectively, the Titans’ starting five has allowed 16 pressures. Some of these numbers may be slightly too favorable, but the point gets across. The Titans have done an excellent job protecting Ward in the passing game. ESPN Analytics has the Titans as a middling unit in pass protection. Whichever metric you believe, the takeaway is similar. The Titans have fielded a pretty good offensive line in protection. Ward is wasting that effort away. Ward has bailed some clean pockets. Inaccurate misses have been a weekly occurrence. The situation reached a boiling point on Sunday when Ward left 14 points on the board through two glaring red-zone errors in Week 3. As a rookie, many of the offense’s shortcomings were blamed on Ward’s supporting cast. That’s no longer the case. The offensive line has been upgraded. The wide receiver corps looks way better with Wan’Dale Robinson and Carnell Tate. The unfortunate truth is that Ward is the biggest preventative factor from the offense showing improvement right now. He’s a young QB who is struggling mightily in a new system, but many of his struggles are issues that date back to his rookie season (bad footwork, inaccurate passes). Ward needs to start playing better before the Titans consider doing something rash in 2027.

title: Sam Cosmi, Nick Cross won’t travel to UK, ruled out for Commanders game
summary: The Washington Commanders announced several roster moves earlier on Tuesday, placing LB Leo Chenal on injured reserve after having successful neck surgery following the Seahawks game. The team also swapped out practice squad edge rushers and officially brought running back Austin Ekeler back to the 53-man roster. Those moves weren’t the only ones made on […]
full_text: The Washington Commanders announced several roster moves earlier on Tuesday, placing LB Leo Chenal on injured reserve after having successful neck surgery following the Seahawks game. The team also swapped out practice squad edge rushers and officially brought running back Austin Ekeler back to the 53-man roster. Those moves weren’t the only ones made on a Tuesday. Why? This isn’t a typical week for Washington. They are “hosting” the Indianapolis Colts in London on Sunday morning and flying across the Atlantic Ocean Tuesday night. That meant that decisions needed to be made on injured players. Jayden Daniels (elbow), Frankie Luvu (groin), and Chig Okonkwo (hamstring) are all flying with the team Ben Standig also reported that Percy Butler was in the concussion protocol following Sunday’s win, but will travel with the team . The Commanders announced on Tuesday evening that guard Sam Cosmi (concussion/throat) and safety Nick Cross (illness/internal injury) will not make the trip, and have therefore been ruled out this week. Cosmi ended last season on IR due to a concussion and then suffered another one, along with a throat injury, from a nasty friendly-fire hit from rookie RB Kaytron Allen at the end of the Cowboys game in Week 2. Cross played the entire game against Dallas, but was hospitalized afterward for what was initially described as an internal injury . The Commanders listed it as an illness on last week’s injury reports, but we haven’t had a clear update on his prognosis since the initial reports. G Sam Cosmi (Concussion/Throat) and S Nick Cross (Illness) will not travel with the team tonight to London and are ruled out for Sunday’s game. — Washington Commanders (@Commanders) September 29, 2026 That will be a blow for Washington. Expect a similar personnel deployment, with Lucas Patrick at center and Nick Allegretti at right guard. Cross didn’t play in Week 3, and Quan Martin partnered with Jeremy Reaves in that situation. The Washington Commanders took a flight to London on Tuesday evening, and will begin their practice week on Wednesday afternoon (BST). title: Washington Commanders can be scary when WR Terry McLaurin goes off
summary: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough made a bold proclamation back in the spring, that Terry McLaurin should get 10 targets per game.   If course, that was in a pre-Stefon Diggs world, when the Commanders’ clear No. 1 receiver was even more front-and-center.   Blough’s intent was clear in that early statement and again in […]
full_text: Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough made a bold proclamation back in the spring , that Terry McLaurin should get 10 targets per game. If course, that was in a pre-Stefon Diggs world, when the Commanders’ clear No. 1 receiver was even more front-and-center. Blough’s intent was clear in that early statement and again in real time, with McLaurin a focal point in the early going. I can already hear you combating that, with McLaurin getting two catches on four targets in the season opener. That was due in large part to Philadelphia taking him away. He’s had nine targets in each game since. The Week 2 affair was inefficient. Per Sharp Football Analysis , an NFL-worst 45% of his targets through two weeks were catchable. The Week 3 contest versus Seattle, however, was an example of both how dominant McLaurin can be, and why he’s vital to the Commanders success. All of that was summed up in one play, a 30-yard touchdown pass from Marcus Mariota completely built on trust. TERRY McLAURIN HOW DO YOU DO?! #NFL #Seahawks #GoHawks #Commanders #RaiseHail #SEAvsWAS pic.twitter.com/Q0PglT4fgQ — Dom (@ZeroChillSports) September 27, 2026 It’s hard to say McLaurin was categorically open. Mariota liked the matchup and believed his No. 1 receiver would make a play. “It kind of changed on the fly,” Mariota said after the 33-31 victory . “He beat (cornerback) Josh (Jobe) really well, or really bad off the line. It was one of those, like, he kind of mail boxed it. Me, if it’s one-on-one, I’m gonna take my shot with Terry every time, and he made an unbelievable catch.” Let’s reiterate part of that quote one more time. “If it’s one-on-one, I’m gonna take my shot with Terry every time.” That’s the mindset required with a player like this. That was a key component in McLaurin being a force and a factor, recording six catches for 77 yards and a touchdown. When he’s covering his face with his hands and then opening them wide, Scary Terry is in full effect. “We don’t try to make a habit of going off key, but at the end of the day, we speak about being ball players out there,” McLaurin said. “When you get a clean release like that, and you have a chance to make a big play, you want to capitalize, and we did that. It definitely worked out in our favor. I actually kind of got a little bit of a one-on-one; they were probably quarters, so I got a little bit of one-on-one coverage with him, and put the ball up, and I just wanted to come down with it.” “That was euphoric. Everybody has been waiting for the mask to get dropped and the celebration, so to see all my teammates doing it, that just means something different to me because they really support and love what you do out there.” The Commanders need effervescence no matter who’s at quarterback. It was sorely missing in 2025. While the full house of cards collapsed last season, not having McLaurin consistently was as big a factor as any in that campaign’s downfall. McLaurin, as one might assume, was humble about his impact on the Commanders’ first victory of the season. “This is the opportunity that was just seized.” Terry McLaurin on why he broke out vs the Seahawks: “I just think this was an opportunity that was seized…I don’t really lose faith in myself and neither do my teammates. So I know the ball is going to come my way, it’s just about being consistent, making the plays…” pic.twitter.com/9jVET7SDdE — brandon (@JayDanielsMVP) September 28, 2026 McLaurin spent all offseason getting in sync with Jayden Daniels after barely playing with him the year before. Then he pivoted when JD5 became unavailable and used a previously established trust with Mariota to help the Commanders pull out a win. “I think, just being a part of this team where they trust me to be a leader and the playmaker,” McLaurin said, “I just wanted to kinda put that on display.” So, you know, what comes next? It’s clear that McLaurin is integral to Commanders success. They need him to be a top 10-15 receiver in this league, who gets open and targeted regardless of coverage or opposition. Part of that is the offensive coordinator – David Blough was pretty darn good on Sunday – find ways to get him involved. David Blough showed some real stuff in Week 3 love this 3rd and 10 call quick snap, catching the Seahawks pre and post-snap movement off rhythm leading to a wide open Terry McLaurin out of the stack pic.twitter.com/qRlYujSLEB — Josh Norris (@JoshNorris) September 29, 2026 Another part involved teammates consistently making plays and forcing defenses to be honest. A final part is Terry being Terry, someone who makex contested catches as well as anyone in the league. Don’t believe what your eyes see? Here are the numbers . Against Seattle, McLaurin had a plus-12% catch rate over expectation; he had a plus-5.2 EPA overall, and earned 2.6 yards per route run. Finding a way to keep McLaurin active is vital moving forward, as Washington tries to stack wins and reach the light following a rough start. “He’s going to get his opportunity,” Mariota said. “He’s going to make the most of it. I thought the first couple of games he did a good job of kind of trying to find ways to allow him to create separation. That’s part of it. Like I said, you’re gonna go against good defenses, you’re gonna go against teams that game plan well. And I just thought we had a great opportunity for him this week, and he really delivered for us.”

title: NFL Power Rankings: Commanders rise after big win over Seahawks
summary: The Washington Commanders are 1-2 after pulling off the 33-31 upset win against the Seattle Seahawks in their home opener. Marcus Mariota led the team, and took full advantage of the three turnovers the defense forced against last season’s Super Bowl champions. Sunday’s win had an odd effect on this week’s power rankings. Everyone but […]
full_text: ARLINGTON, TX - SEPTEMBER 20: Marcus Mariota #8 of the Washington Commanders looks on from the field during an NFL football game against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on September 20, 2026 in Arlington, Texas. (Photo by Cooper Neill/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Washington Commanders are 1-2 after pulling off the 33-31 upset win against the Seattle Seahawks in their home opener. Marcus Mariota led the team, and took full advantage of the three turnovers the defense forced against last season’s Super Bowl champions. Sunday’s win had an odd effect on this week’s power rankings. Everyone but Walter Football moved the Commanders up after winning a home game where they were 8.5-point underdogs. A portion of the power rankers were impressed with the team effort and moved Washington up a decent amount following their first win of the season. The rest of the power rankers need to see a lot more from a team that they have already written off. The Jayden Daniels injury and potential quick return looms large in a lot of people’s minds, and a great performance from a veteran backup QB isn’t moving the needle too much. The outlook on the season has dramatically improved for a lot of fans, but one win is only one win, and there are 14 more games in the season. Next up is an international game against the Indianapolis Colts in London. This is a “home” game for the Commanders, and they are underdogs for the fourth week in a row . This game will be critical for the Commanders season with a home game against the Giants, and a road game against the 49ers coming up before the Week 7 bye. Washington ranks as high as #19 from Pro Football Network based on Marcus Mariota’s performance against the NFL’s best defense, and three turnovers from the Commanders defense. Walter Football was not impressed with the upset win and brings down the Commanders average. High: 19 Low: 29 Average: 23.1 #19 Pro Football Network (Infante) Arguably the biggest upset of Week 3 was the Marcus Mariota-led Washington Commanders picking up the win over the Seahawks on Sunday. The Commanders secured their first win of the season with their 33-31 victory at home thanks to Mariota’s three touchdowns and a pick-six by linebacker Kain Medrano. Washington’s defense was pretty porous against Seattle’s passing attack, but Medrano’s interception and the other two turnovers the defense forced gave the team enough spark to complement an efficient aerial assault. The Commanders’ win came out of nowhere, and it has to be nice to pick up your first win of the season against the defending Super Bowl champions. Last week: 21 Essentially Sports (Hubbard) Washington earned a massive win over Seattle, scoring 33 points against arguably the best defense in football. I don’t want to take anything away from Washington, but Seattle flew across the country, played a game that started at 10am PST and had Sam Darnold coming off an injury. Nine times out of ten, Seattle wins, but props to Washington for securing this one. Last week: 23 #20 USA Today (Davis) Credit to coach Dan Quinn and his veteran leadership from keeping this team from circling the drain in the aftermath of QB Jayden Daniels’ latest elbow injury. Handing the Seahawks their second road loss in 24 months is a good way to spark a turnaround. Last week: 30 Sporting News (Iyer) Marcus Mariota is a gamer and was fearless in facing the Seahawks’ Super Bowl defense, getting the key playmakers involved. The defense also responded in desperation to make plenty of big plays, including a pick six. Last week: 27 The Score The Commanders gave themselves life with Sunday’s huge win over the Seahawks, staving off a dubious 0-3 start by defeating the reigning champs without Jayden Daniels – and without virtually any production from their run game. Now they must carry that momentum overseas, where they’ll take on the Colts in London. Last week: 26 NFL Trade Rumors (Woodie) Marcus Mariota turned back the clock and played a solid game, throwing three touchdowns and sealing the game late with a first-down run. The Commanders’ backs were against the wall coming off two straight losses to divisional opponents and without starting QB Jayden Daniels, but Mariota came through when Washington needed him most. Three winnable games against the Colts, Giants and Eagles are among their next four, and Washington could build some momentum here. Last week: 25 Big Blue View (Falato) Washington pulled off one of the season’s more impressive wins, defeating the Super Bowl champions 33-31 at home. Perhaps it was Sam Darnold jitters, or the dreaded one-o-clock start for a West Coast team — I’m not sure — but it does seem like Washington’s defense has improved, and Marcus Mariota did enough against Mike Macdonald’s talented defense Last week: 26 Team Rankings Last week: 22 #21 NFL.com (Shook) Marcus Mariota hive, stand up! The veteran backup played hero Sunday, powering Washington to the biggest upset of the week. The contest ended in fitting fashion with Mariota scrambling for the game-sealing first down. Equal praise is due for Washington’s defense, which has played above expectation all season and notched a peak showing in the takeaways department, logging two to keep Washington in the game and a third to give them enough of a lead to emerge victorious. Last week: 28 Yahoo Sports (Schwab) It’s not like the Commanders dominated on Sunday. They were outgained 437-258. They allowed 31 points at home. Marcus Mariota threw for just 183 yards and the Commanders averaged 2.6 yards per rush. That doesn’t matter because the Commanders took advantage of all their opportunities to win 33-31, a victory that gives them hope of digging out of an 0-2 hole to start the season. Also, Jayden Daniels could be close to a return. Commanders head coach Dan Quinn told Albert Breer of The MMQB that Daniels is “more likely than not” to travel to London for the team’s Week 4 game against the Colts, which gives him a shot to play two weeks after dislocating his left elbow. Last week: 27 #23 The Athletic (Graff/Kendall) QB confidence: Does weeping count? Backup Marcus Mariota threw three touchdown passes to shock the Seahawks, but Commanders fans are still in a corner crying about Jayden Daniels. Since Daniels’ breakout rookie season, he has missed 11 games because of injury, and Washington is 2-7 in the games he has started. When Daniels returns from his second dislocated elbow, Commanders fans will be holding their collective breath and hoping he can stay healthy and play well again. Last week: 29 Pro Football Talk Marcus Mariota’s performance will accelerate Jayden Daniels’s return. Last week: 30 Clutch Sports (Johrendt) Marcus Mariota stepped into the starting role once again for Jayden Daniels and did his best Superman impression, leading an upset at home over the defending Super Bowl champions. Mariota threw for three touchdowns in the win, connecting with Rachaad White, Terry McLaurin, and Treylon Burks for scores, while backup linebacker Kain Medrano picked off Darnold and took it back to the end zone. Last week: 26 New York Post (Dunleavy) Last week: 29 #24 Fox Sports (Vacchiano) Marcus Mariota pulled off a big and impressive upset against the defending champs (albeit with the help of some errant throws by Seattle QB Sam Darnold). And that was huge for this battered team, knowing that starting QB Jayden Daniels’ return may only be a couple of weeks away. The Commanders didn’t get much of a running game — and now RB Rachaad White is hurt — and Dan Quinn’s defense offered little resistance until two late interceptions. So there are still issues to be fixed. Mariota’s mission is to keep them afloat until Daniels is back. The Colts and Giants are up next, so he’s got a shot. Commanders links Articles ESPN Leo Chenal to have season-ending neck surgery Washington Commanders linebacker Leo Chenal, who was carted off the field during the team’s 33-31 upset win over the the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday, will undergo season-ending neck surgery, sources confirmed to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport. Chenal suffered the injury in the second quarter of Washington’s victory. The fifth-year veteran appeared to lead with his head while tackling Seattle’s Emanuel Wilson and immediately went to the ground as medical personnel were quick to run to his side. The crowd at Northwest Stadium chanted “Leo! Leo!” as Commanders teammates surrounded Chenal, who was taken off on a cart, raising his left hand as he approached the tunnel. Chenal was starting Sunday in place of the injured Frankie Luvu, who was missing his second consecutive game with a groin injury. The Commanders were thin at the position because another inside linebacker, Jordan Magee, was placed on injured reserve after the opener with a hamstring injury. Man, this Leo Chenal injury sounds way more serious than we initially thought. His brother says he’s having surgery to replace his damaged vertebrae with titanium. The positive news is that Leo reportedly has feeling and movement in all his extremities, which is huge. He has played all of three NFL games. Just what did we see from Styles on Sunday in the Commanders’ 33-31 victory over the Super Bowl champion Seattle Seahawks that, for a week, went a long way to saving Washington’s defense? “Tremendous leadership,” veteran defensive tackle Tim Settle said of a player in his third pro game. “Tremendous effort. He willed us to a victory today.” There were all manner of elements that went into this unlikely result. Pick a play that popped, one that sticks in your memory: Terry McLaurin’s brilliant catch of a 30-yard pass from backup quarterback Marcus Mariota that gave Washington a two-touchdown lead in the third quarter. title: Sonny Styles, Marcus Mariota among best Commanders from Week 3
summary: Every victory deserves some serious love in this league, and the players who deliver standout performances deserve to be recognized. After two disheartening weeks, our squad bounced back with a massive, hard-fought 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Northwest Stadium.   To celebrate, I wanted to create a space for us fans […]
full_text: Every victory deserves some serious love in this league, and the players who deliver standout performances deserve to be recognized. After two disheartening weeks, our squad bounced back with a massive, hard-fought 33-31 win over the Seattle Seahawks on Sunday at Northwest Stadium. To celebrate, I wanted to create a space for us fans to give credit where credit is due and honor the guys who truly stepped up when we needed it most. This introduces our new weekly tradition: The Boss Hog of the Week. Moving forward, I hope to keep these fan votes running throughout the entire season. The rules are simple: each week represents a standalone vote, and at the end of the year, I’ll tally up all the weekly winners to crown the official, definitive Boss Hog of the season. Without further ado, let’s look at the standout performers. Here are your nominees for this week’s award: QB Marcus Mariota Stat line: 19-for-31, 183 passing yards, 3 passing TDs, 0 INTs | 5 carries, 11 rushing yards Marcus Mariota stepped into a high-pressure situation and delivered exactly what this team needed. Following a deflating loss to Dallas, Mariota was named the starter for the week with Jayden Daniels sidelined with a left elbow dislocation. In a massive show of confidence, the team also named him an all-season captain — and he rewarded that trust. Mariota led a smart, calculated attack, exploiting a Seattle defense that was missing both starting safeties. While it wasn’t always pretty, it was efficient, largely mistake-free football. He finished the day throwing for three touchdowns and sealed the victory himself, picking up a critical first down on a gritty third-and-7 run to run out the clock. It was a remarkably strong, poised performance from the veteran, who will now look to carry this momentum across the pond as the team heads to London. WR Terry McLaurin Stat line: 5 receptions, 78 receiving Yards, 1 receiving TD Terry McLaurin stepped up when his team needed him most. After frustratingly missing out on the end zone three separate times last week, McLaurin bounced back with a rock-solid performance to finally find paydirt this week. While he didn’t quite match the explosive stat line put up by his opponent, Jaxon Smith-Njigba, his impact on the outcome of the game was undeniable. McLaurin’s clutch 30-yard touchdown reception gave the team the necessary cushion to maintain the lead, serving as a perfect example of a squad that simply refused to give up. It was exactly the kind of gritty, winning football you want to see from a true leader. LB Sonny Styles Stat line: 4 solo tackles, 1 assisted tackle, 1 interception , 2 passes defensed, 1 forced fumble , 1 QB Hit. Sonny Styles had a true breakout performance . Many fans, including myself, thought his transition to this important defensive role would be a steep hill to climb, but he is completely shattering those expectations. He has been progressing week-to-week, proving that, while there are still areas to refine, he is absolutely fearless when facing a challenge. He was an absolute menace and an instant playmaker on Sunday, single-handedly disrupting the offense by being a part of two massive turnovers. His most impressive sequence didn’t even show up on the turnover sheet. It was a jaw-dropping play where he went stride-for-stride down the field with explosive Seattle running back Jadarian Price, perfectly tracking the ball to force a clutch pass breakup. That rare combination of size, speed, and coverage ability is exactly what Washington’s defense was desperately missing all of last season. He isn’t just surviving the transition; he’s becoming a star in the process. CB Amik Robertson Stat line: 6 total tackles (4 Solo), 4 passes defensed, 1 forced fumble The box score won’t reveal Amik Robertson’s true impact. Not just on Sunday, but over the previous weeks. Amik has been head-and-shoulders above the rest as the best cornerback on this team. He has fought tooth-and-nail to make every play miserable and difficult for opposing wide receivers. He was targeted relentlessly on Sunday, ultimately allowing four receptions for 36 yards and a touchdown, all to Seattle’s elite wideout Smith-Njigba. What truly earned Amik a spot on this ballot is his sheer, unyielding effort. Whether it’s laying out for pass breakups, ripping the ball away for a forced fumble or great pursuit to ensure a play doesn’t extend an inch further, he refuses to give up. Amik has established himself as the heart and soul of this defensive backfield, a secondary that should get better when Trey Amos makes his return. LB Kain Medrano The Stat Line: 5 Total Tackles (3 Solo), 1 Interception, 1 Pass Defended, 1 QB Hit, 1 Touchdown (Pick-Six). Welcome to the show, Kain! I had some very strong reservations about Medrano. He still has some clear tackling issues that carried over from his college days, but stepping into the fire the moment Leo Chenal went down was the ultimate test. He didn’t just fill a gap; he made arguably the play of the game with that beautiful interception on Sam Darnold, taking it to the house for a spectacular touchdown. It was an absolutely incredible moment for a player who simply kept his head down, stayed ready, and answered the call the second his chance arrived. OC David Blough David Blough deserves tons of love for this win, too. Seahawks head coach Mike Macdonald’s defense has been an absolute buzzsaw since last season. That background makes this masterpiece of a game even more impressive for our first-year play caller. Blough drew up an excellent game plan and executed it beautifully. Seattle hadn’t given up an explosive play all year until Blough dialed up that 21-yard screen play to receiver Jaylin Lane. Following that up with the 30-yard touchdown strike to Terry McLaurin made it two explosive cracks. Even with several key players missing from his own unit, Blough kept a top defense completely off-balance and confused at times. This was a statement game for Blough, and doing it against a defensive juggernaut is a huge bonus for our coaching staff moving forward. This is the type of game that will either be a once-in-a-blue-moon moment or the exact shift of energy the Commanders needed to bounce back for the rest of the season. But, for right now, let’s just enjoy this massive upset! Be sure to vote in the poll below, and if there’s anyone I missed, make sure to post them in the comments. I hope you all enjoy this new series!

title: NFL Week 4 latest intel, buzz questions, news, fantasy tips
summary: Alarm bells for Justin Herbert and Drake Maye? More QB trades on the way? Growing injury concerns for the 49ers and Panthers? Here's the latest for Week 4.
full_text:
We're onto Week 4 of the  2026 NFL season , and insiders Jeremy Fowler and Dan Graziano have been making calls to sources around the league for the latest news and notable buzz.

 Drake Maye and the Patriots had an ugly game Sunday , but Maye is hardly the only quarterback with a concerning start to the season. Dan and Jeremy asked around the league to get a sense of which QBs land on the early-season panic meter. And after J.J. McCarthy kicked off trading season Monday in going to the Giants , our insiders poked around on more QB trades that could be on deck. Any other passers potentially switching teams?

 Additionally, is the league buying the 3-0 start from the Raiders, who have already matched their win total from 2025? Can Las Vegas keep this up? And which teams -- 3-0 or otherwise -- are getting hit particularly hard with injuries? It's all here, as Jeremy and Dan answer big questions, hand out useful fantasy football nuggets and empty their reporting notebooks heading into Week 4.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 QB panic meter | QB trades 
 Raiders' start | Injury impact 
 Fantasy football advice 

 
 

 Which QB currently sits atop the league's panic meter? 
 Fowler: Three come to mind here -- Drake Maye , Cam Ward and Justin Herbert . All three garner varying degrees of panic, but I'm putting Maye on top for now. The Year 3 regression is startling. He looks shaken right now. Mike Vrabel's comment after the 35-6 loss to Jacksonville was blunt: "My concern level is very high for this football team." Maye is a big part of that after six interceptions in three games. The next day, Vrabel questioned whether the Patriots' offense needs to scale back its game plans a bit, essentially to do less but do it better.

 

 Still, the notion that Maye's play can improve is there. He was considered one of the cleanest quarterback prospects of the past half-decade when he entered the 2024 draft. He played at an MVP level less than a calendar year ago. And to be sure, the Patriots have not played well around Maye and have not adequately protected him, and wide receiver A.J. Brown 's absence is deeply felt. The passing game was designed to feed him the ball often. Josh McDaniels' scheme is also considered to be complex for young passers.

 But dating to last year's playoffs, Maye's seven-game production line is 120-of-200 passing for 1,413 yards, seven touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Those are 1970s QB numbers -- and jarring for a quarterback seemingly on the door of superstardom (to be fair, four of those seven were playoff games against top-shelf defenses).

 So, I'm leaving the door open for Maye to fix it, but the panic can be found in Vrabel's voice right now. I mean, this team was in the Super Bowl last season, so the expectations couldn't have been higher. Perhaps last season's soft schedule masked a quarterback who was still very much in development.

 Graziano: It went largely unnoticed during their run to the Super Bowl, but Maye did not play well during the playoffs last season. And many of the issues that surfaced then have carried into this season. What I'm hearing is that it's not that Maye is a consistently poor decision-maker, it's that he's an occasionally disastrous one, and the mistakes are exceedingly harmful. Through three quarters of the season opener in Seattle, you'd have said Maye was playing well, demonstrating poise in difficult circumstances and putting his team in position to win. Then he fell apart completely in the fourth quarter.

 There are ups and downs with young players, but Maye's downs have been way too far down. And without Brown, the Patriots don't have enough around Maye to overcome the errors. His protection also hasn't been consistent. But while I don't get the sense that people think Maye has regressed, there is concern that we aren't seeing advancement in some of the young-player areas that should be improving for a quarterback who finished second in MVP voting and played in the Super Bowl.

 Fowler: After some conversations this week, I feel certain that Tennessee wants to give Ward more time despite his 3-17 record as a starter. Accuracy and decision-making are issues, but the Titans hope he will build off the late-game growing pains. He also isn't turning the ball over at a high clip (one interception through three games) and the team values his makeup and work ethic. Adjusting to Brian Daboll's offense has taken time, but averaging 12 points can test a front office's -- and locker room's -- patience only for so long.

 Graziano: The sense I get from Tennessee is that things are out of whack there and haven't gotten on track at all. I'm talking about the overall environment around the team, not just Ward. There's an obvious disconnect between Ward and the coaching staff, or at least the scheme, and the time to address and adjust those things was the spring and summer. How do the Titans fix lingering structural issues with their offense and with Ward's development during the season? There's still widespread belief that Ward has the character and the ability to weather early-career struggles and come out stronger for it. But there's also a sense around the league that it should look better than it does right now, and there's curiosity about what's preventing the improvement from happening.

 Fowler: Jumping to Herbert, his play is inexcusably bad, but he's in Year 7 with 98 career starts, with most of those played at a high level. He has proof of concept more so than Maye or Ward. The jumbled offense under offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel hasn't helped. And I'm not exactly sure where they turn next.

 

 Graziano: Yikes. Talk about disconnect between player and scheme. Everything looks "difficult and exhausting" for Herbert, using the words of one evaluator I spoke to last week. There was so much talk in the offseason about how Herbert and his immense natural talent would flourish under McDaniel, but it's clearly not clicking. A fresh wave of offensive line injuries that happened as the season was getting underway certainly didn't help. But the run game can't get going, the receivers haven't taken the jumps we were promised, and Herbert has looked confused and overwhelmed by whatever it is he's being asked to do out there.

 A lot of people have theories on what the Chargers need to do in terms of simplifying things so they can just start having success to build on. But there's also concern that the personnel doesn't fit what the offense is built to do, which might be difficult to overcome.

 Fowler: Next up for the Chargers: at Seattle , vs. Denver , at Kansas City , then a much-needed bye before the Rams , Texans and Ravens await. Oof. Not many get-right games on that schedule.

 Look, Herbert has excelled as a true pocket passer, whereas McDaniel thrived having Tua Tagovailoa throw with anticipation to spots. Either Herbert struggles to do both or McDaniel isn't putting him in a position to show that he can. I still think Herbert has good football in him, but that's harder to sell by the week. And your point about mismatched personnel is a good one.

 

 
 True or false: J.J. McCarthy won't be the only QB traded before the deadline. 
 Graziano: True! A lot of these situations are going to change drastically by midseason. Jacoby Brissett could struggle and prompt the Cardinals to want to see third-round rookie Carson Beck , which could lead to Brissett or veteran backup Gardner Minshew II being dealt. We heard talk in the offseason about the Bears looking into trading Tyson Bagent , and maybe someone gets interested if he gets a start or two during Caleb Williams ' absence and looks good.

 We also heard about the Eagles dealing  Tanner McKee , and they could still do so if they're comfortable with Andy Dalton as QB2. They could also deal Dalton. Joe Flacco is still in the league and always seems to appeal to someone, though I believe Cincinnati values him highly as a fallback should something happen to Joe Burrow .…

title: How NFL players cope with CTE risks, fears and internal debates
summary: We asked over 30 NFL players about CTE concerns, and their answers ranged from fear to resignation.
full_text:
ON A HOT summer day, with sweat dripping from his nose and his body decked out in football pads from head to toe, Will Fries catalogs every step he takes in hope of avoiding chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the progressive, degenerative brain disease known as CTE.

 A diet heavy in fish and omega-3 fatty acids. 

 Glasses that block blue light. 

 Never getting fewer than eight hours' sleep. 

 Fries, a 28-year-old Minnesota Vikings guard in his sixth NFL season, was 17 years old when the movie "Concussion" was released in 2015 and 18 when NFL executive Jeff Miller sat in front of a congressional committee and acknowledged a link between football and CTE.

 "Your football life is short," Fries recently told ESPN, "and then you've got the rest of your life to live."

 Researchers believe CTE is caused by repeated subconcussive hits to the head, the kind that occur on nearly every play at every level of tackle football and in other contact sports. There are no specific symptoms or treatment for CTE, in part because it can't be diagnosed until after death.

 Studies of CTE, the brains of athletes, and the effects of head trauma increased dramatically after links between the disease and football began to emerge alongside reporting that the NFL had led a two-decade campaign to deny such a link before Miller's comments in 2016.

 A study published this summer in the British Medical Journal estimated that at least one in four former NFL players who died between 2016 and 2021 had CTE at the time of their deaths. A study published in January found that suicide rates among former NFL players were 2.6 times higher than NBA and MLB athletes from 2011 to 2019. A 2024 study reported nearly a third of former NFL players believed they had CTE. That group was five times more likely to have suicidal thoughts than those who reported they did not believe they had CTE.

 Ahead of this season, ESPN asked more than 30 active and retired players how the increased attention on brain trauma has affected their lives and career decisions. All were aware of CTE to at least a small degree, an advantage that thousands of their predecessors did not have. Some acknowledged CTE has become a topic of dark humor, including Pittsburgh Steelers safety DeShon Elliott : "Sometimes you might draw a blank and forget something from last week and you go, 'Oh my God, it's that CTE.'"

 Like Fries, some players follow what they consider best practices to minimize their chances of getting CTE. NFL rules changes and attempts to improve equipment -- such as Guardian Caps -- instill confidence in some players. Others consider brain health out of their hands and ultimately an acceptable tradeoff for the benefits of an NFL career.

 

 "I think [for] any football player, that crosses your mind," said 26-year-old Arizona Cardinals receiver Michael Wilson , who's in his fourth season. "But also, that is so far down the line and ... the legacy, the financial gain that you can carve out for yourself to me outweighs the risk of CTE, especially as a wideout.

 "How cool would it be to leave a legacy that generations of my family, the Wilson legacy will talk about? And if CTE is a consequence of that, then so be it. But I also could sleep good at night knowing that I was the one person in the Wilson family that ended up changing our financial, socioeconomic class, like you can point it back to me and say, 'Michael's the one that did it.' So for my kids' kids' kids' kids, they can always look at me and if CTE is a consequence of that, then I'm willing to bet on myself that hopefully I won't get it, but if I do, then I made a decision and I chose that."

 Weeks after the interview, Wilson signed a three-year, $75 million extension.

 "A lot of guys want to have families and that's a goal of mine," the Vikings' Fries said. "Would I trade football for anything? Absolutely not. I love putting in the work and I know the risks of it, and I'm doing everything I can."

 Retired players, especially those who played before the connection between CTE and football was recognized, react to such views with varying emotions.

 Matt Hasselbeck, an NFL quarterback for 17 seasons who announced his retirement on March 9, 2016 -- five days before Miller's appearance at the congressional hearing -- recently announced he will donate his brain for CTE study after his death. In an interview with ESPN, Hasselbeck had pointed words for New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo , who when asked this summer on a podcast whether CTE was real, said: "No, it's an excuse." Skattebo later apologized , saying his response was a "tasteless joke."

 "CTE is a very real thing," Hasselbeck said. "And we have guys who are very conscious of it. We also have guys who are whatever the opposite of that is. We have guys that are rookie running backs slamming their heads into everything with their helmet. And then they're making light of it and they're making jokes of it. And they're, like, 'I don't care. You only live once.' And then they have to come back and apologize.

 "I'm thinking of Cam Skattebo this year. And I played with tons of guys like that. And it's funny in the moment. Teams like it because you're like, 'Oh, you're a warrior. I'll go to battle with you any day.' But it doesn't need to be that way. And there's a balance there where you can't live in fear, but also this is a real thing."

 The NFL's efforts to reduce concussions through major rules changes, helmet technology and technique changes have been well-documented. Regarding CTE, the NFL's chief medical officer Dr. Allen Sills, who has been in his role for over nine years, said the league is following three precepts.

 "We have to continue to do the research to try to understand how these pathologic changes might be caused in life symptoms," Sills said. "No. 2, we have to make sure that people don't self-diagnose and that they get properly evaluated, and that we treat symptoms that we know we can treat. And No. 3, we just double down on our efforts to reduce and prevent head contact where we can."

 In a statement this summer, the NFLPA said in part: "We all share a responsibility to advance research, improve access to care, develop better treatments, and support those affected by the long-term impacts of the game."

 

 FOR MANY NFL players, the movie "Concussion" marked the introduction to the risks of long-term brain injuries from playing football. Among other events, the film dramatized the discovery of CTE in former Pittsburgh Steelers center Mike Webster, who died in poor physical and mental health in 2002 at age 50.

 One NFC defensive lineman said CTE was "a tough thing to think about." An NFC defensive end remembered watching the movie in high school with his mother and said: "It was one of the reasons she didn't want me playing football."

 

 The reminders have continued this summer, most recently when researchers in July determined former Dallas Cowboys defensive end Marshawn Kneeland had CTE when he died by suicide eight months prior.

 And the family of former San Francisco 49ers star Aldon Smith , who died suddenly at the age of 36 in June, is awaiting the results of testing after donating his brain to the Boston University CTE Center to determine whether CTE played a role in his death.

 For some players, a concern for CTE and other long-term health risks prompted them to end their careers earlier than expected. One of the top rookies in 2014, linebacker Chris Borland, retired after just one season at age 24 citing concerns about head trauma . Former Tampa Bay Buccaneers offensive lineman Ali Marpet retired in 2022 at the age of 28. In an interview with ESPN earlier this month, he described it as "one of the hardest decisions I've made in my life."

 He added, "For me, my personal value system [prioritizes] health. And if that's going to be the case, I want to live authentically and in line with those values. And if that's going to be the case, then football…

title: Would NFL players take a test that could diagnose CTE in the living?
summary: Would players want to know if they have the disease? Some would and some wouldn't. Here's what they said.
full_text:
Larry Johnson knows something is not right with him.

 The 46-year-old former All-Pro NFL running back has had no shortage of indicators. He points to his moments of disorientation, when he doesn't know where he is, or when he doesn't remember putting an item in his pocket minutes before. He's also reminded when he struggles to control his emotions.

 "My short-term memory was so bad, I could literally go into a store and 30 minutes later come out and not know where my car is parked," Johnson said. "Or, I'm driving and I just get blanked and I don't even know where I'm going or know where I'm at."

 Johnson, a 2003 first-round pick by the Kansas City Chiefs , is convinced he has chronic traumatic encephalopathy, the progressive, degenerative brain disease known as CTE. It's a product, he believes, of the constant pounding he took during nine seasons as one of the NFL's most physical backs. Researchers believe CTE is caused by repeated sub-concussive hits to the head.

 But Johnson doesn't know for sure if he has the condition.

 He can't.

 Currently, scientists can only diagnose CTE by studying a brain after death, leading many former NFL players to commit their brains to science after they die.

 But what if CTE could be diagnosed in the living?

 

 "I think we're close," said Michael Alosco, a neuropsychologist and associate professor at Boston University. Alosco is part of a team conducting government-funded research in this area through the second phase of the Diagnose CTE Research Project. Alosco said subjects in his study are 50 and older because that's when CTE is generally thought to be developed enough to be captured with testing.

 Researchers have been following over 300 former players -- in addition to Alzheimer's patients who did not play the sport -- since its first phase began in 2015. Now they're looking for patterns to emerge in testing. Putting an exact timeline on these efforts is difficult.

 Clarity from such a test might inform how doctors treat current or former players experiencing symptoms associated with CTE. Definitively diagnosing or ruling out CTE could be a game changer for those who assume they have the disease but don't. 

 "Many of these conditions cause cognitive symptoms that may overlap with CTE, but the difference here is that they are treatable," said Rachel Grashow, a researcher at Harvard University who has studied the health of former NFL players.

 "And ignoring this reality has dire consequences. We know that having cognitive symptoms and these conditions puts players at a much higher risk for believing they have CTE, and at risk for frequent thoughts of self-harm."

 A study published in 2024 reported nearly a third of former NFL players with general health symptoms -- including sleep apnea, hypertension, low testosterone and depression -- believed they had CTE. That group was five times more likely to have suicidal thoughts than those who did not attribute their symptoms to CTE.

 ESPN asked more than 30 active and retired players this summer about a range of CTE-related topics, including whether they would take a test if it could diagnose CTE while they're alive, and how that would impact whether they would continue playing.

 

 Would you take the CTE test if one were available? 

 Marcus Mariota , Washington Commanders QB, 32, in his 12th season : Yeah, I would. I think because at the end of the day, it gives insight to the rest of the NFL, to college kids, to high school kids of what we're getting ourselves into. Then yeah, absolutely.

 And I hope as we get going further into this that there are people that are open to be studied and hopefully you can kind of get answers a little more available and give guys kind of a clearer picture of what this all looks like.

 

 CJ Williams , Jacksonville Jaguars WR, 23, in his first season : I would probably take it post-football. And it would probably be because I love the game so much. I wouldn't quit football knowing it. It'd be a very hard quit for me. But after I'm done playing, I would probably do it because I would make lifestyle changes for that reason.

 Joshua Metellus , Minnesota Vikings safety, 28, in his seventh season: I probably wouldn't want [the test] while I'm in the league, because I think it'll change the way I play. But I know there's a lot of guys who are very curious and would like to know.

 And it would change the way to play ... more safe, play more conscious of it. Or not play.

 DeShon Elliott , Pittsburgh Steelers safety, 29, in his eighth season : Yeah, I would. I definitely would. Because I would like to know, and then I can figure out how I could prevent it.

 

 Mo Alie-Cox , Indianapolis Colts TE, 32, in his ninth season : I don't think I would want to know, because then people will start treating you differently, looking at you differently.

 When people get diagnosed with something, people start trying to baby you and things like that. I don't think I would want to know. But I think if symptoms start to show, then of course I would, just to protect you and everyone else around you. You can treat it if they end up finding a treatment for it. But right now there ain't no treatment and no one knows how to diagnose it. So it's a very complex situation you're dealing with.

 JJ Jansen , Carolina Panthers LS, 40, in his 19th season : If there was sort of a noninvasive way to understand where you stood on your health, I think anyone would do that, right? We're already doing that with blood testing, urine tests. We have one of the most extensive preseason physicals in terms of testing our bodies of probably any league currently, which is obviously a fantastic thing. So I think anyone would at least be willing to consider adding that into their planning purposes.

 Micah McFadden , New York Giants LB, 26, in his fifth season : I probably would, yeah. Yeah. I'd be interested in that.

 Will Fries , Vikings guard, 28, in his sixth season : Oh wow. That is a really good question. I don't know. I don't know what I would do, honestly. Wow. Stumper. I think for me, I'm playing this game because one, I'm very fortunate to be able to play it. I'm really lucky I've worked my whole life to be in this situation and I'm just going to maximize the resources that I have of brain health and prevention.

 Robert Hainsey , Jaguars C, 28, in his sixth season : Yeah, for sure.

 Malik Hooker , Dallas Cowboys safety, 30, in his 10th season : Absolutely. I mean, not only for me but my family as well. I feel like they've sacrificed so much as far as their time, their responsibilities and their lives into helping me and supporting me for my job, the least I could do was make sure I'm up to par as far as my health, my mindset and my mentals.

 

 Would you keep playing if tests showed you had CTE? 

 Green Bay Packers safety Xavier McKinney , 28, in his seventh year : Probably not. No.

 Hainsey : Tough question. Too many variables there, because I don't know how good the test is if they just come out with it. ... If they come up with it now, we're the guinea pigs. We don't freaking know if it's going to work or not. So, I couldn't say. If you knew for sure [if it was accurate], yeah, you'd have to think about it because we got a lot more years to live after football, for sure. But that's a tough one because it's just too hypothetical.

 Jansen : Certainly, if you had information that said you were more susceptible or you were maybe already dealing with stuff, I think guys would feel differently about it. That being said, like you're dealing with a lot of unknowns. And as the science continues to develop and we're learning more about the brain and all of these things, I think guys are making more educated decisions.

 

 Hooker : That would be a discussion I would have to have with my family, obviously the professionals and try to make the best decision not only for myself but my family as well.

title: 2026 NFL Power Rankings: How all 32 teams stack up for Week 4
summary: How do all 32 NFL teams stack up through three weeks? Plus, we picked out each team's biggest fantasy surprise -- good or bad.
full_text:
Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season  was filled with close matchups. There were 12 games decided by eight or fewer points Sunday, tying the record for the most such matchups in a single day, per ESPN Research.

 Along with those close contests came plenty of  intriguing fantasy performances . So in addition to our 1-32 rankings, we asked our NFL Nation reporters to look at every team's fantasy football surprise (good or bad) this season. They went off ESPN Fantasy 's draft rankings ,  average draft position (ADP) and  current scoring leaders in PPR leagues.

 To form the list, our power panel of more than a dozen NFL analysts evaluates how all 32 teams stack up against one another, ranking them from No. 1 to 32. And here are a few highlights from this week's rankings:

 
 The 3-0 Raiders are shooting up our list, climbing six spots after doing the same last week. They're the first team in the common draft era (since 1967) to start 3-0 after selecting a QB No. 1 ( Fernando Mendoza ) in the previous draft, per ESPN Research. And against the Saints, they broke a franchise-worst streak of 39 regular-season games in which they failed to score 30 points. 
 New England fell six more spots after quarterback  Drake Maye  registered a 15.5 Total QBR in a blowout loss to the Jaguars -- a career worst with at least 15 dropbacks. Through three games, the Patriots' offense is averaging the lowest EPA per play and points per drive by any team since the 2023 Jets, who had Zach Wilson at QB, per ESPN Research. 
 After starting 0-3, the Buccaneers are ahead of only the Titans and Dolphins. This is the team's worst record to begin a season since 2014, when it finished 2-14 in its first year under current general manager Jason Licht. And things might not get easier for the Bucs, who are expected  to play undrafted rookie free agent Jalon Daniels in place of the injured Baker Mayfield (thumb) for at least the next three weeks. 
 
 Let's get into the full list, starting with the same No. 1 team as last week.

 Previous rankings: Week 2 | Week 3 

 

 
 Jump to a team: 
 ARI | ATL | BAL | BUF | CAR | CHI | CIN 
 CLE | DAL | DEN | DET | GB | HOU | IND 
 JAX | KC | LAC | LAR | LV | MIA | MIN 
 NE | NO | NYG | NYJ | PHI | PIT | SF 
 SEA | TB | TEN | WSH 

 
 

 

 1. Buffalo Bills (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Chargers 24-16 
 Week 3 ranking: 1 

 Fantasy surprise: TE Dalton Kincaid 

 

 Through three weeks, Kincaid leads all NFL tight ends in receiving yards and has caught 14 of the 17 passes thrown his way. He ranks among the top 10 tight ends in targets, posting the best catch percentage (82.4%) of any tight end or wide receiver with at least that many targets. Not bad for someone who was ranked as TE15 in ESPN's draft rankings. -- Nick Suss 

 
 

 

 2. San Francisco 49ers (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Cardinals 36-30 
 Week 3 ranking: 3 

 Fantasy surprise: TE George Kittle 

 

 Under normal circumstances, it would not be a surprise to see Kittle as the TE4 in fantasy. But given that he  tore his right Achilles on Jan. 11 and missed all of training camp, that he returned in Week 1 close to his usual self is a testament to his passion for the game. And the Niners have needed every bit of his production to help weather the storm of injuries elsewhere. Kittle ranks fifth among all tight ends in receiving yards (174), 11th in receptions (12) and tied for first in touchdowns (three).  -- Nick Wagoner 

 
 

 3. Kansas City Chiefs (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Dolphins 24-10 
 Week 3 ranking: 4 

 Fantasy surprise: RB Kenneth Walker III 

 

 Most fantasy owners knew Walker was a good choice, especially after his impressive postseason run to help the Seahawks win the Super Bowl. But not even the Chiefs could have expected this level of production from Walker, who has the second-most total fantasy points at RB this season. He has already produced 442 scrimmage yards and four total touchdowns. Walker is the first player in franchise history to have two games with a rushing and receiving touchdown within the first three weeks, per ESPN Research.  -- Nate Taylor 

 
 

 4. Seattle Seahawks (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Lost to the Commanders 33-31 
 Week 3 ranking: 2 

 Fantasy surprise: RB Jadarian Price 

 

 Price was 25th among running backs in ADP, reflecting the fact that he was going to be part of a timeshare in Seattle's backfield. But even with those modest expectations, the rookie first-round pick is off to an underwhelming start. He ranks 47th in fantasy points among running backs after a dud of a performance in Week 3, when he totaled 22 scrimmage yards on six touches with a lost fumble. The fumble was Price's second in as many weeks, which was a big reason for his diminished workload. -- Brady Henderson 

 
 

 5. Baltimore Ravens (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Cowboys 34-31 
 Week 3 ranking: 7 

 Fantasy surprise: TE Mark Andrews 

 

 Andrews had surrendered the title of Lamar Jackson 's No. 1 target to WR Zay Flowers , but there was hope that he would remain an option in the red zone. He has only one red zone target on eight routes run this season. Now, he is dealing with a hand injury that limited his playing time in Week 3. Andrews, who was ranked as the TE14 before the season, is currently 19th in scoring at his position.  -- Jamison Hensley 

 
 

 

 6. Denver Broncos (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Rams 30-26 
 Week 3 ranking: 8 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Courtland Sutton 

 

 The Broncos' offensive struggles, especially in first halves, have dragged down everybody's numbers. They haven't found a rhythm much of the time, and save for Jaylen Waddle 's 138-yard effort against the Jaguars in Week 2 , the WRs have been caught up in the wash ( Pat Bryant  has the group's only TD catch). Sutton, who is second in targets to Waddle with 16, could be seen as the biggest disappointment. He has yet to eclipse more than 10 fantasy points in any game. -- Jeff Legwold 

 
 

 7. Los Angeles Rams (1-2) 
 Week 3 result: Lost to the Broncos 30-26 
 Week 3 ranking: 5 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Puka Nacua 

 

 Despite missing part of training camp with a psoas injury , Nacua had an ADP of 9.0. But he has played only in Week 1 because of a groin injury, putting up 12.4 points in PPR leagues. On Sunday, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported  that the injury "has impacted [Nacua's] explosiveness." Last week, coach Sean McVay said  that barring a setback, the expectation is that Nacua will be able to play in Week 4  against the Eagles. -- Sarah Barshop 

 
 

 8. Philadelphia Eagles (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Lost to the Bears 27-7 
 Week 3 ranking: 6 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Dontayvion Wicks 

 

 Wicks has the second-most receptions (nine) and receiving yards (179) on the team behind DeVonta Smith . He is currently the WR30 in fantasy. There was some thought heading into the summer that rookie Makai Lemon could ascend to the No. 2 role, but injuries left him on the sideline for most of camp. In the meantime, Wicks and QB Jalen Hurts  have developed a comfort level with one another, particularly in high-leverage moments.  -- Tim McManus 

 
 

 9. Minnesota Vikings (3-0) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Buccaneers 23-16 
 Week 3 ranking: 12 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Justin Jefferson 

 

 Jefferson had an ADP of 13.4, but he has had only one fantasy-productive game for a variety of reasons. That came in Week 1, when he caught two touchdown passes from backup quarterback Carson Wentz  and scored 31.2 fantasy points. The Vikings played their Week 2 game at rainy Soldier Field, and in Week 3, Jefferson played only one series before departing with an ankle injury . Jefferson could be back as soon as Sunday against the Dolphins, but with the Vikings' offense struggling, it's unclear whether Jefferson can get back on track. -- Kevin Seifert 

 

 
 

 10. Jacksonville Jaguars (2-1) 
 Week 3 result: Beat the Patriots 35-6 
 Week 3 ranking: 13 

 Fantasy surprise: WR Brian Thomas Jr .

title: 2027 NFL draft order projections for Round 1, top pick, more
summary: ESPN's Football Power Index projects the 2027 NFL draft order for Round 1, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.
full_text:
The 2027 NFL draft is still months away, but with the 2026 season underway, we're starting to track pick order in Round 1. Which teams are in position to add elite prospects in the top 10 next April? What about the top five ... or even at No. 1?

 What follows is not the current draft order based on records. It is a projection of what ESPN's Football Power Index thinks the order ultimately will be by the end of the season. Each week during the season, the FPI projects the draft order by simulating the remainder of the season 10,000 times. Game probabilities are based primarily on the model's team ratings and game locations. The draft order is determined by the records the model projects for each team after 17 games, as well as each team's average draft position across the simulations.

 So where do things stand? Here are the full sortable projections, complete with each team's chances to pick in the top five, in the top 10 and at No. 1.

 
 See more on the NFL draft 

 
 

 First-round picks that have been traded: 

 
 The Green Bay Packers ' selection was dealt to the Dallas Cowboys in the Micah Parsons trade . 
 The Indianapolis Colts ' selection was dealt to the New York Jets in the Sauce Gardner trade . 
 The Los Angeles Rams ' selection was dealt to the Cleveland Browns in the Myles Garrett trade . 
 The better of Dallas' two selections (either its own pick or the Packers' original pick) was dealt to the Jets in the Quinnen Williams trade .

title: Super Bowl LXI odds: All 32 teams' odds to win the championship
summary: Every NFL team's win total, as well as odds to win the division, the conference and Super Bowl LXI.
full_text:
For the first time since the NFL season began, the Los Angeles Rams are not the standalone favorites to win Super Bowl LXI. After their second loss of the season, the Rams lengthened to +670, up from the +500 they had coming into the campaign, to tie them with the 3-0 Buffalo Bills , who have improved from the second-best 10-1 they entered the season at.

 

 Next on the odds board is another tie between the Baltimore Ravens and San Francisco 49ers at +900. The former has improved from 10-1 at the beginning of the season, but the latter has made a big jump from 19-1 after an impressive undefeated start to the campaign. San Francisco is also tied with Los Angeles for the best odds to win the NFC at +400. The reigning champion Seattle Seahawks (10-1) and Kansas City Chiefs (+1050) round out the top six.

 One of the most compelling divisions in the young season has been the NFC North, and Week 3's results had a big effect on team futures. The Detroit Lions continue to have the division's best Super Bowl odds at 19-1, but the Chicago Bears and Minnesota Vikings are quickly making up ground, both at 24-1. Meanwhile, the Green Bay Packers have taken a big hit in the future odds after a rocky 1-2 start, showing 55-1 after three weeks -- a significant lengthening from 25-1 a week prior.

 Note: Odds by DraftKings   and subject to change.

title: Seven things Solak thinks entering NFL Week 4
summary: Bowers will go off under Klint Kubiak? The Rams need another pass catcher? Steelers-Browns will be fun? And Lamar Jackson for MVP? Get ready for Week 4 with some takes.
full_text:
Who's ready to put their thinking caps on? Week 3 of the 2026 NFL season will go down in the history books, as 12 -- count 'em, 12! -- Sunday games finished within one score, the new single-day record for the league. Toss in two fun primetime games on Thursday and Monday and that was about as good a week as NFL football gets.

 Every Tuesday of the NFL season , I'll turn the page from the previous week to the upcoming one with seven things I think. These aren't full-scale predictions; those come later. They aren't concrete takeaways from the past week of NFL action, either; those are fired off Sunday or Monday. Instead, these are the uncertain topics. They are things that might be true, but it'll probably take the next few games to find out. And at the bottom, you'll find a few extra half-thoughts ... just those little inklings I'm unable to shake.

 This week, I'll start with the one player I've been most excited to see in his new system, make another pick for MVP (I'm up to two in three weeks) and highlight an intradivisional game between surprising 2-1 teams you should probably watch for fun. Here are seven things I think ahead of Week 4.

 

 
 Jump to: 
 Bowers is the new JSN 
 Jackson for league MVP 
 Lawrence reminds us to be patient with QBs 
 Rams should make one more trade 
 Steelers-Browns is suddenly important 
 I will never trust the Bills 
 McCarthy won't save the Giants 
 Five extra inklings 

 

 
 

 I think ...  Brock Bowers is the new Jaxon Smith-Njigba 
 We had to wait a few extra weeks for it, but one of the most anticipated debuts of the 2026 season struck Sunday. Bowers, the third-year Raiders tight end fresh off a meniscus cleanup, took his first snaps in Klint Kubiak's offense against the Saints. The final card? Ten catches, 116 yards and a score. Bowers has four career games of 10-plus receptions, 100-plus yards and a touchdown. Since he entered the league in 2024, the rest of the NFL's tight ends combined  have only four such games.

 

 So, he picked up where he left off.

 Watching Bowers is such a delight. He has receiver-like instincts and catch technique. He has receiver-like movement skills. He can run receiver-esque routes -- routes other coaches wouldn't think to ask of their tight ends.

 Now, you've likely heard other tight ends erroneously called "quasi-wide receivers." Analysts were obsessed with flex tight ends in the prime of Travis Kelce and Mark Andrews , so we started throwing the label around willy-nilly. It's important, in our appreciation of what Bowers brings to the Raiders' offense, to be objective about the uniqueness of his impact.

 Think of a smaller pass-catching tight end who's having a productive year: Dalton Kincaid with the Bills has been a breakout star. Against the Lions in Week 2, Kincaid had seven targets from traditional wide receiver alignments -- either in the slot or wide -- which was one of the highest among all tight ends this season. Arizona's Trey McBride , the league's preeminent move tight end, had 10 such targets against the Seahawks in Week 2 and the Chargers in Week 1.

 Bowers had 13 on Sunday against the Saints. In fact, all 13 of his targets were from slot or wide alignments. It's the most such targets a tight end has seen in the past three seasons. Specifically out wide, Bowers was targeted eight times, which ties the most out-wide targets a tight end has had since the 2016 season -- as far back as I have alignment data. He caught six passes out wide ... which ties the most out-wide receptions a tight end has had since the 2016 season.

 That is wide receiver usage. The Raiders were in "multi-tight-end" sets on 81% of their snaps Sunday -- the highest rate for any team in a game this season -- because they're not actually multi-tight-end sets . It's really 11.5 personnel, because they have the skeleton key in Bowers.

 Let's see what this looks like in practice. On a key third down late in the third quarter of Sunday's win, the Raiders isolate Bowers on the backside by motioning to a four-strong formation. With all four receivers to the opposite side of the field, the Saints' hands are tied -- they have to play Bowers in man coverage with their best man corner, Kool-Aid McKinstry . Watch Bowers feint the slant, and when McKinstry doesn't bite, he bursts to McKinstry's upfield shoulder to threaten the go-ball and open up space for the back-shoulder throw. It's short, because  Kirk Cousins  underappreciated Bowers' speed, and Bowers makes a great adjustment for the first down.

 

 This is obviously super-duper sick. For most teams, a tight end in isolation on a cornerback is not a win -- for the Raiders, it is.

 What's particularly cool is that Kubiak wants to give these opportunities to Bowers over anyone else on the Raiders' roster. When Kubiak was the Seahawks' offensive coordinator last season, that player for him was star receiver Smith-Njigba. We see almost the exact same play here, in the Seahawks' 2025 Week 7 game against the Texans. Sam Darnold alerts to the man coverage on the backside and throws Smith-Njigba on the vertical route against press coverage, keeping the ball vertical instead of throwing it to the back shoulder given the positioning of the corner.

 

 This is far from the only example we can find of Bowers getting the JSN treatment from Kubiak. Again in isolation on the backside of the formation and again on third down, Bowers uses his reduced alignment to get into an out-breaking route at the sticks. Smith-Njigba was used on similar routes in similar alignments for Kubiak on money downs last season.

 

 Here, Bowers motions into a stack alignment to get a free release into an option route -- look at how easily he widens McKinstry before snapping back into space. He has special burst and body control for a tight end, much as Smith-Njigba has special burst and body control for a wide receiver. Smith-Njigba takes the option route the other direction, but the usage is the same.

 

 That Kubiak is giving Bowers the same plays he gave Smith-Njigba is important because Smith-Njigba was as high volume a receiver as we had seen in decades. Smith-Njigba had a preposterous 44.1% of the Seahawks' receiving yards and 35.9% of the Seahawks' targets through the 2025 season -- the highest share of a team's receiving production since Brandon Marshall with the 2012 Chicago Bears. In one game, Bowers had 46.8% of the team's receiving yards and 41.9% of the team's targets. That's Smith-Njigba usage and Smith-Njigba volume.

 Of course, because Bowers is a tight end, he won't get the same explosive opportunities that Smith-Njigba got down the field. JSN had a heavy dose of crossing patterns that Bowers largely didn't see in Week 3 -- those are big-play run-after-catch chances of play-action. Smith-Njigba could also outrun a corner for a 50-yard vertical, and Bowers isn't doing that.

 But what he is doing, we haven't seen at the tight end position since peak Kelce -- fitting, given the Raiders (3-0) face the Chiefs (3-0) in Week 4. Bowers now has two career games with at least six targets or at least five receptions from wide alignments -- games we could reasonably call "high volume" games on the outside. He is only 30 games into his NFL career. Kelce has played in 168 games since 2016. If Bowers' Week 3 usage keeps up, he'll join prime Kelce as the lone tight end of this era who lines up on the outside and wins , over and over again.

 

 

 It will be interesting to see how the Chiefs handle this. Through three weeks, they have played two teams without a strong tight end feature -- the Broncos (2-1) and the Dolphins (0-3), with the Colts (1-2) and Tyler Warren sandwiched there in the middle. Warren went for 21 yards on six catches (seven targets) against the Chiefs, as the Colts have devolved into targeting him shallow on designed touches to protect the recovering Daniel Jones from long dropbacks. Bowers will be the Chiefs' first real tight end test.

 Now,…

title: Christian Izien stars in strong defensive week for NFL stars with Africa ties
summary: Detroit Lions safety Christian Izien - who is from Far Rockaway, Queens, but has always proudly represented Nigeria too - was a standout among many NFL stars with ties to Africa who shone in Week 3.
full_text:
Detroit Lions safety Christian Izien - who is from Far Rockaway, Queens, but has always proudly represented Nigeria too - was a standout among many NFL stars with ties to Africa who shone in Week 3.

 There were some highlights on offense too - notably from Jaxon Smith-Njigba and John Metchie III - but generally, this was a week where defense shone brightest for the continent's stars.

 Africa Player of the Week: Christian Izien (Detroit Lions) 
 

 Izien was immensely influential for the Detroit Lions in their 31-24 win over the New York Jets, making a total of 11 tackles - nine of which were solo tackles - and defending one pass.

 Izien - who has family ties to Nigeria - made three tackles for loss in addition to a vital intervention to prevent a touchdown right on the stroke of half-time. Geno Smith went for a Hail Mary with the Jets 10-7 down, but amid a sea of bodies from both teams, it was Izien who got to the ball first to tip it away.

 His performance played a key role in the game ending in favour of the Lions - who are 2-1 for the season, with the Jets 1-2.

 Africa Moment of the Week: Thomas Incoom and Maema Njongmeta (Carolina Panthers) 

 There were plenty of big hits to choose from among Africa's NFL stars. However, Incoom (born in Ghana) and Njongmeta (born in Cameroon) get the nod for collaborating in a moment which demonstrated what Africa has to offer the NFL.

 

 As their Carolina Panthers faced the Cleveland Browns, Njongmeta forced a fumble with a huge hit on Malachi Corley and then Incoom - who had earlier set the tone with a massive hit himself - was on hand for the fumble recovery.

 Although the Browns ultimately emerged victorious 21-18, it was not for any want of trying from the West African duo.

 Honorable mentions 

 Jaxon Smith-Njigba - who proudly represents Sierra Leone, with which he has ties through his grandparents - scored two touchdowns among a total of 10 receptions for 128 yards. His Seattle Seahawks lost 33-31 to the Washington Commanders despite his contribution on offense and Uchenna Nwosu (ties to Nigeria) defending a pass.

 John Metchie III - who is of Nigerian and Taiwanese descent and lived in Ghana as a young child - scored a touchdown for the Panthers in their defeat to the Browns. Nigerian-American outside linebacker Princely Umanmielen also made a notable contribution even in defeat for the Panthers, picking up a sack.

 Adetomiwa Adebawore deserves special mention for his 1.5 sacks for the Indianapolis Colts in their 19-17 win over the Houston Texans.

 Ruke Orhorhoro (Jacksonville Jaguars), Ogbo Okoronkwo (San Francisco 49ers), Eyioma Uwazurike (Denver Broncos), and Dayo Odeyingbo (Chicago Bears) - all of Nigerian descent - all picked up sacks in Week 3 wins.

 Osa Odighizuwa, who contributed to the Niners' 36-30 win over the Arizona Cardinals with a pass defended, also has ties to Nigeria.

 So, too, do players who had impressive moments on both sides of the Buffalo Bills' 24-16 win over the LA Chargers - Davison Igbinosun defended a pass for the winning side and Justin Eboigbe forced a fumble for the Chargers.

 Africa-born player watch 

 Ghana's Incoom and Cameroon's Njongmeta did the continent proud with their performances for the Panthers in the Browns loss. It is worth noting that Ruke Orhorhoro, who picked up a sack for the Jacksonville Jaguars in their 35-6 thrashing of the New England Patriots, was born in Lagos - one of many players who flew the Nigerian flag high in Week 3.
